title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄序
上天生賢以輔世其盛也由氣運之昌
教化之洽耳然氣運教化相與流
通恒始于西北而後及于東南虞
之聲教始冀都而以東漸南暨為
極周之風化始豐鎬而以化成南
國為至故當時賢才之生高陽高
辛有八元八凱之舉而萬邦黎獻
===
亦共為帝臣羔羊大夫有正直節
儉之德而在野武夫亦公侯腹心
是皆帝王德化上下與天地同流
舉一世而甄陶之者然也我
國家受
天眷命撫御斯世
太祖高皇帝肇迹淮西
太宗文皇帝定都冀北而東南嶺海之
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄序
上天生賢以輔世，其盛也，由氣運之昌、教化之洽耳。然氣運、教化相與流通，恒始于西北而後及于東南。虞之聲教始冀都，而以東漸南暨為極；周之風化始豐鎬，而以化成南國為至。故當時賢才之生，高陽、高辛有八元、八凱之舉，而萬邦黎獻亦共為帝臣；《羔羊》大夫有正直節儉之德，而在野武夫亦公侯腹心。是皆帝王德化上下與天地同流，舉一世而甄陶之者然也。我國家受天眷命，撫御斯世，太祖高皇帝肇迹淮西，太宗文皇帝定都冀北，而東南嶺海之
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

High Heaven gives birth to worthies to assist the world; their flourishing comes simply from the prosperity of the cosmic vitality and fortune and the pervasiveness of moral instruction and transformation. Yet cosmic fortune and moral transformation circulate together, constantly beginning in the northwest and later reaching the southeast. The renown and instruction of Yu [Shun] began in the capital of Ji, and reached its utmost extent in gradually spreading to the east and extending to the south; the moral influence of the Zhou began in Feng and Hao, and reached its culmination in transforming the southern states. Therefore, in the emergence of worthy talents in those times, Gaoyang and Gaoxin had the elevation of the Eight Worthies (Bayuan) and Eight Talents (Bakai), while theeminent elders of the myriad states also jointly became the sovereign's ministers; the grandees of the "Lambskin" ("Gaoyang") ode possessed the virtues of rectitude and frugality, while even the martial men in the wilds were the trusted confidants ("heart and belly") of dukes and marquises. All of this was so because the virtuous transformation of the emperors and kings flowed above and below together with Heaven and Earth, molding and fashioning the entire world. Our Dynasty received the favored Mandate of Heaven to pacify and govern this world. Grand Progenitor Emperor Gao [the Hongwu Emperor] founded the imperial enterprise in Huixi, and Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen [the Yongle Emperor] established the capital in northern Ji, whereas in the southeastern region of the Nanling mountains and the seas…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
間逖遠
京畿漸被
王化方諸中州能無先後之差乎比于
列聖嗣陳政教益勤益勵已逾百年斯
薰蒸暢達無遠不洽而嶺南賢才
始亦衆盛足以儷中州而應昌運
也矧茲數歲奉
勅總督兩廣軍務兼理巡撫右都御史
===
韓雍來涖斯境威惠兼行夷獠馴
服而興學勸士尤所加意邇者復
同奉
勅總鎮太監陳瑄總兵官平江伯陳銳
開設總府于梧州武備脩舉風教
日新而士習丕變乃成化辛卯秋
當大比興賢而十郡七州之士若
庠序生徒若山林韋布若介胄子
punctuated: 間，逖遠京畿，漸被王化，方諸中州，能無先後之差乎？比于列聖嗣陳政教，益勤益勵，已逾百年。斯薰蒸暢達，無遠不洽，而嶺南賢才始亦衆盛，足以儷中州而應昌運也。矧茲數歲，奉勅總督兩廣軍務兼理巡撫右都御史韓雍來涖斯境，威惠兼行，夷獠馴服，而興學勸士尤所加意。邇者，復同奉勅總鎮太監陳瑄、總兵官平江伯陳銳開設總府于梧州，武備脩舉，風教日新，而士習丕變。乃成化辛卯秋，當大比興賢，而十郡七州之士，若庠序生徒，若山林韋布，若介胄子
translation_en: … region, lying far distant from the metropolitan area, gradually received the royal civilizing influence; compared to the Central Plains, how could there not be a difference of earlier and later? By the time the successive sage emperors inherited the throne and set forth governance and instruction with ever greater diligence and encouragement, more than a hundred years had passed. Thus this permeating and flourishing influence reached everywhere without exception, and worthy talents South of the Passes at last became numerous and thriving as well, sufficient to match the Central Plains and respond to this prosperous era. Moreover, in recent years, the Right Censor-in-Chief Han Yong 韓雍, Supreme Commander of Military Affairs in Liangguang and concurrently Grand Coordinator by imperial command, came to govern this territory. Exercising both awe and benevolence, he brought the non-Chinese tribes into submission, while paying especially close attention to promoting schools and encouraging scholars. Recently, together with the Grand Defender Eunuch Chen Xuan 陳瑄 and the Regional Commander Chen Rui 陳銳, Earl of Pingjiang, both acting by imperial command, he further established the Supreme Headquarters at Wuzhou 梧州. Military defenses have been put in order, moral teaching is renewed day by day, and the ethos of the literati has undergone a great transformation. Now, in the autumn of the xinmao year of the Chenghua reign (1471), at the time of the triennial examination for promoting the worthy, the scholars of the ten prefectures and seven subprefectures—whether students in the local schools, commoners from the mountains and forests, or sons and younger brothers of military families…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
弟預有司舉送者幾二千人先期
提督學校僉事胡榮循例小試擇
其可入場者千二百有奇視往昔
為衆盛矣至期鸞等膺禮聘而来
忝司考校而巡按廣東監察御史
程宏寔監臨其事曁鎖院内而提
調則左布政使張瑄左叅政張瓚
監試則按察使甯良副使章格外
===
而綱維防範則右布政使周鐸左
叅政王佐右叅政卓天錫左叅議
李田副使孔鏞吕洪涂棐僉事王
祐陶魯陳貴林錦方泌姚俊凡諸
執事俱遴選以充而嚴革宿弊咸
秉至公三試之後取其經義論策
典雅純正者七十有五人遵解額
也復遵故事刻小録將以徹
punctuated: 弟預有司舉送者幾二千人。先期，提督學校僉事胡榮循例小試，擇其可入場者千二百有奇，視往昔為衆盛矣。至期，鸞等膺禮聘而来，忝司考校。而巡按廣東監察御史程宏寔監臨其事。曁鎖院，内而提調則左布政使張瑄、左叅政張瓚，監試則按察使甯良、副使章格；外而綱維防範則右布政使周鐸、左叅政王佐、右叅政卓天錫、左叅議李田、副使孔鏞、吕洪、涂棐、僉事王祐、陶魯、陳貴、林錦、方泌、姚俊。凡諸執事俱遴選以充，而嚴革宿弊，咸秉至公。三試之後，取其經義、論、策典雅純正者七十有五人，遵解額也。復遵故事，刻小録，將以徹
translation_en: …military households who were recommended and forwarded by the local authorities numbered nearly two thousand men. Ahead of time, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Directing Education Hu Rong 胡榮 followed precedent in holding a preliminary test, selecting more than twelve hundred who were qualified to enter the examination compound—a more numerous and flourishing turnout than in the past. When the appointed time arrived, I, Luan 鸞, and my colleagues received the courteous invitation and came to humbly take charge of evaluating the papers. Regional Inspector of Guangdong and Investigating Censor Cheng Hong 程宏 actually served as Supervising Official for the affair. Once the examination compound was locked, inside, the Proctors were Left Administration Commissioner Zhang Xuan 張瑄 and Left Administration Vice Commissioner Zhang Zan 張瓚, while the Censorial Supervisors were Surveillance Commissioner Ning Liang 甯良 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhang Ge 章格; outside, those who maintained order and security were Right Administration Commissioner Zhou Duo 周鐸, Left Administration Vice Commissioner Wang Zuo 王佐, Right Administration Vice Commissioner Zhuo Tianxi 卓天錫, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Li Tian 李田, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Kong Yong 孔鏞, Lü Hong 吕洪, and Tu Fei 涂棐, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Wang You 王祐, Tao Lu 陶魯, Chen Gui 陳貴, Lin Jin 林錦, Fang Bi 方泌, and Yao Jun 姚俊. All the various functionaries were carefully selected to fill their posts, strictly eradicating long-standing abuses and all upholding the utmost impartiality. After the three sessions, we selected seventy-five men whose expositions on the Classics, discourses, and policy essays were refined, orthodox, and pure, in compliance with the provincial quota. Following established precedent once again, we have had this small record engraved so that it may be presented for…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
御覽而示方来仰惟
皇明奄有華夏
祖宗創制垂憲盡革近代因循之陋而
遠追虞周文明之治矣然所以弼
贊治化承保
上天純佑命而永建億萬年之基者尚
有頼乎多賢之用也今諸士子荷
聖朝作養造就而獲登名賢書行將與
===
天下士會試禮闈進對
大廷致用有日矣雖然所以進身之階
不外乎文藝而致用立身之本不
在是也要必存心脩德焉耳嘗觀
有虞之世九德咸事而曰嚴祗敬
百僚師師者其心何如也有周之
士不顯亦世而厥猶翼翼有孝有
德者其德何如也諸士子誦詩讀
punctuated: 御覽，而示方来。仰惟皇明奄有華夏，祖宗創制垂憲，盡革近代因循之陋，而遠追虞、周文明之治矣。然所以弼贊治化，承保上天純佑命，而永建億萬年之基者，尚有頼乎多賢之用也。今諸士子荷聖朝作養造就，而獲登名賢書，行將與天下士會試禮闈，進對大廷，致用有日矣。雖然，所以進身之階，不外乎文藝，而致用立身之本，不在是也，要必存心脩德焉耳。嘗觀有虞之世，九德咸事，而曰嚴祗敬，百僚師師者，其心何如也？有周之士，不顯亦世，而厥猶翼翼，有孝有德者，其德何如也？諸士子誦詩讀
translation_en:
… the Imperial gaze and display it for generations to come.

We humbly reflect that the August Ming encompasses all of China. Our Imperial Ancestors established institutions and handed down laws, completely sweeping away the base routines of recent eras and reaching back afar to the enlightened governance of Yu [Shun] and the Zhou dynasty. Yet the means to assist in transformative governance, to receive and preserve the pure and favoring Mandate of Supreme Heaven, and to establish forever the foundation for hundreds of millions of years still depends upon the employment of many worthy men. Now, all you scholars have received the nurturing and training of our Sacred Dynasty and have succeeded in having your names inscribed in the roster of worthies. Soon you will gather with the scholars of the realm to take the Metropolitan Examination at the Ministry of Rites, advance to reply at the Great Court [in the Palace Examination], and the day when you will be put to practical service is at hand.

Even so, while the ladder by which one advances one's career is nothing other than literary art, the fundamental basis for establishing oneself and rendering practical service does not lie therein; in essence, one must simply preserve one's mind and cultivate one's virtue. Let us consider the age of Yu: those possessing the nine virtues all served in office, daily strict, reverent, and respectful, with all the hundred officials emulating one another—what was their state of mind like? And the officers of Zhou: were they not illustrious from generation to generation, their plans reverent and cautious, possessing filial piety and virtue—what was their virtue like? All you scholars, in chanting the Odes and reading…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
書志希古聖賢乆矣苟能日存祗
敬師師而懋昭翼翼孝德則爾之
心即虞廷黎獻之心爾之德即周
家多士之德豈直今世之士云乎
哉有是心有是德而輔世賛化之
功不虞周若者吾未之聞也其或
志功利而飾巧詐矜名譽而競葩
藻玆乃近代浮靡之習而非輔世
===
賛化之用也幸勉之哉幸戒之哉
鸞不佞敢以是言序諸首
山西太原府忻州儒學學正王鸞
謹序
punctuated:
書，志希古聖賢乆矣。苟能日存祗敬、師師，而懋昭翼翼、孝德，則爾之心即虞廷黎獻之心，爾之德即周家多士之德，豈直今世之士云乎哉？有是心，有是德，而輔世賛化之功不虞、周若者，吾未之聞也。其或志功利而飾巧詐，矜名譽而競葩藻，玆乃近代浮靡之習，而非輔世賛化之用也。幸勉之哉！幸戒之哉！鸞不佞，敢以是言序諸首。
山西太原府忻州儒學學正王鸞謹序。
translation_en:
…and reading the Documents, have long aspired to emulate the ancient sages and worthies. If you can daily preserve that reverent vigilance and mutual emulation, and strive to manifest that respectful caution and filial virtue, then your minds will be the very minds of the eminent worthies of the court of Yu, and your virtues will be the very virtues of the multitude of scholars of the House of Zhou—how could you merely be called scholars of the present age? That one might possess such a mind and such virtue, and yet fail to match the eras of Yu and Zhou in the achievement of assisting the world and aiding transformation—of this I have never heard. Should anyone instead set his mind on utility and profit while adorning himself with artful deceit, or boast of reputation while competing in flowery rhetoric, this is merely the frivolous and extravagant habit of recent ages, and is of no use in assisting the world and aiding transformation. Pray strive at this! Pray guard against that! Though I, Luan, am of no talent, I venture to place these words as a preface at the beginning.
Respectfully prefaced by Wang Luan 王鸞, Director of Studies of the Confucian School of Xinzhou in Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi.

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第一場
四書
子曰聽訟吾猶人也必也使無訟乎無
情者不得盡其辭大畏民志此謂知
本
子入太廟每事問或曰孰謂鄹人之子
知禮乎入太廟每事問子聞之曰是
禮也
===
曾子子思同道曾子師也父兄也子思
臣也微也曾子子思易地則皆然
易
直其正也方其義也君子敬以直內義
以方外敬義立而德不孤直方大不
習无不利則不疑其所行也
彖曰大有柔得尊位大中而上下應之
曰大有其德剛健而文明應乎天而
punctuated:
第一場
四書
子曰：「聽訟，吾猶人也。必也使無訟乎！」無情者不得盡其辭。大畏民志，此謂知本。
子入太廟，每事問。或曰：「孰謂鄹人之子知禮乎？入太廟，每事問。」子聞之，曰：「是禮也。」
曾子、子思同道。曾子，師也，父兄也；子思，臣也，微也。曾子、子思易地則皆然。
易
直，其正也；方，其義也。君子敬以直內，義以方外，敬義立而德不孤。「直，方，大，不習，无不利」，則不疑其所行也。
《彖》曰：「大有」，柔得尊位大中，而上下應之，曰「大有」。其德剛健而文明，應乎天而
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books

The Master said, "In hearing litigation, I am no different from anyone else. What is imperative, however, is to bring it about that there is no litigation at all!" Those whose claims lack substance are prevented from fully presenting their false testimony. Thus, a great awe is instilled in the minds of the people. This is called knowing the root.

When the Master entered the Grand Temple, he asked about everything. Someone remarked, "Who says that the son of the man from Zou understands ritual propriety? Upon entering the Grand Temple, he asks about everything." When the Master heard of this, he said, "This in itself is ritual propriety."

Master Zeng (Zengzi 曾子) and Zisi 子思 followed the same Way. Master Zeng was a teacher, in the position of a father or elder brother; Zisi was a minister, in a subordinate position. Had Master Zeng and Zisi exchanged places, they would have acted just the same.

Book of Changes (Yi 易)

"Straightness" means its correctness; "squareness" means its righteousness. The noble man uses reverence to straighten what is within, and righteousness to square what is without. When reverence and righteousness are established, his virtue is not isolated. "Straight, square, great; even without repeated practice, there is nothing that is not advantageous"—this means he has no doubts about what he does.

The Commentary on the Judgments (Tuan 彖) says: In "Possession in Great Measure" (Dayou 大有), a yielding line attains the honored position of great centrality, and the lines above and below respond to it; therefore it is called "Possession in Great Measure." Its virtue is firm, strong, and civilizing, responding to Heaven and…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
時行是以元亨
知變化之道者其知神之所為乎
易曰憧憧往來朋從爾思子曰天下何
思何慮天下同歸而殊塗一致而百
慮天下何思何慮日往則月來月往
則日來日月相推而明生焉寒往則
暑來暑往則寒來寒暑相推而歲成
焉往者屈也來者信也屈信相感而
===
利生焉尺蠖之屈以求信也龍蛇之
蟄以存身也精義入神以致用也利
用安身以崇德也
書
柔遠能邇惇德允元而難任人
厥貢惟球琳琅玕浮于積石至于龍門
西河會于渭汭織皮崐崘析支渠搜
西戎即叙
punctuated:
時行，是以元亨。
知變化之道者，其知神之所為乎？
《易》曰：「憧憧往來，朋從爾思。」子曰：「天下何思何慮？天下同歸而殊塗，一致而百慮。天下何思何慮？日往則月來，月往則日來，日月相推而明生焉。寒往則暑來，暑往則寒來，寒暑相推而歲成焉。往者，屈也；來者，信也。屈信相感而利生焉。尺蠖之屈，以求信也；龍蛇之蟄，以存身也。精義入神，以致用也；利用安身，以崇德也。」
書
柔遠能邇，惇德允元，而難任人。
厥貢惟球、琳、琅玕。浮于積石，至于龍門西河，會于渭汭。織皮崐崘、析支、渠搜，西戎即叙。
translation_en:
… moves with the times; therefore, there is supreme success.

He who knows the Way of change and transformation, does he not know the actions of the spirit?

The Book of Changes (Yi) says: "Unsettled in going and coming, only your friends will follow your thoughts." The Master said: "What need has the world for thought and deliberation? In the world, there are different paths to the same destination, and a hundred deliberations leading to a single end. What need has the world for thought and deliberation? The sun goes and the moon comes; the moon goes and the sun comes; the sun and moon propel each other on, and light is born therefrom. Cold goes and heat comes; heat goes and cold comes; cold and heat propel each other on, and the year is completed therefrom. What goes contracts; what comes expands. Contraction and expansion act upon one another, and benefit is born therefrom. The inchworm contracts in order to seek expansion; dragons and snakes hibernate in order to preserve their bodies. Refining righteousness to the point of entering the spirit is the means to achieve practical application; making use of practical application to secure the person is the means to exalt virtue."

Book of Documents (Shu)

Be gracious to the distant and cultivate the near; give weight to the virtuous, place trust in the good, and reject artful men.

Its tribute consists of resonant jade (qiu), fine jade (lin), and pearl-like stones (langgan). Floating down from Jishi, they reach Longmen on the Western River, and meet at the confluence of the Wei. Felt and skins come from Kunlun, Xizhi, and Qusou; the Western Rong submit to order.

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
旁作穆穆迓衡
公其惟時成周建無窮之基亦有無窮
之聞子孫訓其成式惟乂嗚呼罔曰
弗克惟既厥心罔曰民寡惟慎厥事
欽若先王成烈以休于前政
詩
要之襋之好人服之好人提提宛然左
辟
===
維其有章矣是以有慶矣
清酒既載騂牡既備以享以祀以介景
福瑟彼柞棫民所燎矣豈弟君子神
所勞矣莫莫葛藟施于條枚豈弟君
子求福不回
俾民稼穡有稷有黍有稻有秬奄有下
土纘禹之緒后稷之孫實維大王居
岐之陽實始翦商至于文武纘大王
punctuated:
旁作穆穆迓衡。
公其惟時成周，建無窮之基，亦有無窮之聞。子孫訓其成式，惟乂。嗚呼！罔曰弗克，惟既厥心；罔曰民寡，惟慎厥事。欽若先王成烈，以休于前政。
詩
要之襋之，好人服之。好人提提，宛然左辟。
維其有章矣，是以有慶矣。
清酒既載，騂牡既備，以享以祀，以介景福。瑟彼柞棫，民所燎矣；豈弟君子，神所勞矣。莫莫葛藟，施于條枚；豈弟君子，求福不回。
俾民稼穡，有稷有黍，有稻有秬。奄有下土，纘禹之緒。后稷之孫，實維大王，居岐之陽，實始翦商。至于文武，纘大王
translation_en:
Everywhere create a reverent harmony to meet the balance of governance.

May the Duke at this time establish in Chengzhou a foundation without end, and likewise possess a renown without end. If his descendants follow his completed pattern, there will be order. Oh! Do not say that you are unable, only exhaust your heart; do not say that the people are few, only be cautious in your affairs. Reverently accord with the completed achievements of the former kings, so as to glorify the governance of your predecessors.

Classic of Poetry (Shi)

She makes the waistband, she makes the collar, and the fine person wears it. The fine person is dignified and at ease; courteously she steps aside to the left.

Because he possesses elegance, therefore he enjoys felicity.

The clear wine is set forth, the red bull is prepared, to offer and to sacrifice, so as to increase great blessings. Dense are those oaks and scrub-oaks, which the people gather for firewood; the joyous and fraternal lord is he whom the spirits comfort and reward. Lush are the creepers and vines, spreading over the branches and stems; the joyous and fraternal lord seeks blessings without perversity.

He taught the people to sow and reap, so that there were panicled millet and glutinous millet, rice and black millet. Covering the earth below, he continued the work of Yu. Among the descendants of Hou Ji was indeed King Tai, who dwelt on the southern slope of Mount Qi and first began to clip the wings of Shang. Coming down to King Wen and King Wu, they continued King Tai's…

text:
之緒
春秋
齊人侵我西鄙公追齊師至酅弗及〔僖公〕
〔二十六年〕公會齊侯于夾谷〔定公十年〕

侯伐秦〔文公四年〕

===
于貫〔僖公二年〕遂伐楚盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕
楚人陳侯蔡侯鄭伯許男圍宋〔僖公二十〕
〔七年〕晉侯齊師宋師秦師及楚人戰于
城濮楚師敗績〔僖公二十八年〕楚人圍江
晉陽處父帥師伐楚以救江〔文公三年〕
公及晉侯盟于長樗〔襄公三年〕及向戌盟于
劉〔襄公十五年〕公如晉至河乃復仲孫
何忌及邾子盟于拔〔定公三年〕
punctuated:
之緒。

《春秋》
齊人侵我西鄙，公追齊師至酅，弗及〔僖公〕〔二十六年〕；公會齊侯于夾谷〔定公十年〕。
天王使宰渠伯糾來聘〔桓公四年〕；天王使仍叔之子來聘〔桓公五年〕；秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕；晉侯伐秦〔文公四年〕。
楚人伐鄭〔僖公元年〕；齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人盟于貫〔僖公二年〕；遂伐楚，盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕；楚人、陳侯、蔡侯、鄭伯、許男圍宋〔僖公二十〕〔七年〕；晉侯、齊師、宋師、秦師及楚人戰于城濮，楚師敗績〔僖公二十八年〕；楚人圍江，晉陽處父帥師伐楚以救江〔文公三年〕。
公及晉侯盟于長樗〔襄公三年〕；及向戌盟于劉〔襄公十五年〕；公如晉，至河乃復；仲孫何忌及邾子盟于拔〔定公三年〕。
translation_en:
…the enterprise of [King Tai].

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"Men of Qi invaded our western frontier. The Duke pursued the Qi army as far as Xi, but did not overtake it" [26th year of Duke Xi]; "The Duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu" [10th year of Duke Ding].
"The Heavenly King sent the Steward, Qu Bojiu, to come on a mission of friendly inquiry" [4th year of Duke Huan]; "The Heavenly King sent the son of Reng Shu to come on a mission of friendly inquiry" [5th year of Duke Huan]; "Men of Qin attacked Jin" [3rd year of Duke Wen]; "The Marquis of Jin attacked Qin" [4th year of Duke Wen].
"Men of Chu attacked Zheng" [1st year of Duke Xi]; "The Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, men of Jiang, and men of Huang made a covenant at Guan" [2nd year of Duke Xi]; "Thereupon they attacked Chu, and made a covenant at Shaoling" [4th year of Duke Xi]; "Men of Chu, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, and the Baron of Xu besieged Song" [27th year of Duke Xi]; "The Marquis of Jin, an army of Qi, an army of Song, and an army of Qin fought with men of Chu at Chengpu, and the Chu army was utterly defeated" [28th year of Duke Xi]; "Men of Chu besieged Jiang" and "Yang Chufu of Jin led an army to attack Chu in order to relieve Jiang" [3rd year of Duke Wen].
"The Duke made a covenant with the Marquis of Jin at Changchu" [3rd year of Duke Xiang]; "[The Duke] made a covenant with Xiang Xu at Liu" [15th year of Duke Xiang]; "The Duke went to Jin, but upon reaching the Yellow River returned; Zhongsun Heji made a covenant with the Viscount of Zhu at Ba" [3rd year of Duke Ding].

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
禮記
郊血大饗腥三獻爓一獻孰至敬不饗
味而貴氣臭也諸侯為賓灌用鬱鬯
灌用臭也大饗尚腶脩而已矣
物至知知然後好惡形焉
仁者右也道者左也仁者人也道者義
也厚於仁者薄於義親而不尊厚於
義者薄於仁尊而不親
===
一馬從二馬三馬既立請慶多馬
第貳塲
論
致治之法垂於萬世
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢章帝至魯祠孔子詔
擬唐高宗以狄仁傑為侍御史誥
擬宋賜進士呂溱等瓊林宴及大學篇
punctuated:
《禮記》

郊血，大饗腥，三獻爓，一獻孰。至敬不饗味，而貴氣臭也。諸侯為賓，灌用鬱鬯；灌，用臭也；大饗，尚腶脩而已矣。

物至知知，然後好惡形焉。

仁者，右也；道者，左也。仁者，人也；道者，義也。厚於仁者薄於義，親而不尊；厚於義者薄於仁，尊而不親。

一馬從二馬。三馬既立，請慶多馬。

第貳塲

論

致治之法垂於萬世。

詔、誥、表〔內科一道〕

擬漢章帝至魯祠孔子詔。

擬唐高宗以狄仁傑為侍御史誥。

擬宋賜進士呂溱等瓊林宴及《大學》篇
translation_en:
Record of Rites (Liji)

"At the suburban sacrifice, raw blood is offered; at the great ancestral sacrifice, raw flesh; at the sacrifice of three libations, parboiled meat; at the sacrifice of one libation, fully cooked meat. For in the expression of the highest reverence, taste is not what is relished; rather, it is the vital breath and fragrance that are valued. When feudal lords are received as guests, the libation is made with fragrant millet wine infused with turmeric; this libation is for the sake of its fragrance. At the great banquet for them, spiced dried meat is placed at the head of the offerings, and that is all." [Liji, "Jiao te sheng" 郊特牲]

"When external things arrive and the faculty of knowing becomes aware of them, then likes and dislikes take shape." [Liji, "Yue ji" 樂記]

"Humaneness is like the right hand; the Way is like the left. Humaneness is humanity; the Way is righteousness. One who is generous in humaneness but stinting in righteousness is treated with affection, yet not revered; one who is generous in righteousness but stinting in humaneness is revered, yet not treated with affection." [Liji, "Biao ji" 表記]

"Let one tally-horse follow the two tally-horses. Now that three tally-horses have been set up, I beg leave to offer congratulations on the abundance of your horses." [Liji, "Tou hu" 投壺]

Second Session

Discourse (lun)

"The methods for bringing about good governance are handed down for ten thousand generations."

Edicts (zhao), Mandates of Appointment (gao), and Memorials (biao) [candidates are examined on one of these]

Imitation of an edict by Emperor Zhang of the Han (Han Zhangdi) upon arriving in Lu to sacrifice to Confucius.

Imitation of a mandate of appointment by Emperor Gaozong of the Tang (Tang Gaozong) appointing Di Renjie 狄仁傑 as Attendant Censor.

Imitation of a Song-dynasty [memorial of thanks for] bestowing upon the metropolitan graduates (jinshi) Lü Zhen 呂溱 and others the Qionglin Banquet and copies of the "Great Learning" (Daxue) chapter…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
謝表
判語〔五條〕
舉用有過官吏
私役部民夫匠
卑幼私擅用財
出納官物有違
術士妄言禍福
第三場
===
策
問孔子集羣聖之大成而刪述六經其
事功之大莫過於春秋春秋所載君
臣行事美惡備見矣朱子集諸儒之
大成而緖正羣書其教人之法莫先
於小學小學所載嘉言善行勸戒兼
備矣逮乎我
朝
punctuated:
謝表。
判語〔五條〕：
舉用有過官吏；
私役部民夫匠；
卑幼私擅用財；
出納官物有違；
術士妄言禍福。

第三場
策
問：孔子集羣聖之大成，而刪述六經，其事功之大，莫過於《春秋》。《春秋》所載，君臣行事，美惡備見矣。朱子集諸儒之大成，而緖正羣書，其教人之法，莫先於《小學》。《小學》所載，嘉言善行，勸戒兼備矣。逮乎我朝，

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承尊崇孔子之道表章朱子之書然
太祖高皇帝大誥三編何多載當時臣民之
惡而鮮及其善豈别有勸善之典歟
太宗文皇帝為善陰隲孝順事實何備載古
今善孝之實而無所示戒豈以當時
人皆知勸善歟
宣宗章皇帝纂集五倫書亦與小學明倫篇
所述五倫之義同矣然春秋所書闕
===
於五倫者果何所見歟為善陰隲孝
順事實所載善孝之事亦與春秋傳
所紀魏顆從治考叔遺羹之類同矣
然小學所述及乎陰德孝行者果何
所指歟諸士子樂育庠序誦習
聖訓久矣幸相與言之
問聖人以天下無不可為之事無不可
化之人盖理無事不有以理應事則
punctuated:
列聖相承，尊崇孔子之道，表章朱子之書。然太祖高皇帝《大誥》三編，何多載當時臣民之惡，而鮮及其善，豈别有勸善之典歟？太宗文皇帝《為善陰隲》、《孝順事實》，何備載古今善孝之實，而無所示戒，豈以當時人皆知勸善歟？宣宗章皇帝纂集《五倫書》，亦與《小學》〈明倫篇〉所述五倫之義同矣，然《春秋》所書闕於五倫者，果何所見歟？《為善陰隲》、《孝順事實》所載善孝之事，亦與《春秋傳》所紀魏顆從治、考叔遺羹之類同矣，然《小學》所述及乎陰德孝行者，果何所指歟？諸士子樂育庠序，誦習聖訓久矣，幸相與言之。

問：聖人以天下無不可為之事，無不可化之人。盖理無事不有，以理應事，則
translation_en:
… the successive sage emperors have inherited the throne one after another, revering the Way of Confucius (Kongzi 孔子) and honoring and promoting the writings of Master Zhu (Zhuzi 朱子). Yet why did the Three Compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao sanbian 大誥三編) of the Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu Gao huangdi 太祖高皇帝, the Hongwu Emperor), mostly record the evil deeds of the officials and commoners of that time while rarely touching upon their good deeds—could it be that there were separate canons for encouraging goodness? Why did the Unseen Retribution for Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi 為善陰隲) and the True Accounts of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi 孝順事實) of the Grand Ancestor, Emperor Wen (Taizong Wen huangdi 太宗文皇帝, the Yongle Emperor), exhaustively record actual instances of goodness and filial piety from past and present without setting forth any warnings—could it be because people at that time all knew to encourage one another in goodness? The Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu 五倫書) compiled by the Sovereign Ancestor, Emperor Zhang (Xuanzong Zhang huangdi 宣宗章皇帝, the Xuande Emperor), is likewise identical in meaning to the five human relationships expounded in the section on "Illustrating the Human Relationships" (Minglun pian 明倫篇) of the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue 小學); yet as for those deficiencies in the five human relationships recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋), where indeed are they seen? The deeds of goodness and filial piety recorded in the Unseen Retribution for Doing Good and the True Accounts of Filial Piety are likewise of the same kind as Wei Ke (魏顆) following his father's lucid dying command and Ying Kaoshu (考叔) setting aside soup for his mother, as chronicled in the Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu zhuan 春秋傳); yet as for what the Elementary Learning recounts concerning hidden virtue and filial conduct, to what indeed does it refer? You gentlemen have been happily nurtured in the state and local schools and have recited and studied the imperial instructions for a long time; pray set forth your views on these matters.

Question: The sages held that in all under Heaven there is no affair that cannot be accomplished and no person who cannot be transformed. This is because principle is present in every affair; if one responds to affairs with principle, then …

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
事無不可為性無人不善以善自治
則無不可改過也稽之於事囂訟不
肖子之甚殆矣何卒使授受得中而
天下治平歟汨陳五行父之功隳矣
何卒使六府孔脩而萬世永賴歟並
告無辜民心已失何遽有兆民允懷
之休百姓有過民心已乖何遽有萬
姓悅服之效流言不利避位居東何
===
以致王出郊新逆兩相相揖齊人鼓
譟何以致来歸鄆讙龜陰田此皆聖
人已行之事也可詳其所處之實歟
驗之於人頑嚚與敖似不可化而卒
致不格姦亦允若何歟侮慢自賢似
不可格矣而卒致丕叙来格何歟兹
乃不義習與性成何以使克終允德
弗造哲迪民康何以使教化大行質
punctuated: 事無不可為；性無人不善，以善自治，則無不可改過也。稽之於事：囂訟不肖，子之甚殆矣，何卒使授受得中而天下治平歟？汨陳五行，父之功隳矣，何卒使六府孔脩而萬世永賴歟？「並告無辜」，民心已失，何遽有「兆民允懷」之休？「百姓有過」，民心已乖，何遽有「萬姓悅服」之效？流言不利，避位居東，何以致王出郊新逆？兩相相揖，齊人鼓譟，何以致来歸鄆、讙、龜陰田？此皆聖人已行之事也，可詳其所處之實歟？驗之於人：頑、嚚與敖，似不可化，而卒致「不格姦」、「亦允若」，何歟？「侮慢自賢」，似不可格矣，而卒致「丕叙」、「来格」，何歟？「兹乃不義，習與性成」，何以使「克終允德」？「弗造哲，迪民康」，何以使教化大行？質
translation_en: … there is no affair that cannot be accomplished; and since human nature is good in every person, if one governs oneself with goodness, there is no fault that cannot be reformed. Examining this in terms of affairs: To be quarrelsome and unworthy—such sons placed things in great peril; how did [Yao and Shun] ultimately ensure that the transmission of the throne hit the mean and the realm was brought to peace and order? By throwing the Five Phases into disorder, the father’s [Gun’s] work was ruined; how did [Yu] ultimately ensure that the Six Treasuries were well ordered and ten thousand generations could forever rely on them? When “[the multitudes] all cry out in their innocence,” the hearts of the people had already been lost; how did [Tang] so suddenly achieve the blessing that “the millions of people truly cherished him”? When “the hundred surnames have faults,” the hearts of the people had already been alienated; how did [King Wu] so suddenly achieve the effect that “the myriad surnames gladly submitted”? When rumors proved unfavorable to him and [the Duke of Zhou] withdrew from his position to reside in the east, how did this lead the King [Cheng] to go out to the suburbs to welcome him back in person [reading 新逆 as 親逆]? When the two chief ministers bowed to one another and the men of Qi beat their drums and raised an uproar, how did [Confucius] bring them to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin? These are all affairs already carried out by the sages; can you detail the realities of how they handled them? Testing this in terms of people: Being obstinate, deceitful, and arrogant, [Shun’s family and Danzhu] seemed impossible to transform, yet they were ultimately brought to “not reach wickedness” and “also truly be in accord”—how was this? Being “contemptuous and self-conceited,” [the Sanmiao] seemed impossible to reform, yet they were ultimately brought to “grandly fall into order” and “come to submit”—how was this? When [Taijia] was such that “this was unrighteousness, and habit had become like nature,” how did [Yi Yin] cause him to “be able in the end to be truly virtuous”? When [the recalcitrant people of Yin] “did not attain wisdom or lead the people to tranquility,” how did [Jun Chen and others] cause moral transformation to prevail grandly? One who was simple …

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
魯貨殖之徒性行非不偏也若何而
卒聞一以貫之之道大師亞飯之流
典樂非不久也若何而知踰河蹈海
以去此皆聖人已化之人也可詳其
感之之由歟諸士子窮經致用當以
聖人為法願著于篇以觀處事正人
之學
問士君子以一身之微繫天下之觀望
===
也大矣故善為治者必因眾望之所
向乗其機以用其人則往無不濟而
功無不成焉稽之於古如眾望在循
吏用之則郡國稱治眾望在舊士用
之則江東歸心負節義之重望者一
用則盜賊請降負勳德之重名者一
用則回紇羅拜至若東漢先正有舉
道侔伊呂者用之則能抑姦辨賊有
punctuated:
魯、貨殖之徒，性行非不偏也，若何而卒聞「一以貫之」之道？大師、亞飯之流，典樂非不久也，若何而知踰河蹈海以去？此皆聖人已化之人也，可詳其感之之由歟？諸士子窮經致用，當以聖人為法，願著于篇，以觀處事正人之學。

問：士君子以一身之微，繫天下之觀望也大矣。故善為治者，必因眾望之所向，乗其機以用其人，則往無不濟而功無不成焉。稽之於古，如眾望在循吏，用之則郡國稱治；眾望在舊士，用之則江東歸心；負節義之重望者，一用則盜賊請降；負勳德之重名者，一用則回紇羅拜。至若東漢先正，有舉道侔伊、呂者，用之則能抑姦辨賊；有
translation_en:
… dull-witted and engaged in moneymaking, were not without partiality in their nature and conduct; how was it that in the end they heard the Way of the "one thread running through it all"? Those of the sort of the Grand Music Master and the musician of the second meal were in charge of music for no short time; how was it that they knew to cross the Yellow River and tread the sea to depart? These are all people whom the sages had already transformed; can you detail the reasons why they were moved? You scholars, in mastering the Classics for practical application, ought to take the sages as your model. I wish you to set this forth in your essays, so that I may observe your learning in handling affairs and rectifying people.

Question: How great is the extent to which a scholar-gentleman, in the insignificance of his single person, is bound up with the expectations of the world! Therefore, those skilled in governance must follow the direction of popular expectation and seize the opportunity to employ such men; then wherever they go nothing will fail to succeed, and no achievement will fail to be completed. Examining this in antiquity: when popular expectation rested on upright officials, employing them caused the commanderies and principalities to be praised as well-governed; when popular expectation rested on established scholars of old families, employing them caused the region east of the Yangtze to turn its allegiance to the court; when one who bore great prestige for integrity and righteousness was once employed, bandits and rebels begged to surrender; when one who bore a great reputation for meritorious virtue was once employed, the Uyghurs lined up to pay homage. As for the worthy predecessors of the Eastern Han, there was one recommended as equal in the Way to Yi Yin and Lü Shang, who when employed was able to suppress the wicked and expose traitors; there was…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
文學知名者用之則能論諫舉職有
負恬退清節者用之則兵民悅服是
人望誠有益於人國也方今近而望
於一鄉大而望於一方又大而望於
天下若循吏若舊士若節義若勳德
小大不遺彼此兼錄宜乎臻其效矣
而何郡國間有愁嘆之聲而邊徼尚
有竊發之患哉豈用之者未得其望
===
而所望者未見於用歟抑用所望而
又參以非所望者故掣肘矛盾而然
歟抑別有其故歟伊欲用其衆所望
去其非所望者徵於聖賢之言當以
何者而為其進退之機乎諸士子皆
達於時務者其言之毋隱
問古先聖王之治天下莫不以治歷明
時為先務故曆法之制代代有之然
punctuated:
文學知名者，用之則能論諫舉職；有負恬退清節者，用之則兵民悅服。是人望誠有益於人國也。方今近而望於一鄉，大而望於一方，又大而望於天下，若循吏、若舊士、若節義、若勳德，小大不遺，彼此兼錄，宜乎臻其效矣。而何郡國間有愁嘆之聲，而邊徼尚有竊發之患哉？豈用之者未得其望，而所望者未見於用歟？抑用所望而又參以非所望者，故掣肘矛盾而然歟？抑別有其故歟？伊欲用其衆所望，去其非所望者，徵於聖賢之言，當以何者而為其進退之機乎？諸士子皆達於時務者，其言之毋隱。

問：古先聖王之治天下，莫不以治歷明時為先務，故曆法之制，代代有之。然
translation_en:
… were known for literary learning; when employed, they were able to offer remonstrances and fulfill their official duties. There were those who bore a reputation for quiet retirement and pure integrity; when employed, both soldiers and civilians joyfully submitted to them. Thus popular esteem is truly beneficial to a state. At present, whether those esteemed nearby in a single district, those esteemed more broadly in an entire region, or those esteemed more broadly still throughout the Empire—whether upright officials, veteran scholars, men of integrity and righteousness, or men of meritorious virtue—none, great or small, are overlooked, and all are concurrently selected for office. Surely their efficacy ought to have been achieved! Why is it, then, that among the commanderies and principalities there are occasionally sounds of grief and sighing, and on the frontiers there is still the trouble of sudden outbreaks of banditry? Could it be that those who are employed have not earned such esteem, while those who are esteemed have not yet been put to use? Or is it that while employing those who are esteemed, they are intermingled with those who are not esteemed, thus hindering and contradicting one another so as to bring this about? Or is there some other reason? If one wishes to employ those whom the multitude esteems and remove those whom it does not esteem, verifying this against the words of the sages and worthies, what should be taken as the pivotal criterion for advancing and dismissing them? You gentlemen are all well-versed in current affairs; speak of this without concealment.

Question: When the ancient sage-kings governed the Empire, none failed to take regulating the calendar and clarifying the seasons as their foremost task; therefore, calendrical systems have existed in every dynasty. Yet…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
昉於何時漢曆凡五變唐曆凡八變
宋曆凡十變而孰為最優此外又有
可取者誰歟治曆之法以置閏為急
而氣盈朔虛之㫖何在推測之要以
正閏分而正數成數之言何別有因
造曆而始悟其謬者又誰歟曆書不
越乎二十四氣一氣之運行固有序
矣而每月何以有曰節曰中之分四
===
時曰立固有理也何春秋曰分而夏
冬曰至乎穀雨芒種以穀麥言也何
置之於三月五月之中驚蟄清明以
風雷言也何居於二月三月之內暑
行於春夏而夏至則暑已極何夏至
後乃有小暑大暑耶寒運於秋冬而
冬至則寒已盡何冬至後乃為小寒
大寒耶露一也何以有寒白之分雪
punctuated: 昉於何時？漢曆凡五變，唐曆凡八變，宋曆凡十變，而孰為最優？此外又有可取者，誰歟？治曆之法，以置閏為急，而氣盈朔虛之㫖何在？推測之要，以正閏分，而正數成數之言何別？有因造曆而始悟其謬者，又誰歟？曆書不越乎二十四氣，一氣之運行固有序矣，而每月何以有曰節、曰中之分？四時曰立，固有理也，何春秋曰分，而夏冬曰至乎？穀雨、芒種以穀麥言也，何置之於三月、五月之中？驚蟄、清明以風雷言也，何居於二月、三月之內？暑行於春夏，而夏至則暑已極，何夏至後乃有小暑、大暑耶？寒運於秋冬，而冬至則寒已盡，何冬至後乃為小寒、大寒耶？露一也，何以有寒、白之分？雪
translation_en: …when did it first begin? The calendrical system of the Han underwent five changes in all, that of the Tang eight changes, and that of the Song ten changes—which of these was the most superior? Beyond these, who else devised systems worthy of adoption? In the method of regulating the calendar, the insertion of intercalary months is of the utmost urgency; wherein lies the principle of the solar excess (qiying) and lunar deficiency (shuoxu)? The essentials of calculation and observation depend on rectifying the intercalary fractions; what is the distinction between the terms "regular numbers" (zhengshu) and "completed numbers" (chengshu)? And who was it that only realized the errors of his own calculations after actually compiling a calendar? Calendrical treatises do not go beyond the twenty-four solar terms (qi). The progression of the vital breaths certainly follows an order, yet why does each month have a division between what is called a "nodal" (jie) term and a "medial" (zhong) term? That the beginnings of the four seasons are called "Establishing" (li) certainly has its principle, but why are the midpoints of spring and autumn called "Equinoxes" (fen, division), while those of summer and winter are called "Solstices" (zhi, extreme)? "Grain Rain" (guyu) and "Grain in Ear" (mangzhong) are named with reference to grain and wheat; why are they placed in the middle of the third and fifth months? "Waking of Insects" (jingzhe) and "Pure Brightness" (qingming) are named with reference to wind and thunder; why do they reside within the second and third months? Heat operates during spring and summer, and by the Summer Solstice heat has already reached its peak; why then are there "Lesser Heat" (xiaoshu) and "Greater Heat" (dashu) after the Summer Solstice? Cold circulates during autumn and winter, and by the Winter Solstice cold has already reached its limit; why then do "Lesser Cold" (xiaohan) and "Greater Cold" (dahan) come after the Winter Solstice? Dew is one and the same; why is there a distinction between "Cold" (hanlu) and "White" (bailu)? Snow…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
一也何以有小大之異小指陰道而
言也以小滿居四月之中者何義暑
積陽氣而成者也以處暑在七月之
中者何取以至立雨水於立春之後
介霜降於寒露之餘亦豈無其義哉
凡此皆變化之道神之所為者也博
洽之士必能言之而他日任調元贊
化燮理陰陽之責庶乎有以覘之矣
===
幸毋多讓
問農桑衣食之源民生至急一夫不耕
或受之飢一女不織或受之寒飢寒
迫身而放僻邪侈無所不至雖慈父
不能保其子況君之於民乎故聖王
知其然使民男有餘粟女有餘布生
長老死於仁政者其道何由後世使
民膏粱者不耕而耕者糲飯不充文
punctuated:
一也，何以有小、大之異？小指陰道而言也，以小滿居四月之中者何義？暑積陽氣而成者也，以處暑在七月之中者何取？以至立雨水於立春之後，介霜降於寒露之餘，亦豈無其義哉？凡此皆變化之道、神之所為者也。博洽之士，必能言之；而他日任調元贊化、燮理陰陽之責，庶乎有以覘之矣。幸毋多讓。

問：農桑，衣食之源，民生至急。一夫不耕，或受之飢；一女不織，或受之寒。飢寒迫身，而放僻邪侈，無所不至；雖慈父不能保其子，況君之於民乎？故聖王知其然，使民男有餘粟、女有餘布，生長老死於仁政者，其道何由？後世使民，膏粱者不耕，而耕者糲飯不充；文
translation_en:
… the same, why is there a distinction between Lesser Snow and Greater Snow? "Lesser" (xiao) refers to the Way of Yin; what is the meaning of placing Grain Buds (Xiaoman, lit. "Lesser Fullness") in the middle of the fourth month? Heat is formed by the accumulation of Yang qi; what is the rationale for placing End of Heat (Chushu, lit. "Abiding Heat") in the middle of the seventh month? And when it comes to establishing Rain Water (Yushui) after Start of Spring (Lichun), and interposing Frost's Descent (Shuangjiang) after Cold Dew (Hanlu), how could these be without meaning? All of these are the Way of transformation and the work of the unfathomable spirit. Gentlemen of broad learning will surely be able to explain them; and when in the future you take up the responsibility of harmonizing the primordial forces, assisting transformation, and blending Yin and Yang, perhaps we may see a glimpse of your capacity through this. Pray do not be overly modest in your reply.

Question: Agriculture and sericulture are the source of food and clothing, and the most urgent priority for the people's livelihood. If one man does not plow, someone may suffer hunger because of it; if one woman does not weave, someone may suffer cold because of it. When hunger and cold press upon their bodies, there is no limit to the dissolute, perverse, wicked, and extravagant acts they will commit; even a loving father cannot vouch for his own son, let alone a ruler for his people! Therefore, the sage-kings understood that this was so, and caused the people's men to have surplus grain and their women to have surplus cloth, being born, growing up, aging, and dying under benevolent governance—by what way was this achieved? In later ages, in employing the people, those who dine on fine meats and grain do not plow, while those who plow do not have enough coarse rice to fill themselves; those who wear patterned…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
錦者不蠶而蠶者短褐不足天地好
生之仁幾乎息矣其失何自逮我
皇明撫有四海考課之法守令以農桑為首
版籍所載民戶以事產為先而
大誥又有互知丁業之條其重農之意可
謂詳且至矣宜乎無飢寒之民也柰
何太平既久風俗日侈務本者少趨
末者多彼游於緇黃游於商賈游於
===
市井官宦游於廝役技藝皆資給於
吾農者一人耕百人食一女織百人
衣欲其不飢不寒得乎今欲盡使歸
農則流弊已久於勢或有不可欲聽
其自便則民日益貧於理亦所當憂
此民生之至急不可不究心也諸士
子抱藝而來必有能處之者請為我
言之
punctuated: 錦者不蠶，而蠶者短褐不足，天地好生之仁幾乎息矣，其失何自？逮我皇明撫有四海，考課之法，守令以農桑為首；版籍所載，民戶以事產為先；而《大誥》又有互知丁業之條。其重農之意，可謂詳且至矣，宜乎無飢寒之民也。柰何太平既久，風俗日侈，務本者少，趨末者多。彼游於緇黃、游於商賈、游於市井官宦、游於廝役技藝，皆資給於吾農者。一人耕，百人食；一女織，百人衣；欲其不飢不寒，得乎？今欲盡使歸農，則流弊已久，於勢或有不可；欲聽其自便，則民日益貧，於理亦所當憂。此民生之至急，不可不究心也。諸士子抱藝而來，必有能處之者，請為我言之。
translation_en: …and those who wear figured brocade do not raise silkworms, while those who raise silkworms do not have enough coarse woolens to wear. The life-loving benevolence of Heaven and Earth has nearly ceased—whence did this failing arise? When our August Ming came to pacify and possess the Four Seas, in the regulations for evaluating official performance, Prefects and Magistrates took agriculture and sericulture as their foremost duty; in the household registers, civilian households put occupational livelihood and property first; and the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao) furthermore contained an article on mutual knowledge of adult males' occupations. Its intention of emphasizing agriculture may be called detailed and utmost, so it ought to be that there are no hungry or cold people. Why is it, then, that after a long period of peace, customs grow daily more extravagant, those who attend to the fundamental occupation are few, and those who pursue secondary occupations are many? Those who drift into the Buddhist and Daoist clergy, those who drift into commerce and trade, those who drift about the marketplaces and officialdom, and those who drift into menial service and artisanal crafts all depend upon our farmers for their provisions. If one man plows and a hundred people eat, and one woman weaves and a hundred people are clothed, is it possible to wish that they not go hungry or cold? Today, if we wish to make them all return to farming, the entrenched abuses have lasted so long that in practice it may be unfeasible; yet if we wish to let them do as they please, the people will grow poorer by the day, which in principle is also cause for concern. This is a matter of the utmost urgency for the people's livelihood, to which we cannot fail to devote our minds. You gentlemen have come bearing your learning, and there must be those among you able to manage this—please speak of it for me.

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
四書義
子曰聽訟吾猶人也必也使無訟乎無情者不
得盡其辭大畏民志此謂知本
郭應仁
同考試官教諭林批作此題者多分截不明且於
本末先後處體認不切求其理
明辭確僅見此篇是宜錄出
考試官教諭鄭批大學本末先後之義發明
殆盡
===
考試官學正王批辭簡理明
大賢引聖人之言而推言其本所以釋本末之先後
也盖聽訟末也明明德而使民無訟本也大賢引聖
言而推本言之則明德新民之本末先後可知矣昔
曾子傳大學引夫子之言謂夫民情有欲則争不能
以無訟也然因其訟而辨其是非因其争而斷其曲
直吾固無異於人也此但治其末塞其流耳必也正
其本使民利欲之争息而自無訟可聽焉清其源使
民情欲之感正而自無訟可辨焉曾子引之於此而
punctuated:
四書義

「子曰：『聽訟，吾猶人也。必也使無訟乎！』無情者不得盡其辭，大畏民志，此謂知本。」

郭應仁

同考試官教諭林批：作此題者，多分截不明，且於本末、先後處體認不切。求其理明辭確，僅見此篇，是宜錄出。

考試官教諭鄭批：《大學》本末、先後之義，發明殆盡。

考試官學正王批：辭簡理明。

大賢引聖人之言而推言其本，所以釋本末之先後也。盖聽訟，末也；明明德而使民無訟，本也。大賢引聖言而推本言之，則明德、新民之本末、先後可知矣。昔曾子傳《大學》，引夫子之言，謂夫民情有欲則争，不能以無訟也。然因其訟而辨其是非，因其争而斷其曲直，吾固無異於人也。此但治其末、塞其流耳。必也正其本，使民利欲之争息，而自無訟可聽焉；清其源，使民情欲之感正，而自無訟可辨焉。曾子引之於此，而
translation_en:
Expositions on the Four Books (Sishu)

"The Master said, 'In hearing litigation, I am no different from anyone else. What is necessary, however, is to bring it about that there is no litigation at all!' Those whose claims are unfounded are unable to carry out their false statements to the end, because a great awe has been instilled in the people's minds. This is called knowing the root."

Guo Yingren 郭應仁

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Lin 林: Among those writing on this topic, most failed to divide the sections clearly, and furthermore did not grasp closely the distinction between root and branch, and what comes first and what comes last. Seeking an essay whose principles are clear and phrasing is precise, only this piece was found; it is fitting that it be selected for publication.

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zheng 鄭: The meaning of root and branch, and of what comes first and what comes last in the Great Learning (Daxue), is elucidated almost exhaustively here.

Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Wang 王: The phrasing is concise and the principles are clear.

The great worthy quotes the words of the Sage and extends them to speak of their root, thereby explaining the sequence of what comes first and what comes last between root and branch. For hearing litigation is the branch; illustrating illustrious virtue so as to cause the people to have no litigation is the root. When the great worthy quotes the Sage's words and traces them to their fundamental root, then the root and branch, and the sequence of first and last regarding illustrating virtue and renewing the people, can be known.

Formerly, when Zengzi 曾子 transmitted the Great Learning, he quoted the Master's words, saying that because the feelings of the people have desires, they contend with one another, and thus cannot be without litigation. Yet in distinguishing right from wrong on the basis of their lawsuits, and in judging crooked from straight on the basis of their contentions, I am indeed no different from anyone else. This is merely treating the branch and stopping up the current. What is necessary is to rectify the root, causing the people's contentions over profit and desire to cease, so that naturally there is no litigation to be heard; and to purify the source, causing the stirrings of the people's passions and desires to become upright, so that naturally there is no litigation to be distinguished. Zengzi quotes this here, and…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
言訟之不息由無情者得以盡其辭也聖人能使無
實之人不敢盡其虛誕之辭盖我之明德既明自然
有以大服乎人之心故訟之曲直不待聽而自無矣
我之德盛仁熟自然有以大畏乎民之志故訟之是
非不待辨而自息矣觀於此言則知明德為本而在
所當先新民為末而在所當後矣所謂本末先後之
義豈不著明矣乎抑嘗考之虞舜好生之德洽于民
心故民協于中而不犯于有司文王徽柔懿恭之德
光于四方故虞芮爭田而不敢履其庭是皆聖人明
===
德新民止於至善而使民無訟者也欲盡大學之道
者可不以聖人為法乎
子入太廟每事問或曰孰謂鄹人之子知禮乎
入太廟每事問子聞之曰是禮也
楊季芳
同考試官教諭陳批此題本平易作者多於每事
問處講說不明唯此篇辭理俱
到宜表而出之
考試官教諭鄭批識理明白而文足以發之
punctuated:
言：訟之不息，由無情者得以盡其辭也。聖人能使無實之人不敢盡其虛誕之辭，盖我之明德既明，自然有以大服乎人之心，故訟之曲直不待聽而自無矣；我之德盛仁熟，自然有以大畏乎民之志，故訟之是非不待辨而自息矣。觀於此言，則知明德為本而在所當先，新民為末而在所當後矣。所謂本末先後之義，豈不著明矣乎？抑嘗考之：虞舜好生之德洽于民心，故民協于中而不犯于有司；文王徽柔懿恭之德光于四方，故虞、芮爭田而不敢履其庭。是皆聖人明德、新民、止於至善，而使民無訟者也。欲盡《大學》之道者，可不以聖人為法乎？

「子入太廟，每事問。或曰：『孰謂鄹人之子知禮乎？入太廟，每事問。』子聞之，曰：『是禮也。』」
楊季芳
同考試官教諭陳批：此題本平易，作者多於「每事問」處講說不明，唯此篇辭理俱到，宜表而出之。
考試官教諭鄭批：識理明白，而文足以發之。
translation_en:
… says that the reason litigation does not cease is because those whose claims are groundless are able to pour out their words in full. The sage is able to make people without honest substance not dare to pour out their false and extravagant words. For once one's own luminous virtue is already made bright, one naturally has that whereby to greatly win the submission of people's hearts; therefore, the crooked and straight in litigation do not wait to be heard before there ceases to be any litigation at all. Once one's own virtue is abundant and benevolence mature, one naturally has that whereby to greatly awe the wills of the people; therefore, the right and wrong in litigation do not wait to be distinguished before they cease of themselves. Looking at these words, one knows that making bright one's luminous virtue is the root and what ought to come first, while renewing the people is the branch and what ought to come after. Is not the meaning of what is called root and branch, first and last, thus made clearly manifest? Moreover, I have examined this in history: Yu Shun's virtue of loving life permeated the hearts of the people, and thus the people harmonized in the mean and did not offend against the authorities; King Wen's gentle, mild, admirable, and reverent virtue shone throughout the four quarters, and thus the rulers of Yu and Rui, disputing over fields, did not dare to tread his court. These were both cases of sages making bright their luminous virtue, renewing the people, and resting in the highest good, thereby causing the people to have no litigation. Can those who wish to fulfill the Way of the Great Learning (Daxue) fail to take the sages as their model?

"The Master entered the Grand Temple and asked about everything. Someone said, 'Who says that the son of the man of Zou knows ritual? On entering the Grand Temple, he asks about everything.' The Master heard of it and said, 'This is ritual.'"
Yang Jifang 楊季芳
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, County Director of Schools: This topic is inherently plain and easy, yet most writers failed to explain clearly the phrase "asked about everything." Only this essay achieves both expression and principle, and it ought to be singled out for distinction.
Comment by Examiner Zheng, County Director of Schools: His understanding of principle is clear, and his writing is sufficient to bring it forth.

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正王批不拘不泛
聖人助祭而詳審其事時人譏其不知乎禮聖人言
其所以為禮盖禮者敬而已矣聖人助祭而詳審其
事者敬謹之至乃所以為禮也時人不知而譏之得
不明言以曉之哉且夫太廟魯周公廟也孔子當始
仕之時入而助祭也凡制度儀則雖已知之而必詳
問以審其事焉器物節文雖已講之而必更問以驗
其實焉聖人謹禮如此或人不知而譏之曰鄹人之
子自少以知禮聞也然知禮者不待問而問非知禮
===
者也今入太廟而每事問孰謂其知禮乎或人之譏
若此聖人聞之遂明言以曉之謂夫禮主於敬入廟而
每事問者敬之大也敬之大即禮意之所存也祭所當
謹雖知亦問者謹之至也謹之至即禮意之所在也
然則聖人謹禮之意豈或人之所知而其辭氣和平
德量宏大亦豈常人之所及哉大抵聖人所為眾人
所不識者非特此也若事君盡禮則譏其為諂諱君
之惡則疑其有黨疾固而斥以為佞正名而指以為
迂噫使無顏子以發其蘊宰我子貢稱賛其盛子思
punctuated:
考試官學正王批：不拘不泛。
聖人助祭而詳審其事，時人譏其不知乎禮，聖人言其所以為禮。盖禮者，敬而已矣。聖人助祭而詳審其事者，敬謹之至，乃所以為禮也。時人不知而譏之，得不明言以曉之哉？且夫太廟，魯周公廟也。孔子當始仕之時，入而助祭也。凡制度儀則，雖已知之，而必詳問以審其事焉；器物節文，雖已講之，而必更問以驗其實焉。聖人謹禮如此，或人不知而譏之曰：「鄹人之子，自少以知禮聞也。然知禮者不待問，而問非知禮者也。今入太廟而每事問，孰謂其知禮乎？」或人之譏若此，聖人聞之，遂明言以曉之。謂夫禮主於敬，入廟而每事問者，敬之大也，敬之大即禮意之所存也；祭所當謹，雖知亦問者，謹之至也，謹之至即禮意之所在也。然則聖人謹禮之意，豈或人之所知？而其辭氣和平、德量宏大，亦豈常人之所及哉？大抵聖人所為，眾人所不識者，非特此也。若事君盡禮，則譏其為諂；諱君之惡，則疑其有黨；疾固而斥以為佞；正名而指以為迂。噫！使無顏子以發其蘊，宰我、子貢稱賛其盛，子思、
translation_en:
Examiner Wang, Subprefectural Director of Studies, comments: Neither rigid nor vague.

When the Sage assisted at the sacrifice and carefully examined into its affairs, people of the time ridiculed him for not knowing ritual, and the Sage explained why this was itself ritual. For ritual is nothing other than reverence. That the Sage assisted at the sacrifice and carefully examined into its affairs was the utmost of reverence and caution, which is precisely what constitutes ritual. When people of the time did not understand and ridiculed him, how could he not speak plainly to enlighten them?

Now the Grand Temple was the temple of the Duke of Zhou in Lu. At the time when Confucius first took office, he entered it to assist at the sacrifice. Regarding all the institutional rules and ceremonial standards, although he already knew them, he necessarily asked in detail so as to examine into the affairs; regarding the ritual vessels and detailed forms, although he had already studied them, he necessarily asked again so as to verify the reality. The Sage was thus cautious about ritual, yet someone, not understanding this, ridiculed him, saying: "The son of the man of Zou has been known since youth for understanding ritual. Yet one who understands ritual does not need to ask, and one who asks is not someone who understands ritual. Now he enters the Grand Temple and asks about everything—who says he understands ritual?"

Such was this person's ridicule. When the Sage heard it, he thereupon spoke plainly to enlighten him, meaning that ritual is centered on reverence: entering the temple and asking about everything is great reverence, and great reverence is precisely where the meaning of ritual resides; sacrifice is something in which one must be cautious, so asking even though one already knows is the utmost of caution, and the utmost of caution is precisely where the meaning of ritual lies. This being so, how could the Sage's intention in being cautious toward ritual be understood by that person? And how could his gentle tone and vast moral capacity be matched by ordinary men?

In general, what the Sage did that the multitude failed to recognize was not limited to this alone. When he served his ruler with full ritual, people ridiculed him as flattering; when he concealed his ruler's faults, they suspected him of partisanship; when he detested obstinacy, they dismissed it as glibness; when he sought to rectify names, they pointed to him as impractical. Alas! Had there been no Master Yan (Yan Hui 顏回) to bring forth his profound store, no Zai Wo 宰我 and Zigong 子貢 to praise his greatness, and no Zisi 子思 and…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
孟子闡明推尊其道則後世孰從而知其聖歟
易義
直其正也方其義也君子敬以直内義以方外
敬義立而德不孤直方大不習无不利則不
疑其所行也
潘鉁
同考試官訓導郭批此題本以學言場中作者往往專
指爻辭立說殊戾本旨是篇體認
不差詞理縝密其得易之旨深乎
===
同考試官教諭汪批此題本平易作者類多穿鑿
不合本義理明辭暢惟見此篇
取冠本房孰曰不宜
考試官教諭鄭批此作為學之義明𥇒尤得旨
考試官學正王批得本義旨
文言發明坤六二之爻義必以學而言之也盖君子
之學内外兼脩則德無不盛而所行自無不順矣文
言發明坤六二之爻義而必以學言之厥旨深矣昔
吾夫子於坤之文言而申六二之象傳意謂柔順正
punctuated:
孟子闡明推尊其道，則後世孰從而知其聖歟！

易義

「直其正也，方其義也。君子敬以直内，義以方外，敬義立而德不孤。『直方大，不習无不利』，則不疑其所行也。」
潘鉁
同考試官訓導郭批：此題本以學言，場中作者往往專指爻辭立說，殊戾本旨。是篇體認不差，詞理縝密，其得《易》之旨深乎！
同考試官教諭汪批：此題本平易，作者類多穿鑿，不合《本義》。理明辭暢，惟見此篇，取冠本房，孰曰不宜？
考試官教諭鄭批：此作為學之義明𥇒，尤得旨。
考試官學正王批：得《本義》旨。

《文言》發明坤六二之爻義，必以學而言之也。盖君子之學，内外兼脩，則德無不盛，而所行自無不順矣。《文言》發明坤六二之爻義，而必以學言之，厥旨深矣。昔吾夫子於《坤》之《文言》，而申六二之《象傳》，意謂柔順正
translation_en:
…and Mencius (Mengzi) to elucidate and exalt his Way, how then would later generations have come to know his sagehood?

Exposition on the Classic of Changes (Yi)

"Rectitude is its correctness; squareness is its righteousness. The superior man maintains reverence to straighten the interior, and righteousness to square the exterior. When reverence and righteousness are established, his virtue is not solitary. 'Straight, square, and great, without practice, nothing is unfavorable'—then he has no doubts about what he does."

By Pan Zhen 潘鉁.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Guo: This topic fundamentally speaks in terms of learning. Writers in the examination hall often establish their arguments solely by pointing to the line statements, which goes quite against the original purport. This essay grasps the meaning without error, and its diction and reasoning are closely woven; how deeply it has attained the purport of the Classic of Changes!
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Wang: This topic is fundamentally plain and accessible, yet writers mostly indulge in forced interpretations that do not accord with the Original Meaning (Benyi). Clarity of principle and fluency of diction are seen only in this essay; to select it to head this ward—who would say it is inappropriate?
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zheng: In this composition, the meaning of pursuing learning is clear and lucid, especially attaining the purport.
Comment by Examiner and Director of Studies Wang: It attains the purport of the Original Meaning.

When the Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) elucidates the meaning of the second Yin line (Six in the second place) of the Kun hexagram, it necessarily speaks of it in terms of learning. title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
固坤之直也而直非人心本體之正乎賦形有定坤
之方也而方非人心裁制之義乎君子人與主敬以
直其內而無委曲之私則持守之工夫至而內自然
端直矣守義以方其外而有一定之理則講學之工
夫盡而外截然方正矣既不專於主敬又不偏於守
義敬義夾持內外交脩則衆善畢集德極其盛而自
不孤矣由是在我之敬義即坤之直方在我之不孤
即坤之大也直方而大則不待學習而無適不宜不
假脩為而無往不利以之事君則忠於君坦然由之
===
而無疑也以之事親則悅於親釋然行之而不惑也
謂之不疑其所行信乎無一事之或疑矣又何假於
習而後利哉吾夫子文言而以是發明六二之義其
至矣乎抑嘗兼乾坤論之乾九三言誠坤六二言敬
誠敬者乾坤之別也先儒誠敬之學起於此乾九二
言仁坤六二言義仁義者陰陽之辯也先儒論仁義
之用取諸此後之學易者可不合而觀之乎
易曰憧憧往来朋從爾思子曰天下何思何慮
天下同歸而殊塗一致而百慮天下何思何
punctuated:
固，坤之直也；而直非人心本體之正乎？賦形有定，坤之方也；而方非人心裁制之義乎？君子人與！主敬以直其內，而無委曲之私，則持守之工夫至，而內自然端直矣；守義以方其外，而有一定之理，則講學之工夫盡，而外截然方正矣。既不專於主敬，又不偏於守義，敬義夾持，內外交脩，則衆善畢集，德極其盛，而自不孤矣。由是在我之敬義，即坤之直方；在我之不孤，即坤之大也。直方而大，則不待學習而無適不宜，不假脩為而無往不利。以之事君，則忠於君，坦然由之而無疑也；以之事親，則悅於親，釋然行之而不惑也。謂之「不疑其所行」，信乎無一事之或疑矣，又何假於習而後利哉！吾夫子《文言》而以是發明六二之義，其至矣乎！抑嘗兼乾、坤論之：乾九三言誠，坤六二言敬，誠、敬者，乾、坤之別也，先儒誠敬之學起於此；乾九二言仁，坤六二言義，仁、義者，陰、陽之辯也，先儒論仁義之用取諸此。後之學《易》者，可不合而觀之乎？

《易》曰：「憧憧往来，朋從爾思。」子曰：「天下何思何慮？天下同歸而殊塗，一致而百慮。天下何思何
translation_en:
…and firm is the straightness of Kun (the Receptive); and is not straightness the rectitude of the original substance of the human mind? Giving definite form to things is the squareness of Kun; and is not squareness the righteousness by which the human mind regulates and decides? Such is the superior man! When he abides in reverence to straighten his inner self, free from crooked selfishness, then the effort of preservation and maintenance reaches its utmost, and the interior naturally becomes upright and straight. When he upholds righteousness to square his outer actions, adhering to definite principles, then the effort of pursuing learning is exhausted, and the exterior becomes distinctly square and upright. Neither focusing exclusively on abiding in reverence, nor leaning one-sidedly toward upholding righteousness, when reverence and righteousness support each other from both sides and the inner and outer are cultivated together, all goodness gathers completely, virtue reaches its utmost flourishing, and he naturally does not stand alone. Thus, reverence and righteousness within oneself are none other than the straightness and squareness of Kun; not standing alone within oneself is none other than the greatness of Kun. Being straight, square, and great, one finds nothing unsuitable without having to learn and practice, and nothing disadvantageous without having to rely on artificial effort. When applied to serving one's ruler, one is loyal to the ruler, following this path calmly without doubt; when applied to serving one's parents, one brings joy to the parents, practicing it with ease and without perplexity. To call this "having no doubt as to what he does"—truly there is not a single matter in which he might hesitate! What need is there to rely on repeated practice before it becomes advantageous? For our Master, in the Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan), to elucidate the meaning of the Six in the Second place in this way—how supreme it is! Furthermore, I have considered Qian (the Creative) and Kun together: Nine in the Third place of Qian speaks of sincerity, while Six in the Second place of Kun speaks of reverence. Sincerity and reverence mark the distinction between Qian and Kun, and the learning of sincerity and reverence of former Confucian scholars originated from this. Nine in the Second place of Qian speaks of benevolence, while Six in the Second place of Kun speaks of righteousness. Benevolence and righteousness mark the differentiation between Yin and Yang, and the discussions of former Confucian scholars on the function of benevolence and righteousness were drawn from this. How could later students of the Book of Changes (Yi) fail to examine them together?

The Book of Changes says: "Unsettled in yourellings to and fro, only your friends will follow your thoughts." The Master said: "What need has the world for thought and deliberation? In the world, there are many different roads, but the destination is the same; there are a hundred deliberations, but the result is one. What need has the world for thought and…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
慮日往則月来月往則日来日月相推而明
生焉寒往則暑来暑往則寒来寒暑相推而
歲成焉往者屈也来者信也屈信相感而利
生焉尺蠖之屈以求信也龍蛇之蟄以存身
也精義入神以致用也利用安身以崇德也
王演
同考試官訓導郭批此題釋爻辭言感應之理莫非自然
諸作多講貫不明是篇詞約理備兼
文論策俱優有學識之士也
===
同考試官教諭汪批此題歷舉象言無心之感應所以破咸
九四有心感應之出於私也作者多昧乎
此得之者惟此篇焉高薦何忝
考試官教諭鄭批易義貴精微此作得之
考試官學正王批說得感應之理盡
大傳舉爻辭而釋以感應之理無容心尤即造化物
理聖學以明之也盖感應之理莫非自然固不假於
思慮也聖人釋爻而尤即造化物理聖學以明之不
其至乎且咸之九四為心之象感之主也往者為感
punctuated:
慮？日往則月来，月往則日来，日月相推而明生焉。寒往則暑来，暑往則寒来，寒暑相推而歲成焉。往者屈也，来者信也，屈信相感而利生焉。尺蠖之屈，以求信也；龍蛇之蟄，以存身也。精義入神，以致用也；利用安身，以崇德也。
王演
同考試官訓導郭批：此題釋爻辭，言感應之理莫非自然。諸作多講貫不明，是篇詞約理備，兼文論策俱優，有學識之士也。
同考試官教諭汪批：此題歷舉象，言無心之感應，所以破咸九四有心感應之出於私也。作者多昧乎此，得之者惟此篇焉，高薦何忝。
考試官教諭鄭批：《易》義貴精微，此作得之。
考試官學正王批：說得感應之理盡。
大傳舉爻辭而釋以感應之理無容心，尤即造化、物理、聖學以明之也。盖感應之理，莫非自然，固不假於思慮也。聖人釋爻，而尤即造化、物理、聖學以明之，不其至乎！且《咸》之九四，為心之象，感之主也。往者為感，
translation_en:
… deliberation? When the sun goes, the moon comes; when the moon goes, the sun comes. The sun and moon push each other on, and light is generated thereby. When cold goes, heat comes; when heat goes, cold comes. Cold and heat push each other on, and the year is completed thereby. Going is contraction; coming is expansion. Contraction and expansion affect each other, and benefit is generated thereby. The inchworm contracts in order to seek expansion; dragons and snakes hibernate in order to preserve their bodies. Refining righteousness to enter the unfathomable is how one achieves practical application; benefiting from practical application to bring peace to the person is how one exalts virtue.

Wang Yan 王演

Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Guo 郭: This topic explains the line statement, stating that the principle of stimulus and response is nothing other than natural. Most other essays failed to explain and connect this clearly, whereas this essay is concise in wording and complete in principle. Moreover, his essays, discourse, and policy essays are all excellent; he is a scholar of learning and insight.

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Wang 汪: This topic enumerates images to speak of unintentional stimulus and response, thereby refuting the intentional stimulus and response arising from selfishness in the Nine in the Fourth place of the Xian 咸 [Influence] hexagram. Most writers were blind to this; this essay alone grasped it. How could a high recommendation be undeserved?

Comment by Examiner Instructor Zheng 鄭: Essays on the Classic of Changes (Yi 易) value subtlety and precision; this composition has achieved it.

Comment by Examiner Subprefectural Categorized Instructor Wang 王: It thoroughly explains the principle of stimulus and response.

The "Great Treatise" (Dazhuan 大傳) cites the line statement and explains that the principle of stimulus and response allows no room for deliberate intent, especially illustrating this through cosmic transformation, the principles of things, and sage learning.
