title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
九四累於私而憧憧於其往来者為應九四昵於私
而憧憧於其来則但朋類從之不復能及遠矣爻辭
如此吾夫子引而釋之謂夫天下何思何慮理之在
心者同因其事之不同而所行之塗各殊理之在心
者一因其事之不一而所發之慮有百塗雖殊慮雖
百而應事之理則同而一也天下果何思慮之有哉
彼自造化而觀之日之往而感月之来月之往而感
日之来二曜相推而明生不匱焉寒之往而感暑之
来暑之往而感寒之来二氣迭運而歲成不缺焉日
===
月寒暑之往者理之屈也而屈所以感夫信日月寒
暑之来者理之信也而信所以感夫屈屈信往来之
相感則明生歲成之利生矣此造化感應自然之理
也非特造化為然以物理言之尺蠖不屈則不能信
其所以屈者将以求其信而可行也龍蛇不蟄則不
能奮其所以蟄者将以存其身而可奮也非物理感
應之自然乎以聖學言之精研其義至於入神屈之
至也然乃所以為出而致用之本利其施用無適不
安信之極也然乃所以為入而崇德之資非聖學感
punctuated: 九四累於私，而憧憧於其往；来者為應，九四昵於私，而憧憧於其来，則但朋類從之，不復能及遠矣。爻辭如此。吾夫子引而釋之，謂夫天下何思何慮？理之在心者同，因其事之不同，而所行之塗各殊；理之在心者一，因其事之不一，而所發之慮有百。塗雖殊，慮雖百，而應事之理則同而一也，天下果何思慮之有哉？彼自造化而觀之：日之往而感月之来，月之往而感日之来，二曜相推而明生不匱焉；寒之往而感暑之来，暑之往而感寒之来，二氣迭運而歲成不缺焉。日月寒暑之往者，理之屈也，而屈所以感夫信；日月寒暑之来者，理之信也，而信所以感夫屈。屈信往来之相感，則明生歲成之利生矣，此造化感應自然之理也。非特造化為然，以物理言之：尺蠖不屈則不能信，其所以屈者，将以求其信而可行也；龍蛇不蟄則不能奮，其所以蟄者，将以存其身而可奮也。非物理感應之自然乎？以聖學言之：精研其義，至於入神，屈之至也，然乃所以為出而致用之本；利其施用，無適不安，信之極也，然乃所以為入而崇德之資。非聖學感
translation_en: … Nine in the Fourth Place is encumbered by selfishness and is unsettled in its going; what comes is response, and Nine in the Fourth Place is bound by partiality and is unsettled in its coming. Thus only those of its own faction follow it, and it can no longer reach far. Such is the line statement. Our Master cited and explained it, saying: What need is there in the world for thought and deliberation? The principle residing in the mind is the same, though because the affairs differ, the paths taken diverge; the principle residing in the mind is one, though because the affairs are not uniform, the deliberations that arise are a hundredfold. Although the paths diverge and the deliberations are a hundredfold, the principle for responding to affairs is the same and is one—what need, indeed, is there in the world for thought and deliberation? Looking at it from the perspective of the creative transformations of nature: the going of the sun stimulates the coming of the moon, and the going of the moon stimulates the coming of the sun; the two luminaries push each other forward, and light is generated without exhaustion. The going of cold stimulates the coming of heat, and the going of heat stimulates the coming of cold; the two vital forces alternate in their movement, and the year is brought to completion without fail. The going of the sun, moon, cold, and heat is the contraction of principle, and contraction is that by which extension is stimulated; the coming of the sun, moon, cold, and heat is the extension of principle, and extension is that by which contraction is stimulated. When contraction and extension, going and coming, mutually stimulate one another, the benefits of generating light and completing the year arise. This is the natural principle of stimulus and response in the creative transformations of nature. Nor is this true only of the creative transformations of nature. To speak in terms of the principles of things: if the inchworm does not contract, it cannot extend; the reason it contracts is that it seeks to extend so that it may move forward. If dragons and snakes do not hibernate, they cannot rouse themselves; the reason they hibernate is that they seek to preserve their bodies so that they may rouse themselves. Is this not the spontaneity of stimulus and response in the principles of things? To speak in terms of sage learning: investigating significance with precision to the point of entering the numinous is the utmost of contraction, yet it is the foundation for going forth and putting it to practical use; making its application beneficial so that nowhere is one ill at ease is the ultimate of extension, yet it is the resource for entering within and exalting virtue. Is this not the spontaneity of stimulus and…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
應之自然乎夫造化物理聖學之感應莫非自然如
此又豈若咸九四之憧憧往來而以思慮為哉大抵
往來者感應之常理也無心則公而憧憧則私公則
溥而觀諸衆理為可見私則狹而不過朋類之相從
故吾夫子特舉而釋之其亦欲人有事於感應者當
以咸九四而為戒也與
書義
厥貢惟球琳琅玕浮于積石至于龍門西河會
于渭汭織皮崑崙析支渠搜西戎即叙
===
鄧應仁
同考試官教諭林批此題言中外貢法之行見大
禹治水之成功是作得之
考試官教諭鄭批此作言水土既平華夷入貢
究見神禹治功之成深合
本旨
考試官學正王批形容大禹治水功成殆無餘蘊
紀一州之貢而著其貢道之異附三國之貢以見其
就功之同盖經國之制莫要於因地而制貢也雍州
punctuated:
應之自然乎？夫造化、物理、聖學之感應，莫非自然如此，又豈若咸九四之「憧憧往來」而以思慮為哉？大抵往來者，感應之常理也。無心則公，而憧憧則私。公則溥，而觀諸衆理為可見；私則狹，而不過朋類之相從。故吾夫子特舉而釋之，其亦欲人有事於感應者，當以咸九四而為戒也與！

書義
厥貢惟球琳琅玕，浮于積石，至于龍門西河，會于渭汭。織皮崑崙、析支、渠搜，西戎即叙。

鄧應仁
同考試官教諭林批：此題言中外貢法之行，見大禹治水之成功，是作得之。
考試官教諭鄭批：此作言水土既平，華夷入貢，究見神禹治功之成，深合本旨。
考試官學正王批：形容大禹治水功成，殆無餘蘊。

紀一州之貢，而著其貢道之異；附三國之貢，以見其就功之同。盖經國之制，莫要於因地而制貢也。雍州
translation_en:
… naturalness of stimulus and response in sage learning? Indeed, the stimulus and response in the creative transformations of nature, the principles of physical things, and sage learning are all naturally like this—how could they be like the Nine in the Fourth place of the Xian hexagram, "vacillating to and fro," acting out of deliberate calculation? Generally speaking, coming and going are the constant principle of stimulus and response. When there is no deliberate mind, it is impartial; when there is vacillating calculation, it is selfish. Being impartial, it is universal, as can be seen by observing the multitude of principles; being selfish, it is narrow, amounting to no more than the following of one's own clique. Therefore, our Master specially singled this out to explain it—surely he desired that those who engage in stimulus and response should take the Nine in the Fourth place of Xian as a warning!

Essay on the Book of Documents
"Its tribute is qiu and lin jades and langgan precious stones. They float from Jishi, arriving at Longmen and the West River, and meet at the bend of the Wei. Felt and skins come from Kunlun, Xizhi, and Qusou; the Western Rong were brought to order."

Deng Yingren 鄧應仁
Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Lin 林: This topic speaks of the implementation of the tribute system both within China and beyond, demonstrating the success of Great Yu's controlling of the waters. This essay grasps it well.
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Zheng 鄭: This essay states that once the waters and land were pacified, both Chinese and non-Chinese peoples presented tribute, ultimately revealing the completion of the divine Yu's work of flood control. It deeply accords with the original meaning of the text.
Comment by Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang 王: It describes the completion of Great Yu's achievement in controlling the waters, leaving almost nothing unexpressed.

The text records the tribute of a single province and sets forth the differences in its tribute routes; it appends the tribute of three states to show their commonality in submitting to the achievement of order. For among the institutions for governing the state, none is more essential than establishing tribute in accordance with the land. In Yongzhou…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
水土既平而貢法行於中外史臣得不并記之以見
聖世大一統之治歟何則雍州之域地之最高者也
向也治水施功未及貢法固未定矣今焉禹功告成
則其地產之美惟球琳之玉可以為禮器者制之使
入貢焉琅玕之石可以為服飾者定之為常貢焉然
貢道之來有出於東北境者則隨其貢物之便浮于
積石至於龍門西河以達於帝都矣有出於西南境
者則因其物產之近會于渭汭以達於河矣此中國
之貢然也至若西戎之域地之最遠者也向也雍州
===
水土未平功叙亦未就矣今焉禹功所及不惟崑崙
之國以織皮為貢而效其奉上之誠而析支渠搜亦
以織皮為獻而將其來王之敬夫崑崙乃西方戎落
之地其來貢王朝則其被餘功而就叙也可知矣析
支渠搜亦西方戎落之地其入獻中國則其慕王化
而即功也可見矣吁貢法既定於中國餘功復及於
西戎何莫而非神禹之成功也耶抑考雍州之境禹
治水施功最後者也當時九州水土皆已平治故其
上文所記水土成功則曰弱水既西曰三危既宅三
punctuated: 水土既平，而貢法行於中外，史臣得不并記之，以見聖世大一統之治歟？何則？雍州之域，地之最高者也。向也治水施功未及，貢法固未定矣。今焉禹功告成，則其地產之美，惟球琳之玉可以為禮器者，制之使入貢焉；琅玕之石可以為服飾者，定之為常貢焉。然貢道之來，有出於東北境者，則隨其貢物之便，浮于積石，至於龍門西河，以達於帝都矣；有出於西南境者，則因其物產之近，會于渭汭，以達於河矣。此中國之貢然也。至若西戎之域，地之最遠者也。向也雍州水土未平，功叙亦未就矣。今焉禹功所及，不惟崑崙之國以織皮為貢，而效其奉上之誠；而析支、渠搜亦以織皮為獻，而將其來王之敬。夫崑崙乃西方戎落之地，其來貢王朝，則其被餘功而就叙也可知矣；析支、渠搜亦西方戎落之地，其入獻中國，則其慕王化而即功也可見矣。吁！貢法既定於中國，餘功復及於西戎，何莫而非神禹之成功也耶？抑考雍州之境，禹治水施功最後者也。當時九州水土皆已平治，故其上文所記水土成功，則曰「弱水既西」，曰「三危既宅，三…
translation_en:
…Once the waters and land of [Yong Province] were pacified and the system of tribute operated both inside and outside the realm, how could the court historian not record them together so as to manifest the governance of the great unification in a sagely age?

Why is this so? The territory of Yong Province (Yongzhou) is the highest in elevation. Previously, when the work of controlling the waters had not yet reached it, the tribute system was naturally not yet established. Now that the work of Yu has been brought to completion, among the fine products of its land, the sounding-stone and fine jades (qiulin) suitable for making ritual vessels are regulated to be sent in as tribute; and the langgan precious stones suitable for ornaments and attire are established as regular tribute. Moreover, as for the routes by which the tribute comes: for that which sets out from the northeastern border, according to the convenience of transporting the tribute goods, it floats from Jishi and arrives at Longmen on the western Yellow River so as to reach the imperial capital; for that which sets out from the southwestern border, by virtue of the proximity of its local products, it converges at the bend of the Wei River (Weirui) so as to reach the Yellow River. Such is the tribute of the Central States.

As for the territory of the Western Rong (Xirong), it is the most distant of lands. Previously, when the waters and land of Yong Province were not yet pacified, the ordering of their work was likewise not yet accomplished. Now, where the achievements of Yu have reached, not only does the state of Kunlun offer woven hides and furs as tribute to show its sincerity in serving the ruler above, but Xizhi and Qusou also present woven hides and furs to convey their reverence in coming to pay allegiance to the king. Now, Kunlun is a land of Rong settlements in the west; since it comes to offer tribute to the royal court, one may know that it has received the overflow of his achievements and come into order. Xizhi and Qusou are likewise lands of Rong settlements in the west; since they enter to present offerings to the Central States, it can be seen that they admire the royal transformation and have attained orderly accomplishment. Ah! With the tribute system settled in the Central States and the overflow of his achievements extending further to the Western Rong, what is there that is not the successful accomplishment of the divine Yu?

Furthermore, if we examine the territory of Yong Province, it was the very last place where Yu applied his labor in controlling the waters. At that time, the waters and land of the Nine Provinces had all been pacified and brought to order. Therefore, when the preceding passage records the successful ordering of the waters and land, it says, "The Ruo River has been conducted westward," and it says, "Sanwei has become habitable, and the San[miao]…"

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
苗丕叙而此記是州貢法則曰崐崘析支渠搜西戎
即叙皆極其遠而言之于以見聖人平治之功無間
於遠邇而道德之化無限於內外也所謂地平天成
六府三事允治萬世永賴者豈虛語哉
公其惟時成周建無窮之基亦有無窮之聞子
孫訓其成式惟乂嗚呼罔曰弗克惟既厥心
罔曰民寡惟慎厥事欽若先王成烈以休于
前政
鄧應仁
===
同考試官教諭林批破題明潔講語純正當□□
冠本經
考試官教諭鄭批康王命畢公以保釐之責
其期勉之辭如此是作能發
其意是宜錄出
考試官學正王批理明辭暢深得康王命畢公之意
賢王之命大臣既期其立可久之業而垂於後必勉
其任成終之責以光于前甚矣保釐之責之重也賢
王於大臣既以垂於後者期之得不以光于前者□□
punctuated:
苗丕叙，而此記是州貢法，則曰崐崘、析支、渠搜、西戎即叙，皆極其遠而言之。于以見聖人平治之功無間於遠邇，而道德之化無限於內外也。所謂「地平天成，六府三事允治，萬世永賴」者，豈虛語哉！

公其惟時成周，建無窮之基，亦有無窮之聞。子孫訓其成式惟乂。嗚呼！罔曰弗克，惟既厥心；罔曰民寡，惟慎厥事。欽若先王成烈，以休于前政。
鄧應仁
同考試官教諭林批：破題明潔，講語純正，當□□冠本經。
考試官教諭鄭批：康王命畢公以保釐之責，其期勉之辭如此。是作能發其意，是宜錄出。
考試官學正王批：理明辭暢，深得康王命畢公之意。

賢王之命大臣，既期其立可久之業而垂於後，必勉其任成終之責以光于前。甚矣，保釐之責之重也！賢王於大臣，既以垂於後者期之，得不以光于前者□□
translation_en:
… the Sanmiao were brought into great order; and here, in recording the tribute system of this province, it says that Kunlun, Xizhi, Qusou, and the Western Rong came into order—in all cases speaking of the most distant regions. From this one can see that the sage’s achievement of pacification and governance made no distinction between far and near, and the transformation of his moral virtue had no boundary between inner and outer. That which is called “The earth is pacified and heaven’s work is completed; the six treasuries and three affairs are truly governed, to be relied upon forever for ten thousand generations”—how could these be empty words!

“May you, Duke, solely in this Chengzhou, establish an boundless foundation, and you shall also have boundless renown. Your sons and grandsons will follow your established model and govern well. Oh! Do not say that you are unable; only exhaust your heart. Do not say that the people are few; only be cautious in your affairs. Reverently conform to the accomplished achievements of the former kings, so as to bring glory to the previous administration.”

Deng Yingren 鄧應仁

Comment by Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Lin: The opening statement of the theme is clear and concise, and the exposition is pure and orthodox; it ought [to be placed?] first in this Classic.
Comment by Examiner County Director of Studies Zheng: King Kang charged the Duke of Bi with the responsibility of protecting and regulating, and his words of expectation and encouragement were like this. This composition is able to bring out his meaning; it is fitting that it be selected for publication.
Comment by Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang: The principles are clear and the diction is fluent; it deeply grasps King Kang’s intention in charging the Duke of Bi.

When a worthy king gives a charge to a great minister, having expected him to establish an enduring enterprise to be handed down to posterity, he must also encourage him to take up the responsibility of bringing things to completion so as to shed glory upon his predecessors. Great indeed is the weight of the responsibility of protecting and regulating! Since a worthy king expects of his great minister that which will be handed down to posterity, how could he not [encourage him?] with that which will shed glory upon his predecessors…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之哉康王命畢公保釐東郊而終及乎此意以成周
之眾蕞爾甚微而所係甚重公其惟時成化殷之功
則足以立無窮之事業而勳德樹於永世將亦有無
窮之聲聞而名實昭于後世是公之身有賴乎此而
勳譽之隆千載一時也公之子孫承殷民之化則可
以順其成法而事無不治遵其成憲而政無不乂是
公之子孫亦有賴乎此而垂憲乃後百世一日也成
周所係若此其重則夫畢公任成終之責可不勉哉
於是復嘆息而告之謂夫事之不立非視之太重而
===
畏其難則視之太輕而忽其易公於保釐之事勿畏
其難而不敢為惟往盡乃心耳盡乃心則雖難而無
所畏矣勿易其民以為不足為惟克謹乃事耳謹其
事則雖易而不敢忽矣彼其式化厥訓者先王之成
烈周公謹始所致也公必敬順之弗懈使周公之政
於焉而有光允升大猷者亦先王之成烈君陳和中
所底也公必祗若之無怠俾君陳之政於焉而益美
夫既立無窮之業而復盡成終之責保釐之治孰有
加於此哉吁畢公四世元老勳業之隆若無待於期
punctuated: 之哉？康王命畢公保釐東郊，而終及乎此。意以成周之眾，蕞爾甚微，而所係甚重。公其惟時成化殷之功，則足以立無窮之事業，而勳德樹於永世；將亦有無窮之聲聞，而名實昭于後世。是公之身有賴乎此，而勳譽之隆，千載一時也。公之子孫，承殷民之化，則可以順其成法而事無不治，遵其成憲而政無不乂。是公之子孫亦有賴乎此，而垂憲乃後，百世一日也。成周所係若此其重，則夫畢公任成終之責，可不勉哉？於是復嘆息而告之，謂夫事之不立，非視之太重而畏其難，則視之太輕而忽其易。公於保釐之事，勿畏其難而不敢為，惟往盡乃心耳，盡乃心則雖難而無所畏矣；勿易其民以為不足為，惟克謹乃事耳，謹其事則雖易而不敢忽矣。彼其式化厥訓者，先王之成烈，周公謹始所致也，公必敬順之弗懈，使周公之政於焉而有光；允升大猷者，亦先王之成烈，君陳和中所底也，公必祗若之無怠，俾君陳之政於焉而益美。夫既立無窮之業，而復盡成終之責，保釐之治，孰有加於此哉？吁！畢公四世元老，勳業之隆，若無待於期
translation_en:
… [exhort] him? When King Kang (Kangwang 康王) commanded the Duke of Bi (Bigong 畢公) to protect and regulate the eastern suburbs, he concluded by touching upon this very idea. He considered that the multitude of Chengzhou, though tiny and insignificant in size, was of the utmost importance in what depended upon it. If the Duke would at this time bring to completion the work of transforming the people of Yin, it would suffice to establish boundless achievements, with his meritorious virtue planted for eternal generations; and he would also enjoy boundless renown, with both his name and reality shining forth to later ages. Thus the Duke's own person depended upon this, and the eminence of his merit and fame was an opportunity of a thousand years. And when the Duke's descendants inherited the transformation of the Yin people, they would be able to follow his established methods so that no affair would go unManaged, and observe his established statutes so that no governance would go unordered. Thus the Duke's descendants likewise depended upon this, handing down statutes to posterity so that a hundred generations would be as a single day. Since what depended on Chengzhou was of such great weight, how could the Duke of Bi not exert himself in bearing the responsibility of bringing the work to its final completion?

Thereupon the King sighed again and admonished him, saying that when affairs fail to be established, if it is not because one views them as too weighty and fears their difficulty, then it is because one views them as too light and neglects their ease. In the matter of protecting and regulating, the Duke must not fear its difficulty and dare not act, but should simply go forth and exhaust his heart in it; if he exhausts his heart, then even though it is difficult, there will be nothing to fear. Nor must he take the people lightly and deem them unworthy of effort, but should simply be able to attend carefully to his affairs; if he attends carefully to his affairs, then even though they seem easy, he will not dare to neglect them. That the people had been transformed by instruction was the accomplished功績 (merit) of the former kings, brought about by the Duke of Zhou's (Zhougong 周公) careful beginning; the Duke of Bi must reverently comply with it unremittingly, causing the governance of the Duke of Zhou thereby to gain luster. That they had truly ascended to the great way of moral order was likewise the accomplished merit of the former kings, attained through Jun Chen's (君陳) harmonizing middle course; the Duke of Bi must respectfully accord with it tirelessly, causing the governance of Jun Chen thereby to become even more admirable. Having both established a boundless enterprise and fulfilled the responsibility of bringing the work to completion, what governance of protection and regulation could surpass this?

Alas! The Duke of Bi was a senior statesman of four reigns; the eminence of his merit and achievements would seem to have had no need of…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
望矣克勤小物亦無待於戒勉矣而康王之命尤惓
惓焉蓋期以無窮之業者尊敬之至也勉以成終之
責者願望之深也厥后畢公果能化服殷民卒使保
於周者八百年可謂無愧於先王無愧於周公君陳
而亦無負於康王之命矣
詩義
維其有章矣是以有慶矣
周叙
同考試官教諭陳批此題本平易作者於有章
有慶處謬說紛紜殊紊
㫖此作得之所宜録出
===
考試官教諭鄭批辭理簡明尤如初考
考試官學正王批王者美諸侯之意宛然在目
王者之美諸侯惟有德著於外斯有福集於已蓋德
者福之本今諸侯之德既著於外則其有福慶也宜
矣此天子美諸侯之辭蓋以荅瞻彼洛矣也謂夫諸
侯之來朝也非特乗其四駱六轡沃若而已觀其彼
交匪紓威儀抑抑粲然其有文則德之𢎞中彪外者
punctuated:
望矣，克勤小物，亦無待於戒勉矣，而康王之命尤惓惓焉。蓋期以無窮之業者，尊敬之至也；勉以成終之責者，願望之深也。厥后畢公果能化服殷民，卒使保於周者八百年，可謂無愧於先王，無愧於周公、君陳，而亦無負於康王之命矣。

《詩》義
維其有章矣，是以有慶矣。
周叙
同考試官教諭陳批：此題本平易，作者於「有章」、「有慶」處謬說紛紜，殊紊㫖。此作得之，所宜録出。
考試官教諭鄭批：辭理簡明，尤如初考。
考試官學正王批：王者美諸侯之意，宛然在目。

王者之美諸侯，惟有德著於外，斯有福集於已。蓋德者，福之本。今諸侯之德既著於外，則其有福慶也宜矣。此天子美諸侯之辭，蓋以荅《瞻彼洛矣》也。謂夫諸侯之來朝也，非特乗其四駱，六轡沃若而已；觀其彼交匪紓，威儀抑抑，粲然其有文，則德之𢎞中彪外者
translation_en:
…expectations; and since he was able to be diligent even in small matters, he likewise had no need of admonition or encouragement. Yet the charge of King Kang (康王) was especially earnest. Indeed, expecting him to establish a boundless enterprise was the utmost of respect; encouraging him with the responsibility of bringing the work to completion was the deepest of hopes. Thereafter, the Duke of Bi (畢公) was indeed able to transform and win the submission of the Yin people, ultimately ensuring their preservation under the Zhou for eight hundred years. He may truly be said to have been worthy of the former kings, worthy of the Duke of Zhou (周公) and Jun Chen (君陳), and also true to the charge of King Kang.

Exposition on the Classic of Poetry (Shijing 詩經)
"Because they possess refinement, therefore they enjoy blessings."
By Zhou Xu (周叙)
Comment by Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Chen: This topic is inherently straightforward, yet candidates offered all manner of erroneous explanations regarding the phrases "possessing refinement" and "enjoying blessings," greatly confusing the main purport [?]. This essay grasps it, and ought appropriately to be selected for publication.
Comment by Examiner and County Director of Studies Zheng: The diction and reasoning are concise and clear; I concur all the more with the initial evaluation.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang: The true king's intent in praising the feudal lords is vividly before one's eyes.

When the true king praises the feudal lords, it is only because their virtue is manifest on the outside that blessings gather upon their persons. Indeed, virtue is the root of blessing. Now that the virtue of the feudal lords is already manifest on the outside, it is only fitting that they should enjoy blessings and felicity. These are the words of the Son of Heaven praising the feudal lords, composed in reply to the ode "Look at the Luo River" (Zhan bi Luo yi 瞻彼洛矣). It means that when the feudal lords come to court, they do not merely ride their teams of four white horses with black manes, holding their six reins glossy and soft; when one observes how in their intercourse they are not remiss, and how their dignified bearing is so circumspect—resplendent in their refinement—then how their virtue is ample within and brilliantly displayed without…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
可知非特赤芾在股邪幅在下而已觀其彼交匪敖
淑愼爾止蔚然其有章則德之睟面盎背者可見然
諸侯德之彰著如此則豈不有福慶乎是以向也折
王之圭而維藩維垣固嘗受福矣今也來朝於東都
燕笑語兮有譽處兮而有以享是福於悠久焉昔也
儹王之爵而之屏之翰巳嘗有慶矣今也會同於洛
水天子命之福禄申之而有以衍是慶於無窮焉吁
德著於外福集於巳宜詩人形諸詠歌以美之也抑
考瞻彼洛矣之詩諸侯所以美天子也旣願其享福
===
禄而保家邦矣此天子之答諸侯不惟言其以德獲
福而下二章又言其車馬威儀之盛才德之全備焉
噫上下之間交相忠愛如此此所以為有周盛世之
君臣也與
清酒旣載騂牡旣備以享以祀以介景福瑟彼
柞棫民所燎矣豈弟君子神所勞矣莫莫葛
藟施于條枚豈弟君子求福不回
嵇本芳
同考試官教諭陳批場中作此題者多冗長可
punctuated:
可知；非特「赤芾在股，邪幅在下」而已，觀其「彼交匪敖」，淑愼爾止，蔚然其有章，則德之睟面盎背者可見。然諸侯德之彰著如此，則豈不有福慶乎？是以向也折王之圭，而「維藩維垣」，固嘗受福矣；今也來朝於東都，「燕笑語兮，有譽處兮」，而有以享是福於悠久焉。昔也儹王之爵，而「之屏之翰」，巳嘗有慶矣；今也會同於洛水，「天子命之，福禄申之」，而有以衍是慶於無窮焉。吁！德著於外，福集於巳，宜詩人形諸詠歌以美之也。抑考《瞻彼洛矣》之詩，諸侯所以美天子也，旣願其享福禄而保家邦矣；此天子之答諸侯，不惟言其以德獲福，而下二章又言其車馬威儀之盛、才德之全備焉。噫！上下之間，交相忠愛如此，此所以為有周盛世之君臣也與！
「清酒旣載，騂牡旣備，以享以祀，以介景福。瑟彼柞棫，民所燎矣；豈弟君子，神所勞矣。莫莫葛藟，施于條枚；豈弟君子，求福不回。」
嵇本芳
同考試官教諭陳批：場中作此題者，多冗長可
translation_en:
…can be known; it is not merely that "their red knee-covers are on their shins, their slant-wrapped leg-bindings are below," for when we observe that "in their intercourse they are not arrogant," carefully guarding their deportment, luxuriantly displaying refinement, then the virtue that shines gently in the face and generously fills out the back can be seen. Since the virtue of the feudal lords is so manifestly displayed, how could they not possess blessings and felicity? Therefore, in the past, when they received the split jade-tablets of the king and served as "a fence and a wall," they had assuredly already received blessings; and now, as they come to court at the Eastern Capital, "feasting, laughing, and talking, having renown and peace," they have the means to enjoy these blessings in perpetuity. Formerly, when they shared in the noble ranks of the king and served as "a screen and a bulwark," they had already known felicity; and now, as they assemble together at the Luo River, "the Son of Heaven commands them, and blessings and emoluments are renewed for them," so that they have the means to extend this felicity without end. Ah! When virtue is manifest on the outside, blessings gather upon oneself; it is fitting indeed that the poet gave form to this in song to praise them. Furthermore, if we examine the ode "Look at the Luo" (Zhan bi Luo yi), by which the feudal lords praised the Son of Heaven, they already wished that he might enjoy blessings and emoluments and preserve his royal house and state; here, in the Son of Heaven's reply to the feudal lords, not only does he speak of their obtaining blessings through virtue, but the following two stanzas also speak of the splendour of their carriages, horses, and dignified demeanour, and the complete perfection of their talent and virtue. Alas! That superiors and inferiors shared such mutual loyalty and affection—is this not what made them ruler and ministers of the flourishing age of the Zhou!

"The clear wine is placed in the vessels, the red bull is ready, to offer and to sacrifice, so as to increase great blessings. Luxuriant are those oaks and scrub-oaks, which the people gather for firewood; easy and self-possessed is our lord, whom the spirits comfort and reward. Thickly grow the creeper-vines, spreading over the branches and stems; easy and self-possessed is our lord, who seeks blessings without perversity."

Ji Benfang 嵇本芳.

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
厭唯此篇辭簡理明敻□
衆作况他篇俱優本房
無出其右者健羨健羨
考試官教諭鄭批此作形容文王以德受福之
㫖簡當可觀
考試官學正王批辭理俱到
詩人美聖人祭必受福也既興其得福之由復與其
得福之正夫聖人有豈弟之德則祭必受福然亦由
乎神之眷而出乎心之正爾詩人所託興而詠歌之
===
也宜哉是詩亦詠歌文王之德謂夫文王之祭有清
酒焉則載而在尊矣有騂牡焉則備而全具矣于以
享乎神則景福之必至于以祀乎神則繁祉之必集
是何也以文王有豈弟之德也夫文王有德而祭必
受福如此亦豈無所自耶故託興以謂彼瑟然茂密
之柞棫乃叢生小木耳尚可供燎而濟民生之用况
豈弟樂易之君子豈不為神所勞乎吾知神之聽之
而有慰撫之休故福於是而攸降也夫文王以德受
福雖由乎神之勞而其心一出乎正也故又託興以
punctuated:
厭，唯此篇辭簡理明，敻□衆作，况他篇俱優，本房無出其右者，健羨健羨。
考試官教諭鄭批：此作形容文王以德受福之㫖，簡當可觀。
考試官學正王批：辭理俱到。

詩人美聖人祭必受福也，既興其得福之由，復與其得福之正。夫聖人有豈弟之德，則祭必受福，然亦由乎神之眷，而出乎心之正爾。詩人所託興而詠歌之也，宜哉！是詩亦詠歌文王之德，謂夫文王之祭，有清酒焉，則載而在尊矣；有騂牡焉，則備而全具矣。于以享乎神，則景福之必至；于以祀乎神，則繁祉之必集。是何也？以文王有豈弟之德也。夫文王有德而祭必受福如此，亦豈無所自耶？故託興以謂：彼瑟然茂密之柞棫，乃叢生小木耳，尚可供燎而濟民生之用，况豈弟樂易之君子，豈不為神所勞乎？吾知神之聽之，而有慰撫之休，故福於是而攸降也。夫文王以德受福，雖由乎神之勞，而其心一出乎正也。故又託興以
translation_en:
…tedious. Only this essay is concise in diction and clear in principle, far [surpassing?] the compositions of the crowd. Moreover, his other essays are all excellent; in this examination ward there is none who surpasses him. Truly admirable, truly admirable!
Examiner and Instructor Zheng's comment: This composition describes the purport of King Wen's receiving blessings through virtue in a way that is concise, apt, and well worth reading.
Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Wang's comment: Both diction and principle hit the mark.

When the poet praises the sage for invariably receiving blessings when offering sacrifices, he first uses an evocative image (xing) to show the source of his obtaining blessings, and then again [uses an evocative image, 興 misprinted as 與?] to show the rectitude of his obtaining blessings. Now, because the sage possesses easy and fraternal virtue, when he sacrifices he invariably receives blessings; yet this also stems from the favor of the spirits and issues from the rectitude of his own heart. How fitting it is that the poet entrusted his meaning to evocative imagery to sing of this! This ode also sings of the virtue of King Wen, saying that in King Wen's sacrifice, there is clear wine, which is set forth and contained in the goblets; there are red bulls, which are prepared and completely provided. Through offering them to the spirits, great blessings will surely arrive; through sacrificing to the spirits, abundant favors will surely gather. Why is this? Because King Wen possesses easy and fraternal virtue. Now, since King Wen possesses virtue and thus invariably receives blessings when sacrificing like this, how could it be without a source? Therefore, the poet uses an evocative image to say: those densely luxuriant oak and white-oak trees are merely small shrubs growing in thickets, yet they can still supply firewood to aid the needs of the people's livelihood; how much more so an easy, fraternal, and amiable lord—how could he not be comforted and rewarded by the spirits? We know that the spirits hearken to him and grant the grace of their solace and comfort, and therefore blessings thereupon descend. Now, although King Wen's receiving blessings through virtue stems from the comforting reward of the spirits, his heart issues entirely from rectitude. Therefore, the poet again uses an evocative image to…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
謂莫然茂盛之葛藟乃蔓生微草耳尚有所托而施
條枚之上況豈弟樂易之君子其受福豈待於求耶
亦惟厥德不回而無覬倖之心故福不求而自至也
是則德之所在福之所在文王之為神所勞為福所
歸何莫非一德所致哉抑通考是詩一章言文王得
福之有道二章言文王得福之自然三章言文王作
人之妙至此則言其受福之本求福之心也大哉聖
人豈弟之德乎其所以為作人受福之本乎此詩人
所以歷叙而詠歌之也猗歟盛哉
===
春秋義
齊人侵我西鄙公追齊師至酅弗及僖公二十六年公
會齊侯于夾谷定公十年
曹鼎
同考試官訓導李批場中作此題者多拘泥而文
少通暢合題意而詞不冗者
僅見此篇是宜錄出
考試官教諭鄭批理明辭整
考試官學正王批理完氣充當是作者
punctuated:
謂莫然茂盛之葛藟，乃蔓生微草耳，尚有所托而施條枚之上；況豈弟樂易之君子，其受福豈待於求耶？亦惟厥德不回，而無覬倖之心，故福不求而自至也。是則德之所在，福之所在，文王之為神所勞、為福所歸，何莫非一德所致哉！抑通考是詩：一章言文王得福之有道，二章言文王得福之自然，三章言文王作人之妙，至此則言其受福之本、求福之心也。大哉聖人豈弟之德乎！其所以為作人受福之本乎！此詩人所以歷叙而詠歌之也。猗歟盛哉！
《春秋》義：
「齊人侵我西鄙，公追齊師至酅，弗及。」〔僖公二十六年〕「公會齊侯于夾谷。」〔定公十年〕
曹鼎
同考試官訓導李批：場中作此題者多拘泥而文少通暢，合題意而詞不冗者，僅見此篇，是宜錄出。
考試官教諭鄭批：理明辭整。
考試官學正王批：理完氣充，當是作者。
translation_en:
…say that the luxuriantly thriving creepers and vines, though merely creeping little plants, still have something to rely on and spread over the branches and stems; how much more so the affable and easygoing noble man—how could his receiving of blessings depend upon seeking them? It is only that his virtue does not deviate and he harbors no mind for undeserved fortune; therefore, blessings arrive of themselves without being sought. Thus, where virtue resides, there blessings reside. That King Wen was consoled by the spirits and was the one to whom blessings repaired—how could any of this not be brought about by his singular virtue? Moreover, examining this ode as a whole: the first stanza speaks of the way by which King Wen obtained blessings; the second stanza speaks of the naturalness with which King Wen obtained blessings; the third stanza speaks of the subtlety with which King Wen cultivated men; and arriving here, it speaks of the foundation of his receiving blessings and his mind in seeking blessings. Great indeed is the affable and easygoing virtue of the sage! Is it not the foundation both for cultivating men and for receiving blessings? This is why the poet recounted it in order and sang of it. How admirable, how grand!

Essays on the Meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
"The men of Qi invaded our western border. The Duke pursued the army of Qi as far as Xi, but did not overtake it." [Twenty-sixth year of Duke Xi] "The Duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu." [Tenth year of Duke Ding]
Cao Ding 曹鼎
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Li 李: In the examination hall, those writing on this topic were mostly overly rigid and their prose lacked fluency. Only in this essay do we see one that conforms to the meaning of the topic without wordiness; it ought to be selected for publication.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zheng 鄭: The reasoning is clear and the diction is well-ordered.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang 王: The reasoning is complete and the vital breath is full; he must be an accomplished writer.

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
大國肆虐內之威而畏於赴敵者可譏大國懷陵內
之謀而勇於却敵者可喜此僖公不敢及齊之師聖
人能却齊之衆春秋備書而勇怯見矣且魯之與齊
以先世言之周公太公夾輔周室嘗有世好之盟也
以春秋之時論之桓公創伯糾合諸侯昭舊職也奚
有私怨之脩乎今也齊孝嗣世棄命廢職乃舉無名
之衆肆為西鄙之侵陵虐我郊保荼毒我人民則曲
而老者在齊直而壯者在魯矣齊何足畏哉夫何僖
公在位方齊之至而無防禦之策及齊之去而舉追
===
逐之師深入其地弗及而返夫以齊之強豈能勝秦
以魯之衆何弱於趙然澠池之會藺相如一奮其氣
威信敵國秦雖虎狼猶不敓動况以千乘之君而畏
齊之若是乎噫自反而縮雖千萬人吾往矣而僖公
不足以語此迨夫春秋之季齊景代興陵魯之志又
有甚於齊孝者矣有如夾谷之會聽犁彌之言為執
魯之計兩君就壇鼓譟而起則齊有莫敵之勢而魯
有不測之禍矣魯將如之何哉幸而聖人相禮左右
司馬之具足以破其詐裔夷亂華之卻足以革其心
punctuated: 大國肆虐內之威，而畏於赴敵者可譏；大國懷陵內之謀，而勇於却敵者可喜。此僖公不敢及齊之師，聖人能却齊之衆，《春秋》備書而勇怯見矣。且魯之與齊，以先世言之，周公、太公夾輔周室，嘗有世好之盟也；以春秋之時論之，桓公創伯，糾合諸侯，昭舊職也，奚有私怨之脩乎？今也齊孝嗣世，棄命廢職，乃舉無名之衆，肆為西鄙之侵，陵虐我郊保，荼毒我人民，則曲而老者在齊，直而壯者在魯矣，齊何足畏哉？夫何僖公在位，方齊之至而無防禦之策，及齊之去而舉追逐之師，深入其地，弗及而返。夫以齊之強，豈能勝秦？以魯之衆，何弱於趙？然澠池之會，藺相如一奮其氣，威信敵國，秦雖虎狼，猶不敓動，况以千乘之君而畏齊之若是乎？噫！「自反而縮，雖千萬人吾往矣」，而僖公不足以語此。迨夫春秋之季，齊景代興，陵魯之志又有甚於齊孝者矣。有如夾谷之會，聽犁彌之言，為執魯之計，兩君就壇，鼓譟而起，則齊有莫敵之勢，而魯有不測之禍矣，魯將如之何哉？幸而聖人相禮，左右司馬之具，足以破其詐；「裔夷亂華」之卻，足以革其心。
translation_en:
When a great state unleashes its intimidating might to ravage one's territory, yet one is too timid to engage the enemy, that is worthy of ridicule; when a great state harbors schemes to encroach upon one's territory, yet one is brave enough to repel the enemy, that is worthy of praise. Thus, Duke Xi (Xigong 僖公) did not dare to overtake the army of Qi, whereas the Sage was able to repel the hosts of Qi; the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) recorded both in full, and therein bravery and cowardice are revealed.

Moreover, regarding the relationship between Lu and Qi: if we speak of former generations, the Duke of Zhou (Zhougong 周公) and the Grand Duke (Taigong 太公) jointly assisted the royal house of Zhou, and had sworn covenants of hereditary friendship; if we discuss the era of the Spring and Autumn period, Duke Huan (Huangong 桓公) established the霸 hegemony, assembling the feudal lords to make bright their old duties—how could there have been the nursing of private grudges? Now Duke Xiao of Qi (Qi Xiao 齊孝) succeeded to the rule, cast aside commands and abandoned his duties, raising a host without just cause to wantonly invade our western frontier, ravaging our suburban strongholds andBringing misery upon our people. Thus, being in the wrong and exhausted lay with Qi, while being in the right and vigorous lay with Lu—what was there to fear in Qi? Why then did Duke Xi, occupying the throne, have no plan for defense while Qi was arriving, and only after Qi had departed raise a pursuing army, penetrating deep into their territory only to return without overtaking them?

Now, with the strength of Qi, how could it surpass Qin? With the multitude of Lu, how was it weaker than Zhao? Yet at the meeting at Mianchi, once Lin Xiangru 藺相如 roused his spirit, his prestige extended over the rival state; though Qin was like a tiger or wolf, it still did not dare [reading 敓 as 敢] to make a move—how much less should the ruler of a state of a thousand chariots fear Qi like this! Alas! "If on self-examination I find that I am upright, I will go forward against thousands and tens of thousands"—but Duke Xi was not worthy of speaking of this.

Coming down to the end of the Spring and Autumn period, Duke Jing of Qi (Qi Jing 齊景) rose in turn, and his ambition to encroach upon Lu was even worse than that of Duke Xiao of Qi. For instance, at the meeting at Jiagu, he listened to the words of Li Mi 犁彌 and formed a plot to seize the ruler of Lu. When the two rulers approached the altar and a clamor of drums arose, Qi had an irresistible momentum while Lu faced an unfathomable disaster—what was Lu going to do? Fortunately, the Sage assisted with the rites: the provision of the Left and Right Marshals (Sima 司馬) was sufficient to shatter their deceit, and his repulse of "frontier barbarians throwing the Central States into disorder" was sufficient to reform their hearts. …

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
故揖讓指麾齊遂感服彼向也齊孝之衆不足以當
齊景僖公之世足以勝定公之末年舉兵追齊尚不
敢及詎意仲尼一言而能却齊之若此乎噫善養氣
者匹夫不為千乘屈於聖人有足徴雖然僖公之無
勇固不足論吾夫子之聖綏來動和神妙不測豈特
能變齊而已耶行乎季孫三月不違二邑迭毀變魯
之幾又可驗矣使魯克終用之則吾其東周之志不
徒托諸空言也奈何女樂魯庭聖轍汶上千載之下
不能不為之太息
===
楚人伐鄭〔僖公元年〕齊侯宋公江人黃人盟于貫〔僖公〕
〔二年〕遂伐楚盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕楚人陳侯蔡
侯鄭伯許男圍宋〔僖公二十七年〕晉侯齊師宋師秦
師及楚人戰于城濮楚師敗績〔僖公二十八年〕楚人
圍江晉陽處父帥師伐楚以救江〔文公三年〕
沈□
同考試官訓導李批題本平易作者語多陳腐
令人厭觀融會傳註成文亦作
得之矣非熟於麟經者能之
punctuated:
故揖讓指麾，齊遂感服。彼向也，齊孝之衆不足以當齊景，僖公之世足以勝定公之末年，舉兵追齊尚不敢及；詎意仲尼一言，而能却齊之若此乎？噫！善養氣者，匹夫不為千乘屈，於聖人有足徴。雖然，僖公之無勇，固不足論；吾夫子之聖，綏來動和，神妙不測，豈特能變齊而已耶？行乎季孫，三月不違，二邑迭毀，變魯之幾又可驗矣。使魯克終用之，則「吾其東周」之志，不徒托諸空言也。奈何女樂魯庭，聖轍汶上，千載之下，不能不為之太息！
楚人伐鄭〔僖公元年〕；齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人盟于貫〔僖公〕〔二年〕，遂伐楚，盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕；楚人、陳侯、蔡侯、鄭伯、許男圍宋〔僖公二十七年〕，晉侯、齊師、宋師、秦師及楚人戰于城濮，楚師敗績〔僖公二十八年〕；楚人圍江，晉陽處父帥師伐楚以救江〔文公三年〕。
沈□
同考試官訓導李批：題本平易，作者語多陳腐，令人厭觀。融會傳註成文，亦作得之矣，非熟於麟經者能之
translation_en:
… Therefore, through bowing and yielding in ceremonial command, Qi was moved to submit. Previously, the forces of Duke Xiao of Qi (Qi Xiao 齊孝) were no match for those of Duke Jing of Qi (Qi Jing 齊景), and the era of Duke Xi (Xi Gong 僖公) was superior to the final years of Duke Ding (Ding Gong 定公), yet when raising troops to pursue Qi, Duke Xi still did not dare to overtake them; how could one have expected that with a single word from Zhongni 仲尼 [Confucius], he could repulse Qi like this? Alas! That one who is good at nourishing his vital energy, even as a commoner, will not bend before the lord of a thousand chariots, is amply attested in the Sage. Even so, Duke Xi's lack of courage is certainly not worth discussing; as for the sageliness of our Master—"pacifying them so they come, moving them so they are harmonious," wondrous and unfathomable—could it merely be capable of transforming Qi and nothing more? When he acted with the Jisun 季孫 clan, for three months they did not违 [deviate from benevolence], and two fortified cities were successively dismantled; theincipient sign of transforming Lu could also be verified. Had Lu been able to employ him to the end, then his aspiration of "making an Eastern Zhou" would not have been merely entrusted to empty words. Yet what could be done when female musicians entered the court of Lu, and the Sage's chariot tracks turned toward the Wen River (Wenshang 汶上)? A thousand years later, one cannot help but heave a deep sigh over this!

"The people of Chu invaded Zheng" [1st year of Duke Xi]; "The Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the people of Jiang, and the people of Huang made a covenant at Guan" [2nd year of Duke Xi]; "Subsequently they invaded Chu and made a covenant at Shaoling" [4th year of Duke Xi]; "The people of Chu, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, and the Baron of Xu besieged Song" [27th year of Duke Xi]; "The Marquis of Jin, the army of Qi, the army of Song, and the army of Qin fought with the people of Chu at Chengpu, and the army of Chu was utterly defeated" [28th year of Duke Xi]; "The people of Chu besieged Jiang, and Yang Chufu 陽處父 of Jin led an army to invade Chu in order to rescue Jiang" [3rd year of Duke Wen].

Shen □ 沈□

By synthesizing the commentaries and annotations to compose the essay, this piece too has succeeded in grasping it; could anyone not thoroughly versed in the Classic of the Unicorn (Linjing 麟經, i.e., the Spring and Autumn Annals) be capable of this…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
乎故取之以冠本房
考試官教諭鄭批斷桓文晉襄用兵得失殆
無餘蘊
考試官學正王批得胡傳之意
外患迭加於大國而伯主得安攘之道可予外患繼
加於小國而伯主失安攘之道可譏夫伯者之責莫
大乎攘夷安夏而尤在乎用兵之有法也春秋備書
桓文晉襄攘楚之事而得失見矣何則楚之始封辟
在荊山篳路藍縷以處草莽桃弧棘矢以共禦王事
===
而已豈意其暴橫憑陵如春秋之世耶始也怒鄭即
齊則興兵以伐鄭繼也怒宋從晉則合兵以圍宋夫
宋鄭大國非附庸比也楚人伐之豈不恣暴橫以文
偕行乎使桓文之伯急於救患而失用兵之法則是
必長驅中原而宋鄭之患不可紓矣幸而不然彼江
黃楚之羽翼也桓則遠結盟之以孤其勢合八國伐
楚而楚遂求盟曹衞楚之黨與也文則私許復之以
携其心會四國戰楚而楚遂敗績不必勞師救鄭而
伐鄭之謀自罷不待分兵救宋而圍宋之役自解桓
punctuated:
乎？故取之以冠本房。
考試官教諭鄭批：斷桓、文、晉襄用兵得失，殆無餘蘊。
考試官學正王批：得胡傳之意。
外患迭加於大國，而伯主得安攘之道，可予；外患繼加於小國，而伯主失安攘之道，可譏。夫伯者之責，莫大乎攘夷安夏，而尤在乎用兵之有法也。《春秋》備書桓、文、晉襄攘楚之事，而得失見矣。何則？楚之始封，辟在荊山，篳路藍縷，以處草莽，桃弧棘矢，以共禦王事而已，豈意其暴橫憑陵如春秋之世耶？始也，怒鄭即齊，則興兵以伐鄭；繼也，怒宋從晉，則合兵以圍宋。夫宋、鄭大國，非附庸比也，楚人伐之，豈不恣暴橫以文偕行乎？使桓、文之伯，急於救患而失用兵之法，則是必長驅中原，而宋、鄭之患不可紓矣。幸而不然。彼江、黃，楚之羽翼也，桓則遠結盟之以孤其勢，合八國伐楚，而楚遂求盟；曹、衞，楚之黨與也，文則私許復之以携其心，會四國戰楚，而楚遂敗績。不必勞師救鄭，而伐鄭之謀自罷；不待分兵救宋，而圍宋之役自解。桓、
translation_en:
… [who is not thoroughly versed in the Classic of the Unicorn could be capable of] this? Therefore I have selected it to head the papers of my examination ward.
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: It judges the successes and failures of Dukes Huan and Wen and Duke Xiang of Jin in their use of military force, leaving almost nothing unexpressed.
Examiner Wang, Director of Studies, comments: It captures the meaning of Hu's Commentary.
When foreign aggression was repeatedly inflicted upon great states, and the hegemons grasped the way of pacifying the interior and repelling the exterior, they were worthy of praise; when foreign aggression was subsequently inflicted upon a small state, and the hegemon lost the way of pacifying the interior and repelling the exterior, he was worthy of criticism. Now, no responsibility of a hegemon is greater than repelling the barbarians and pacifying the Chinese states, and this lies above all in having a proper method in the use of military force. The Spring and Autumn Annals fully records the deeds of Duke Huan [of Qi], Duke Wen [of Jin], and Duke Xiang of Jin in repelling Chu, and their successes and failures are thereby revealed. Why is this? When Chu was first enfeoffed, it lay far off in the Jing Mountains, riding in wicker carts and wearing ragged clothes to dwell in the wild brush, with peach-wood bows and thorn arrows merely to join in defending the king's affairs. Who would have expected its violent arrogance and aggressive encroachment to become what they were in the Spring and Autumn period? At first, angered that Zheng had aligned with Qi, it raised troops to attack Zheng; subsequently, angered that Song had followed Jin, it combined forces to besiege Song. Now Song and Zheng were great states, not comparable to dependent statelets. When the men of Chu attacked them, did they not march forth in full force, indulging their violent arrogance [?]? Had Dukes Huan and Wen as hegemons been over-hasty in rescuing them from peril and lost the proper method of using military force, then [Chu] would surely have driven deep into the Central Plains, and the peril of Song and Zheng could not have been relieved. Fortunately, it was not so. Those states of Jiang and Huang were the wings of Chu; Duke Huan formed distant alliances with them to isolate Chu's power, and when he united eight states to attack Chu, Chu consequently sued for a covenant. Cao and Wei were the partisans of Chu; Duke Wen privately promised to restore them in order to divide their loyalties, and when he assembled four states to battle Chu, Chu consequently suffered a crushing defeat. Without needing to toil the army to rescue Zheng, the plot to attack Zheng ceased of itself; without waiting to divide the troops to rescue Song, the campaign besieging Song dissolved of itself. The achievements of Huan…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
文之功不其偉哉自是而後晉襄嗣伯楚復陸梁以
報沈之役興圍江之師夫江國小而弱非能與宋鄭
比也楚人圍之豈待徹四境屯戍守禦之眾與宿衛
盡行乎使晉襄能效桓文之為則楚必震恐而江圍
自解矣計不出此商臣之罪覆載不容也不能聲其
罪以致魯齊秦之兵天下莫強也不能用其兵以為
援乃遣處父之孤軍遠攻陸梁之強國門于方城而
止遇夫息公而還既無以挫楚人暴狠之鋒又無以
解江人倒懸之苦晉襄之失不亦大哉雖然以功利
===
言之則桓文襄之得失較然矣以道義論之伐楚之
役不請王命擅合諸侯豈天吏之伐歟城濮之戰伐
衛致楚陰謀取勝豈王者之事歟噫仲尼之徒無道
桓文之事其有以夫
禮記義
仁者右也道者左也仁者人也道者義也厚於
仁者薄於義親而不尊厚於義者薄於仁尊
而不親
霍峩
punctuated:
文之功，不其偉哉！自是而後，晉襄嗣伯，楚復陸梁，以報沈之役，興圍江之師。夫江，國小而弱，非能與宋、鄭比也。楚人圍之，豈待徹四境屯戍守禦之眾，與宿衛盡行乎？使晉襄能效桓、文之為，則楚必震恐，而江圍自解矣。計不出此：商臣之罪，覆載不容也，不能聲其罪以致魯；齊、秦之兵，天下莫強也，不能用其兵以為援。乃遣處父之孤軍，遠攻陸梁之強國，門于方城而止，遇夫息公而還。既無以挫楚人暴狠之鋒，又無以解江人倒懸之苦，晉襄之失，不亦大哉！雖然，以功利言之，則桓、文、襄之得失較然矣；以道義論之，伐楚之役，不請王命，擅合諸侯，豈天吏之伐歟？城濮之戰，伐衛致楚，陰謀取勝，豈王者之事歟？噫！仲尼之徒，無道桓、文之事，其有以夫！
禮記義
「仁者，右也；道者，左也。仁者，人也；道者，義也。厚於仁者薄於義，親而不尊；厚於義者薄於仁，尊而不親。」
霍峩
translation_en:
… [Were not] the achievements of [Duke Huan of Qi and Duke] Wen [of Jin] truly great? From this time onward, Duke Xiang of Jin succeeded as hegemon, and Chu once again grew unruly; to avenge the campaign against Shen, it raised an army to besiege Jiang. Now Jiang was a small and weak state, not comparable to Song or Zheng. When the men of Chu besieged it, did they need to withdraw all the garrison and defense forces from their four borders and march out with their entire palace guard? Had Duke Xiang of Jin been able to emulate the deeds of Dukes Huan and Wen, Chu would certainly have trembled in fear, and the siege of Jiang would have been lifted of its own accord. Yet his strategy did not come to this: the crime of Shangchen [of Chu, who murdered his father,] was something neither Heaven nor Earth could tolerate, yet he could not proclaim this crime to summon Lu; the armies of Qi and Qin were the strongest in the world, yet he could not employ their troops as support. Instead, he sent the isolated force of [Yang] Chufu to attack a powerful and unruly state from afar, going only so far as to assault the gates of Fangcheng and turning back upon encountering the Duke of Xi. Having neither the means to blunt the fierce and brutal edge of the men of Chu, nor the means to relieve the people of Jiang from their desperate plight, was not the failure of Duke Xiang of Jin great indeed? Even so, speaking in terms of utilitarian success, the merits and faults of Dukes Huan, Wen, and Xiang are obvious; but judging by moral principle, in the campaign to attack Chu, [Duke Huan] did not request the King's mandate and presumptuously assembled the feudal lords—how could that be the punitive expedition of a "minister of Heaven"? And in the Battle of Chengpu, [Duke Wen] attacked Wei to draw out Chu, using covert schemes to seize victory—how could that be the business of a true king? Alas! That the disciples of Confucius gave no account of the affairs of Dukes Huan and Wen—there was surely good reason for it!

Expositions on the Record of Rites (Liji)
"Benevolence is the right; the Way is the left. Benevolence is humanity; the Way is righteousness. One who is generous in benevolence but stinting in righteousness is affectionate yet not respected; one who is generous in righteousness but stinting in benevolence is respected yet not affectionate."
Huo E

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭蕭批此題似易而難場中作者多
泛而不切講貫詳明而於理
不失者僅見此篇是宜録出
考試官教諭鄭批此作以仁右道左通貫一篇之旨
最為切當
考試官學正王批辭理通貫
知仁道相資以為用當知仁義偏厚為有失盖仁也
道也義也並行而不相悖也然仁之與道既先後之
相資則夫仁義偏一又豈無所失哉今夫仁者人之
===
體也將有為也將有行也非仁則無以任重於先故
曰仁者右也以右者人所有事凡人之舉動必先之
也道者天之理也仁至于不可行不可節則理有所
不得已而為之輔故曰道者左也以左居不用之地
而助右之所不及也然是仁也非自外而至內也即
吾身所具之理而已故又曰仁者人也是道也非冥
行而妄作也即吾心制事之宜而已故又曰道者義
也道非仁不立義非人不行仁道相資為用如此則
仁義又豈可偏於一哉夫仁莫隆於父子父子之道
punctuated:
同考試官教諭蕭批：此題似易而難，場中作者多泛而不切，講貫詳明而於理不失者，僅見此篇，是宜録出。
考試官教諭鄭批：此作以仁右道左通貫一篇之旨，最為切當。
考試官學正王批：辭理通貫。
知仁道相資以為用，當知仁義偏厚為有失。盖仁也，道也，義也，並行而不相悖也。然仁之與道，既先後之相資，則夫仁義偏一，又豈無所失哉？今夫仁者，人之體也，將有為也，將有行也，非仁則無以任重於先，故曰：「仁者，右也。」以右者，人所有事，凡人之舉動必先之也。道者，天之理也，仁至于不可行、不可節，則理有所不得已而為之輔，故曰：「道者，左也。」以左居不用之地，而助右之所不及也。然是仁也，非自外而至內也，即吾身所具之理而已，故又曰：「仁者，人也。」是道也，非冥行而妄作也，即吾心制事之宜而已，故又曰：「道者，義也。」道非仁不立，義非人不行，仁道相資為用如此，則仁義又豈可偏於一哉？夫仁莫隆於父子，父子之道，
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Instructor Xiao's comment: This topic appears easy yet is difficult. Most writers in the examination hall were vague and off the mark; only in this essay do we see an exposition that is thorough, clear, and does not lose sight of principle. It ought to be selected for publication.
Examiner and Instructor Zheng's comment: This composition uses "benevolence as the right and the Way as the left" to thread through the thesis of the entire piece; it is most apt and fitting.
Examiner and Director of Studies Wang's comment: Its diction and reasoning are thoroughly coherent.
When one understands that benevolence and the Way rely on each other to function, one ought to understand that favoring either benevolence or righteousness at the expense of the other is a flaw. For benevolence, the Way, and righteousness operate in parallel without contradicting one another. Yet since benevolence and the Way mutually support each other in sequence, how could leaning one-sidedly toward either benevolence or righteousness be free of error? Now, benevolence is the substance of humanity. When one is about to act or about to proceed, without benevolence there is nothing to shoulder the weighty responsibility at the outset. Therefore it is said: "Benevolence is the right." This is because the right hand is what a person uses for action; in all human movements, it necessarily takes the lead. The Way is the principle of Heaven. When benevolence reaches a point where it cannot be carried out or cannot be regulated, then principle must of necessity act as its aid. Therefore it is said: "The Way is the left." This is because the left occupies the position of non-action, yet assists where the right cannot reach. However, this benevolence does not enter from the outside into the interior; it is simply the principle endowed in our own person. Therefore it is also said: "Benevolence is humanity." And this Way is not blind action or reckless behavior; it is simply the appropriateness with which our mind regulates affairs. Therefore it is also said: "The Way is righteousness." The Way is not established without benevolence, and righteousness is not practiced without the human person. Since benevolence and the Way rely on each other to function in this manner, how then could one lean one-sidedly toward either benevolence or righteousness? Now, benevolence is nowhere more exalted than between father and son, and the Way of father and son…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
親親也義莫重於君臣君臣之道尊尊也仁之與義
皆原於所降之衷初未嘗有厚薄之分也惟其不知
道左以輔乎仁則厚於仁者薄於義矣故知有其親
而不知有其尊焉義之與仁皆根於固有之性亦未
嘗有厚薄之間也惟其不知仁右以先乎義則厚於
義者薄於仁矣故知有其尊而不知有其親焉誠知
其所以為左右則尊尊親親並行不悖又豈有厚薄
也哉抑考表記一篇言仁義之道不一而足上文既
曰仁者天下之表也義者天下之制也下文又曰仁
===
有數義有長短小大合是而觀于以見仁義之用於
已者不同而其體之所存者無不同仁義之施於人
者雖殊而其理之相資者無或殊讀禮者宜深味之
一馬從二馬三馬既立請慶多馬
河津
同考試官教諭蕭批投壺一篇本房作者頗多
而於一馬二馬處俱欠發揮
此篇融會傳註組織成文故
表而出之
punctuated:
親親也；義莫重於君臣，君臣之道尊尊也。仁之與義，皆原於所降之衷，初未嘗有厚薄之分也。惟其不知道左以輔乎仁，則厚於仁者薄於義矣，故知有其親而不知有其尊焉。義之與仁，皆根於固有之性，亦未嘗有厚薄之間也。惟其不知仁右以先乎義，則厚於義者薄於仁矣，故知有其尊而不知有其親焉。誠知其所以為左右，則尊尊、親親並行不悖，又豈有厚薄也哉！抑考《表記》一篇，言仁義之道不一而足：上文既曰「仁者天下之表也，義者天下之制也」，下文又曰「仁有數，義有長短小大」。合是而觀，于以見仁義之用於已者不同，而其體之所存者無不同；仁義之施於人者雖殊，而其理之相資者無或殊。讀《禮》者宜深味之。

「一馬從二馬，三馬既立，請慶多馬。」
河津
同考試官教諭蕭批：投壺一篇，本房作者頗多，而於一馬、二馬處俱欠發揮。此篇融會傳註，組織成文，故表而出之。
translation_en:
…is affection for kin; nothing in righteousness is weightier than the relation of ruler and minister, and the Way of ruler and minister is reverence for the honorable. Benevolence and righteousness both originate in the moral sense conferred by Heaven; from the beginning, there has never been any distinction of thick or thin between them. It is only when one does not understand that the Way is like the left hand assisting benevolence that those who are thick in benevolence become thin in righteousness, and thus know only their kin without knowing the honorable. Righteousness and benevolence are both rooted in our inherent nature; there has likewise never been any gap of thick or thin between them. It is only when one does not understand that benevolence is like the right hand taking precedence over righteousness that those who are thick in righteousness become thin in benevolence, and thus know only the honorable without knowing their kin. If one truly understands why they act as left and right, then revering the honorable and loving one's kin will proceed together without conflict—how could there be any partiality of thick or thin! Furthermore, examining the single chapter Record on Example (Biaoji), its discussions of the Way of benevolence and righteousness are far from singular: the preceding passage already says, "Benevolence is the standard of the world; righteousness is the regulation of the world," and the following passage again says, "Benevolence has its degrees; righteousness has its long and short, small and great." Viewing these together, one may see that while the application of benevolence and righteousness in oneself differs, the substance in which they reside is never different; though the bestowal of benevolence and righteousness upon others varies, the principle by which they mutually support one another never varies. Readers of the Rites (Li) ought to savor this deeply.

"One horse-counter joins the two horse-counters. Now that the three horse-counters are set up, I beg to congratulate the one with more horse-counters."
He Jin
Comment by Associate Examiner and Confucian Instructor (jiaoyu) Xiao: Quite a few candidates in my examination ward wrote on the Pitch-Pot (Touhu) chapter, yet all lacked elaboration on the passage concerning the one horse-counter and two horse-counters. This essay thoroughly integrates the commentaries and annotations, weaving them into a coherent composition; therefore I have singled it out for distinction.

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭鄭批此作能發投壺立馬之意
必熟於禮者
考試官學正王批文有發揮
以少筭而附多筭得一成而宜舉賀此司射告賓之
辭也夫投壺立馬所以表勝司射告賓安得不詳致
其辭哉記禮者知其然謂夫燕飲非投壺則無以樂
賓投壺非立馬則無以表勝勝者立馬取筭以為馬
者所以表其勝之數也謂筭為馬者馬乃威武之用
投壺亦是習武故云馬也司射於此宜何如哉必告
===
之曰禮以三勝為成但勝偶未必專頻得三如四矢
順入正爵既行此一勝而立一馬者也故必以此一
馬從夫勝偶之二馬用以足乎三馬之數焉八筭俱
釋勝飲罍舉此再勝而立二馬者也故必取彼一馬
益乎在巳之二馬庸以備夫三馬之筭焉夫以一馬
從二馬則三馬於焉而立矣三馬既立是其勝已成
之時也馬之少者寧可以不之慶乎于以酌彼金罍
以慶夫多馬之人焉頻得三勝則三勝於焉而成矣
三勝既成是其禮垂畢之際也偶之劣者寧可以不
punctuated:
考試官教諭鄭批：此作能發投壺立馬之意，必熟於禮者。
考試官學正王批：文有發揮。
以少筭而附多筭，得一成而宜舉賀，此司射告賓之辭也。夫投壺立馬所以表勝，司射告賓安得不詳致其辭哉？記禮者知其然，謂夫燕飲非投壺則無以樂賓，投壺非立馬則無以表勝。勝者立馬，取筭以為馬者，所以表其勝之數也；謂筭為馬者，馬乃威武之用，投壺亦是習武，故云馬也。司射於此宜何如哉？必告之曰：禮以三勝為成，但勝偶未必專頻得三。如四矢順入，正爵既行，此一勝而立一馬者也，故必以此一馬從夫勝偶之二馬，用以足乎三馬之數焉；八筭俱釋，勝飲罍舉，此再勝而立二馬者也，故必取彼一馬益乎在巳之二馬，庸以備夫三馬之筭焉。夫以一馬從二馬，則三馬於焉而立矣。三馬既立，是其勝已成之時也，馬之少者寧可以不之慶乎？于以酌彼金罍，以慶夫多馬之人焉。頻得三勝，則三勝於焉而成矣。三勝既成，是其禮垂畢之際也，偶之劣者寧可以不

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zheng: "This composition succeeds in bringing out the meaning of setting up the 'horses' in the pitch-pot game; the author must be well-versed in the Rites."
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Wang: "The essay shows elaboration."
To attach the fewer tally-counters to the greater number of counters, and upon achieving a completed game to appropriately offer congratulations—these are the words with which the Master of Archery addresses the guests. Now, setting up the "horses" in the pitch-pot game (touhu) is the means of marking victories; how could the Master of Archery, in addressing the guests, fail to deliver his words in full detail? The recorder of the Rites understood this to be so, holding that at a banquet, without the pitch-pot game there is no way to entertain the guests, and in the pitch-pot game, without setting up "horses" there is no way to mark victories. When a winner sets up a "horse," taking a tally-counter to serve as a "horse" is the means to mark the number of his victories; as for calling the tally-counter a "horse," the horse is an instrument of martial might, and the pitch-pot game is likewise a practice of martial arts, which is why it is called a "horse." What, then, should the Master of Archery do at this point? He must announce to them, saying: "According to ritual, three victories constitute a completed game, yet the winning contestant does not necessarily win all three in succession by himself. For instance, when four arrows enter in order and the regular penalty cup has been circulated, this is a single victory for which one 'horse' is set up; therefore, one must take this one 'horse' and join it to the two 'horses' of the other winning contestant, thereby completing the number of three 'horses.' When all eight tally-counters have been laid down and the jar for the winner to give drink has been raised, this is a double victory for which two 'horses' are set up; therefore, one must take that one 'horse' and add it to the two 'horses' already in one's own possession, thereby fulfilling the count of three 'horses.'" Now, when one "horse" is joined to two "horses," the three "horses" are thereupon set up. Once the three "horses" have been set up, it is the moment when victory is complete; how could the one with fewer "horses" fail to congratulate the other? Thereupon he pours from that bronze jar to congratulate the person who had more "horses." And when someone wins three victories in succession, the three victories are thereupon completed. title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
□□乎于以稱彼兕觥以賀夫得勝之偶焉司射之
□□者如此豈特虚文而已哉大抵投壺射禮之細
乃男子之所有事者也故其舉行之間必貍首是歌
若夫是告欲其志正體直持之審固而後可以言中
也是則雖曰且以樂賓實則可以習容講藝而觀德
矣此先王所以不廢也歟
論
致治之法垂於萬世
王□
===
同考試官訓導郭批本房論幾三百卷求其詞理條
暢足以發題意者僅見是篇
同考試官教諭汪批立論於典實之中不騁浮辭
而意已獨至可羨可羨
考試官教諭鄭批議論典實能發聖人作經之□
考試官學正王批有發越
聖人有功於世道其大矣哉何也盖扶世立教
聖人之本心也使其達而在上則致治之迹固
著於有爲矣特其窮而在下故不得已於有言
punctuated:
□□乎？于以稱彼兕觥，以賀夫得勝之偶焉。司射之□□者如此，豈特虚文而已哉？大抵投壺，射禮之細，乃男子之所有事者也。故其舉行之間，必《貍首》是歌，「若夫」是告，欲其志正體直，持之審固，而後可以言中也是。則雖曰「且以樂賓」，實則可以習容、講藝而觀德矣。此先王所以不廢也歟！

論
致治之法垂於萬世
王□

同考試官訓導郭批：本房論幾三百卷，求其詞理條暢、足以發題意者，僅見是篇。
同考試官教諭汪批：立論於典實之中，不騁浮辭，而意已獨至，可羨，可羨！
考試官教諭鄭批：議論典實，能發聖人作經之□。
考試官學正王批：有發越。

聖人有功於世道，其大矣哉！何也？盖扶世立教，聖人之本心也。使其達而在上，則致治之迹固著於有爲矣；特其窮而在下，故不得已於有言，
translation_en:
… [congratulate] them? Therefore they raise that rhinoceros-horn goblet to congratulate the winning pair. What the Director of Archery (Sishe) [does/announces?] is like this—how could it merely be empty formality? On the whole, the pitch-pot game (touhu) is a minor form of the archery ritual, which is the proper business of men. Therefore, during its performance, the ode "Lishou" must be sung and the admonition beginning "Ruofu" announced, desiring that their intentions be upright and their bodies straight, holding the arrows with care and firmness, and only then can they speak of hitting the mark. Thus, although it is said to be "for the sementara entertainment of the guests," in reality it serves to practice deportment, cultivate skill, and observe virtue. Is this not why the former kings did not abolish it?

Discourse
The Methods for Achieving Good Order Handed Down for Ten Thousand Generations
Wang [illegible]

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Guo: Among the nearly three hundred discourse papers in my ward, in seeking one whose diction and reasoning are well-ordered and fluent enough to bring out the meaning of the theme, I have found only this piece.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Wang: It establishes its argument upon classical substance; without indulging in florid rhetoric, its meaning reaches a singular height. Admirable, admirable!
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zheng: The argument is classically grounded and substantial, able to bring out the [meaning/intent?] of the Sage in composing the Classics.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Wang: Possesses spirited elevation.

How great is the Sage's meritorious service to the Way of the world! Why is this so? Because to support the world and establish teachings is the fundamental mind of the Sage. Had he achieved eminence and occupied a position above, the traces of his bringing about good order would certainly have been manifested in active deeds; it was only because he was in distress and remained below that he had no choice but to speak,…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而致治之法垂於萬世實萬世之幸也聖人有
功於世道不既大乎盖嘗因是而論之天下之
生久矣或氣化有盛衰而人事之得失於是乎
生或人事有得失而氣化之盛衰於是乎轉治
亂相因理之常也聖人之生斯世亦惟撥亂而
歸治焉耳若吾夫子者正有心於行道濟時者
也假使其得邦家則綏来動和神妙不測而致
治之道行矣惜乎有德無位窮而在下所以作
春秋垂致治之法於萬世焉或者乃曰帝如堯
===
舜其德足以教天下致治之法垂於萬世宜矣
王而禹湯文武其功足以勸天下致治之法垂
於萬世似矣彼孔子也或絕粮於陳或見畏於
匡未嘗得志於當時也而致治之法安在或伐
木於衛或削迹於宋未嘗有土於當世也而致
治之法何有噫此以窮達論聖人也聖人果可
以窮達論哉聖人身雖窮而道則達也豈肯果
於忘世乎周室東遷王綱解紐人心不正甚矣
名分不明久矣人心不正治道之累也名分不
punctuated: 而致治之法垂於萬世，實萬世之幸也。聖人有功於世道，不既大乎！蓋嘗因是而論之：天下之生久矣，或氣化有盛衰，而人事之得失於是乎生；或人事有得失，而氣化之盛衰於是乎轉。治亂相因，理之常也。聖人之生斯世，亦惟撥亂而歸治焉耳。若吾夫子者，正有心於行道濟時者也。假使其得邦家，則綏來動和，神妙不測，而致治之道行矣。惜乎有德無位，窮而在下，所以作《春秋》，垂致治之法於萬世焉。或者乃曰：「帝如堯、舜，其德足以教天下，致治之法垂於萬世，宜矣；王而禹、湯、文、武，其功足以勸天下，致治之法垂於萬世，似矣。彼孔子也，或絕粮於陳，或見畏於匡，未嘗得志於當時也，而致治之法安在？或伐木於衛，或削迹於宋，未嘗有土於當世也，而致治之法何有？」噫！此以窮達論聖人也，聖人果可以窮達論哉？聖人身雖窮而道則達也，豈肯果於忘世乎？周室東遷，王綱解紐，人心不正甚矣，名分不明久矣。人心不正，治道之累也；名分不
translation_en: … and the model for bringing about order was handed down to ten thousand generations—this is truly the good fortune of ten thousand generations! Is not the sage's merit toward the moral order of the world great indeed? Let us discuss the matter on this basis: The world has existed for a long time. Sometimes the cosmic transformations of vital force wax and wane, and from this the successes and failures of human affairs arise; sometimes human affairs have successes and failures, and through this the waxing and waning of the cosmic transformations turn. Order and disorder follow upon one another; this is the constant norm of principle. When a sage is born into this world, his sole concern is simply to quell disorder and restore order. Someone like our Master was precisely one whose heart was set on putting the Way into practice and rescuing the age. Had he gained a state or a ruling house, he would have comforted the people so that they came to him, and moved them so that they became harmonious, with a wondrous subtlety beyond fathoming, and the Way of bringing about order would have prevailed. Alas, he possessed virtue but no position, and remained in obscurity below; therefore he composed the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) to hand down the model for bringing about order to ten thousand generations. Yet someone might say: "With emperors like Yao and Shun, their virtue was sufficient to instruct the world, so it is fitting that their model for bringing about order was handed down to ten thousand generations; with kings like Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, their achievements were sufficient to encourage the world, so it seems reasonable that their model for bringing about order was handed down to ten thousand generations. As for that Confucius, at times he ran out of provisions in Chen, and at times he was menaced at Kuang; he never realized his ambitions in his own time, so where is his model for bringing about order? At times he had the tree felled over him in Wei [?], and at times his footprints were wiped away in Song; he never possessed territory in his own age, so what model for bringing about order could he have?" Alas! This is to judge the sage in terms of adversity and success. Can a sage really be judged in terms of adversity and success? Though the sage's person was in adversity, his Way succeeded; how could he have been willing to resolutely forget the world? When the Zhou house moved east, the royal纲 (guiding cords of rule) came undone; human minds had become gravely unrighteous, and hierarchical obligations and statuses had long been obscured. When human minds are unrighteous, it is an impediment to the Way of governance; when hierarchical obligations and statuses are not…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
明治法之害也聖人天理之所在不以為已任
而誰可於是托南面之權行天子之事假魯史
以寓王法撥亂世反之正叙先後之倫秩上下
之分而惇典庸禮之法立有德者必褒有罪者
必貶而命德討罪之用行百王之法度在是萬
世之準繩在是所以遏人欲於横流存天理於
既滅使亂臣有所懼而不得售其奸賊子知所
警而不得肆其欲為後世慮也至深遠矣是以
由一世至於百世而致治之法昭然而莫掩由
===
百世至於萬世而致治之法秩然而不泯凡其
人心以正而無邪慝之患者人皆以為世之治
也而不知所以然者伊誰之功歟聖人致治之
法有以維持之也名分以明而無凌抗之失者
人咸以為世之治也而不知所以爾者伊誰之
力歟聖人致治之法有以軌範之也法垂於一
世即聖人道在於一世而有一世之功也法垂
於百世即聖人道在於百世而有百世之功也
致治之法垂於萬世則萬世即聖人之道也非
punctuated: 明，治法之害也。聖人，天理之所在，不以為已任而誰可？於是托南面之權，行天子之事，假魯史以寓王法，撥亂世反之正。叙先後之倫，秩上下之分，而惇典庸禮之法立；有德者必褒，有罪者必貶，而命德討罪之用行。百王之法度在是，萬世之準繩在是。所以遏人欲於横流，存天理於既滅，使亂臣有所懼而不得售其奸，賊子知所警而不得肆其欲，為後世慮也至深遠矣。是以由一世至於百世，而致治之法昭然而莫掩；由百世至於萬世，而致治之法秩然而不泯。凡其人心以正而無邪慝之患者，人皆以為世之治也，而不知所以然者伊誰之功歟？聖人致治之法有以維持之也。名分以明而無凌抗之失者，人咸以為世之治也，而不知所以爾者伊誰之力歟？聖人致治之法有以軌範之也。法垂於一世，即聖人道在於一世，而有一世之功也；法垂於百世，即聖人道在於百世，而有百世之功也。致治之法垂於萬世，則萬世即聖人之道也，非
translation_en: …clear is a harm to the laws of governance. The sage is the embodiment of Heavenly Principle; if he did not take this responsibility upon himself, then who could? Thereupon, assuming the authority of a south-facing monarch and performing the duties of the Son of Heaven, he borrowed the history of Lu to lodge the kingly law within it, bringing order out of a chaotic age and returning it to rectitude. He ordered the relationships of precedence and ranked the distinctions between superior and inferior, and thus the laws for honoring the constant norms and employing the rites were established; he inevitably praised those with virtue and censured those with guilt, and thus the functions of rewarding the virtuous and punishing the guilty were put into practice. Herein lie the institutions of a hundred kings; herein lies the standard for ten thousand generations. By this means he stemmed human desires in their rampant flow and preserved Heavenly Principle when it had nearly been extinguished, causing rebellious ministers to be afraid and unable to peddle their treachery, and bandit sons to know warning and be unable to indulge their desires—his concern for later generations was most profound and far-reaching. Therefore, from one generation to a hundred generations, the laws for bringing about order are luminous and cannot be obscured; from a hundred generations to ten thousand generations, the laws for bringing about order are orderly and cannot be obliterated. Whenever men's minds are rectified so that there is no affliction of evil and depravity, everyone considers it the orderliness of the age, yet they do not know whose achievement makes it so—it is that the sage's laws for bringing about order are there to uphold them. Whenever titles and statuses are made clear so that there is no fault of transgression or defiance, all consider it the orderliness of the age, yet they do not know whose strength makes it thus—it is that the sage's laws for bringing about order are there to serve as a model for them. When his laws are handed down to one generation, the Way of the sage abides in that one generation, and he has the achievement of one generation; when his laws are handed down to a hundred generations, the Way of the sage abides in those hundred generations, and he has the achievement of a hundred generations. Since his laws for bringing about order are handed down to ten thousand generations, then ten thousand generations are themselves the Way of the sage—is this not…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
有功於萬世乎故日月有時而薄蝕陰陽有時
而失行聖人致治之法萬世猶一日也山川有
時而騰沸陵谷有時而變遷聖人致治之法萬
古猶一時也彼絶粮見畏伐木削迹不過窮聖
人之身於一時耳焉能窮萬世致治之法乎聖
人有功於世道愈遠而愈不窮矣豈曰小補之
哉雖然孔子致治之法固垂於萬世矣然孟軻
氏之欲正人心息邪說距詖行放淫辭亦所以
開先聖致治之法而垂於萬世者也噫窮而在
===
下之聖賢固如此若達而在上之聖人則致治
見於有為如禹抑洪水周公兼夷狄驅猛獸是
已要之致治之迹與致治之法雖不同而同一
有功於世道也千載而下纘神禹之績紹周公
之功而尊崇孔子之道幸有我
朝
祖宗列聖與今日
聖天子在上
表
punctuated:
有功於萬世乎？故日月有時而薄蝕，陰陽有時而失行，聖人致治之法，萬世猶一日也；山川有時而騰沸，陵谷有時而變遷，聖人致治之法，萬古猶一時也。彼絶粮見畏、伐木削迹，不過窮聖人之身於一時耳，焉能窮萬世致治之法乎？聖人有功於世道，愈遠而愈不窮矣，豈曰小補之哉！雖然，孔子致治之法固垂於萬世矣，然孟軻氏之欲正人心、息邪說、距詖行、放淫辭，亦所以開先聖致治之法而垂於萬世者也。噫！窮而在下之聖賢固如此，若達而在上之聖人，則致治見於有為，如禹抑洪水、周公兼夷狄驅猛獸是已。要之，致治之迹與致治之法雖不同，而同一有功於世道也。千載而下，纘神禹之績，紹周公之功，而尊崇孔子之道，幸有我朝祖宗列聖與今日聖天子在上。

表
translation_en:
…a meritorious service to ten thousand generations? Therefore, though the sun and moon at times suffer eclipse and yin and yang at times lose their regular course, the sage's model for bringing about order remains across ten thousand generations as if it were a single day; though mountains and streams at times boil up and hills and valleys at times shift and change, the sage's model for bringing about order remains through all antiquity as if it were a single moment. Those episodes of running out of provisions, being threatened at Kuang, having the tree cut down in Song, and having his footprints erased in Wei merely reduced the sage's person to extremity for a brief moment—how could they exhaust his model for bringing about order for ten thousand generations? The sage's meritorious service to the Way of the world grows ever more inexhaustible the further it reaches in time; how could it be called a mere minor help! Even so, while the model of Confucius (Kongzi 孔子) for bringing about order has indeed been handed down to ten thousand generations, Mencius's (Meng Ke 孟軻) desire to rectify human minds, put an end to perverse doctrines, oppose one-sided deeds, and banish licentious speech was likewise a means of elucidating the former sage's model for bringing about order and handing it down to ten thousand generations. Alas! Sages and worthies who were in adversity and in low station were certainly like this; as for sages who achieved eminence and occupied high station, their bringing about of order was manifested in active accomplishments—such as Yu 禹 repressing the floodwaters, and the Duke of Zhou (Zhougong 周公) absorbing the Yi and Di tribes and driving away wild beasts. In sum, although the visible traces of bringing about order and the model for bringing about order are different, they are one and the same in having meritorious service toward the Way of the world. A thousand years later, in continuing the achievements of the divine Yu, carrying on the merits of the Duke of Zhou, and revering the Way of Confucius, we are fortunate to have the successive sage ancestors of our dynasty and today's Sacred Son of Heaven reigning above.

Memorial (Biao 表)

伏以道配乾坤，世際皇風之清穆；星聯奎璧，時逢文運之昌隆。澤霈清班，歡騰善類。共惟○○○○，聰明睿哲，恭儉寛仁。好察邇言，有虞舜之智；克艱厥后，躬大禹之勤。歌九叙、勸九功，黎元安養；闢四門、明四目，賢俊登庸。臣溱等秉性凡愚，賦才疎薄。粗知儒術，學不逮于古人；偶擢賢科，名有慚於進士。叨賜瓊林之宴，載頒《大學》之篇。寵渥駢臻，戰兢交集。際風雲之慶會，依
translation_en:
Imitating a Song-Dynasty Memorial of Thanks for Bestowing upon the Metropolitan Graduates Lü Zhen 呂溱 and Others the Qionglin Banquet and the Text of the Great Learning (Daxue)

Comment by Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Lin 林: "Classically grounded, substantive, and appropriate in style."
Comment by Examiner and County Director of Studies Zheng 鄭: "Captures the style of a Song-dynasty memorial."
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang 王: "Exemplary and well worth reading."

We humbly reflect: When the Way matches Heaven and Earth, the age encounters the pure serenity of the August Wind; when the stars align in the Kui and Bi constellations, the era meets with the flourishing prosperity of literary fortune. Imperial grace showers upon the pure ranks of officials, and joy surges among good men. We reverently think of [Your Majesty] ○○○○, intelligent, perspicacious, and wise, reverent, frugal, magnanimous, and benevolent. Delighting in examining near words, You possess the wisdom of Yu Shun 虞舜; able to recognize the difficulties of sovereign rule, You personally practice the diligence of Great Yu 大禹. Singing of the nine orders and encouraging with the nine songs of merit, the common people are peacefully nourished; throwing open the four gates and making clear the four eyes, the worthy and eminent are elevated and employed. Your servants Zhen and others are endowed with ordinary and foolish natures, and gifted with meager and shallow talents. Though roughly acquainted with Confucian arts, our learning does not reach that of the ancients; having chanced to be selected in the examination for the worthy, we feel ashamed to bear the title of metropolitan graduate (jinshi). Unworthily we have been bestowed the banquet at the Qionglin Garden, and further granted the text of the Great Learning. As rich favors arrive side by side, trembling and awe mingle within us.
