title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
日月之光華臣敢不益究厥心益精于業効涓埃
而圖補念夙夜以惟寅明德新民期多士聿崇
乎正學
敬
天法祖願萬年永保乎
丕基臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉表稱
謝以
===
聞
策
第一問
同考試官教諭陳批五策筆勢滔滔此篇敷答尤詳
必有學之士也
考試官教諭鄭批敷答昭代立教之意詳明可嘉
考試官學正王批條答詳明
聖賢講學於下欲正綱常之道必立言以發後
punctuated:
日月之光華。臣敢不益究厥心，益精于業，効涓埃而圖補，念夙夜以惟寅？明德新民，期多士聿崇乎正學；敬天法祖，願萬年永保乎丕基。臣無任瞻天仰聖，激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

策
第一問
同考試官教諭陳批：五策筆勢滔滔，此篇敷答尤詳，必有學之士也。
考試官教諭鄭批：敷答昭代立教之意，詳明可嘉。
考試官學正王批：條答詳明。

聖賢講學於下，欲正綱常之道，必立言以發後
translation_en:
… [leaning upon] the glorious radiance of the sun and moon. How could your servant dare not to examine his mind even more deeply and refine his studies even further, offering a tiny drop or speck of dust in hopes of making some small contribution, and keeping reverent mindfulness from dawn till night? In manifesting luminous virtue and renewing the people, we hope that the multitude of scholars will venerate orthodox learning; in revering Heaven and emulating the Ancestors, we pray that for ten thousand years the great foundation of the dynasty will be forever preserved. Your servant is overcome with the utmost emotion and trepidation as he gazes up toward Heaven and looks up to Your Sacred Majesty, and respectfully presents this memorial of gratitude for Your Majesty's hearing.

Policy Essays
First Question
Associate Examiner and Instructor Chen comments: The brushwork across all five policy essays flows like a torrent, and the exposition in this answer is especially detailed; he must certainly be a scholar of true learning.
Examiner and Instructor Zheng comments: His exposition of the intent behind the educational institutions established by our illustrious dynasty is detailed, clear, and commendable.
Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang comments: His point-by-point response is detailed and clear.

When sages and worthies expound upon learning from below, wishing to rectify the Way of the three bonds and five constant virtues, they necessarily establish words to enlighten later…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
世
聖皇建極於上欲盡君師之責必敷言以教當世焉
聖賢立教不外乎明倫理以正綱常別善惡而
備勸戒也肆孔子之作春秋朱子之集小學暨
我
朝
列聖之頒誥布書何莫而非聖賢立言垂世之法皇
極敷言教民之理歟昔孔子生周衰之時承堯
舜禹湯文武之統集群聖之大成雖刪詩書定
===
禮樂賛周易而載諸行事則莫大於春秋也其
載君臣行事如宰咺歸賵則書名子突救衛則
書字美齊桓服楚而譏其專予晉文之奬王而
著其譎固美惡備載矣朱子生有宋之時紹周
程張邵之傳而集諸儒之大成雖集詩傳著易
本義註釋學庸論孟諸書而教人之法莫先於
小學也其述嘉言善行顏孟之可學杜季良之
不可效高允以直見旌翟黑子以欺獲誅之類
亦勸戒兼備矣洪惟我
punctuated: 世；聖皇建極於上，欲盡君師之責，必敷言以教當世焉。聖賢立教，不外乎明倫理以正綱常，別善惡而備勸戒也。肆孔子之作《春秋》、朱子之集《小學》，暨我朝列聖之頒誥布書，何莫而非聖賢立言垂世之法、皇極敷言教民之理歟？昔孔子生周衰之時，承堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之統，集群聖之大成，雖刪《詩》、《書》，定《禮》、《樂》，賛《周易》，而載諸行事，則莫大於《春秋》也。其載君臣行事，如宰咺歸賵則書名，子突救衛則書字；美齊桓服楚而譏其專，予晉文之奬王而著其譎，固美惡備載矣。朱子生有宋之時，紹周、程、張、邵之傳，而集諸儒之大成，雖集《詩傳》，著《易本義》，註釋《學》、《庸》、《論》、《孟》諸書，而教人之法，莫先於《小學》也。其述嘉言善行，顏、孟之可學，杜季良之不可效，高允以直見旌，翟黑子以欺獲誅之類，亦勸戒兼備矣。洪惟我
translation_en:
…later generations; when sacred sovereigns establish the supreme standard from above, wishing to fulfill the duties of ruler and teacher, they must set forth words to instruct the present age. The teachings established by sages and worthies consist in nothing other than clarifying human relationships to rectify the cardinal principles and constant virtues, and distinguishing good from evil to provide both encouragement and warning. Thus, Confucius's authoring of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), Master Zhu's [Zhu Xi 朱熹] compiling of the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue), and the promulgating of grand pronouncements and distributing of books by the successive sacred emperors of our dynasty—how could any of these be anything other than the sages' and worthies' model of establishing words to be handed down to future generations, and the supreme standard's principle of setting forth words to instruct the people?

In antiquity, Confucius was born in the era of the Zhou dynasty's decline. Carrying on the tradition of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu, he brought together the great achievements of all the sages. Although he edited the Odes (Shi) and the Documents (Shu), fixed the Rites (Li) and Music (Yue), and wrote commentaries on the Changes of Zhou (Zhouyi), when it came to manifesting principles in actual deeds, nothing was greater than the Spring and Autumn Annals. In its recording of the deeds of rulers and ministers—such as writing the personal name when Administrator Xuan (Zai Xuan 宰咺) brought funerary gifts, or writing the courtesy name when Zitu 子突 rescued Wei; praising Duke Huan of Qi (Qi Huan 齊桓) for subduing Chu while criticizing his arbitrariness, or approving Duke Wen of Jin's (Jin Wen 晉文) aiding the King while exposing his craftiness—both the admirable and the reprehensible were indeed fully recorded.

Master Zhu was born during the Song dynasty. Continuing the transmission of Zhou [Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤], the Chengs [Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤], Zhang [Zhang Zai 張載], and Shao [Shao Yong 邵雍], he brought together the great achievements of all the Confucian scholars. Although he compiled the Transmission of the Odes (Shizhuan), authored the Original Meaning of the Changes (Yi benyi), and annotated the Great Learning (Daxue), the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), the Analects (Lunyu), the Mencius (Mengzi), and other books, as a method for instructing people, nothing took precedence over the Elementary Learning. In its recounting of admirable words and good deeds—such as how Yan [Yan Hui 顏回] and Meng [Mencius] should be emulated, how Du Jiliang 杜季良 should not be imitated, how Gao Yun 高允 was honored for his uprightness, and how Zhai Heizi 翟黑子 was executed for his deceit—encouragement and warning were likewise both fully provided.

Reflecting deeply upon our…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝臨御之日尊崇聖道表章儒書嘗
頒大誥三編具載李子安余仁三之徒奸貪兇頑
之罪無所示勸盖當時勸善之典功臣賢相有
誥券制勅之褒孝順節義有旌表門閭之
詔皆誥所未載也
太宗文皇帝為善陰隲書首蔣王靈應終周婦感悟
孝順事實書首虞舜大孝終劉婦孝姑備載古
今善孝之實而無所示戒盖當時際
重熙累洽之運四海被仁漸義摩之化既歷三紀
===
世變風移之時臣民皆知勸善故示戒之事皆
書所不錄也逮乎
宣宗章皇帝五倫書采輯古今嘉言善行有關於君
臣父子夫婦兄弟朋友之道者雖詳略不同其
義即小學明倫篇五倫之事也而春秋隱公元
年不書即位以正父子君臣之倫書公及邾儀
父盟于蔑鄭伯克段于鄢天王使宰咺來歸惠
公仲子之賵以正朋友兄弟夫婦之倫者其明
綱常之義寧有殊乎為善陰隲孝順事實所采
punctuated: 太祖高皇帝臨御之日，尊崇聖道，表章儒書，嘗頒《大誥》三編，具載李子安、余仁三之徒奸貪兇頑之罪，無所示勸。盖當時勸善之典，功臣賢相有誥券制勅之褒，孝順節義有旌表門閭之詔，皆《誥》所未載也。太宗文皇帝《為善陰隲書》首「蔣王靈應」，終「周婦感悟」；《孝順事實書》首「虞舜大孝」，終「劉婦孝姑」，備載古今善孝之實，而無所示戒。盖當時際重熙累洽之運，四海被仁漸義摩之化，既歷三紀，世變風移之時，臣民皆知勸善，故示戒之事，皆書所不錄也。逮乎宣宗章皇帝《五倫書》，采輯古今嘉言善行有關於君臣、父子、夫婦、兄弟、朋友之道者，雖詳略不同，其義即《小學》〈明倫篇〉五倫之事也。而《春秋》隱公不書即位，以正父子、君臣之倫；書「公及邾儀父盟于蔑」、「鄭伯克段于鄢」、「天王使宰咺來歸惠公仲子之賵」，以正朋友、兄弟、夫婦之倫者，其明綱常之義，寧有殊乎？《為善陰隲》、《孝順事實》所采
translation_en: …In the days when Emperor Gao, the Grand Progenitor (Taizu), reigned, he revered the Way of the Sages and honored the books of the Confucians. He once promulgated the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao), which recorded in full the treacherous, greedy, vicious, and obstinate crimes of such men as Li Zi'an 李子安 and Yu Rensan 余仁三, without presenting anything by way of encouragement. This was because in the canons for encouraging goodness at that time, meritorious ministers and worthy grand councilors received the praise of patents of investiture, iron tallies, imperial decrees, and commands, while the filial, obedient, chaste, and righteous received imperial edicts honoring their family gates—none of which were included in the Pronouncements. Emperor Wen, the Grand Ancestor (Taizong), in his Book of the Unseen Rewards of Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi shu), began with "The Numinous Response of Prince Jiang" and ended with "The Awakening of the Wife of Zhou"; in his Book of True Accounts of Filial Piety and Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi shu), he began with "The Great Filial Piety of Shun of Yu" and ended with "The Wife of Liu's Filial Piety Toward Her Mother-in-law," fully recording true accounts of goodness and filial piety from antiquity to the present, yet without presenting anything by way of warning. This was because that era met with a destiny of successive splendor and cumulative harmony, when the Four Seas had been bathed in the transforming influence of benevolence and righteousness for three twelve-year cycles (thirty-six years); at a time when the world had changed and customs had shifted, officials and commoners alike knew to encourage goodness, and thus matters meant as warnings were omitted from these books. Coming down to the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu) of Emperor Zhang, the Proclaiming Ancestor (Xuanzong), it compiled fine words and good deeds from antiquity to the present concerning the ways of ruler and minister, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger brother, and friends. Although varying in degree of detail, its meaning is none other than the matters of the five human relationships in the "Elucidating Human Relationships" ("Minglun") section of the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue). And when the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) in the first year of Duke Yin does not record his accession to the throne in order to rectify the relationships of father and son and of ruler and minister; and when it records "The Duke and Yifu of Zhu made a covenant at Mie," "The Earl of Zheng overcame Duan at Yan," and "The Heavenly King sent the Administrator Xuan to come and present funerary gifts for Duke Hui and Zhongzi" in order to rectify the relationships of friends, of elder and younger brother, and of husband and wife—how could its meaning in elucidating the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues be any different? What the Unseen Rewards of Doing Good and the True Accounts of Filial Piety and Obedience selected…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
陰德行孝之人雖多寡不一其事即春秋傳魏
顆從治考叔遺羹之類也而小學所稱叔敖黃
香劉寬之徒所紀虞舜文武之聖曾閔子路之
賢者其善孝之實寧有異乎嗟夫孔子朱子窮
而在下立言垂世既以正綱常備勸戒為要
祖宗列聖達而在上建極敷言亦以正綱常備勸戒
為急是可見千聖一心萬古一理而脩道之教
先聖後聖其揆一也愚生被
樂育之恩躬誦習之勤謹因明問所及略舉以對
===
惟執事進教之幸甚
第二問
鄧應仁
同考試官教諭林批書卷三百餘求其三場勻稱者
少茲卷前二場既優五策俱佳而
此策尤詳明取置魁選允恊輿情
考試官教諭鄭批此策善得聖人處事化人之方非
有學識者不能
考試官學正王批允稱前場
punctuated:
陰德行孝之人，雖多寡不一，其事即《春秋傳》魏顆從治、考叔遺羹之類也；而《小學》所稱叔敖、黃香、劉寬之徒，所紀虞舜、文、武之聖，曾、閔、子路之賢者，其善孝之實寧有異乎？嗟夫！孔子、朱子窮而在下，立言垂世，既以正綱常、備勸戒為要；祖宗列聖達而在上，建極敷言，亦以正綱常、備勸戒為急。是可見千聖一心，萬古一理，而脩道之教，先聖後聖，其揆一也。愚生被樂育之恩，躬誦習之勤，謹因明問所及，略舉以對，惟執事進教之，幸甚。

第二問
鄧應仁
同考試官教諭林批：書卷三百餘，求其三場勻稱者少。茲卷前二場既優，五策俱佳，而此策尤詳明。取置魁選，允恊輿情。
考試官教諭鄭批：此策善得聖人處事化人之方，非有學識者不能。
考試官學正王批：允稱前場。
translation_en:
… those who accumulated secret virtue or practiced filial piety, although the number of examples varies, the deeds themselves are of the same kind as those in the Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu zhuan), such as Wei Ke following his father's lucid instructions and Ying Kaoshu setting aside soup for his mother; and compared to those praised in the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue) such as Sun Shu'ao, Huang Xiang, and Liu Kuan, or its accounts of the sages Yu Shun, King Wen, and King Wu, and the worthies Zengzi, Min Ziqian, and Zilu—how could the substance of their goodness and filiality be any different? Alas! Confucius and Master Zhu, when in obscurity and occupying lowly stations, established teachings to pass down to future generations, taking the rectification of the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues and the provision of exhortations and warnings as their essential aim; the successive sage emperors of our imperial ancestors, when in prominence and occupying the throne on high, established the supreme standard and set forth their teachings, likewise taking the rectification of the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues and the provision of exhortations and warnings as their urgent priority. From this it can be seen that a thousand sages share a single mind, ten thousand ages share a single principle, and in the instruction that cultivates the Way, the standards of former sages and later sages are one and the same. I, a foolish student, having received the grace of being nurtured and educated, and having personally devoted myself to diligent recitation and study, respectfully cite these brief points in response to what Your Excellency's clear question has touched upon. I only pray that Your Excellency will deign to instruct me further; I would be most fortunate.

Second Question
Deng Yingren
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Lin: Among the more than three hundred scripts on the Book of Documents, few are evenly balanced across all three sessions. In this paper, the first two sessions are already excellent, and all five policy essays are fine, with this essay being especially detailed and clear. Selecting him to be placed among the top ranks truly accords with public sentiment.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zheng: This policy essay aptly grasps the sages' methods for handling affairs and transforming people; none without learning and insight could have written it.
Comment by Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang: Truly matches the quality of his earlier sessions.

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天下之事常變不一也聖人處之惟一理天下
之人賢否不齊也聖人感之惟一心夫理乎
其聖人處事之要乎至哉心乎其聖人感人之
本乎知此則可復明問之萬一矣夫聖如帝堯
胤子丹朱囂訟不肖而用殄厥世聖如大禹父
鯀治水悻戾自用而汨陳五行此父子之變事
之難處者也堯乃不傳位於子而傳於舜遂使
授受得中而天下治平禹乃三過其門不入而
脩鯀之功遂使六府孔脩而萬世永賴蓋當禪
===
則禪當脩則脩允執厥中理之常也成湯當有
夏季世萬方百姓並告無辜武王當有商季世
百姓有過在予一人此君臣之變事之難處者
也湯乃興鳴條之師而為放桀之舉由是代虐
以寬而兆民允懷武乃因諸侯之會而為牧野
之誓由是大賚四海而萬姓悅服蓋當放則放
當伐則伐順天應人理之正也周公位冢宰正
百官群叔流言欲以間王室也而公避位居東
赤舄几几德音不瑕後因風雷之變成王遂感
punctuated:
天下之事，常變不一也，聖人處之惟一理；天下之人，賢否不齊也，聖人感之惟一心。夫理乎，其聖人處事之要乎！至哉心乎，其聖人感人之本乎！知此，則可復明問之萬一矣。

夫聖如帝堯，胤子丹朱囂訟不肖，而用殄厥世；聖如大禹，父鯀治水悻戾自用，而汨陳五行。此父子之變，事之難處者也。堯乃不傳位於子而傳於舜，遂使授受得中而天下治平；禹乃三過其門不入而脩鯀之功，遂使六府孔脩而萬世永賴。蓋當禪則禪，當脩則脩，允執厥中，理之常也。成湯當有夏季世，萬方百姓並告無辜；武王當有商季世，百姓有過，在予一人。此君臣之變，事之難處者也。湯乃興鳴條之師，而為放桀之舉，由是代虐以寬，而兆民允懷；武乃因諸侯之會，而為牧野之誓，由是大賚四海，而萬姓悅服。蓋當放則放，當伐則伐，順天應人，理之正也。周公位冢宰，正百官，群叔流言，欲以間王室也。而公避位居東，赤舄几几，德音不瑕，後因風雷之變，成王遂感
translation_en:
In the affairs of the world, normal and anomalous circumstances are not uniform, yet the sage handles them with a single principle; among the people of the world, the worthy and the unworthy are not alike, yet the sage moves them with a single mind. Ah, principle—is it not the essential key by which the sage handles affairs! Supreme indeed is the mind—is it not the fundamental root by which the sage moves people! Understanding this, one may reply to a ten-thousandth part of this sagely inquiry.

Now, for all the sageliness of Emperor Yao, his heir Danzhu was quarrelsome and unworthy, thereby bringing ruin upon his line; for all the sageliness of the Great Yu, his father Gun, in controlling the floods, was perverse and self-willed, throwing the Five Phases into disorder. These were anomalies between father and son, affairs that were difficult to handle. Yao thereupon did not transmit the throne to his son, but transmitted it to Shun, thus causing the giving and receiving of the throne to attain the mean and the world to be well-governed and at peace. Yu thereupon passed his own door three times without entering in order to carry forward Gun's work, thus causing the Six Treasuries to be thoroughly regulated and ten thousand generations to rely upon them forever. Indeed, yielding the throne when it was proper to yield, and carrying forward the work when it was proper to carry it forward, sincerely holding fast the Mean—this is the constancy of principle.

Cheng Tang lived in the final age of the Xia, when the common people of the myriad regions all cried out in their innocence; King Wu lived in the final age of the Shang, declaring that if the common people had faults, it rested upon him, the One Man, alone. These were anomalies between ruler and minister, affairs that were difficult to handle. Tang thereupon raised the army at Mingtiao and undertook the banishment of Jie, thereby replacing tyranny with leniency so that the millions of people truly cherished him; Wu thereupon availed himself of the assembly of the feudal lords and made the oath at Muye, thereby bestowing great largesse throughout the four seas so that the myriad surnames gladly submitted. Indeed, banishing when it was proper to banish, and launching a punitive expedition when it was proper to launch a punitive expedition, acting in accordance with Heaven and in response to men—this is the rectitude of principle.

The Duke of Zhou held the position of Premier and rectified the hundred officials, yet his younger brothers spread rumors, seeking to sow dissension in the royal house. The Duke stepped aside from his post and dwelt in the east; with his red slippers calm and composed, his virtuous reputation remained unblemished. Later, because of the portents of wind and thunder, King Cheng was moved to…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
悟而出郊以迎之孔子相定公會齊侯于夾谷
齊人鼓譟而起欲以劫魯君也而孔子俘不干
盟兵不偪好之言威重於三軍齊遂知罪而歸
三田以謝之處變而無疑懼知禮而却萊兵亦
惟順乎理耳此皆聖人處事之實也至若父頑
母嚚象敖勢若難化矣而卒致不格姦亦允若
者由舜之心純乎誠孝之至然也侮慢自賢嚚
固不服跡若難格矣而卒致三苗丕叙七旬來
格者由舜禹之心不尚威武專施德教然也太
===
甲嗣位欲敗度縱敗禮其失若習與性成也伊
尹營于桐宫居憂三年而遂致克終允德成王
幼冲弗造哲迪民康其性非卓然高明也周公
作無逸陳王業以訓告之而遂致教化大行盖
伊周之心拳拳忠愛者有以感之曾子子貢之
在聖門或質魯或貨殖賦性用心之偏者也聖
人甞語之使知自勵由是曾子随事精察之久
子貢博學多識之積卒聞一以貫之之道焉太
師亞飯之為樂官或樂官之長或以樂侑食亦
punctuated: 悟，而出郊以迎之。孔子相定公會齊侯于夾谷，齊人鼓譟而起，欲以劫魯君也，而孔子「俘不干盟，兵不偪好」之言，威重於三軍，齊遂知罪，而歸三田以謝之。處變而無疑懼，知禮而却萊兵，亦惟順乎理耳。此皆聖人處事之實也。至若父頑、母嚚、象敖，勢若難化矣，而卒致「不格姦，亦允若」者，由舜之心純乎誠孝之至然也。侮慢自賢，嚚固不服，跡若難格矣，而卒致「三苗丕叙，七旬來格」者，由舜、禹之心不尚威武，專施德教然也。太甲嗣位，欲敗度，縱敗禮，其失若「習與性成」也；伊尹營于桐宫，居憂三年，而遂致「克終允德」。成王幼冲，弗造哲迪民康，其性非卓然高明也；周公作《無逸》，陳王業以訓告之，而遂致教化大行。盖伊、周之心拳拳忠愛者，有以感之。曾子、子貢之在聖門，或質魯，或貨殖，賦性用心之偏者也；聖人甞語之，使知自勵，由是曾子随事精察之久，子貢博學多識之積，卒聞「一以貫之」之道焉。太師、亞飯之為樂官，或樂官之長，或以樂侑食，亦
translation_en:
… came to understand, and went out to the suburbs to welcome him back. When Confucius (Kongzi 孔子) assisted Duke Ding (Ding Gong 定公) at the meeting with the Marquis of Qi (Qi Hou 齊侯) at Jiagu 夾谷, the men of Qi rose up beating drums and shouting in an attempt to seize the ruler of Lu 魯; yet Confucius's words—that "captives do not interfere with covenants, and weapons do not press upon friendly relations"—carried greater awe and weight than the Three Armies, so that Qi recognized its fault and returned the three tracts of land by way of apology. Facing crisis without doubt or fear, and repelling the troops of Lai 萊 through knowledge of ritual propriety, both came simply from following principle. All these are the actual facts of how the sages handled affairs.

As for having an obstinate father, a deceitful mother, and an arrogant brother Xiang 象, the situation seemed difficult to transform; yet that it ultimately resulted in "their not arriving at wickedness, and also being truly harmonious" was because Shun's 舜 mind was purely of the utmost sincere filiality. Being insolent, self-conceited, and stubbornly unsubmissive, their conduct seemed difficult to win over; yet that it ultimately resulted in "the Sanmiao 三苗 being brought into great order" and "coming to submit within seventy days" was because the minds of Shun and Yu 禹 did not prize martial force, but exclusively applied moral instruction. When Tai Jia 太甲 succeeded to the throne, he ruined the norms through his desires and ruined ritual propriety through his self-indulgence, his failings seeming as though "habit had become second nature"; Yi Yin 伊尹 built a palace at Tong 桐, where Tai Jia dwelt in mourning for three years, and thus brought about his "being able in the end to have sincere virtue." When King Cheng (Cheng Wang 成王) was young and immature, not yet having attained the wisdom to guide the people to peace, his nature was not outstandingly brilliant; the Duke of Zhou (Zhou Gong 周公) composed "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi 無逸), setting forth the royal enterprise to instruct and admonish him, and thus brought about the great prevalence of moral transformation. This was because the earnestly loyal and loving minds of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou had the means to move them.

When Master Zeng (Zengzi 曾子) and Zigong 子貢 were at the Sage's gate, the one was dull by temperament and the other engaged in accumulating wealth—both having biases in their endowed natures or the application of their minds. The Sage spoke to them so that they knew how to exert themselves; hence, after Master Zeng had long examined things precisely as they arose, and after Zigong had accumulated broad learning and much knowledge, both finally heard the Way of "one thread binding it all together." As for the Grand Music Master (Taishi 太師) and the Musician of the Second Meal (Yafan 亞飯) serving as music officials—whether as chief of the music officials or as one who accompanied meals with music—they too were…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
人典是職者也聖人自衛反魯而正樂由是伶
人賤工識樂之正皆知逾河蹈海以去焉盖聖
人之心同乎天地者有以化之此皆聖人感人
之由也雖然事無不可為者以其有此理人無
不可化者以其同此心聖人窮理盡性而廓然
大公故無不可為之事無不可化之人也學者
取法聖人當自存心觀理始管見如斯未知是
否姑此以塞明問
第三問
===
蕭鍋
同考試官訓導郭批人望一策塲中答者多無事
實此作條答無遺是宜録出
同考試官教諭汪批此策随問随答畧無凝滯其
達於時務者歟
考試官教諭鄭批有考據有斷制策塲中之優者
考試官學正王批區處用人望在審衆論甚當
治天下之大要在乎收人望收人望之大幾在
乎審衆論盖人望不收則治功不成人望不審
punctuated:
人典是職者也。聖人自衛反魯而正樂，由是伶人賤工，識樂之正，皆知逾河蹈海以去焉。盖聖人之心同乎天地者，有以化之。此皆聖人感人之由也。雖然，事無不可為者，以其有此理；人無不可化者，以其同此心。聖人窮理盡性而廓然大公，故無不可為之事，無不可化之人也。學者取法聖人，當自存心觀理始。管見如斯，未知是否，姑此以塞明問。

第三問
蕭鍋
同考試官訓導郭批：人望一策，塲中答者多無事實，此作條答無遺，是宜録出。
同考試官教諭汪批：此策随問随答，畧無凝滯，其達於時務者歟！
考試官教諭鄭批：有考據，有斷制，策塲中之優者。
考試官學正王批：區處用人望在審衆論，甚當。

治天下之大要在乎收人望，收人望之大幾在乎審衆論。盖人望不收則治功不成，人望不審
translation_en:
… men who held those offices. When the Sage returned from Wei to Lu and rectified the music, even lowly musicians and humble artisans came to understand the correctness of music, and all knew enough to cross the Yellow River or take to the sea to depart. This is because the mind of the Sage, being one with Heaven and Earth, had the power to transform them. All of these are the reasons why the sages were able to move people. Even so, there is no affair that cannot be accomplished, because this principle exists within it; there is no person who cannot be transformed, because they share this same mind. The sages exhaustively investigated principles, fully realized their nature, and were broad-minded and utterly impartial; therefore, for them there was no affair that could not be accomplished and no person who could not be transformed. For scholars who take the sages as their model, they must begin by preserving the mind and observing principles. My narrow view is such as this; I do not know whether it is correct, and tentatively offer this to fulfill your sagacious question.

The Third Question
Xiao Guo 蕭鍋
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Guo 郭 comments: For the policy question on men of popular esteem, most respondents in the examination hall lacked factual substance, whereas this composition answers item by item without omission; it is fitting to record and publish it.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Wang 汪 comments: This policy essay answers each question as it is posed, without the slightest hesitation or obstruction—truly one who understands current affairs!
Examiner and Instructor Zheng 鄭 comments: Well-grounded in evidence and decisive in judgment; an outstanding piece among the policy essays in the examination hall.
Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang 王 comments: Its arrangement of how to employ men of popular esteem rests upon examining public opinion, which is most appropriate.

The great essential in governing the empire lies in gathering men of popular esteem, and the crucial pivot in gathering men of popular esteem lies in examining public opinion. For if men of popular esteem are not gathered, the achievements of governance cannot be completed; if men of popular esteem are not carefully examined…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則賢否雜進能審眾論以收人望則治天下之
大要豈有加於此哉且士君子以一身之微繫
天下之觀望大矣因其人望而用之是所謂以
民治民以天下治天下何往而不濟何功而不
成哉是以古之循吏若召父杜母眾望之所在
也用之則吏民稱誦而郡國向治焉舊士如顧
榮賀循眾望之所歸也用之以結人心則江東
皆歸焉負節義之重望者李固也用焉而盜賊
請降負勳德之重名者郭子儀也用之而回紇
===
羅拜之二人者非繫於人望者乎且以東廣一
方言之如張九齡之道侔伊呂用之而能抑奸
辨賊余靖之文學知名用之而能論諫舉職他
如崔與之用之則兵民悅服而晚節恬退可尚
矣是則人望之有益於人國如此洪惟我
朝
列聖相承任賢圖治近而望於一鄉大而望於一方
又大而望於天下秉鈞持軸皆洞識天人之士
折衝禦侮皆才兼文武之人掌刑掌教者藹藹
punctuated: 則賢否雜進。能審眾論以收人望，則治天下之大要，豈有加於此哉！且士君子以一身之微，繫天下之觀望大矣。因其人望而用之，是所謂以民治民，以天下治天下，何往而不濟，何功而不成哉！是以古之循吏若召父、杜母，眾望之所在也，用之則吏民稱誦，而郡國向治焉；舊士如顧榮、賀循，眾望之所歸也，用之以結人心，則江東皆歸焉；負節義之重望者李固也，用焉而盜賊請降；負勳德之重名者郭子儀也，用之而回紇羅拜。之二人者，非繫於人望者乎？且以東廣一方言之，如張九齡之道侔伊、呂，用之而能抑奸辨賊；余靖之文學知名，用之而能論諫舉職；他如崔與之，用之則兵民悅服，而晚節恬退可尚矣。是則人望之有益於人國如此。洪惟我朝列聖相承，任賢圖治，近而望於一鄉，大而望於一方，又大而望於天下，秉鈞持軸，皆洞識天人之士；折衝禦侮，皆才兼文武之人；掌刑掌教者，藹藹
translation_en: …then the worthy and the unworthy will be advanced indiscriminately. If one can carefully examine public opinion in order to gather those who command popular esteem, then as for the great essential in governing the realm, how could anything surpass this! Moreover, although a scholar-gentleman in his own person is slight, the hopes and expectations of the realm that rest upon him are great indeed. To employ men in accordance with their popular esteem is what is meant by governing the people by means of the people, and governing the realm by means of the realm—where could one go and not succeed, and what achievement could not be brought to completion! Therefore, among the upright officials of antiquity, men like "Father Shao" [Shao Xinchen 召信臣] and "Mother Du" [Du Shi 杜詩] were the focus of popular expectations; when they were employed, subofficial functionaries and the common people praised them, and the commanderies and principalities moved toward order. Established scholars of old families like Gu Rong 顧榮 and He Xun 賀循 were the ones to whom popular expectations turned; when they were employed to win the hearts of the people, all the region east of the Yangtze gave its allegiance. He who bore lofty esteem for integrity and righteousness was Li Gu 李固; when he was employed, bandits and rebels begged to surrender. He who bore a weighty reputation for meritorious achievement and virtue was Guo Ziyi 郭子儀; when he was employed, the Uyghurs lined up to prostrate themselves. Did not these two men embody popular esteem? Furthermore, to speak of the single region of eastern Guangdong: men such as Zhang Jiuling 張九齡, whose Way equaled that of Yi Yin 伊尹 and Lü Shang 呂尚, when employed was able to curb the treacherous and discern rebels; Yu Jing 余靖, renowned for his literary learning, when employed was able to remonstrate and fulfill his duties; and others such as Cui Yuzhi 崔與之, when employed won the joyful submission of soldiers and civilians alike, while his calm retirement in his later years was worthy of high esteem. Thus it is that men of popular esteem benefit a state to such an extent. Humbly reflecting upon our Dynasty, as the successive sacred emperors have inherited the throne one after another, employing the worthy and planning for good governance, they have drawn upon those esteemed locally in a single district, more broadly in a single region, and even more broadly throughout the entire realm. Those who hold the balance of power and grasp the pivot of state are all scholars with penetrating insight into Heaven and man; those who repel enemy thrusts and ward off aggression are all men whose talents combine the civil and the military; those who take charge of punishments and of education are genial…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之吉人也典禮典樂者濟濟之多士也維藩維
垣而旬宣激揚之有方作郡作邑而撫摩鞠育
之有道所謂循吏舊士節義勳德咸舉用之而
無遺美以故百年之間治道之盛覃布於海宇
仁恩之廣浹洽於人心黎元樂業邊塵不飛太
平之盛無有過於今日者矣柰何近年以来旱
澇相仍而郡國間有愁嘆之聲夷虜桀驁而邊
徼或有竊發之患是豈用非其望而然乎實由
負實德者固以人望而舉釣虛名者或以非望
===
而進賢否混淆故相掣肘矛盾而然耳為今之
計誠如周人用賢之法因民之所自擇而使之
入長出治如孟子用賢之術必徇國人之言而
徐加採擇則所用者皆所望而非所望者不得
以倖進而又持之以公道而不徇於私情專之
以委任而不雜於非人又何患愁嘆之聲不轉
為謳歌之音竊發之患不變為来格之化哉愚
也學不足以博古識不足以通今非敢以達時
務之俊傑自負也第以明問所及故忘其狂斐
punctuated: 之吉人也，典禮典樂者，濟濟之多士也。維藩維垣，而旬宣激揚之有方；作郡作邑，而撫摩鞠育之有道。所謂循吏、舊士、節義、勳德，咸舉用之而無遺美。以故百年之間，治道之盛，覃布於海宇；仁恩之廣，浹洽於人心。黎元樂業，邊塵不飛，太平之盛，無有過於今日者矣。柰何近年以来，旱澇相仍，而郡國間有愁嘆之聲；夷虜桀驁，而邊徼或有竊發之患。是豈用非其望而然乎？實由負實德者固以人望而舉，釣虛名者或以非望而進。賢否混淆，故相掣肘矛盾而然耳。為今之計，誠如周人用賢之法，因民之所自擇，而使之入長出治；如孟子用賢之術，必徇國人之言，而徐加採擇。則所用者皆所望，而非所望者不得以倖進。而又持之以公道，而不徇於私情；專之以委任，而不雜於非人。又何患愁嘆之聲不轉為謳歌之音，竊發之患不變為来格之化哉？愚也學不足以博古，識不足以通今，非敢以達時務之俊傑自負也。第以明問所及，故忘其狂斐…
translation_en:
…admirable gentlemen; those who direct rites and music are a multitude of dignified scholars. Those who serve as screens and bulwarks [in the provinces] have effective methods for diffusing royal virtue and rousing the pure while suppressing the corrupt; those who govern prefectures and districts have the proper way to soothe, comfort, and nurture the people. Those known as model officials, veteran scholars, men of integrity and righteousness, and men of merit and virtue have all been promoted and employed without leaving any admirable talent behind. For this reason, over the course of a hundred years, the flourishing of the way of governance has spread throughout the realm, and the breadth of benevolent grace has steeped into the hearts of the people. The common folk rejoice in their livelihoods, dust does not fly on the frontiers, and the splendor of great peace has never surpassed that of today.

Why is it, then, that in recent years droughts and floods have followed one another, and among the prefectures and principalities there are at times the sounds of愁 sighing and lamentation; the foreign tribes are unruly and arrogant, and along the frontier marches there are occasionally troubles from covert outbreaks? Could this really be so because those employed are not the ones people look up to? In truth, it is because while those who possess genuine virtue are indeed recommended on account of their popular esteem, those who angle for empty reputation sometimes advance without such esteem. The worthy and the unworthy are mingled in confusion, and thus they hinder and contradict one another—that is all.

As a plan for today, if we truly follow the Zhou people's method of employing the worthy—relying on whom the people themselves choose, and causing them to enter to lead and go out to govern—and follow Mencius's art of employing the worthy—necessarily heeding the words of the people of the state and then deliberately selecting from among them—then those who are employed will all be those whom the people look up to, and those not looked up to will be unable to advance by lucky chance. If, furthermore, this is maintained with impartiality and does not yield to private feelings, and if responsibilities are entrusted with focused authority and not mixed with the wrong men, then what worry would there be that the sounds of sighing and lamentation would not turn into the music of songs of praise, or that the troubles of covert outbreaks would not be transformed into the civilizing influence of coming in submission?

Ignorant as I am, my learning is insufficient to be broadly versed in antiquity, and my insight is insufficient to comprehend the present; I would not dare to pride myself on being an outstanding talent who understands current affairs. Merely because your enlightened question touched upon this, I have forgotten my rashness and inadequacy…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而陳之如此惟執事進而教之幸甚
第四問
何津
同考試官教諭蕭批曆法學者多不究心此篇隨
問而答必博洽之士也
考試官教諭鄭批考究詳明是殆用心於古學者
考試官學正王批不遺事實
論曆法之得失當明乎置閏論節氣之運行當
考其名義夫為政之本以治曆為先而治曆之
===
要又豈外乎置閏之與節氣哉此置閏之得失
不可以不明而節氣之名義不可以不知也粤
自黄帝迎日推策而曆書之傳其來尚矣逮夫
炎漢曆凡五變而莫善於太初豈非本於司馬
遷鄧平等所推而以律起者乎延及李唐曆凡
八變而莫善於太衍又非出於僧一行所作而
以數推者乎以至宋曆則太史局秘書省銅儀
之制極為精密此又其十變中之最者也自此
之外若杜預春秋長曆王朴欽天曆為可採焉
punctuated:
而陳之如此，惟執事進而教之，幸甚。

第四問
何津
同考試官教諭蕭批：曆法學者多不究心，此篇隨問而答，必博洽之士也。
考試官教諭鄭批：考究詳明，是殆用心於古學者。
考試官學正王批：不遺事實。

論曆法之得失，當明乎置閏；論節氣之運行，當考其名義。夫為政之本，以治曆為先，而治曆之要，又豈外乎置閏之與節氣哉？此置閏之得失不可以不明，而節氣之名義不可以不知也。粤自黄帝迎日推策，而曆書之傳，其來尚矣。逮夫炎漢，曆凡五變，而莫善於《太初》，豈非本於司馬遷、鄧平等所推，而以律起者乎？延及李唐，曆凡八變，而莫善於《太衍》，又非出於僧一行所作，而以數推者乎？以至宋曆，則太史局、秘書省銅儀之制，極為精密，此又其十變中之最者也。自此之外，若杜預《春秋長曆》、王朴《欽天曆》為可採焉，
translation_en:
…and set them forth in this manner. Should Your Excellency summon me forward and instruct me, I would be most fortunate.

Fourth Policy Question
He Jin 何津

Comment by Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Xiao 蕭: Scholars mostly do not apply their minds to calendrical science. This essay responds point by point to the question; the author must be a man of broad and thorough learning.
Comment by Examiner and County Director of Studies Zheng 鄭: The investigation is detailed and clear; this is likely someone who has applied his mind to ancient learning.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang 王: It omits none of the factual realities.

In discussing the merits and flaws of calendrical methods, one must be clear about the intercalation of months; in discussing the revolution of the solar terms, one must examine their names and meanings. Now, at the root of governance, regulating the calendar comes first, and how could the essentials of regulating the calendar lie outside of intercalation and the solar terms? Thus the merits and flaws of intercalation cannot go unclarified, and the names and meanings of the solar terms cannot go unknown. Ever since the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi 黃帝) observed the sun and calculated with counting rods, the transmission of calendrical writings has had a long history. Coming down to the fiery Han dynasty, the calendar underwent five changes in all, and none was better than the Grand Inception (Taichu 太初) calendar—was it not based on the calculations of Sima Qian 司馬遷, Deng Ping 鄧平, and others, taking pitch-pipes as its starting point? Extending to the Li Tang dynasty, the calendar underwent eight changes in all, and none was better than the Great Expansion (Dayan 大衍) calendar—and did it not come from the work of the monk Yixing 一行, calculated by means of numerical principles? Coming down to the calendars of the Song dynasty, the bronze astronomical instruments constructed by the Astrological Service and the Palace Library were extremely precise, and these were the finest among its ten calendrical reforms. Apart from these, such works as Du Yu's 杜預 Long Calendar of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu changli 春秋長曆) and Wang Pu's 王朴 Revering Heaven Calendar (Qintian li 欽天曆) are worthy of adoption,…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其餘則不足言矣然造曆之法當以置閏為急
彼其日與天會而多五日為氣盈月與日會而
少五日為朔虛曰氣盈曰朔虛非閏月所由生
乎推測之要當以正閏而分故易曰三年一閏
五年再閏又曰凡三百六十當期之日此以其
正數言也書曰以閏月定四時又曰朞三百有
六旬有六日此以其成數言也曰正數曰成數
非正閏所由分乎厥後秦用十月為歲首而常
以九月為閏則大失其推測之要矣宜乎漢武
===
帝之悟其謬也至若曆之為書不越乎二十四
氣氣之行有序而亦莫不有理存焉槩而言之
每月有節氣有中氣如丑之終寅之始則為節
寅之半則為中也一年有四立即是四時之節
氣二分二至即是四時之中氣也九十日之氣
往者過而來者續故謂之立焉春秋謂之分者
以其居乎九十日之半也夏冬謂之至者非以
其介乎巳陽午陰亥陰子陽之間乎穀雨□□
以穀麥言也穀必原其生之始故居穀雨□□
punctuated: 其餘則不足言矣。然造曆之法，當以置閏為急。彼其日與天會而多五日為氣盈，月與日會而少五日為朔虛。曰氣盈，曰朔虛，非閏月所由生乎？推測之要，當以正閏而分。故《易》曰：「三年一閏，五年再閏。」又曰：「凡三百六十，當期之日。」此以其正數言也。《書》曰：「以閏月定四時。」又曰：「朞三百有六旬有六日。」此以其成數言也。曰正數，曰成數，非正閏所由分乎？厥後秦用十月為歲首，而常以九月為閏，則大失其推測之要矣。宜乎漢武帝之悟其謬也。至若曆之為書，不越乎二十四氣。氣之行有序，而亦莫不有理存焉。槩而言之，每月有節氣、有中氣，如丑之終、寅之始則為節，寅之半則為中也。一年有四立，即是四時之節氣；二分二至，即是四時之中氣也。九十日之氣，往者過而來者續，故謂之立焉。春、秋謂之分者，以其居乎九十日之半也。夏、冬謂之至者，非以其介乎巳陽午陰、亥陰子陽之間乎？穀雨、□□，以穀、麥言也。穀必原其生之始，故居穀雨□□
translation_en:
… As for the rest, they are not worth mentioning. Yet in the method of making a calendar, the insertion of intercalary months must be treated as an urgent priority. When the sun meets the heavens and exceeds the mean by five days, this is the solar excess (qiying); when the moon meets the sun and falls short by five days, this is the lunar deficit (shuoxu). That which is called solar excess and that which is called lunar deficit—are they not that from which intercalary months arise? The essential point of astronomical calculation must be distinguished according to regular and intercalary periods. Thus the Book of Changes (Yi) says: "In three years there is one intercalation, and in five years two intercalations." It also says: "In all, three hundred and sixty, corresponding to the days of a year." This speaks in terms of the regular number. The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "By means of the intercalary month, fix the four seasons." It also says: "A full year is three hundred and six tens and six days." This speaks in terms of the completed number. That which is called the regular number and that which is called the completed number—are they not that by which the regular and the intercalary are distinguished? Thereafter, the Qin used the tenth month as the head of the year and invariably placed the intercalary month after the ninth month, thereby greatly losing the essentials of calculation. How fitting it was that Emperor Wu of Han realized their error!

As for the calendar as a book, it goes no further than the twenty-four solar terms (qi). The progression of the solar terms has an order, and in none of them is an underlying principle absent. Broadly speaking, each month has a nodal qi (jieqi) and a medial qi (zhongqi); for example, the end of the chou month and the beginning of the yin month is the nodal qi, while the middle of the yin month is the medial qi. In a year there are the Four Establishments (sili), which are the nodal qi of the four seasons; and the Two Equinoxes (erfen) and Two Solstices (erzhi), which are the medial qi of the four seasons. In the ninety-day qi of a season, the departing passes away and the coming continues it, so they are called "Establishment" (li). Spring and autumn have what are called "Equinoxes" (fen, division) because they occupy the midpoint of the ninety days. Summer and winter have what are called "Solstices" (zhi, culmination)—is it not because they lie on the boundary between the yang of si and the yin of wu, and between the yin of hai and the yang of zi? "Grain Rain" (Guyu) and [Grain in Ear (Mangzhong)] are spoken of in terms of grain and wheat. For grain, one must trace the beginning of its growth, so "Grain Rain" is placed [in the third]…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
月之中麥必要其成之終故處芒種於五月之
内驚蟄清明以風雷言也驚蟄者萬物出乎震
震為雷雷乃發聲於二月故居於二月焉清明
者萬物齊乎巽巽為風風乃潔齊於三月故居
之三月焉五月暑之始六月暑之終故小暑大
暑而在夏至之後也七月寒之始十二月寒之
終故小寒大寒而在冬至之後也八月節白露
九月節寒露然秋屬金金色白白者露之色寒
者露之氣色先白而氣始寒寒固有漸矣十月
===
中小雪十一月節大雪然寒氣始於露中於霜
終於雪雪由小而至大能無漸歟居小滿於四
月之中盖一陰方此而萌當致防微杜漸之意
也置處暑於七月之内盖以暑氣於此而止非
如既雨既處之處乎秋分水始涸立冬水始氷
冬至水泉動至於立春則水氣流行矣立雨水
於立春之後者此也霜之前為露露由白而寒
至於寒露則露結為霜矣介霜降於寒露之餘
者亦非以此歟凡此皆變化之道神之所為也
punctuated: 月之中；麥必要其成之終，故處芒種於五月之内。驚蟄、清明，以風雷言也。驚蟄者，萬物出乎震，震為雷，雷乃發聲於二月，故居於二月焉；清明者，萬物齊乎巽，巽為風，風乃潔齊於三月，故居之三月焉。五月暑之始，六月暑之終，故小暑、大暑而在夏至之後也；七月寒之始，十二月寒之終，故小寒、大寒而在冬至之後也。八月節白露，九月節寒露，然秋屬金，金色白，白者露之色，寒者露之氣，色先白而氣始寒，寒固有漸矣。十月中小雪，十一月節大雪，然寒氣始於露，中於霜，終於雪，雪由小而至大，能無漸歟？居小滿於四月之中，盖一陰方此而萌，當致防微杜漸之意也；置處暑於七月之内，盖以暑氣於此而止，非如「既雨既處」之處乎？秋分水始涸，立冬水始氷，冬至水泉動，至於立春則水氣流行矣，立雨水於立春之後者此也。霜之前為露，露由白而寒，至於寒露則露結為霜矣，介霜降於寒露之餘者，亦非以此歟？凡此，皆變化之道、神之所為也。
translation_en: … the middle of the [third] month; wheat must be reckoned at the completion of its ripening, so Grain in Ear (Mangzhong) is placed within the fifth month. Awakening of Insects (Jingzhe) and Pure Brightness (Qingming) are spoken of in terms of wind and thunder. As for Awakening of Insects, the myriad things emerge in Zhen; Zhen corresponds to thunder, and thunder first sounds forth in the second month, so it is placed in the second month. As for Pure Brightness, the myriad things are made uniform in Xun; Xun corresponds to wind, and the wind cleanses and orders things in the third month, so it is placed in the third month. The fifth month is the beginning of heat, and the sixth month is the culmination of heat; therefore Lesser Heat (Xiaoshu) and Greater Heat (Dashu) come after the Summer Solstice (Xiazhi). The seventh month is the beginning of cold, and the twelfth month is the culmination of cold; therefore Lesser Cold (Xiaohan) and Greater Cold (Dahan) come after the Winter Solstice (Dongzhi). The nodal qi of the eighth month is White Dew (Bailu), and the nodal qi of the ninth month is Cold Dew (Hanlu). Now, autumn belongs to Metal, and the color of Metal is white; white is the color of dew, and cold is the qi of dew. The color first turns white and only then does the qi become cold—coldness indeed develops gradually! The medial qi of the tenth month is Lesser Snow (Xiaoxue), and the nodal qi of the eleventh month is Greater Snow (Daxue). Now, cold qi begins with dew, reaches its midpoint with frost, and culminates in snow. As snow proceeds from lesser to greater, how could it be without gradual progression? Placing Grain Buds (Xiaoman, lit. "Lesser Fullness") in the middle of the fourth month is because the single yin is just beginning to sprout at this point, and one ought to apply the principle of guarding against the minute and checking gradual tendencies. Placing End of Heat (Chushu, lit. "Stopping of Heat") within the seventh month is because the hot qi comes to a halt at this point—is this not "stopping" (chu) in the sense of the phrase "the rain has fallen and has stopped" (ji yu ji chu)? At the Autumnal Equinox (Qiufen) water begins to dry up; at the Beginning of Winter (Lidong) water begins to freeze; at the Winter Solstice (Dongzhi) spring water stirs; and by the Beginning of Spring (Lichun) the water qi flows freely once more—this is why Rain Water (Yushui) is established after the Beginning of Spring. Before frost there is dew; dew proceeds from being white to being cold, and by the time of Cold Dew, the dew condenses into frost—is not placing Frost's Descent (Shuangjiang) in the aftermath of Cold Dew also for this reason? All of these are the Way of transformation and the work of the inscrutable spirit. …

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也愚何足以知此姑掇拾所聞以復惟執事進
教之幸甚
第五問
沈瓛
同考試官訓導李批
時務一策正欲觀士子學識
此作敷答詳明處置得當宜
在優選
考試官教諭鄭批議論正當切於時務
考試官學正王批有斷制
===
為政之道莫先於養民養民之要莫切於農桑
農桑為衣食之本而民生之至急者也衣食不
足則放僻邪侈無不為已雖有善政善教將安
施乎故孔子答問政以足食為先孟子論王道
以養民為首蓋此謂也古聖王知其然於是制
閭里均井地百畝之田勿奪其時五畝之宅樹
之以桑其惰者有三推九推之化以勸之其游
者有里布夫家之征以懲之其力之贏乏也有
受田歸田之期以節之其地之肥磽也有一易
punctuated:
也？愚何足以知此？姑掇拾所聞以復，惟執事進教之，幸甚。

第五問
沈瓛
同考試官訓導李批：時務一策，正欲觀士子學識。此作敷答詳明，處置得當，宜在優選。
考試官教諭鄭批：議論正當，切於時務。
考試官學正王批：有斷制。

為政之道，莫先於養民；養民之要，莫切於農桑。農桑為衣食之本，而民生之至急者也。衣食不足，則放僻邪侈，無不為已，雖有善政善教，將安施乎？故孔子答問政以足食為先，孟子論王道以養民為首，蓋此謂也。古聖王知其然，於是制閭里，均井地；百畝之田，勿奪其時；五畝之宅，樹之以桑。其惰者，有三推、九推之化以勸之；其游者，有里布、夫家之征以懲之；其力之贏乏也，有受田、歸田之期以節之；其地之肥磽也，有一易、
translation_en:
… How am I, in my ignorance, sufficient to know this? I have merely gathered together what I have heard by way of reply; I only pray that Your Honors will advance and instruct me, which would be most fortunate.

Fifth Question
Shen Huan 沈瓛
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Li 李: A policy question on current affairs is intended precisely to observe the learning and insight of the candidates. This composition sets forth its answers in clear detail and handles the matters appropriately; it deserves to be placed among the superior selections.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zheng 鄭: The arguments are sound and pertinent to current affairs.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Wang 王: It possesses decisive judgment.

In the Way of governance, nothing comes before nourishing the people; in the essentials of nourishing the people, nothing is more urgent than agriculture and sericulture. Agriculture and sericulture are the foundation of clothing and food, and the most pressing necessities of the people's livelihood. If clothing and food are insufficient, the people will stop at nothing in waywardness, perversity, wickedness, and extravagance; even if there are good government and good instruction, how could they be applied? Therefore, when Confucius 孔子 answered a question about governance, he put sufficient food first, and when Mencius 孟子 discussed the Kingly Way, he placed nourishing the people at the head—this is what they meant. The sage-kings of antiquity knew this to be so, and thereupon established neighborhood communities and equalized the well-fields; for the fields of a hundred mu, they did not rob the people of their seasonal time; for the homesteads of five mu, they had them planted with mulberry trees. For the indolent, there was the transformative example of the three pushes and nine pushes of the ritual plow to encourage them; for the idle, there were the penalty cloth of the neighborhood and the labor-service levies on households to punish them; for the waxing and waning of their physical strength, there were the fixed ages for receiving fields and returning fields to regulate them; for the fertility or barrenness of the soil, there were the systems of biennial…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
二易之法以更之故男有餘粟女有餘布生長
老死於仁政者此也降及後世秦不師古任商
鞅廢井田開阡陌聽其所耕不限多少三代良
法美意殄滅盡矣由是富者田連阡陌而兼并
之患起貧者地無立錐而游手之民興況稍桀
黠有資力者率舍勞就逸以趨末業而守耒耜
縁南畝者盡蚩蚩之氓賣絲糶穀常稱貸於其
前徴租索錢每取盈於其後終歲勤動而室遂
為之一空矣何怪乎膏粱者不耕而耕者糲飯
===
不充文繍者不蠶而蠶者裋褐不足天地生生
之仁幾乎息矣逮我
皇明受天明命撫有四海百年于茲恐民之飢寒也
故考課於守令者以農桑為首慮民之游惰也
故載之於版籍者以事產為先以至於
大誥又有互知丁業之條凡所以重農養民之法
無不備舉是宜老者衣帛食肉黎民不飢不寒
措天下於仁壽之域躋斯世於熈皥之天自二
帝三王以来未有盛於今日者也執事猶以太
punctuated: 二易之法以更之。故男有餘粟，女有餘布，生長老死於仁政者，此也。降及後世，秦不師古，任商鞅廢井田、開阡陌，聽其所耕，不限多少，三代良法美意殄滅盡矣。由是富者田連阡陌，而兼并之患起；貧者地無立錐，而游手之民興。況稍桀黠有資力者，率舍勞就逸以趨末業；而守耒耜、縁南畝者，盡蚩蚩之氓。賣絲糶穀，常稱貸於其前；徴租索錢，每取盈於其後。終歲勤動，而室遂為之一空矣。何怪乎膏粱者不耕，而耕者糲飯不充；文繍者不蠶，而蠶者裋褐不足，天地生生之仁幾乎息矣。逮我皇明受天明命，撫有四海，百年于茲。恐民之飢寒也，故考課於守令者以農桑為首；慮民之游惰也，故載之於版籍者以事產為先。以至於《大誥》，又有互知丁業之條。凡所以重農養民之法，無不備舉。是宜老者衣帛食肉，黎民不飢不寒，措天下於仁壽之域，躋斯世於熈皥之天，自二帝三王以来，未有盛於今日者也。執事猶以太
translation_en:
… or biennial fallow rotation to alternate them. Thus men had surplus grain and women had surplus cloth, and people were born, grew up, aged, and died under benevolent governance; this was the reason. Coming down to later ages, Qin did not model itself on antiquity. It employed Shang Yang 商鞅 to abolish the well-field system and open up the field paths, allowing people to cultivate as they pleased without limiting the amount, and the good laws and fine intentions of the Three Dynasties were utterly destroyed. From this, the rich had fields stretching across the paths, and the evil of land annexation arose; the poor had not enough land to stand an awl on, and idle vagrants multiplied. Moreover, those who were somewhat crafty and possessed financial means generally abandoned hard labor for ease in order to pursue secondary occupations; whereas those who kept to the plowshares and worked the southern acres were all simple, ignorant folk. Selling silk and grain, they constantly had to borrow beforehand; when rents were levied and money demanded, full payment was always exacted afterward. Though they toiled diligently all year round, their houses were consequently swept completely bare. What wonder is it that those who dine on rich meats do not plow, while those who plow do not have enough coarse grain to fill themselves; that those who wear embroidered silks do not raise silkworms, while those who raise silkworms do not have enough short coarse cloth? The life-giving benevolence of Heaven and Earth nearly ceased!

When Our August Ming received the bright mandate of Heaven and came to rule soothingly over the Four Seas, a hundred years have passed to the present. Fearing that the people might suffer hunger and cold, in evaluating the performance of Prefects and Magistrates it places agriculture and sericulture first; concerned that the people might be idle and lazy, in recording them in the household registers it gives priority to their occupations and property. Even in the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao), there is also the statute on mutual knowledge of adult males' occupations. Every method for emphasizing agriculture and nourishing the people has been fully instituted. It is fitting that the aged wear silk and eat meat, the common people suffer neither hunger nor cold, the realm is placed in a region of benevolence and longevity, and this world is raised to a heaven of prosperous peace; since the Two Emperors and Three Kings, there has never been an era more flourishing than today. Yet Your Excellency still regards the…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
平既久風俗日侈務本者少趨末者多以為意
外之憂欲求所以處之之法愚以為莫若定經
費抑兼并擇賢守令躬行勸率不妄興工役以
奪其時不横加賦斂以困其力勤有賞惰有戒
又於緇黄商賈市井官宦廝役技藝數者之中
擇其理所當禁者而驅之使復業理所當容者
而聽之使自便於勢有所不論焉守之以定力
持之以悠久則何患民有飢寒之憂乎吁救流
弊於積習之餘憂患害於未發之先此固儒者
===
所當究心也愚生處之之術不外乎此不識執
事以為何如
punctuated: 平既久，風俗日侈，務本者少，趨末者多，以為意外之憂，欲求所以處之之法。愚以為莫若定經費，抑兼并，擇賢守令，躬行勸率，不妄興工役以奪其時，不横加賦斂以困其力，勤有賞，惰有戒；又於緇黄、商賈、市井、官宦、廝役、技藝數者之中，擇其理所當禁者而驅之使復業，理所當容者而聽之使自便，於勢有所不論焉。守之以定力，持之以悠久，則何患民有飢寒之憂乎？吁！救流弊於積習之餘，憂患害於未發之先，此固儒者所當究心也。愚生處之之術，不外乎此，不識執事以為何如？
translation_en: …peace has long prevailed, customs grow daily more extravagant, few devote themselves to the fundamental occupation [agriculture], and many pursue secondary occupations, which you regard as an unforeseen cause for concern, and you wish to seek a method for dealing with it. In my humble opinion, nothing is better than fixing regular expenditures, curbing land annexation, and selecting worthy prefects and magistrates to personally lead and encourage the people—not recklessly initiating public works and corvée labor to rob them of their farming seasons, nor arbitrarily imposing taxes and levies to exhaust their strength, rewarding the diligent and warning the lazy. Furthermore, among those several categories—Buddhist monks and Daoist priests, merchants and traders, marketplace idlers, official underlings and menial servants, and artisans—we should select those whom principle requires to be prohibited and drive them back to their fundamental occupation, while allowing those whom principle permits to be tolerated to do as suits their convenience, without regard to influence or power. If we uphold this with resolute determination and maintain it over a long period of time, what need will there be to worry that the people might suffer from hunger and cold? Alas! To remedy widespread abuses in the wake of long-accumulated habits, and to worry about calamities and harms before they have even broken out—this is assuredly what Confucian scholars ought to devote their minds to examining. The method by which this foolish student would deal with the matter goes no further than this; I do not know what you, sir, think of it?

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
皇上臨御之七年歲在辛卯實當大比
賓興之秋総督兩廣軍務兼理巡
撫都察院右都御史韓雍巡按廣
東監察御史程宏暨藩憲大臣恪
遵
成憲預聘師儒為考試官至期斂所
部十郡士以試之凡百執事罔不
===
勤慎各共乃職而重光等司考校
者亦精白一心以公去取事竣得
其文之協準繩者七十五人皆精
選也小錄告成僉謂重光宜有言
以序末簡夫治本於道道載於經
明夫經者道必深深於道者文必
工若孔子所謂有德者必有言是
已肆我
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序

皇上臨御之七年，歲在辛卯，實當大比賓興之秋。総督兩廣軍務兼理巡撫、都察院右都御史韓雍，巡按廣東監察御史程宏，暨藩、憲大臣，恪遵成憲，預聘師儒為考試官。至期，斂所部十郡士以試之。凡百執事，罔不勤慎，各共乃職；而重光等司考校者，亦精白一心，以公去取。事竣，得其文之協準繩者七十五人，皆精選也。小錄告成，僉謂重光宜有言以序末簡。夫治本於道，道載於經。明夫經者，道必深；深於道者，文必工。若孔子所謂「有德者必有言」，是已。肆我
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In the seventh year of His Majesty's reign, the cyclical year xinmao (1471), it was indeed the autumn of the triennial examination for recommending worthy talents as guests of the state. The Supreme Commander of Military Affairs in Liangguang and Concurrent Grand Coordinator, Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate Han Yong 韓雍, the Regional Investigating Censor of Guangdong Cheng Hong 程宏, together with the high officials of the Provincial Administration Commission and Surveillance Commission, respectfully observed the established statutes and in advance invited Confucian teachers to serve as Examiners. When the appointed time arrived, they gathered the scholars from the ten prefectures under their jurisdiction to examine them. Among all the various functionaries, there were none who were not diligent and cautious, each fulfilling his respective duties; while I, Chongguang 重光, and the others in charge of grading the papers also maintained pure and united hearts to make selections and rejections impartially. When the affair was completed, we obtained seventy-five men whose essays conformed to the standards—all of them fine selections. With the Examination Record completed, everyone said that I, Chongguang, ought to offer some words as a postface on the final pages. Now, governance is rooted in the Way, and the Way is recorded in the Classics. Those who illuminate the Classics must be profound in the Way, and those who are profound in the Way must be skillful in literary composition. This is just what Confucius meant by saying, "Those who have virtue must have something to say." Therefore our…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
國家設科取士而試以文百有餘年
于茲無非欲得道德之士以為致
治之本也
列聖相承寔同一心
皇上協重華之德躋重熙之運恢弘治
道益崇科目故士之豪傑者胥此
焉出矧東廣為天下雄藩川嶽鍾
秀代不乏人文章節義照耀古今
===
諸士子生長是邦沐
國家作養之恩充聖賢體用之學故
其發而為文根經據理竒本乎易
葩原乎詩疏通發乎書之奧莊敬
著乎禮之經而筆削謹嚴又倣乎
春秋之旨誦而觀之瑲然瓊琚玉
珮之音越也燦然山龍華蟲之采
列也儼然夏圭商敦之器陳也非
punctuated: 國家設科取士，而試以文，百有餘年于茲，無非欲得道德之士，以為致治之本也。列聖相承，寔同一心。皇上協重華之德，躋重熙之運，恢弘治道，益崇科目，故士之豪傑者，胥此焉出。矧東廣為天下雄藩，川嶽鍾秀，代不乏人，文章節義，照耀古今。諸士子生長是邦，沐國家作養之恩，充聖賢體用之學，故其發而為文，根經據理，竒本乎《易》，葩原乎《詩》，疏通發乎《書》之奧，莊敬著乎《禮》之經，而筆削謹嚴，又倣乎《春秋》之旨。誦而觀之，瑲然瓊琚玉珮之音越也，燦然山龍華蟲之采列也，儼然夏圭商敦之器陳也。非
translation_en: … dynasty has established the examination system to select scholars and tested them through literary composition for more than a hundred years up to the present, with no other aim than to obtain men of moral way and virtue as the foundation for bringing about good governance. Successive Sacred Emperors have carried on this legacy, truly sharing a single mind. His Majesty matches the virtue of Chonghua [Emperor Shun] and ascends to an era of compounded splendor; he expands the Way of governance and increasingly esteems the examination system, so that outstanding heroes among the scholars all emerge from here. Moveover, eastern Guangdong is a mighty province in the realm, where rivers and mountains concentrate their finest essence; no generation has lacked talent, and their literary accomplishments and moral integrity have shone through antiquity and the present. The candidates, born and raised in this region, have been bathed in the dynasty's grace of nurturing and cultivation, and have filled themselves with the learning of the sages and worthies regarding substance and function. Therefore, when they express this in writing, it is rooted in the Classics and grounded in principle: its marvelousness is based on the Book of Changes (Yi), its luxuriance originates in the Book of Odes (Shi), its fluent comprehension unfolds the profundities of the Book of Documents (Shu), its solemn reverence manifests the standards of the Record of Rites (Li), and its strictness in phrasing and editing imitates the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu). When one recites and examines their compositions, they ring clearly like the resonant sound of fine jade pendants; they gleam brilliantly like the arrayed colors of mountains, dragons, and variegated pheasants on ceremonial robes; and they stand with solemn dignity like the displayed ritual jade tablets of the Xia and bronze vessels of the Shang. Unless…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
雋味道腴卒澤於聖學之淵海者
能之乎登名是錄固非倖然自茲
以往論秀春官擢第
大廷為名進士有官守言責之寄尚
當體道出治輔世康民以媲美乎
前烈垂耀於後世益有以見是科
得人之盛而主司選拔之公顧不
偉歟借使籍是為决科計而行不
===
逮焉者則非余之所望而亦非諸
士子之所以自期待也尚期勗之
成化七年秋八月既望江西饒州
府餘干縣儒學教諭鄭重光謹序
punctuated:
雋味道腴，卒澤於聖學之淵海者，能之乎？登名是錄，固非倖然。自茲以往，論秀春官，擢第大廷，為名進士，有官守、言責之寄，尚當體道出治，輔世康民，以媲美乎前烈，垂耀於後世，益有以見是科得人之盛，而主司選拔之公，顧不偉歟！借使籍是為决科計，而行不逮焉者，則非余之所望，而亦非諸士子之所以自期待也。尚期勗之。
成化七年秋八月既望，江西饒州府餘干縣儒學教諭鄭重光謹序。
translation_en:
…savored the rich essence of the Way, and thoroughly steeped themselves in the deep sea of sage learning, could they have achieved this? Having their names entered in this record is certainly no matter of mere luck. From this point onward, when their talents are evaluated by the Ministry of Rites and they are advanced to success in the Great Court to become renowned metropolitan graduates (jinshi), entrusted with official duties or responsibilities for remonstrance, they should all the more embody the Way in bringing forth good governance, assisting the age and bringing peace to the people, so as to rival the splendor of past worthies and hand down their glory to future generations. This will even more clearly demonstrate the abundance of talent obtained in this examination and the fairness of the examiners' selection—would that not be magnificent! If, however, anyone were to rely on this merely as a means to pass the examinations while their conduct failed to measure up to it, that would neither be what I hope for, nor what the scholars themselves expect of their own persons. Let them take heart and strive!

Respectfully written as a postface by Zheng Chongguang 鄭重光, Instructor in the Confucian School of Yugan County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, on the sixteenth day of the eighth month in the autumn of the seventh year of the Chenghua era [September 1, 1471].

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄序
上天生賢以輔世其盛也由氣運之昌
教化之洽耳然氣運教化相與流
通恒始于西北而後及于東南虞
之聲教始冀都而以東漸南暨為
極周之風化始豐鎬而以化成南
國為至故當時賢才之生高陽高
辛有八元八凱之舉而萬邦黎獻
===
亦共為帝臣羔羊大夫有正直節
儉之德而在野武夫亦公侯腹心
是皆帝王德化上下與天地同流
舉一世而甄陶之者然也我
國家受
天眷命撫御斯世
太祖高皇帝肇迹淮西
太宗文皇帝定都冀北而東南嶺海之
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄序

上天生賢以輔世，其盛也，由氣運之昌、教化之洽耳。然氣運、教化相與流通，恒始于西北，而後及于東南。虞之聲教始冀都，而以東漸南暨為極；周之風化始豐鎬，而以化成南國為至。故當時賢才之生，高陽、高辛有八元、八凱之舉，而萬邦黎獻亦共為帝臣；《羔羊》大夫有正直節儉之德，而在野武夫亦公侯腹心。是皆帝王德化上下與天地同流，舉一世而甄陶之者然也。我國家受天眷命，撫御斯世，太祖高皇帝肇迹淮西，太宗文皇帝定都冀北，而東南嶺海之
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

High Heaven brings forth worthies to assist the world; their flourishing comes simply from the prosperity of the cosmic vitality and the pervasiveness of moral transformation through teaching. Yet as cosmic vitality and moral teaching circulate together, they invariably begin in the northwest and only afterward reach the southeast. The renown and teachings of Yu [Shun] began in the capital at Ji and took soaking into the east and extending to the south as their furthest reach; the moral customs of the Zhou began in Feng and Hao and took the complete transformation of the southern states as their culmination. Thus, in the birth of worthy talents at those times, under Gaoyang and Gaoxin there was the elevation of the Eight Worthies (Bayuan) and Eight Harmonies (Bakai), while the myriad states' eminent subjects among the black-haired people also joined in serving as ministers to the sovereign; the grandees of the "Lambskin" (Gaoyang) ode possessed the virtues of rectitude and frugality, while even the martial men in the wilds were the trusted confidants of dukes and marquises. All of this was because the moral transformation of the sovereigns flowed above and below in harmony with Heaven and Earth, molding and fashioning the entire age. Our dynasty received the favored mandate of Heaven to pacify and govern this world. Grand Progenitor Emperor Gao founded the dynastic enterprise in Huaisi, and Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen established the capital in northern Ji, while [in the region] of the mountains and seas of the southeast…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
間逖遠
京畿漸被
王化方諸中州能無先後之差乎比于
列聖嗣陳政教益勤益勵已逾百年斯
薰蒸暢達無遠不洽而嶺南賢才
始亦衆盛足以儷中州而應昌運
也矧茲數歲奉
勅總督兩廣軍務兼理巡撫右都御史
韓雍來涖斯境威惠兼行夷獠馴
服而興學勸士尤所加意邇者復
同奉
勅總鎮太監陳瑄總兵官平江伯陳銳
開設總府于梧州武備脩舉風教
日新而士習丕變乃成化辛卯秋
當大比興賢而十郡一州之士若
庠序生徒若山林韋布若介胄子
punctuated: 間，逖遠京畿，漸被王化，方諸中州，能無先後之差乎？比于列聖嗣陳政教，益勤益勵，已逾百年，斯薰蒸暢達，無遠不洽，而嶺南賢才始亦衆盛，足以儷中州而應昌運也。矧茲數歲，奉勅總督兩廣軍務兼理巡撫右都御史韓雍來涖斯境，威惠兼行，夷獠馴服，而興學勸士，尤所加意。邇者復同奉勅總鎮太監陳瑄、總兵官平江伯陳銳，開設總府于梧州，武備脩舉，風教日新，而士習丕變。乃成化辛卯秋，當大比興賢，而十郡一州之士，若庠序生徒，若山林韋布，若介胄子
translation_en: … region, far removed from the imperial capital, gradually came under the influence of royal civilization; compared to the Central Plains, how could there not be a difference in whether this occurred earlier or later? By the time the successive sage emperors inherited the throne and set forth governance and instruction, growing ever more diligent and encouraging for over a hundred years, this permeating and flourishing influence reached everywhere no matter how distant. Thus, worthy talents in Lingnan (South of the Ranges) also began to grow numerous and flourishing, sufficient to rival the Central Plains and respond to this prosperous era. Moreover, in recent years, the Right Censor-in-Chief Supreme Commander of Military Affairs of Liangguang and concurrently Grand Coordinator by Imperial Command, Han Yong 韓雍, came to govern this territory. Exercising both awe-inspiring authority and benevolence, he brought the non-Chinese tribes (Yi and Liao) into submission, while paying especial attention to promoting schools and encouraging scholars. Recently, together with the Grand Defender Eunuch Director by Imperial Command Chen Xuan 陳瑄 and the Regional Commander, Earl of Pingjiang, Chen Rui 陳銳, he established the Supreme Command Headquarters at Wuzhou 梧州. Military defenses have been put in order, moral teaching is renewed daily, and the customs of the literati have undergone a great transformation. Now, in the autumn of the xinmao year of the Chenghua reign (1471), at the time of the triennial examination to promote the worthy, the scholars from the ten prefectures and one subprefecture—whether students in the local schools, commoners in the mountains and forests, or sons and younger brothers of military officers…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
弟預有司舉送者幾二千人先期
提督學校僉事胡榮循例小試擇
其可入場者千二百有竒視往昔
為衆盛矣至期鸞等膺禮聘而来
忝司考校而巡按廣東監察御史
程宏寔監臨其事暨鎖院內而提
調則左布政使張瑄左叅政張瓚
監試則按察使甯良副使章格外
===
而綱維防範則右布政使周鐸左
叅政王佐右叅政卓天錫左叅議
李田副使孔鏞吕洪涂棐僉事王
祐陶魯陳貴林錦芳泌姚俊凡諸
執事俱遴選以充而嚴革宿弊咸
秉至公三試之後取其經義論策
典雅純正者七十有五人遵解額
也復遵故事刻小録將以徹
punctuated: 弟，預有司舉送者幾二千人。先期，提督學校僉事胡榮循例小試，擇其可入場者千二百有竒，視往昔為衆盛矣。至期，鸞等膺禮聘而来，忝司考校。而巡按廣東監察御史程宏寔監臨其事。暨鎖院，內而提調，則左布政使張瑄、左叅政張瓚；監試，則按察使甯良、副使章格；外而綱維防範，則右布政使周鐸、左叅政王佐、右叅政卓天錫、左叅議李田、副使孔鏞、吕洪、涂棐，僉事王祐、陶魯、陳貴、林錦、芳泌、姚俊。凡諸執事，俱遴選以充，而嚴革宿弊，咸秉至公。三試之後，取其經義、論、策典雅純正者七十有五人，遵解額也。復遵故事刻小録，將以徹
translation_en: …sons and younger brothers of military officers—who participated in the recommendation and forwarding by the local authorities numbered nearly two thousand men. Prior to the scheduled date, the Education Intendant Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Hu Rong 胡榮 followed precedent in conducting a preliminary test, selecting over twelve hundred men qualified to enter the examination compound, a turnout more numerous and flourishing than in bygone days. When the time came, [I,] Luan 鸞, and my colleagues received the courteous invitation and arrived, unworthily taking charge of the examining and grading. Meanwhile, Regional Inspector of Guangdong and Investigating Censor Cheng Hong 程宏 truly served as Supervising Official over the affair. Once the examination compound was locked, on the inside, serving as Proctors were Left Administration Commissioner Zhang Xuan 張瑄 and Left Administration Vice Commissioner Zhang Zan 張瓚; serving as Examination Overseers were Surveillance Commissioner Ning Liang 甯良 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhang Ge 章格; on the outside, maintaining overall order and security precautions were Right Administration Commissioner Zhou Duo 周鐸, Left Administration Vice Commissioner Wang Zuo 王佐, Right Administration Vice Commissioner Zhuo Tianxi 卓天錫, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Li Tian 李田, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Kong Yong 孔鏞, Lü Hong 吕洪, and Tu Fei 涂棐, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Wang You 王祐, Tao Lu 陶魯, Chen Gui 陳貴, Lin Jin 林錦, Fang Bi 芳泌, and Yao Jun 姚俊. All the various functionaries were carefully selected to fill their posts; longstanding abuses were strictly eradicated, and everyone upheld the utmost impartiality. After the three sessions, we selected seventy-five men whose essays on the meaning of the Classics, discourses, and policy essays were refined and pure, in compliance with the provincial quota. Following precedent once again, we have engraved this brief record, which is about to be presented for…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
御覽而示方来仰惟
皇明奄有華夏
祖宗創制垂憲盡革近代因循之陋而
遠追虞周文明之治矣然所以弼
賛治化承保
上天純佑命而永建億萬年之基者尚
有賴乎多賢之用也今諸士子荷
聖朝作養造就而獲登名賢書行將與
===
天下士會試禮闈進對
大廷致用有日矣雖所以進身之階
不外乎文藝而致用立身之本不
在是也要必存心脩德焉耳嘗觀
有虞之世九德咸事而曰嚴祗敬
百僚師師者其心何如也有周之
士不顯亦世而厥猶翼翼有孝有
德者其德何如也諸士子誦詩讀
punctuated: 御覽，而示方来。仰惟皇明奄有華夏，祖宗創制垂憲，盡革近代因循之陋，而遠追虞、周文明之治矣。然所以弼賛治化，承保上天純佑命，而永建億萬年之基者，尚有賴乎多賢之用也。今諸士子荷聖朝作養造就，而獲登名賢書，行將與天下士會試禮闈，進對大廷，致用有日矣。雖所以進身之階不外乎文藝，而致用立身之本不在是也，要必存心脩德焉耳。嘗觀有虞之世，九德咸事，而曰嚴祗敬、百僚師師者，其心何如也？有周之士，不顯亦世，而厥猶翼翼、有孝有德者，其德何如也？諸士子誦詩讀
translation_en: … for His Majesty's perusal and to serve as a record for posterity. Looking up in reverence, Our August Ming encompasses all of China; our Imperial Ancestors established institutions and handed down laws, completely abolishing the perfunctory bad habits of recent ages and reaching back to the enlightened governance of Yu [Shun] and the Zhou dynasty. Yet that by which we assist and promote transformative governance, receive and preserve the pure and благоприятный mandate of High Heaven, and forever establish a foundation for a myriad ages still depends upon the employment of many worthy men. Now, all you scholars have received the nurturing and training of Our Sacred Dynasty and have succeeded in having your names inscribed in the register of worthies; soon you will join the scholars of the realm to take the Metropolitan Examination at the Ministry of Rites, advance to reply at the Great Court [in the Palace Examination], and the day when you will be put to practical use is at hand. Although the stepping-stone by which one advances oneself is nothing other than literary art, the fundamental basis for practical service and establishing oneself does not lie in this; in essence, it must simply lie in preserving one's mind and cultivating one's virtue. I have observed that in the age of Yu, men of all nine virtues served in office, and when it is said that they "daily practiced strict reverence" and "all the officials emulated one another," what was their mind like? Among the officers of the Zhou, "were they not illustrious from generation to generation?" and when it is said that "their plans were reverent and cautious" and they "possessed filial piety and possessed virtue," what was their virtue like? All you scholars have chanted the Odes and read…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
書志希古聖賢久矣苟能日存祗
敬師師而懋昭翼翼孝德則爾之
心即虞廷黎獻之心爾之德即周
家多士之德豈直今世之士云乎
哉有是心有是德而輔世賛化之
功不虞周若者吾未之間也其或
志功利而飾巧詐矜名譽而競葩
藻兹乃近代浮靡之習而非輔世
===
賛化之用也幸勉之哉幸戒之哉
鸞不佞敢以是言序諸首
山西太原府忻州儒學學正王鸞
謹序
punctuated:
書，志希古聖賢久矣。苟能日存祗敬、師師，而懋昭翼翼、孝德，則爾之心即虞廷黎獻之心，爾之德即周家多士之德，豈直今世之士云乎哉？有是心，有是德，而輔世賛化之功不虞、周若者，吾未之間也。其或志功利而飾巧詐，矜名譽而競葩藻，兹乃近代浮靡之習，而非輔世賛化之用也。幸勉之哉！幸戒之哉！鸞不佞，敢以是言序諸首。
山西太原府忻州儒學學正王鸞謹序。
translation_en:
… History, and have long aspired to emulate the ancient sages and worthies. If you can daily maintain reverent respect and mutual emulation, and strive to manifest cautious diligence and filial virtue, then your minds will be the very minds of the eminent worthies of the court of Yu, and your virtue will be the very virtue of the multitude of scholars of the House of Zhou—how could you merely be called scholars of the present age? That someone possessing such a mind and such virtue should fail to equal the achievements of Yu and Zhou in assisting the world and aiding transformation is something I have never heard of [reading 間 as 聞]. Should anyone instead set their ambitions on utility and profit while adorning themselves with artful deceit, or boast of fame and reputation while competing in flowery rhetoric, this is merely the frivolous and extravagant habit of recent ages, and is of no use for assisting the world and aiding transformation. Please strive in this! Please be on guard against that! Though I, Luan, am without talent, I venture to place these words as a preface at the beginning.
Respectfully prefaced by Wang Luan 王鸞, Director of Studies of the Confucian School of Xinzhou in Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi.

子曰聽訟吾猶人也必也使無訟乎無
情者不得盡其辭大畏民志此謂知
本
子入太廟每事問或曰孰謂鄹人之子
知禮乎入太廟每事問子聞之曰是
禮也
曾子子思同道曾子師也父兄也子思
臣也微也曾子子思易地則皆然
易
直其正也方其義也君子敬以直内義
以方外敬義立而德不孤直方大不
習无不利則不疑其所行也
彖曰大有柔得尊位大中而上下應之
曰大有其德剛健而文明應乎天而
punctuated:
第一場

四書
子曰：「聽訟，吾猶人也。必也使無訟乎！」無情者不得盡其辭，大畏民志，此謂知本。
子入太廟，每事問。或曰：「孰謂鄹人之子知禮乎？入太廟，每事問。」子聞之，曰：「是禮也。」
曾子、子思同道。曾子，師也，父兄也；子思，臣也，微也。曾子、子思易地則皆然。

易
直其正也，方其義也。君子敬以直内，義以方外，敬義立而德不孤。「直、方、大，不習无不利」，則不疑其所行也。
《彖》曰：「大有」，柔得尊位，大中而上下應之，曰「大有」。其德剛健而文明，應乎天而
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said, "In hearing litigation, I am no different from anyone else. What is necessary, however, is to cause there to be no litigation!" Thus those without substance to their claims do not dare to fully air their baseless words, because deep awe has been instilled in the people's minds. This is called knowing the root.

When the Master entered the Grand Temple, he asked about everything. Someone said, "Who says that the son of the man of Zou knows ritual propriety? On entering the Grand Temple, he asks about everything." When the Master heard of this, he said, "This is itself ritual propriety."

Zengzi and Zisi shared the same Way. Zengzi was a teacher, in the position of a father or elder brother; Zisi was a minister, in a subordinate position. Had Zengzi and Zisi exchanged places, each would have acted just as the other did.

Book of Changes (Yi)

"Straight" means one's uprightness; "square" means one's righteousness. The gentleman uses reverence to straighten the inner self, and righteousness to square the outer conduct. When reverence and righteousness are established, virtue does not stand alone. "Straight, square, and great; even without repeated practice, there is nothing that is not advantageous"—thus he has no doubts about what he does.

The Commentary on the Judgment (Tuan) says: In "Great Possession" (Dayou), the yielding line attains the honored position, holds the great center, and those above and below respond to it; therefore it is called "Great Possession." title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
時行是以元亨
知變化之道者其知神之所為乎
易曰憧憧往來朋從爾思子曰天下何
思何慮天下同歸而殊塗一致而百
慮天下何思何慮日往則月來月往
則日來日月相推而明生焉寒往則
暑來暑往則寒來寒暑相推而歲成
焉往者屈也來者信也屈信相感而
===
利生焉尺蠖之屈以求信也龍蛇之
蟄以存身也精義入神以致用也利
用安身以崇德也
書
柔遠能邇惇德允元而難任人
厥貢惟球琳琅玕浮于積石至于龍門
西河會于渭汭織皮崐崘析支渠搜
西戎即叙
punctuated:
時行，是以元亨。
知變化之道者，其知神之所為乎？
《易》曰：「憧憧往來，朋從爾思。」子曰：「天下何思何慮？天下同歸而殊塗，一致而百慮。天下何思何慮？日往則月來，月往則日來，日月相推而明生焉。寒往則暑來，暑往則寒來，寒暑相推而歲成焉。往者屈也，來者信也，屈信相感而利生焉。尺蠖之屈，以求信也；龍蛇之蟄，以存身也。精義入神，以致用也；利用安身，以崇德也。」

書
柔遠能邇，惇德允元，而難任人。
厥貢惟球、琳、琅玕。浮于積石，至于龍門、西河，會于渭汭。織皮崐崘、析支、渠搜，西戎即叙。
translation_en:
… proceeds in accordance with the times, and therefore enjoys supreme success.

He who knows the Way of transformation and change surely knows what is done by the spirit!

The Book of Changes says: "Unsettled in going and coming, only friends follow your thoughts." The Master said: "In the world, what need is there for thought and what need for anxiety? In the world, all return to the same destination though by different paths, and reach one goal through a hundred deliberations. In the world, what need is there for thought and what need for anxiety? When the sun goes, the moon comes; when the moon goes, the sun comes. The sun and moon impel each other, and light is born therefrom. When cold goes, heat comes; when heat goes, cold comes. Cold and heat impel each other, and the year is completed therefrom. What goes contracts; what comes expands. Contraction and expansion act upon each other, and benefit is born therefrom. The inchworm contracts in order to seek expansion; dragons and snakes hibernate in order to preserve their bodies. Investigating righteousness to the finest point until entering the realm of the spirit is how one attains practical application; benefiting from practical application and securing the person is how one exalts virtue."

Book of Documents (Shu)

Be gracious to the distant and cultivate the near; give weight to the virtuous, place trust in the good, and reject artful flatterers.

Its tribute consists of fine jades—qiu, lin, and langgan. One floats from Jishi down to Longmen and the Western River (Xihe), meeting at the confluence of the Wei (Weirui). Felt and furs come from Kunlun, Xizhi, and Qusou; the Western Rong submit to order.

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
旁作穆穆迓衡
公其惟時成周建無窮之基亦有無窮
之聞子孫訓其成式惟乂嗚呼罔曰
弗克惟既厥心罔曰民寡惟慎厥事
欽若先王成烈以休于前政
詩
要之襋之好人服之好人提提宛然左
辟
===
維其有章矣是以有慶矣
清酒既載騂牡既備以享以祀以介景
福瑟彼柞棫民所燎矣豈弟君子神
所勞矣莫莫葛藟施于條枚豈弟君
子求福不回
俾民稼穡有稷有黍有稻有秬奄有下
土纘禹之緒后稷之孫實維大王居
岐之陽實始翦商至于文武纘大王
punctuated:
旁作穆穆，迓衡。
公其惟時成周，建無窮之基，亦有無窮之聞，子孫訓其成式惟乂。嗚呼！罔曰弗克，惟既厥心；罔曰民寡，惟慎厥事。欽若先王成烈，以休于前政。
詩
要之襋之，好人服之。好人提提，宛然左辟。
維其有章矣，是以有慶矣。
清酒既載，騂牡既備，以享以祀，以介景福。瑟彼柞棫，民所燎矣；豈弟君子，神所勞矣。莫莫葛藟，施于條枚；豈弟君子，求福不回。
俾民稼穡，有稷有黍，有稻有秬。奄有下土，纘禹之緒。后稷之孫，實維大王，居岐之陽，實始翦商。至于文武，纘大王
translation_en:
“In all directions exert a reverent harmony, to welcome an even balance of government.”

“May you, O Duke, constantly think of Chengzhou, establishing an endless foundation and likewise possessing endless renown, so that your descendants will follow your completed pattern and bring about good order. Oh! Do not say that you are unable; only exhaust your heart. Do not say that the people are few; only be cautious in your affairs. Reverently accord with the accomplished achievements of the former kings, so as to bring glory to the administration of your predecessor.”

Classic of Poetry (Shi)

“She makes the waistband, she makes the collar; the fine person wears it. The fine person is dignified and composed; courteously he steps aside to the left.”

“Because he possesses elegance and refinement, therefore prosperity is his.”

“The clear wine is already in the vessels, the red bull is ready, with which to make offerings and to sacrifice, so as to increase great blessings. Luxuriant are those oaks and scrub-oaks, which the people gather for firewood; the joyous and easygoing lord is he whom the spirits comfort and reward. Dense and luxuriant are the creepers and vines, spreading over the branches and stems; the joyous and easygoing lord seeks blessings without perversity.”

“He taught the people to sow and reap, and there were panicled millet and glutinous millet, rice and black millet. Covering the whole land below, he continued the work of Yu. Among the descendants of Hou Ji there was King Tai, who dwelt on the southern slope of Mount Qi and first began to clip the wings of Shang. Down to Kings Wen and Wu, they continued King Tai’s…”

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之緒
春秋
齊人侵我西鄙公追齊師至酅弗及〔僖公〕
〔二十六年〕公會齊侯于夾谷〔定公十年〕
天王使宰渠伯糾來聘〔桓公四年〕天王使仍
叔之子來聘〔桓公五年〕秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕晉
侯伐秦〔文公四年〕
楚人伐鄭〔僖公元年〕齊侯宋公江人黃人盟
===
于貫〔僖公二年〕遂伐楚盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕
楚人陳侯蔡侯鄭伯許男圍宋〔僖公二十〕
〔七年〕晉侯齊師宋師秦師及楚人戰于
城濮楚師敗績〔僖公二十八年〕楚人圍江
晉陽處父帥師伐楚以救江〔文公三年〕

劉〔襄公十五年〕公如晉至河乃復仲孫
何忌及邾子盟于拔〔定公三年〕
punctuated:
之緒。
《春秋》
齊人侵我西鄙，公追齊師至酅，弗及〔僖公二十六年〕；公會齊侯于夾谷〔定公十年〕。
天王使宰渠伯糾來聘〔桓公四年〕；天王使仍叔之子來聘〔桓公五年〕；秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕；晉侯伐秦〔文公四年〕。
楚人伐鄭〔僖公元年〕；齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人盟于貫〔僖公二年〕；遂伐楚，盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕；楚人、陳侯、蔡侯、鄭伯、許男圍宋〔僖公二十七年〕；晉侯、齊師、宋師、秦師及楚人戰于城濮，楚師敗績〔僖公二十八年〕；楚人圍江；晉陽處父帥師伐楚以救江〔文公三年〕。
公及晉侯盟于長樗〔襄公三年〕；及向戌盟于劉〔襄公十五年〕；公如晉，至河乃復；仲孫何忌及邾子盟于拔〔定公三年〕。
translation_en:
… enterprise.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

The people of Qi invaded our western frontier; the Duke pursued the Qi army to Xi, but did not overtake it [26th year of Duke Xi]. The Duke met with the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu [10th year of Duke Ding].

The Heavenly King sent the Grand Administrator (Zai) Qu Bojiu to come on a mission of friendly inquiry [4th year of Duke Huan]. The Heavenly King sent the son of Reng Shu to come on a mission of friendly inquiry [5th year of Duke Huan]. The people of Qin attacked Jin [3rd year of Duke Wen]. The Marquis of Jin attacked Qin [4th year of Duke Wen].

The people of Chu attacked Zheng [1st year of Duke Xi]. The Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the people of Jiang, and the people of Huang made a covenant at Guan [2nd year of Duke Xi]. Thereupon they attacked Chu and made a covenant at Shaoling [4th year of Duke Xi]. The people of Chu, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, and the Baron of Xu besieged Song [27th year of Duke Xi]. The Marquis of Jin, the Qi army, the Song army, and the Qin army fought with the people of Chu at Chengpu; the Chu army was utterly defeated [28th year of Duke Xi]. The people of Chu besieged Jiang; Yang Chufu of Jin led an army to attack Chu in order to rescue Jiang [3rd year of Duke Wen].

The Duke and the Marquis of Jin made a covenant at Changchu [3rd year of Duke Xiang]. [He] made a covenant with Xiang Xu at Liu [15th year of Duke Xiang]. The Duke went to Jin, but upon reaching the Yellow River returned; Zhongsun Heji and the Viscount of Zhu made a covenant at Ba [3rd year of Duke Ding].

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
禮記
郊血大饗腥三獻爓一獻孰至敬不饗
味而貴氣臭也諸侯為賓灌用鬱鬯
灌用臭也大饗尚腶脩而已矣
物至知知然後好惡形焉
仁者右也道者左也仁者人也道者義
也厚於仁者薄於義親而不尊厚於
義者薄於仁尊而不親
===
一馬從二馬三馬既立請慶多馬
第貳場
論
致治之法垂於萬世
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢章帝至魯祠孔子詔
擬唐高宗以狄仁傑為侍御史誥
擬宋賜進士呂溱等瓊林宴及大學篇
punctuated:
《禮記》：
「郊血，大饗腥，三獻爓，一獻孰。至敬不饗味而貴氣臭也。諸侯為賓，灌用鬱鬯，灌用臭也。大饗，尚腶脩而已矣。」
「物至知知，然後好惡形焉。」
「仁者右也，道者左也。仁者人也，道者義也。厚於仁者薄於義，親而不尊；厚於義者薄於仁，尊而不親。」
「一馬從二馬。」「三馬既立，請慶多馬。」

第貳場：
論：
「致治之法垂於萬世」
詔、誥、表〔內科一道〕：
擬漢章帝至魯祠孔子詔
擬唐高宗以狄仁傑為侍御史誥
擬宋賜進士呂溱等瓊林宴及《大學》篇
translation_en:
Record of Rites (Liji):
"At the suburban sacrifice, raw blood is offered; at the great ancestral sacrifice, raw flesh; at the sacrifice of three libations, parboiled flesh; at the sacrifice of one libation, thoroughly cooked flesh. The utmost reverence does not savor flavor, but prizes the vital breath and fragrance. When the feudal lords are treated as guests, the libation is made with fragrant black-millet wine; this libation employs fragrance. At a great banquet of feudal lords, spiced dried meat is given pride of place, and nothing more."
"When things arrive and the mind's faculty of knowing knows them, only then do likes and dislikes take shape therein."
"Benevolence is the right; the Way is the left. Benevolence is humanity; the Way is righteousness. One who is generous in benevolence is sparing in righteousness, and so is loved with affection but not revered; one who is generous in righteousness is sparing in benevolence, and so is revered but not loved with affection."
"Let the single horse follow the two horses." "Since all three horses have now been set up, I beg to offer congratulations on your abundance of horses."

Second Session:
Discourse:
"The methods for bringing about order are handed down to ten thousand generations."
Imperial Edict, Patent of Appointment, and Memorial (choose one):
An Imperial Edict in imitation of Emperor Zhang of Han on arriving in Lu to sacrifice to Confucius.
A Patent of Appointment in imitation of Emperor Gaozong of Tang appointing Di Renjie as Attendant Censor.
A Memorial of Thanks in imitation of the metropolitan graduates (jinshi) of the Song dynasty, Lü Zhen and others, upon being granted the Qionglin Banquet and the "Great Learning" (Daxue) chapter…

===

策
