title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承尊崇孔子之道表章朱子之書然
太祖高皇帝大誥三編何多載當時臣民之
惡而鮮及其善豈别有勸善之典歟
太宗文皇帝為善陰騭孝順事實何備載古
今善孝之實而無所示戒豈以當時
人皆知勸善歟
宣宗章皇帝纂集五倫書亦與小學明倫篇
所述五倫之義同矣然春秋所書關
===
於五倫者果何所見歟為善陰騭孝
順事實所載善孝之事亦與春秋傳
所紀魏顆從治考叔遺羹之類同矣
然小學所述及乎陰德孝行者果何
所指歟諸士子樂育庠序誦習
聖訓久矣幸相與言之
問聖人以天下無不可為之事無不可
化之人盖理無事不有以理應事則
punctuated:
列聖相承，尊崇孔子之道，表章朱子之書。然太祖高皇帝《大誥》三編，何多載當時臣民之惡，而鮮及其善？豈别有勸善之典歟？太宗文皇帝《為善陰騭》、《孝順事實》，何備載古今善孝之實，而無所示戒？豈以當時人皆知勸善歟？宣宗章皇帝纂集《五倫書》，亦與《小學》〈明倫篇〉所述五倫之義同矣；然《春秋》所書關於五倫者，果何所見歟？《為善陰騭》、《孝順事實》所載善孝之事，亦與《春秋傳》所紀魏顆從治、考叔遺羹之類同矣；然《小學》所述及乎陰德、孝行者，果何所指歟？諸士子樂育庠序，誦習聖訓久矣，幸相與言之。
問：聖人以天下無不可為之事，無不可化之人。盖理無事不有，以理應事，則
translation_en:
…the successive sagely emperors have inherited one another's legacy, revering the Way of Confucius (Kongzi 孔子) and honoring and promoting the books of Master Zhu (Zhuzi 朱子, Zhu Xi 朱熹). Yet why do the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao 大誥) of Emperor Gao, the Grand Progenitor (Taizu Gao Huangdi 太祖高皇帝, the Hongwu Emperor), mostly record the evil deeds of officials and commoners of that time while rarely touching upon their good deeds? Could it be that there were separate canons for encouraging goodness? And why do the Unseen Rewards for Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi 為善陰騭) and True Accounts of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi 孝順事實) of Emperor Wen, the Grand Ancestor (Taizong Wen Huangdi 太宗文皇帝, the Yongle Emperor), fully record true instances of goodness and filiality from antiquity to the present without setting forth warnings? Could it be because people of that time all knew to encourage one another in goodness? The Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu 五倫書), compiled by Emperor Zhang, the Proclaiming Ancestor (Xuanzong Zhang Huangdi 宣宗章皇帝, the Xuande Emperor), is likewise identical in meaning to the Five Human Relationships expounded in the "Clarifying Human Relationships" (Minglun 明倫) chapter of the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue 小學); yet where indeed can one see entries in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋) that pertain to the Five Human Relationships? The deeds of goodness and filiality recorded in Unseen Rewards for Doing Good and True Accounts of Filial Piety are likewise akin to such accounts in the Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu zhuan 春秋傳) as Wei Ke 魏顆 following his father's lucid command and Ying Kaoshu 穎考叔 setting aside soup for his mother; yet what specifically do the passages in the Elementary Learning that touch upon unseen virtue and filial conduct refer to? You scholars have long been happily nurtured in the local schools, reciting and studying the sagely instructions; please set forth your views on these matters together.

Question: The sages held that in the world there is no affair that cannot be accomplished and no person who cannot be transformed. For principle is present in every affair; if one responds to affairs with principle, then…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
事無不可為性無人不善以善自治
則無不可改過也稽之於事囂訟不
肖子之世殄矣何卒使授受得中而
天下治平歟汨陳五行父之功隳矣
何卒使六府孔脩而萬世永賴歟並
告無辜民心已失何遽有兆民允懷
之休百姓有過民心已乖何遽有萬
姓悅服之效流言不利避位居東何
===
以致王出郊新逆兩相相揖齊人鼓
譟何以致來歸鄆讙龜陰田此皆聖
人已行之事也可詳其所處之實歟
驗之於人頑囂與敖似不可化而卒
致不格姦亦允若何歟侮慢自賢似
不可格矣而卒致丕叙來格何歟兹
乃不義習與性成何以使克終允德
弗造哲迪民康何以使教化大行質
punctuated: 事無不可為；性無人不善，以善自治，則無不可改過也。稽之於事：囂訟不肖，子之世殄矣，何卒使授受得中而天下治平歟？汨陳五行，父之功隳矣，何卒使六府孔脩而萬世永賴歟？並告無辜，民心已失，何遽有「兆民允懷」之休？百姓有過，民心已乖，何遽有「萬姓悅服」之效？流言不利，避位居東，何以致王出郊親迎？兩相相揖，齊人鼓譟，何以致來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田？此皆聖人已行之事也，可詳其所處之實歟？驗之於人：頑囂與傲，似不可化，而卒致「不格姦」、「亦允若」，何歟？侮慢自賢，似不可格矣，而卒致「丕叙」、「來格」，何歟？「兹乃不義，習與性成」，何以使「克終允德」？「弗造哲，迪民康」，何以使教化大行？質…
translation_en:
…there is no affair that cannot be accomplished; since there is no person whose nature is not good, if one governs oneself with goodness, there is no one who cannot reform their faults.

If we examine this in terms of affairs: When a son was quarrelsome and unworthy [i.e., Yao's son Danzhu], the succession through his own line was cut off; how did [Yao] finally bring it about that the transmission and reception of the throne attained the Mean and the empire was well-governed and at peace? When the Five Elements were thrown into disorder, a father's [i.e., Gun's] work was ruined; how did [Yu] finally bring it about that the Six Treasuries were greatly ordered and ten thousand generations could forever rely on them? When the people all cried out in their innocence [under Jie], the hearts of the populace had already been lost; how did [Tang] so suddenly achieve the blessing of "the millions of people truly cherishing him"? When "the hundred surnames had faults" [as King Wu took responsibility for them], the hearts of the people had already been alienated [under Zhou]; how did he so suddenly achieve the effect of "the myriad surnames submitting with joy"? When rumors were unfavorable [to the Duke of Zhou] and he withdrew from his position to reside in the east, how did this lead to the King [Cheng] going out to the suburbs to welcome him in person [reading 新逆 as 親迎]? When the two ministers bowed to each other and the men of Qi raised an uproar [at the Jiagu meeting], how did [Confucius] bring it about that they came to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin? These are all affairs already carried out by the sages; can you explain in detail the realities of how they handled them?

If we test this in terms of people: Being obstinate, deceitful, and arrogant [like Shun's parents and half-brother Xiang], they seemed impossible to transform, yet in the end they were brought to "not reach wickedness" and "also truly be in harmony"—why was this? Being insolent and self-conceited [like the Miao], they seemed impossible to correct, yet in the end they were brought to "great order" and "coming to submit"—why was this? Of one of whom it was said, "This is unrighteousness; habit has become his nature" [King Taijia], how did [Yi Yin] cause him to "be able in the end to be truly virtuous"? Of one of whom it was said, "He does not make himself wise to lead the people to tranquility" [Kangshu's charge regarding the people of Yin], how was it caused that moral transformation greatly prevailed? Simple…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
魯貨殖之徒性行非不偏也若何而
卒聞一以貫之之道大師亞飯之流
典樂非不久也若何而知踰河蹈海
以去此皆聖人已化之人也可詳其
感之之由歟諸士子窮經致用當以
聖人為法願著于篇以觀處事正人
之學
問士君子以一身之微繫天下之觀望
===
也大矣故善為治者必因衆望之所
向乘其機以用其人則往無不濟而
功無不成焉稽之於古如衆望在循
吏用之則郡國稱治衆望在舊臣用
之則江東歸心負節義之重望者一
用則盜賊請降負勲德之重名者一
用則回紇羅拜至若東廣先正有舉
道侔伊吕者用之則能抑姦辦賊有
punctuated:
魯、貨殖之徒，性行非不偏也，若何而卒聞「一以貫之」之道？大師、亞飯之流，典樂非不久也，若何而知踰河蹈海以去？此皆聖人已化之人也，可詳其感之之由歟？諸士子窮經致用，當以聖人為法，願著于篇，以觀處事正人之學。

問：士君子以一身之微，繫天下之觀望也大矣。故善為治者，必因衆望之所向，乘其機以用其人，則往無不濟而功無不成焉。稽之於古，如衆望在循吏，用之則郡國稱治；衆望在舊臣，用之則江東歸心；負節義之重望者，一用則盜賊請降；負勲德之重名者，一用則回紇羅拜。至若東廣先正，有舉「道侔伊呂」者，用之則能抑姦辦賊；有
translation_en:
… was dull-witted and the one who engaged in commercial speculation [i.e., Zeng Shen 曾參 and Zigong 子貢] were certainly not without biases in their natures and conduct; how was it that in the end they came to hear the Way of "one thread binding it all together"? Those such as the Grand Music Master and the musician of the second meal had been in charge of music for no short time; how was it that they knew to cross the Yellow River and tread the sea to depart? These are all people whom the sages transformed; can you detail the reasons whereby they moved them? You scholars, in exhaustively studying the Classics for practical application, ought to take the sages as your model. Please set this forth in your essays, so that we may observe your learning in handling affairs and rectifying men.

Question: Though a scholar-gentleman is but a single, humble individual, the expectations of the world that rest upon him are great indeed. Therefore, those who excel at governance must follow the direction of popular expectations, seizing the opportune moment to employ such men; then wherever they go nothing will fail to succeed, and no achievement will fail to be accomplished. Examining antiquity: when popular expectations rested upon upright officials, employing them brought praise for good governance across the commanderies and kingdoms; when popular expectations rested upon veteran ministers, employing them caused the region east of the Yangtze (Jiangdong 江東) to submit in heart; when one bearing high renown for integrity and righteousness was once employed, bandits and rebels begged to surrender; when one bearing a weighty reputation for meritorious virtue was once employed, the Uyghurs (Huihe 回紇) lined up to bow in homage. As for the former worthies of eastern Guangdong (Dongguang 東廣): there was one recommended as "matching Yi Yin 伊尹 and Lü Shang 呂尚 in the Way" [Zhang Jiuling 張九齡], who, when employed, was able to suppress the treacherous and deal with rebels; there was one…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
文學知名者用之則能論諫舉職有
負恬退清節者用之則兵民悅服是
人望誠有益於人國也方今近而望
於一鄉大而望於一方又大而望於
天下若循吏若舊士若節義若勳德
小大不遺彼此兼錄宜乎臻其效矣
而何郡國間有愁嘆之聲而邊徼尚
有竊發之患哉豈用之者未得其望
===
而所望者未見於用歟抑用所望而
又參以非所望者故掣肘矛盾而然
歟抑別有其故歟伊欲用其眾所望
去其非所望者徵於聖賢之言當以
何者而為其進退之機乎諸士子皆
達於時務者其言之毋隱
問古先聖王之治天下莫不以治歷明
時為先務故曆法之制代代有之然
punctuated:
文學知名者，用之則能論諫舉職；有負恬退清節者，用之則兵民悅服。是人望誠有益於人國也。方今近而望於一鄉，大而望於一方，又大而望於天下，若循吏、若舊士、若節義、若勳德，小大不遺，彼此兼錄，宜乎臻其效矣。而何郡國間有愁嘆之聲，而邊徼尚有竊發之患哉？豈用之者未得其望，而所望者未見於用歟？抑用所望而又參以非所望者，故掣肘矛盾而然歟？抑別有其故歟？伊欲用其眾所望，去其非所望者，徵於聖賢之言，當以何者而為其進退之機乎？諸士子皆達於時務者，其言之毋隱。
問：古先聖王之治天下，莫不以治歷明時為先務，故曆法之制代代有之。然
translation_en:
…renowned for literary learning, who when employed could remonstrate and fulfill his duties; and there was one who possessed a reputation for quiet retirement and pure integrity, who when employed won the joyful submission of soldiers and civilians alike. Thus popular esteem is truly beneficial to a state. At present, from those esteemed locally within a single district, to those esteemed more broadly across a region, and still more broadly across the entire realm—whether upright officials, veteran scholars, men of principle and righteousness, or men of meritorious virtue—none, great or small, are overlooked, and all are employed together. Surely this ought to have achieved its full effect! Why then are sounds of grief and sighing still occasionally heard in the commanderies and principalities, and why are there still outbreaks of banditry along the frontiers? Could it be that those who are employed have not earned such esteem, while those who are esteemed have not yet been put to use? Or is it that those who are esteemed are employed alongside those who are not, resulting in mutual hindrance and contradiction? Or is there some other reason? If one wishes to employ those whom the multitude esteems and remove those whom they do not, when we verify this against the words of the sages and worthies, what should serve as the decisive criterion for advancing or dismissing them? All you gentlemen are well-versed in current affairs; speak of this and hold nothing back.

Question: When the ancient sage-kings governed the realm, none failed to make regulating the calendar and clarifying the seasons their first priority; therefore, calendrical systems have existed in every dynasty. Yet…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
昉於何時漢曆凡五變唐曆凡八變
宋曆凡十變而孰為最優此外又有
可取者誰歟治曆之法以置閏為急
而氣盈朔虛之旨何在推測之要以
正閏分而正數成數之言何別有因
造曆而始悟其謬者又誰歟曆書不
過乎二十四氣一氣之運行固有序
也而每月何以有曰節曰中之分四
===
時曰立固有理也何春秋曰分而夏
冬曰至乎穀雨芒種以穀麥言也何
置之於三月五月之中驚蟄清明以
風雷言也何居於二月三月之內暑
行於春夏而夏至則暑已極何夏至
後乃有小暑大暑耶寒運於秋冬而
冬至則寒已盡何冬至後乃為小寒
大寒耶露一也何以有寒白之分雪
punctuated: 昉於何時？漢曆凡五變，唐曆凡八變，宋曆凡十變，而孰為最優？此外又有可取者，誰歟？治曆之法以置閏為急，而氣盈朔虛之旨何在？推測之要以正閏分，而正數、成數之言何別？有因造曆而始悟其謬者，又誰歟？曆書不過乎二十四氣，一氣之運行固有序也，而每月何以有曰節、曰中之分？四時曰「立」，固有理也，何春秋曰「分」而夏冬曰「至」乎？穀雨、芒種以穀、麥言也，何置之於三月、五月之中？驚蟄、清明以風、雷言也，何居於二月、三月之內？暑行於春夏，而夏至則暑已極，何夏至後乃有小暑、大暑耶？寒運於秋冬，而冬至則寒已盡，何冬至後乃為小寒、大寒耶？露一也，何以有寒、白之分？雪…
translation_en: …when did it first originate? The calendar of the Han dynasty underwent five reforms in all, the calendar of the Tang underwent eight, and the calendar of the Song underwent ten; which among them was the most superior? Beyond these, who else devised calendars worthy of adoption? In the method of regulating the calendar, the insertion of intercalary months is of the utmost urgency; wherein lies the principle of the solar excess (qiying) and the lunar deficiency (shuoxu)? The essentials of astronomical calculation are divided between regular and intercalary periods; what is the distinction between the terms "regular numbers" (zhengshu) and "completed numbers" (chengshu)? And who was it that only realized his own errors upon actually constructing a calendar? Calendrical treatises go no further than the twenty-four solar terms (qi). The revolution of a single vital breath (qi) certainly follows an order, yet why is there a division within every month between what is called a "nodal" term (jie) and a "medial" term (zhong)? That the beginnings of the four seasons are called "Establishment" (li) certainly has its principle, yet why are the midpoints of spring and autumn called "Equinox" (fen, division) while those of summer and winter are called "Solstice" (zhi, extreme)? "Grain Rain" (Guyu) and "Grain in Ear" (Mangzhong) are named with reference to grain and wheat; why are they placed in the middle of the third and fifth months? "Awakening of Insects" (Jingzhe) and "Pure Brightness" (Qingming) are named with reference to wind and thunder; why do they reside within the second and third months? Heat moves through spring and summer, and by the Summer Solstice heat has already reached its peak; why then are "Lesser Heat" (Xiaoshu) and "Greater Heat" (Dashu) placed after the Summer Solstice? Cold circulates through autumn and winter, and by the Winter Solstice cold has already reached its limit; why then do "Lesser Cold" (Xiaohan) and "Greater Cold" (Dahan) come after the Winter Solstice? Dew is one and the same; why is there a distinction between "Cold Dew" (Hanlu) and "White Dew" (Bailu)? Snow…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
一也何以有小大之異小指陰道而
言也以小滿居四月之中者何義暑
積陽氣而成者也以處暑在七月之
中者何取以至立雨水於立春之後
介霜降於寒露之餘亦豈無其義哉
凡此皆變化之道神之所為者也博
洽之士必能言之而他日任調元賛
化燮理陰陽之責庶乎有以覘之矣
===
幸毋多讓
問農桑衣食之源民生至急一夫不耕
或受之飢一女不織或受之寒飢寒
迫身而放僻邪侈無所不至雖慈父
不能保其子况君之於民乎故聖王
知其然使民男有餘粟女有餘布生
長老死於仁政者其道何由後世使
民膏粱者不耕而耕者糲飯不充文
punctuated:
一也，何以有小、大之異？小，指陰道而言也，以小滿居四月之中者，何義？暑，積陽氣而成者也，以處暑在七月之中者，何取？以至立雨水於立春之後，介霜降於寒露之餘，亦豈無其義哉？凡此皆變化之道，神之所為者也。博洽之士，必能言之，而他日任調元賛化、燮理陰陽之責，庶乎有以覘之矣。幸毋多讓。

問：農桑衣食之源，民生至急。一夫不耕，或受之飢；一女不織，或受之寒。飢寒迫身，而放僻邪侈，無所不至，雖慈父不能保其子，况君之於民乎？故聖王知其然，使民男有餘粟，女有餘布，生長老死於仁政者，其道何由？後世使民膏粱者不耕，而耕者糲飯不充；文
translation_en:
…is one and the same; why is there a difference between Lesser Snow (Xiaoxue) and Greater Snow (Daxue)? "Lesser" (xiao) refers to the Way of Yin; what is the meaning of placing Lesser Fullness (Xiaoman) in the middle of the fourth month? Heat (shu) is formed by the accumulation of Yang vital force (qi); what is the basis for placing Limit of Heat (Chushu) in the middle of the seventh month? And when it comes to establishing Rain Water (Yushui) after Beginning of Spring (Lichun), and interposing Frost's Descent (Shuangjiang) after Cold Dew (Hanlu), how could these also be without meaning? All of these belong to the Way of transformation and change, the workings of the numinous. Scholars of broad learning must be able to explain them; and on a future day when you bear the responsibility of harmonizing the primordial forces, assisting in cosmic transformation, and blending and regulating Yin and Yang, perhaps we may have a means to observe your capacity through this. Pray do not be overly modest.

Question: Farming and sericulture are the source of clothing and food, the most urgent matters for the people's livelihood. If one man does not plow, someone may suffer hunger because of it; if one woman does not weave, someone may suffer cold because of it. When hunger and cold press upon the body, people stop at nothing in reckless, perverse, depraved, and extravagant conduct; even a loving father cannot guarantee the conduct of his son, how much less a ruler that of his people? Therefore, the sage-kings knew this to be so, and caused the people—men having surplus grain and women having surplus cloth—to be born, grow up, grow old, and die under benevolent governance; by what way was this achieved? In later ages, the people have been caused to live such that those who eat fine grain and rich meat do not plow, while those who plow do not have enough coarse rice to fill themselves; those who wear patterned…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
織者不蠶而蠶者桓褐不足天地生
生之仁幾乎息矣其失何自逮我
聖明撫有四海考課之法守令以農桑為首
版籍所載民戶以事産為先而
大誥又有互知丁業之條其重農之意可
謂詳且至矣宜乎無飢寒之民也柰
何太平既久風俗日侈務本者少趨
末者多彼游於緇黃游於商賈游於
===
市井官宦游於廝役技藝皆資給於
吾農者一人耕百人食一女織百人
衣欲其不飢不寒得乎伊欲盡使歸
農則流弊已久於勢或有不可欲聽
其自便則民日益貧於理在所當憂
此民生之至急不可不究心也諸士
子抱藝而來必有能處之者請為我
言之
punctuated: 織者不蠶，而蠶者桓褐不足，天地生生之仁幾乎息矣，其失何自？逮我聖明撫有四海，考課之法，守令以農桑為首；版籍所載，民戶以事産為先；而《大誥》又有互知丁業之條。其重農之意，可謂詳且至矣，宜乎無飢寒之民也。柰何太平既久，風俗日侈，務本者少，趨末者多。彼游於緇黃、游於商賈、游於市井官宦、游於廝役技藝，皆資給於吾農者。一人耕，百人食；一女織，百人衣。欲其不飢不寒，得乎？伊欲盡使歸農，則流弊已久，於勢或有不可；欲聽其自便，則民日益貧，於理在所當憂。此民生之至急，不可不究心也。諸士子抱藝而來，必有能處之者，請為我言之。
translation_en:
…those who wear patterned silks do not raise silkworms, while those who raise silkworms do not have enough coarse woolens [? 桓褐, likely for 短褐]—the life-giving benevolence of Heaven and Earth has nearly ceased! Where did this failing originate?

Coming down to our Sacred and Enlightened Dynasty, which holds and pacifies the Four Seas: in the regulations for personnel evaluation, prefects and magistrates have agriculture and sericulture placed first; in what is recorded in the population and tax registers, civilian households have their occupational livelihood and property placed foremost; and the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao) furthermore contain an article requiring mutual knowledge of adult males' occupations. Its intention in emphasizing agriculture may be called detailed and thorough indeed, so it ought to be that there are no hungry or cold people. Why is it, then, that after a long period of peace, customs have grown daily more extravagant, so that few attend to the fundamental occupation while many pursue secondary ones? Those who drift into the ranks of Buddhist monks and Daoist priests, who drift into commerce and trade, who drift into the marketplaces and officialdom's retinues, or who drift into menial service and crafts—all of them depend on our farmers for their supply. When one man plows and a hundred eat, when one woman weaves and a hundred are clothed, even if one wishes them not to go hungry or cold, is that possible?

If we wish to make them all return to agriculture, the accumulated abuses have lasted so long that in practical terms it may be impossible; yet if we wish to let them do as they please, the people will grow poorer day by day, which in principle is something we must worry about. This is the most urgent matter of the people's livelihood, to which we cannot fail to devote careful thought. You gentlemen have come bearing your learning and skills; there must be those among you capable of dealing with this. Please set it forth for me.

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人七十五名
第一名鄧應仁南海縣學生書
第二名楊季芳番禺縣學生詩
第三名蒲鋼南海縣學生易
第四名沈璣潮州府學生春秋
第五名何津南海縣學增廣生禮記
第六名王淮惠州府學生易
===
第七名周叙廣州府學生詩
第八名霍扆順德縣學增廣生禮記
第九名歐敞博羅縣學生書
第十名曹鼎海陽縣學軍生春秋
第十一名何綸順德縣學生詩
第十二名戴昌言德慶州學生易
第十三名李經綸德慶州學生書
第十四名蔡軾東莞縣儒士詩
punctuated:
中式舉人七十五名：

第一名，鄧應仁，南海縣學生，《書》。
第二名，楊季芳，番禺縣學生，《詩》。
第三名，蒲鋼，南海縣學生，《易》。
第四名，沈璣，潮州府學生，《春秋》。
第五名，何津，南海縣學增廣生，《禮記》。
第六名，王淮，惠州府學生，《易》。
第七名，周叙，廣州府學生，《詩》。
第八名，霍扆，順德縣學增廣生，《禮記》。
第九名，歐敞，博羅縣學生，《書》。
第十名，曹鼎，海陽縣學軍生，《春秋》。

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
四書義
子曰聽訟吾猶人也必也使無訟乎無情者不
得盡其辭大畏民志此謂知本
鄧應仁
同考試官教諭林批作此題者多分截不明且於
本末先後處體認不切求其理
明辭確僅見此篇是宜錄出
考試官教諭鄭批大學本末先後之義發明
殆盡
===
考試官學正王批辭簡理明
大賢引聖人之言而推言其本所以釋本末之先後
也盖聽訟末也明明德而使民無訟本也大賢引聖
言而推本言之則明德新民之本末先後可知矣昔
曽子傳大學引夫子之言謂夫民情有欲則争不能
以無訟也然因其訟而辨其是非因其争而斷其曲
直吾固無異於人也此但治其末塞其流耳必也正
其本使民利欲之争息而自無訟可聽焉清其源使
民情欲之感正而自無訟可辨焉曽子引之於此而
punctuated:
四書義

子曰：「聽訟，吾猶人也。必也使無訟乎！」無情者不得盡其辭。大畏民志，此謂知本。

鄧應仁

同考試官教諭林批：作此題者，多分截不明，且於本末先後處體認不切。求其理明辭確，僅見此篇，是宜錄出。

考試官教諭鄭批：《大學》本末先後之義，發明殆盡。

考試官學正王批：辭簡理明。

大賢引聖人之言而推言其本，所以釋本末之先後也。盖聽訟，末也；明明德而使民無訟，本也。大賢引聖言而推本言之，則明德、新民之本末先後可知矣。昔曽子傳《大學》，引夫子之言，謂夫民情有欲則争，不能以無訟也。然因其訟而辨其是非，因其争而斷其曲直，吾固無異於人也。此但治其末、塞其流耳。必也正其本，使民利欲之争息，而自無訟可聽焉；清其源，使民情欲之感正，而自無訟可辨焉。曽子引之於此，而
translation_en:
Expositions on the Four Books

The Master said, "In hearing litigation, I am like anyone else. What is necessary is to cause the people to have no litigation!" So those without genuine substance dare not exhaust their false arguments. Greatly overawing the people's minds—this is called knowing the root.

Deng Yingren 鄧應仁

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Lin: Those who wrote on this topic mostly failed to divide the sections clearly, and moreover lacked a penetrating grasp of the root and the branch, what comes first and what comes after. Looking for one whose reasoning is clear and phrasing is precise, I found only this essay; it is fitting that it be selected for publication.

Comment by Examiner Instructor Zheng: The meaning of root and branch, first and last in the Great Learning (Daxue) is expounded almost exhaustively here.

Comment by Examiner Director of Studies Wang: The language is concise and the reasoning is clear.

The Great Worthy quotes the words of the Sage and extends them to speak of their root, in order to explain the sequence of root and branch. For hearing litigation is the branch; illustrating illustrious virtue and thereby causing the people to have no litigation is the root. When the Great Worthy quotes the Sage's words and traces them back to the root, the root and branch, the first and last, of illustrating virtue and renewing the people can thus be known. In the past, when Master Zeng (Zengzi 曾子) transmitted the Great Learning, he quoted the Master's words, saying that because the feelings of the people have desires, they contend with one another, and thus cannot be without litigation. Yet in distinguishing right and wrong on the basis of their litigation, and judging crooked and straight on the basis of their contention, I am indeed no different from anyone else. This is merely treating the branch and damming the stream. What is necessary is to rectify the root, causing the people's contentions over profit and desire to cease, so that naturally there will be no litigation to hear; and to cleanse the source, causing the stirrings of the people's feelings and desires to become upright, so that naturally there will be no litigation to distinguish. Master Zeng quotes this here, and…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
夫訟之不息由無情者得以盡其辭也聖人能使無
實之人不敢盡其虛誕之辭盖我之明德既明自然
有以大服乎人之心故訟之曲直不待聽而自無矣
我之德盛仁熟自然有以大畏乎民之志故訟之是
非不待辨而自息矣觀於此言則知明德為本而在
所當先新民為末而在所當後矣所謂本末先後之
義豈不著明矣乎抑嘗考之虞舜好生之德洽于民
心故民協于中而不犯于有司文王徽柔懿恭之德
光于四方故虞芮爭田而不敢履其庭是皆聖人明
===
德新民止於至善而使民無訟者也欲盡大學之道
者可不以聖人為法乎
子入太廟每事問或曰孰謂鄹人之子知禮乎
入太廟每事問子聞之曰是禮也
楊季芳
同考試官教諭陳批此題本平易作者多於每事
問處講說不明唯此篇辭理俱
到宜表而出之
考試官教諭鄭批識理明白而文足以發之
punctuated:
夫訟之不息，由無情者得以盡其辭也。聖人能使無實之人不敢盡其虛誕之辭，盖我之明德既明，自然有以大服乎人之心，故訟之曲直不待聽而自無矣；我之德盛仁熟，自然有以大畏乎民之志，故訟之是非不待辨而自息矣。觀於此言，則知明德為本而在所當先，新民為末而在所當後矣。所謂本末先後之義，豈不著明矣乎？抑嘗考之：虞舜好生之德洽于民心，故民協于中而不犯于有司；文王徽柔懿恭之德光于四方，故虞、芮爭田而不敢履其庭。是皆聖人明德新民止於至善，而使民無訟者也。欲盡《大學》之道者，可不以聖人為法乎？

「子入太廟，每事問。或曰：『孰謂鄹人之子知禮乎？入太廟，每事問。』子聞之，曰：『是禮也。』」
楊季芳
同考試官教諭陳批：此題本平易，作者多於「每事問」處講說不明，唯此篇辭理俱到，宜表而出之。
考試官教諭鄭批：識理明白，而文足以發之。
translation_en:
… Now the reason litigation does not cease is that those devoid of truth are able to exhaust their arguments. The sage is able to make people without substance not dare to exhaust their false and absurd words. For once one's own illustrious virtue is made bright, there is naturally that by which one greatly wins the submission of people's minds, so the crooked and the straight in litigation require no hearing and are absent of themselves; once one's virtue is abundant and one's benevolence mature, there is naturally that by which one greatly awes the will of the people, so the right and wrong in litigation require no adjudication and cease of themselves. Looking at these words, one knows that making bright one's illustrious virtue is the root and ought to come first, while renewing the people is the branch and ought to come after. Is not the meaning of what are called root and branch, first and last, thus made manifest? Moreover, I have examined the past: the virtue of Yu Shun in loving life permeated the minds of the people, and therefore the people conformed to the mean and did not offend against the authorities; the fine, gentle, admirable, and reverent virtue of King Wen shone throughout the four quarters, and therefore when Yu and Rui disputed over fields, they did not dare to tread his court. These were both cases in which the sages, in making bright their illustrious virtue and renewing the people, rested in the highest good and caused the people to have no litigation. Can those who wish to fulfill the Way of the Great Learning (Daxue) fail to take the sages as their model?

"The Master entered the Grand Temple and asked about everything. Someone said, 'Who says the son of the man of Zou knows ritual? On entering the Grand Temple, he asks about everything.' The Master heard of it and said, 'This is ritual.'"
By Yang Jifang 楊季芳.
Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Chen comments: This topic is inherently plain and easy, yet writers mostly fail to explain clearly the part about "asking about everything." Only this essay achieves both expression and principle; it should be singled out for publication.
Examiner Instructor Zheng comments: His understanding of principle is clear, and his writing is sufficient to bring it forth.

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正王批不拘不泛
聖人助祭而詳審其事時人譏其不知乎禮聖人言
其所以為禮盖禮者敬而已矣聖人助祭而詳審其
事者敬謹之至乃所以為禮也時人不知而譏之得
不明言以曉之哉且夫太廟魯周公廟也孔子當始
仕之時入而助祭也凡制度儀則雖已知之而必詳
問以審其事焉器物節文雖已講之而必更問以驗
其實焉聖人謹禮如此或人不知而譏之曰鄹人之
子自少以知禮聞也然知禮者不待問而問非知禮
===
者也今入太廟而每事問孰謂其知禮乎或人之譏
若此聖人聞之遂明言以曉之謂夫禮主於敬入廟而
每事問者敬之大也敬之大即禮意之所存也祭所當
謹雖知亦問者謹之至也謹之至即禮意之所在也
然則聖人謹禮之意豈或人之所知而其辭氣和平
德量宏大亦豈常人之所及哉大抵聖人所為衆人
所不識者非特此也若事君盡禮則譏其為諂諱君
之惡則疑其有黨疾固而斥以為佞正名而指以為
迂噫使無顔子以發其蘊宰我子貢稱賛其盛子思
punctuated:
考試官學正王批：不拘不泛。

聖人助祭而詳審其事，時人譏其不知乎禮，聖人言其所以為禮。盖禮者，敬而已矣。聖人助祭而詳審其事者，敬謹之至，乃所以為禮也。時人不知而譏之，得不明言以曉之哉？且夫太廟，魯周公廟也。孔子當始仕之時，入而助祭也。凡制度儀則，雖已知之，而必詳問以審其事焉；器物節文，雖已講之，而必更問以驗其實焉。聖人謹禮如此，或人不知而譏之曰：「鄹人之子，自少以知禮聞也。然知禮者不待問，而問非知禮者也。今入太廟而每事問，孰謂其知禮乎？」或人之譏若此。聖人聞之，遂明言以曉之。謂夫禮主於敬，入廟而每事問者，敬之大也，敬之大即禮意之所存也；祭所當謹，雖知亦問者，謹之至也，謹之至即禮意之所在也。然則聖人謹禮之意，豈或人之所知？而其辭氣和平、德量宏大，亦豈常人之所及哉？大抵聖人所為，衆人所不識者，非特此也。若事君盡禮，則譏其為諂；諱君之惡，則疑其有黨；疾固而斥以為佞；正名而指以為迂。噫！使無顔子以發其蘊，宰我、子貢稱賛其盛，子思、
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Wang, Subprefectural Director of Studies: Neither rigid nor diffuse.

When the Sage assisted at a sacrifice and carefully verified its details, a contemporary ridiculed him for not understanding ritual, whereupon the Sage explained why this very conduct was ritual. For ritual is simply a matter of reverence. When the Sage assisted at the sacrifice and carefully verified its details, it was the utmost of reverence and caution, and that is precisely what constitutes ritual. When a contemporary did not understand this and ridiculed him, how could he not speak plainly to enlighten him? Now the Grand Temple was the temple of the Duke of Zhou in the state of Lu. At the time when Confucius first took office, he entered it to assist at the sacrifice. Regarding all the institutional regulations and ceremonial rules, although he already knew them, he nonetheless made detailed inquiries in order to verify the procedures; regarding the ritual vessels and detailed forms, although he had already studied them, he nonetheless asked further questions in order to confirm their reality. Such was the Sage's caution in ritual, yet someone, not understanding this, ridiculed him, saying: "The son of the man from Zou has been renowned since youth for knowing ritual. Yet one who knows ritual has no need to ask, and one who asks is not someone who knows ritual. Now he enters the Grand Temple and asks about everything—who says he knows ritual?" Such was that person's ridicule. When the Sage heard of it, he thereupon spoke plainly to enlighten him. He meant that ritual is centered on reverence: entering the temple and asking about everything is the height of reverence, and the height of reverence is precisely where the spirit of ritual resides; a sacrifice is something requiring caution, and asking even when one already knows is the utmost of caution, and the utmost of caution is precisely where the meaning of ritual lies. This being so, how could that person understand the Sage's intention in being cautious about ritual? And how could ordinary people ever match the gentleness of his tone and expression, or the vastness of his moral capacity? On the whole, this was not the only instance in which the actions of the Sage were not understood by the multitude. When in serving his ruler he observed ritual to the fullest, they ridiculed him as flattering; when he concealed his ruler's faults, they suspected him of partisanship; when he detested obstinacy, they dismissed it as glibness; when he spoke of rectifying names, they pointed to it as impracticality. Alas! Had there been no Master Yan (Yan Hui 顏回) to bring forth his profound store of virtue, no Zai Wo 宰我 and Zigong 子貢 to praise his magnificence, and no Zisi 子思 and…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
孟子闡明推尊其道則後世孰從而知其聖歟
易義
直其正也方其義也君子敬以直內義以方外
敬義立而德不孤直方大不習无不利則不
疑其所行也
潘鋼
同考試官訓導郭批此題本以學言場中作者往往專
指爻辭立說殊戻本旨是篇體認
不差詞理縝密其得易之旨綮乎
===
同考試官教諭汪批此題本平易作者類多穿鑿
不合本義理明辭暢僅見此篇
取冠本房孰曰不宜
考試官教諭鄭批此作發為學之義明楚亦得旨
考試官學正王批得本義旨
文言發明坤六二之爻義必以學而言之也盖君子
之學內外兼脩則德無不盛而所行自無不順矣文
言發明坤六二之爻義而必以學言之厥旨深矣昔
吾夫子於坤之文言而申六二之象傳意謂柔順正
punctuated:
孟子闡明推尊其道，則後世孰從而知其聖歟！

易義

「直其正也，方其義也。君子敬以直內，義以方外，敬義立而德不孤。『直方大，不習无不利』，則不疑其所行也。」

潘鋼
同考試官訓導郭批：此題本以學言，場中作者往往專指爻辭立說，殊戻本旨。是篇體認不差，詞理縝密，其得《易》之旨綮乎！
同考試官教諭汪批：此題本平易，作者類多穿鑿，不合《本義》。理明辭暢，僅見此篇。取冠本房，孰曰不宜？
考試官教諭鄭批：此作發為學之義明楚，亦得旨。
考試官學正王批：得《本義》旨。

《文言》發明《坤》六二之爻義，必以學而言之也。盖君子之學，內外兼脩，則德無不盛，而所行自無不順矣。《文言》發明《坤》六二之爻義，而必以學言之，厥旨深矣。昔吾夫子於《坤》之《文言》，而申六二之《象傳》，意謂柔順正
translation_en:
… and Mencius (Mengzi) to elucidate and exalt his Way, how then would later generations have come to know his sagehood!

Exposition on the Book of Changes (Yijing)

"Straightness means its correctness; squareness means its righteousness. The noble man applies reverence to straighten the interior, and righteousness to square the exterior. When reverence and righteousness are established, virtue is not isolated. 'Straight, square, and great, without practice, nothing is unfavorable'—thus he has no doubts about what he does."

By Pan Gang 潘鋼.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Guo 郭: This topic actually speaks in terms of learning, yet writers in the examination hall often set up their arguments by referring exclusively to the line statement, which runs quite counter to the fundamental purport. This essay's comprehension is unerring, and its diction and reasoning are closely knit—surely it has grasped the essential crux of the Book of Changes!
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Wang 汪: This topic is inherently plain and accessible, yet writers mostly resort to forced interpretations that do not accord with the Original Meaning of the Book of Changes (Benyi). Clarity of principle and fluency of expression are seen only in this essay. Having selected it to head this examination ward, who would say it is inappropriate?
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zheng 鄭: This composition elucidates the meaning of pursuing learning with clarity and neatness, and also grasps the purport.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Wang 王: It grasps the purport of the Original Meaning of the Book of Changes (Benyi).

When the Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) elucidates the meaning of the Six in the Second place line of the Kun hexagram, it necessarily speaks of it in terms of learning. For when the learning of the noble man cultivates both the interior and the exterior together, his virtue is unfailingly abundant, and what he does is naturally unfailingly smooth. That the Commentary on the Words of the Text elucidates the meaning of the Six in the Second place line of Kun and necessarily speaks of it in terms of learning has a profound purport indeed. Of old, our Master, in the Commentary on the Words of the Text on Kun, expanded upon the Commentary on the Images (Xiangzhuan) for the Six in the Second place, meaning that gentle compliance and firm correctness …

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
固坤之直也而直非人心本體之正乎賦形有定坤
之方也而方非人心裁制之義乎君子人與主敬以
直其内而無委曲之私則持守之工夫至而内自然
端直矣守義以方其外而有一定之理則講學之工
夫盡而外截然方正矣既不專於主敬又不偏於守
義敬義夾持内外交脩則眾善畢集德極其盛而自
不孤矣由是在我之敬義即坤之直方在我之不孤
即坤之大也直方而大則不待學習而無適不宜不
假脩為而無往不利以之事君則忠於君坦然由之
===
而無疑也以之事親則悅於親釋然行之而不惑也
謂之不疑其所行信乎無一事之或疑矣又何假於
習而後利哉吾夫子文言而以是發明六二之義其
至矣乎抑嘗兼乾坤論之乾九三言誠坤六二言敬
誠敬者乾坤之别也先儒誠敬之學起於此乾九二
言仁坤六二言義仁義者陰陽之辨也先儒論仁義
之用取諸此後之學易者可不合而觀之乎
易曰憧憧往來朋從爾思子曰天下何思何慮
天下同歸而殊塗一致而百慮天下何思何
punctuated:
固，坤之直也；而「直」非人心本體之正乎？賦形有定，坤之方也；而「方」非人心裁制之義乎？君子人與，主敬以直其内，而無委曲之私，則持守之工夫至，而内自然端直矣；守義以方其外，而有一定之理，則講學之工夫盡，而外截然方正矣。既不專於主敬，又不偏於守義，敬義夾持，内外交脩，則眾善畢集，德極其盛，而自「不孤」矣。由是，在我之敬義，即坤之直方；在我之不孤，即坤之大也。直方而大，則不待學習而無適不宜，不假脩為而無往不利。以之事君，則忠於君，坦然由之而無疑也；以之事親，則悅於親，釋然行之而不惑也。謂之「不疑其所行」，信乎無一事之或疑矣！又何假於習而後利哉？吾夫子《文言》，而以是發明六二之義，其至矣乎！抑嘗兼乾、坤論之：乾九三言誠，坤六二言敬，誠、敬者，乾、坤之别也，先儒誠敬之學起於此；乾九二言仁，坤六二言義，仁、義者，陰、陽之辨也，先儒論仁義之用取諸此。後之學《易》者，可不合而觀之乎？

《易》曰：「憧憧往來，朋從爾思。」子曰：「天下何思何慮？天下同歸而殊塗，一致而百慮。天下何思何
translation_en:
…and firm is the "straightness" of Kun (the Receptive); yet is not "straightness" the correctness of the original substance of the human mind? That endowed forms are determinate is the "squareness" of Kun; yet is not "squareness" the righteousness of the human mind's regulative judgment? Is he not a noble man! When one maintains reverence to straighten one's inner self, without any crooked selfishness, the effort of preservation and holding fast reaches its utmost, and the inside is naturally upright and straight. When one abides by righteousness to square one's outer conduct, following determinate principles, the effort of pursuing learning is exhausted, and the outside is distinctly square and proper. Neither focusing exclusively on maintaining reverence nor leaning one-sidedly toward abiding by righteousness, when reverence and righteousness support one another from both sides and the inner and outer are cultivated together, all goodness gathers completely; one's virtue reaches its highest flourishing, and one is naturally "not solitary." Consequently, the reverence and righteousness within oneself are none other than the straightness and squareness of Kun; the not being solitary within oneself is none other than the "greatness" of Kun. Being straight, square, and great, then without waiting for study and practice there is nowhere one goes that is not fitting, and without relying on artificial effort there is nowhere one goes that is not advantageous. If one uses this to serve one's ruler, one will be loyal to the ruler, following this path with ease and without doubt; if one uses this to serve one's parents, one will bring joy to the parents, practicing this with clarity and without delusion. When it is called "having no doubt about what one does," truly there is not a single matter in which one might hesitate! What need is there, then, to rely on practice before it becomes advantageous? For our Master, in the "Words on the Text" (Wenyan), to elucidate the meaning of the Six in the Second place by these means—how supreme it is! Furthermore, I have considered Qian (the Creative) and Kun together: the Nine in the Third place of Qian speaks of sincerity, whereas the Six in the Second place of Kun speaks of reverence. Sincerity and reverence are the distinction between Qian and Kun, and the former Confucians' learning of sincerity and reverence originated from this. The Nine in the Second place of Qian speaks of benevolence, whereas the Six in the Second place of Kun speaks of righteousness. Benevolence and righteousness are the differentiation between Yin and Yang, and the former Confucians' discussions on the function of benevolence and righteousness were drawn from this. For later students of the Book of Changes (Yi), how could they not combine and examine them together?

The Book of Changes says: "Going and coming in unsettled commotion, only your friends will follow your thoughts." The Master said: "What need is there in the world for thought and deliberation? In the world, all return to the same destination though by different paths; there is one result though a hundred deliberations. What need is there in the world for thought and…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
慮日往則月来月往則日来日月相推而明
生焉寒往則暑来暑往則寒来寒暑相推而
歲成焉往者屈也来者信也屈信相感而利
生焉尺蠖之屈以求信也龍蛇之蟄以存身
也精義入神以致用也利用安身以崇德也
王淮
同考試官訓導郭批此題釋爻辭言感應之理莫非自然
諸作多講貫不明是篇詞約理備參
之論策俱優有學識之士也
===
同考試官教諭汪批此題歷舉造化無心之感應所以破咸
九四有心感應之出於私也作者多昧乎
此得之者惟此篇焉高薦何忝
考試官教諭鄭批易義貴精微此作得之
考試官學正王批說得感應之理盡
大傳舉爻辭而釋以感應之理無容心尤即造化物
理聖學以明之也盖感應之理莫非自然固不假於
思慮也聖人釋爻而尤即造化物理聖學以明之不
其至乎且咸之九四為心之象感之主也往者為感
punctuated:
慮？日往則月来，月往則日来，日月相推而明生焉。寒往則暑来，暑往則寒来，寒暑相推而歲成焉。往者屈也，来者信也，屈信相感而利生焉。尺蠖之屈，以求信也；龍蛇之蟄，以存身也。精義入神，以致用也；利用安身，以崇德也。」

王淮
同考試官訓導郭批：此題釋爻辭，言感應之理莫非自然。諸作多講貫不明，是篇詞約理備，參之論、策俱優，有學識之士也。
同考試官教諭汪批：此題歷舉造化無心之感應，所以破咸九四有心感應之出於私也。作者多昧乎此，得之者惟此篇焉，高薦何忝？
考試官教諭鄭批：易義貴精微，此作得之。
考試官學正王批：說得感應之理盡。

《大傳》舉爻辭而釋以感應之理無容心，尤即造化、物理、聖學以明之也。盖感應之理莫非自然，固不假於思慮也。聖人釋爻，而尤即造化、物理、聖學以明之，不其至乎！且《咸》之九四，為心之象、感之主也。往者為感，
translation_en:
… deliberation? When the sun goes, the moon comes; when the moon goes, the sun comes. Sun and moon push each other on, and light is born therefrom. When cold goes, heat comes; when heat goes, cold comes. Cold and heat push each other on, and the year is completed therefrom. What goes contracts; what comes expands. Contraction and expansion stimulate and respond to each other, and benefit is born therefrom. The inchworm contracts in order to seek expansion; dragons and snakes hibernate in order to preserve their bodies. Refining righteousness to the point of entering the mysterious is how one attains practical application; making use of that application to secure one's person is how one exalts virtue."

Wang Huai 王淮
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Guo: This question explains the line statement, stating that the principle of stimulus and response is nothing other than natural. Most compositions fail to explain this thoroughly and clearly, whereas this essay is concise in wording and complete in principle. Checked against his discourse and policy essays, which are also superior, he is a scholar of learning and insight.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Wang: This question enumerates the uncontrived stimulus and response of creation in order to refute the contrived stimulus and response arising from selfishness in the Nine in the Fourth place of the Xian hexagram. Most writers are blind to this; this essay alone has grasped it. How could a high recommendation be undeserved?
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zheng: Exegesis of the Book of Changes (Yi) values subtlety and precision; this composition has grasped it.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang: It explains the principle of stimulus and response exhaustively.

The Great Commentary (Dazhuan) cites the line statement and explains it in terms of the principle that stimulus and response admit of no deliberate intent, and furthermore illustrates this by drawing upon cosmic creation, the principles of things, and sage learning. Indeed, the principle of stimulus and response is nothing other than natural and certainly does not depend upon thought and deliberation. When the Sage explains the line and furthermore illustrates it by drawing upon cosmic creation, the principles of things, and sage learning, is this not the ultimate? Moreover, the Nine in the Fourth place of the Xian hexagram is the image of the mind and the master of stimulus. That which goes is stimulus; …

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
九四累於私而憧憧於其往来者為應九四昵於私
而憧憧於其来則但朋類從之不復能及遠矣爻辭
如此吾夫子引而釋之謂夫天下何思何慮理之在
心者同因其事之不同而所行之塗各殊理之在心
者一因其事之不一而所發之慮有百塗雖殊慮雖
百而應事之理則同而一也天下果何思慮之有哉
彼自造化而觀之日之往而感月之来月之往而感
日之来二曜相推而明生不匱焉寒之往而感暑之
来暑之往而感寒之来二氣迭運而歲成不缺焉日
===
月寒暑之往者理之屈也而屈所以感夫信日月寒
暑之来者理之信也而信所以感夫屈屈信往来之
相感則明生歲成之利生矣此造化感應自然之理
也非特造化為然以物理言之尺蠖不屈則不能信
其所以屈者将以來其信而可行也龍蛇不蟄則不
能奮其所以蟄者將以存其身而可奮也非物理感
應之自然乎以聖學言之精研其義至於入神屈之
至也然乃所以為出而致用之本利其施用無適不
安信之極也然乃所以為入而崇德之資非聖學感
punctuated: 九四累於私而憧憧於其往；来者為應，九四昵於私而憧憧於其来，則但朋類從之，不復能及遠矣。爻辭如此，吾夫子引而釋之，謂夫天下何思何慮？理之在心者同，因其事之不同而所行之塗各殊；理之在心者一，因其事之不一而所發之慮有百。塗雖殊，慮雖百，而應事之理則同而一也，天下果何思慮之有哉？彼自造化而觀之，日之往而感月之来，月之往而感日之来，二曜相推而明生不匱焉；寒之往而感暑之来，暑之往而感寒之来，二氣迭運而歲成不缺焉。日月寒暑之往者，理之屈也，而屈所以感夫信；日月寒暑之来者，理之信也，而信所以感夫屈。屈信往来之相感，則明生歲成之利生矣，此造化感應自然之理也。非特造化為然，以物理言之，尺蠖不屈則不能信，其所以屈者，将以來其信而可行也；龍蛇不蟄則不能奮，其所以蟄者，將以存其身而可奮也，非物理感應之自然乎？以聖學言之，精研其義至於入神，屈之至也，然乃所以為出而致用之本；利其施用無適不安，信之極也，然乃所以為入而崇德之資，非聖學感
translation_en:
… Nine in the fourth place is encumbered by selfishness and is restless in its going; what comes is response, and Nine in the fourth place is bound to selfishness and is restless in its coming, so that only its own kind follow it, and it can no longer reach far. Such is the line statement, which our Master cited and explained, saying: What need is there for thought and deliberation in the world? The principle in the mind is the same, though because affairs are not the same, the paths taken each differ; the principle in the mind is one, though because affairs are not one, the deliberations that arise are a hundredfold. Although the paths differ and the deliberations are a hundredfold, the principle for responding to affairs is the same and is one; what need is there indeed for thought and deliberation in the world?

Viewed from the perspective of the creative transformations of nature: the going of the sun induces the coming of the moon, and the going of the moon induces the coming of the sun; the two luminaries push each other forward and light is generated without exhaustion. The going of cold induces the coming of heat, and the going of heat induces the coming of cold; the two vital energies alternate in their movement and the year is completed without fail. The going of the sun, moon, cold, and heat is the contraction of principle, and contraction is that whereby extension is induced; the coming of the sun, moon, cold, and heat is the extension of principle, and extension is that whereby contraction is induced. When contraction and extension, going and coming, mutually induce one another, the benefits of generating light and completing the year are produced. This is the natural principle of stimulus and response in the creative transformations of nature.

Not only is it so with the creative transformations of nature; speaking in terms of the principles of things, if the inchworm does not contract, it cannot extend—that whereby it contracts is in order to bring about its extension so that it may advance. If dragons and snakes do not hibernate, they cannot rouse themselves—that whereby they hibernate is in order to preserve their bodies so that they may rouse themselves. Is this not the naturalness of stimulus and response in the principles of things?

Speaking in terms of sage learning, to investigate meanings with精微 (subtlety) to the point of entering the numinous is the utmost of contraction, yet this is the foundation for going forth to put it into practice; to make one's application beneficial so that nowhere is one ill at ease is the extreme of extension, yet this is the resource for entering within to exalt virtue. Is this not the [naturalness of] stimulus [and response] in sage learning …

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
應之自然乎夫造化物理聖學之感應莫非自然如
此又豈若咸九四之憧憧往來而以思慮爲哉大抵
往來者感應之常理也無心則公而憧憧則私公則
溥而觀諸衆理爲可見私則狹而不過朋類之相從
故吾夫子特舉而釋之其亦欲人有事於感應者當
以咸九四而爲戒也與
書義
厥貢惟球琳琅玕浮于積石至于龍門西河會
于渭汭織皮崑崙析支渠搜西戎卽叙
===
鄧應仁
同考試官教諭林批此題言中外貢法之行見大
禹治水之成功是作得之
考試官教諭鄭批此作言水土旣平華夷入貢
宛見神禹治功之成深合
本旨
考試官學正王批形容大禹治水功成殆無餘蘊
紀一州之貢而著其貢道之異附三國之貢以見其
就功之同盖經國之制莫要於因地而制貢也雍州
punctuated:
應之自然乎？夫造化、物理、聖學之感應，莫非自然如此，又豈若咸九四之憧憧往來，而以思慮爲哉？大抵往來者，感應之常理也。無心則公，而憧憧則私；公則溥，而觀諸衆理爲可見；私則狹，而不過朋類之相從。故吾夫子特舉而釋之，其亦欲人有事於感應者，當以咸九四而爲戒也與！

書義

厥貢惟球、琳、琅玕。浮于積石，至于龍門、西河，會于渭汭。織皮：崑崙、析支、渠搜，西戎卽叙。

鄧應仁
同考試官教諭林批：此題言中外貢法之行，見大禹治水之成功，是作得之。
考試官教諭鄭批：此作言水土旣平，華夷入貢，宛見神禹治功之成，深合本旨。
考試官學正王批：形容大禹治水功成，殆無餘蘊。

紀一州之貢，而著其貢道之異；附三國之貢，以見其就功之同。盖經國之制，莫要於因地而制貢也。雍州
translation_en:
… the spontaneity of stimulus and response in sagely learning? Indeed, the stimulus and response in creative transformation, the principles of things, and sagely learning are all naturally so like this; how could they be like the fourth nine line of the Xian hexagram, going back and forth in unsettled thought, acting out of deliberate calculation? On the whole, going back and forth is the constant principle of stimulus and response. To have no deliberate mind is impartial, whereas unsettled thought is selfish; impartiality is universal, as can be seen by observing the multitude of principles, whereas selfishness is narrow, amounting to nothing more than the following of one's own clique. Therefore, our Master specially cited and explained it—surely because he wished that those who engage in stimulus and response should take the fourth nine line of the Xian hexagram as a warning!

Exposition on the Book of Documents

"Its tribute is qiu and lin jades, and langgan precious stones. They float from Jishi, reaching Longmen and the West River, and meet at the bend of the Wei. Felt and skins: Kunlun, Xizhi, and Qusou; the Western Rong were brought to order."

By Deng Yingren 鄧應仁.
Associate Examiner Instructor Lin 林 comments: This topic speaks of the implementation of the tribute system within and without, showing the success of the Great Yu's controlling of the waters; this essay grasps it.
Examiner Instructor Zheng 鄭 comments: This essay speaks of how, once water and soil were pacified, both Chinese and barbarians presented tribute, vividly revealing the completion of the divine Yu's work of regulation and deeply according with the fundamental purport.
Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang 王 comments: It depicts the completion of the Great Yu's achievement in controlling the waters, leaving almost nothing unexpressed.

It records the tribute of a single province and sets forth the differences in its tribute routes; it appends the tribute of three states in order to show their uniformity in bringing their work to completion. For among the institutions for governing the state, nothing is more essential than establishing tribute in accordance with the land. Once Yongzhou's …

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
水土旣平而貢法行於中外史臣得不幷記之以見
聖世大一統之治歟何則雍州之域地之最高者也
向也治水施功未及貢法固未定矣今焉禹功告成
則其地產之美惟璆琳之玉可以為禮器者制之使
入貢焉琅玕之石可以為服飾者定之為常貢焉然
貢道之來有出於東北境者則隨其貢物之便浮于
積石至於龍門西河以達於帝都矣有出於西南境
者則因其物產之近會于渭汭以達於河矣此中國
之貢然也至若西戎之域地之最遠者也向也雍州
===
水土未平功叙亦未就矣今焉禹功所及不惟崐崘
之國以織皮為貢而效其奉上之誠而析支渠搜亦
以織皮為獻而將其來王之敬夫崐崘乃西方戎落
之地其來貢王朝則其被餘功而就叙也可知矣析
支渠搜亦西方戎落之地其入獻中國則其慕王化
而即功也可見矣吁貢法旣定於中國餘功復及於
西戎何莫而非神禹之成功也耶抑考雍州之境禹
治水施功最後者也當時九州水土皆已平治故其
上文所記水土成功則曰弱水旣西曰三危旣宅三
punctuated: 水土旣平，而貢法行於中外，史臣得不幷記之以見聖世大一統之治歟？何則？雍州之域，地之最高者也。向也治水施功未及，貢法固未定矣。今焉禹功告成，則其地產之美，惟璆琳之玉可以為禮器者，制之使入貢焉；琅玕之石可以為服飾者，定之為常貢焉。然貢道之來，有出於東北境者，則隨其貢物之便，浮于積石，至於龍門西河，以達於帝都矣；有出於西南境者，則因其物產之近，會于渭汭，以達於河矣。此中國之貢然也。至若西戎之域，地之最遠者也。向也雍州水土未平，功叙亦未就矣。今焉禹功所及，不惟崐崘之國以織皮為貢，而效其奉上之誠；而析支、渠搜亦以織皮為獻，而將其來王之敬。夫崐崘乃西方戎落之地，其來貢王朝，則其被餘功而就叙也可知矣；析支、渠搜亦西方戎落之地，其入獻中國，則其慕王化而即功也可見矣。吁！貢法旣定於中國，餘功復及於西戎，何莫而非神禹之成功也耶？抑考雍州之境，禹治水施功最後者也。當時九州水土皆已平治，故其上文所記水土成功，則曰「弱水旣西」，曰「三危旣宅，三
translation_en:
… Once the waters and land of Yongzhou were pacified and the system of tribute operated both within and beyond the realm, how could the court historian not record them together so as to manifest the governance of the great unification in a sagely age? Why is this so? The territory of Yongzhou is the highest of lands. Previously, before the labor of controlling the waters had reached it, the tribute regulations were naturally not yet settled. Now that Yu's labor was brought to completion, among the fine products of its land, the qiulin jade suitable for making ritual vessels was regulated to be presented as tribute, and the langgan stones suitable for adorning garments were established as regular tribute. Moreover, as for the routes by which the tribute came: for that emerging from the northeastern border, according to the convenience of transporting the tribute goods, it floated from Jishi as far as the Western River at Longmen so as to reach the imperial capital; for that emerging from the southwestern border, by virtue of the proximity of its local products, it converged at the bend of the Wei River so as to reach the Yellow River. Such was the tribute of the Central States.

As for the territory of the Western Rong, it is the most distant of lands. Previously, when the waters and land of Yongzhou were not yet pacified, order and achievement had likewise not yet been attained there. Now, as far as Yu's achievements extended, not only did the polity of Kunlun present woven hides and furs as tribute to display its sincerity in serving the sovereign, but Xizhi and Qusou also offered woven hides and furs to convey their reverence in coming to pay homage to the king. Now, Kunlun was a territory of western Rong settlements; from its coming to present tribute to the royal court, one may know that it had received the overflow of his achievements and come into order. Xizhi and Qusou were likewise territories of western Rong settlements; from their entering to present offerings to the Central States, one can see that they admired the royal transformation and acceded to his achievement. Ah! Once the tribute system was settled in the Central States, the overflow of his achievements further reached the Western Rong—what part of this was not the accomplished work of the divine Yu? Furthermore, if we examine the territory of Yongzhou, it was the very last place where Yu applied his labor in controlling the waters. At that time, the waters and land of the Nine Provinces had all already been pacified and brought under control. Therefore, when the preceding passage records the successful pacification of the waters and land, it says, "The Ruo River was conducted westward," and it says, "Sanwei was made habitable, and the San… [miao]"

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
苗丕叙而此記是州貢法則曰崐崘析支渠搜西戎
即叙皆極其遠而言之于以見聖人平治之功無間
於遠邇而道德之化無限於內外也所謂地平天成
六府三事允治萬世永賴者豈虛語哉
公其惟時成周建無窮之基亦有無窮之間子
孫訓其成式惟乂嗚呼罔曰弗克惟既厥心
罔曰民寡惟慎厥事欽若先王成烈以休于
前政
鄧應仁
===
同考試官教諭林批破題明潔講語純妥當取以
冠本經
考試官教諭鄭批康王命畢公以保釐之責
其期勉之辭如此此作能發
其意是宜錄出
考試官學正王批理明辭暢深得康王命畢公之意
賢王之命大臣既期其立可久之業而垂於後必勉
其任成終之責以光于前甚矣保釐之責之重也賢
王於大臣既以垂於後者期之得不以光于前者勉
punctuated:
苗丕叙，而此記是州貢法，則曰崐崘、析支、渠搜，西戎即叙，皆極其遠而言之。于以見聖人平治之功無間於遠邇，而道德之化無限於內外也。所謂「地平天成，六府三事允治，萬世永賴」者，豈虛語哉！

公其惟時成周，建無窮之基，亦有無窮之間。子孫訓其成式惟乂。嗚呼！罔曰弗克，惟既厥心；罔曰民寡，惟慎厥事。欽若先王成烈，以休于前政。
鄧應仁
同考試官教諭林批：破題明潔，講語純妥，當取以冠本經。
考試官教諭鄭批：康王命畢公以保釐之責，其期勉之辭如此。此作能發其意，是宜錄出。
考試官學正王批：理明辭暢，深得康王命畢公之意。

賢王之命大臣，既期其立可久之業而垂於後，必勉其任成終之責以光于前，甚矣保釐之責之重也！賢王於大臣，既以垂於後者期之，得不以光于前者勉
translation_en:
… the Sanmiao were brought into great order." And here, in recording the tribute system of this province, it says, "Kunlun, Xizhi, and Qusou—the Western Rong were brought into order," in all cases speaking of the most distant regions. From this we can see that the sage's achievement of pacification and governance made no distinction between far and near, and the transformation of his moral virtue had no boundary between inner and outer. That which is called "The earth is leveled and heaven is completed; the six treasuries and three affairs are truly governed, to be relied upon forever for ten thousand generations"—how could these be empty words!

"May you, Duke, at this time in Chengzhou, establish an boundless foundation, and you shall also have boundless renown [間, error for 聞]. Your descendants will follow your established model and govern well. Oh! Do not say that you are unable; only exhaust your heart. Do not say that the people are few; only be cautious in your affairs. Reverently accord with the completed achievements of the former kings, so as to bring glory to the previous administration."
Deng Yingren

Comment by Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Lin: The opening statement of the theme is clear and concise, and the explication is pure and fitting. It should be selected to top this Classic.
Comment by Examiner County Director of Studies Zheng: King Kang charged the Duke of Bi with the responsibility of protecting and regulating, and his words of expectation and encouragement were like this. This composition is able to bring out their meaning, so it is fitting to transcribe and publish it.
Comment by Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang: The principles are clear and the phrasing is fluent; it deeply grasps King Kang's intention in charging the Duke of Bi.

When a worthy king gives a charge to a great minister, since he expects him to establish an enduring enterprise to be handed down to posterity, he must also encourage him to shoulder the responsibility of bringing things to completion so as to bring glory to his predecessors. Great indeed is the weight of the responsibility of protecting and regulating! Since a worthy king expects of his great minister that which will be handed down to posterity, how could he not encourage…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之哉康王命畢公保釐東郊而終及乎此意以成周
之衆蕞爾甚微而所係甚重公其惟時成化殷之功
則足以立無窮之事業而勳德樹於永世將亦有無
窮之聲聞而名實昭于後世是公之身有賴乎此而
勳譽之隆千載一時也公之子孫承殷民之化則可
以順其成法而事無不治遵其成憲而政無不乂是
公之子孫亦有賴乎此而垂憲乃後百世一日也成
周所係若此其重則夫畢公任成終之責可不勉哉
於是復嘆息而告之謂夫事之不立非視之太重而
===
畏其難則視之太輕而忽其易公於保釐之事勿畏
其難而不敢為惟往盡乃心耳盡乃心則雖難而無
所畏矣勿易其民以為不足為惟克謹乃事耳謹其
事則雖易而不敢忽矣彼其式化厥訓者先王之成
烈周公謹始所致也公必敬順之弗懈使周公之政
於焉而有光允升大猷者亦先王之成烈君陳和中
所厎也公必祗若之無怠俾君陳之政於焉而益美
夫既立無窮之業而復盡成終之責保釐之治孰有
加於此哉吁畢公四世元老勳業之隆若無待於期
punctuated: 之哉？康王命畢公保釐東郊，而終及乎此。意以成周之衆，蕞爾甚微，而所係甚重。公其惟時成化殷之功，則足以立無窮之事業，而勳德樹於永世；將亦有無窮之聲聞，而名實昭于後世。是公之身有賴乎此，而勳譽之隆，千載一時也。公之子孫，承殷民之化，則可以順其成法，而事無不治；遵其成憲，而政無不乂。是公之子孫亦有賴乎此，而垂憲乃後，百世一日也。成周所係若此其重，則夫畢公任成終之責，可不勉哉？於是復嘆息而告之，謂夫事之不立，非視之太重而畏其難，則視之太輕而忽其易。公於保釐之事，勿畏其難而不敢為，惟往盡乃心耳。盡乃心，則雖難而無所畏矣。勿易其民以為不足為，惟克謹乃事耳。謹其事，則雖易而不敢忽矣。彼其式化厥訓者，先王之成烈，周公謹始所致也，公必敬順之弗懈，使周公之政於焉而有光；允升大猷者，亦先王之成烈，君陳和中所厎也，公必祗若之無怠，俾君陳之政於焉而益美。夫既立無窮之業，而復盡成終之責，保釐之治，孰有加於此哉！吁！畢公四世元老，勳業之隆，若無待於期
translation_en:
… glorify the past? When King Kang (Kangwang 康王) commanded the Duke of Bi (Bigong 畢公) to protect and regulate the eastern suburbs, he concluded by touching upon this very idea. His thought was that although the multitude of Chengzhou was tiny and insignificant in size, what depended upon it was of the utmost weight. If the Duke would now complete the work of transforming the Yin people, it would suffice to establish a boundless enterprise, with his meritorious virtue planted for eternal generations; and he would also possess boundless renown, with both his name and reality shining forth to later ages. Thus the Duke's own person depended upon this, and the flourishing of his merit and fame was an opportunity of a thousand years in a single moment. When the Duke's descendants inherited the transformation of the Yin people, they would be able to follow his established methods so that no affair would go unManaged, and abide by his established statutes so that no governance would go unordered. Thus the Duke's descendants also depended upon this, and in handing down models to posterity, a hundred generations would be as a single day.

Since what depended on Chengzhou was of such great weight, how could the Duke of Bi not exert himself in bearing the responsibility of bringing the work to a successful conclusion? Thereupon the King sighed again and admonished him, saying that when affairs fail to be established, if it is not because one views them as too weighty and fears their difficulty, then it is because one views them as too light and neglects their ease. In the matter of protecting and regulating, the Duke must not say "It is too difficult" and dare not act, but should simply go forth and exhaust his heart in it. If he exhausts his heart, then even though it is difficult, there will be nothing to fear. He must not take the people lightly, thinking them not worth the effort, but should simply be able to attend carefully to his affairs. If he attends carefully to his affairs, then even though it seems easy, he will not dare to neglect it. That they were transformed by instructions was the accomplished merit of the former kings, brought about by the Duke of Zhou's (Zhougong 周公) careful beginning; the Duke of Bi must respectfully follow this without slacking, causing the governance of the Duke of Zhou thereby to gain glory. That they truly ascended to the great plan was likewise the accomplished merit of the former kings, achieved by Junchen's 君陳 harmonizing of the middle stage; the Duke of Bi must reverently accord with this without idleness, causing the governance of Junchen thereby to become even more admirable.

Having both established a boundless enterprise and fulfilled the responsibility of bringing the work to a successful conclusion, what governance of protection and regulation could surpass this? Alas! The Duke of Bi was a senior statesman of four reigns; the height of his meritorious achievements seemed to have no need of expectations…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
望矣克勤小物亦無待於戒勉矣而康王之命尤拳
拳焉盖期以無窮之業者尊敬之至也勉以成終之
責者顒望之深也厥后畢公果能化服殷民卒使依
於周者八百年可謂無愧於先王無愧於周公君陳
而亦無負於康王之命矣
詩義
維其有章矣是以有慶矣
周叙
同考試官教諭陳批此題本平易作者於有章
===
有慶處課說紛紜殊失本
旨此作得之所宜錄出
考試官教諭鄭批辭理簡明允如初考
考試官學正王批王者美諸侯之意宛然在目
王者之美諸侯惟有德著於外斯有福集於已盖德
者福之本今諸侯之德既著於外則其有福慶也宜
矣此天子美諸侯之辭盖以荅瞻彼洛矣也謂夫諸
侯之来朝也非特乗其四駱六轡沃若而已觀其彼
交匪紓威儀抑抑粲然其有文則德之ccf中彪外者
punctuated:
望矣，克勤小物，亦無待於戒勉矣，而康王之命尤拳拳焉。盖期以無窮之業者，尊敬之至也；勉以成終之責者，顒望之深也。厥后畢公果能化服殷民，卒使依於周者八百年，可謂無愧於先王，無愧於周公、君陳，而亦無負於康王之命矣。

詩義
維其有章矣，是以有慶矣。
周叙
同考試官教諭陳批：此題本平易，作者於「有章」、「有慶」處課說紛紜，殊失本旨。此作得之，所宜錄出。
考試官教諭鄭批：辭理簡明，允如初考。
考試官學正王批：王者美諸侯之意，宛然在目。

王者之美諸侯，惟有德著於外，斯有福集於已。盖德者，福之本。今諸侯之德既著於外，則其有福慶也宜矣。此天子美諸侯之辭，盖以荅《瞻彼洛矣》也。謂夫諸侯之来朝也，非特乗其四駱、六轡沃若而已；觀其彼交匪紓、威儀抑抑，粲然其有文，則德之ccf中彪外者…
translation_en:
…expectations; being able to be diligent even in small matters, he also had no need for admonition and encouragement. Yet King Kang's charge was especially earnest in this regard. Indeed, looking to him for boundless achievements was the utmost of respect, and encouraging him with the responsibility of bringing things to final completion was the deepest of hopes. Thereafter, the Duke of Bi was indeed able to transform and win the submission of the Yin people, ultimately causing them to rely on the Zhou for eight hundred years. He can truly be said to have been worthy of the former kings, worthy of the Duke of Zhou and Jun Chen, and also not to have failed the charge of King Kang.

Exposition on the Classic of Poetry (Shiyi)
"Because they have outward grace, therefore they have blessings."
Zhou Xu
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Chen: This topic is inherently plain and accessible, yet the candidates offered confused and varied explanations on the points of "outward grace" and "having blessings," completely missing the original purport. This essay grasps it and ought to be selected for publication.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zheng: The diction and reasoning are concise and clear; I concur with the initial assessment.
Comment by Examiner and Director of Studies Wang: The true king's intention in praising the feudal lords is vividly before one's eyes.

When the true king praises the feudal lords, it is only because their virtue is manifested on the outside that blessings gather upon them. For virtue is the root of blessings. Now, since the virtue of the feudal lords is already manifested on the outside, it is only fitting that they enjoy blessings and felicity. These are the words with which the Son of Heaven praises the feudal lords, composed in reply to the ode "Look at the Luo River" (Zhan bi Luo yi). It means that when the feudal lords come to court, it is not merely that they ride their teams of four white horses with black manes, with six reins glossy and soft; when one observes how in their intercourse they are not remiss, and how their dignified demeanor is so cẩn-controlled and resplendently refined, then how their virtue is accumulated within [?] and shines forth on the outside…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
可知非特赤芾在股邪幅在下而已觀其彼交匪敖
淑愼爾止蔚然其有章則德之睟面盎背者可見然
諸侯德之彰著如此則豈不有福慶乎是以向也析
王之圭而維藩維垣固嘗受福矣今也來朝於東都
燕笑語兮有譽處兮而有以享是福於悠久焉昔也
儐王之爵而之屏之翰巳嘗有慶矣今也會同於洛
水天子命之福祿申之而有以衍是慶於無窮焉吁
德著於外福集於巳宜詩人形諸詠歌以美之也抑
考瞻彼洛矣之詩諸侯所以美天子也旣願其享福
===
祿而保家邦矣而天子之答諸侯不惟言其以德獲
福而下二章又言其車馬威儀之盛才德之全備焉
噫上下之間交相忠愛如此此所以為有周盛世之
君臣也與
清酒旣載騂牡旣備以享以祀以介景福瑟彼
柞棫民所燎矣豈弟君子神所勞矣莫莫葛
藟施于條枚豈弟君子求福不回
魏應芳
同考試官教諭陳批場中作此題者多冗長可

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
厭唯此篇辭簡理明夐出
眾作况他篇俱優本房
無出其右者健羨健羨
考試官教諭鄭批此作形容文王以德受福之
旨簡當可觀
考試官學正王批辭理俱到
詩人美聖人祭必受福也既興其得福之由復興其
得福之正夫聖人有豈弟之德則祭必受福然亦由
乎神之眷而出乎心之正爾詩人兩託興而詠歌之
===
也宜哉是詩亦詠歌文王之德謂夫文王之祭有清
酒焉則載而在尊矣有騂牡焉則備而全具矣于以
享乎神則景福之必至于以祀乎神則繁祉之必集
是何也以文王有豈弟之德也夫文王有德而祭必
受福如此亦豈無所自耶故託興以謂彼瑟然茂密
之柞棫乃叢生小木耳尚可供燎而濟民生之用况
豈弟樂易之君子豈不為神所勞乎吾知神之聽之
而有慰撫之休故福於是而攸降也夫文王以德受
福雖由乎神之勞而其心一出乎正也故又託興以
punctuated:
厭，唯此篇辭簡理明，夐出眾作。况他篇俱優，本房無出其右者，健羨健羨。
考試官教諭鄭批：此作形容文王以德受福之旨，簡當可觀。
考試官學正王批：辭理俱到。
詩人美聖人祭必受福也，既興其得福之由，復興其得福之正。夫聖人有豈弟之德，則祭必受福，然亦由乎神之眷，而出乎心之正爾。詩人兩託興而詠歌之也，宜哉！是詩亦詠歌文王之德，謂夫文王之祭，有清酒焉，則載而在尊矣；有騂牡焉，則備而全具矣。于以享乎神，則景福之必至；于以祀乎神，則繁祉之必集。是何也？以文王有豈弟之德也。夫文王有德而祭必受福如此，亦豈無所自耶？故託興以謂：彼瑟然茂密之柞棫，乃叢生小木耳，尚可供燎而濟民生之用；况豈弟樂易之君子，豈不為神所勞乎？吾知神之聽之，而有慰撫之休，故福於是而攸降也。夫文王以德受福，雖由乎神之勞，而其心一出乎正也，故又託興以
translation_en:
…tedious. Only this essay is concise in diction and clear in principle, standing far above the rest of the compositions. Moreover, his other essays are all excellent; in this examination ward there is none that surpasses him. Truly admirable, truly admirable!

Examiner and Instructor Zheng commented: This composition portrays the purport of King Wen receiving blessings through his virtue; it is concise, apt, and worthy of note.

Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Wang commented: Both diction and principle hit the mark.

When the poet praises the sage for invariably receiving blessings upon offering sacrifice, he first evokes the reason for his obtaining blessings, and then again evokes the rectitude by which he obtains blessings. Now, because the sage possesses easy and fraternal virtue, when he sacrifices he invariably receives blessings; yet this also stems from the favor of the spirits and issues from the rectitude of his own mind. That the poet twice employs evocative metaphor (xing) to sing of it is fitting indeed!

This ode likewise sings of the virtue of King Wen. It says that in King Wen's sacrifice, there is clear wine, which is set forth and held in the goblets; there are red bulls, which are prepared and completely provided. When with these he makes offering to the spirits, great blessings are certain to arrive; when with these he sacrifices to the spirits, abundant felicities are certain to gather. Why is this? Because King Wen possesses easy and fraternal virtue. Now, when King Wen possesses virtue and thus invariably receives blessings upon sacrificing in this manner, how could it be without a source? Therefore, the poet employs an evocative metaphor to say: Those densely luxuriant oaks (zuo) and white oaks (yu) are merely small trees growing in thickets, yet they can still supply firewood and serve the needs of the people's livelihood; how much more so will the easy, fraternal, joyous, and genial lord not be rewarded and comforted by the spirits? I know that the spirits hearken to him and bestow the grace of consolation and comfort, and therefore blessings are thereupon sent down. Now, although King Wen's receiving blessings through his virtue stems from the rewarding comfort of the spirits, his mind issues wholly from rectitude; therefore, the poet again employs an evocative metaphor to…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
謂莫然茂盛之葛藟乃蔓生微草耳尚有所托而施
條枚之上況豈弟樂易之君子其受福豈待於求耶
亦惟厥德不回而無覬倖之心故福不求而自至也
是則德之所在福之所在文王之為神所勞為福所
歸何莫非一德所致哉抑通考是詩一章言文王得
福之有道二章言文王得福之自然三章言文王作
人之妙至此則言其受福之本求福之心也大哉聖
人豈弟之德乎其所以為作人受福之本乎此詩人
所以歷叙而詠歌之也猗歟盛哉
===
春秋義
齊人侵我西鄙公追齊師至酅弗及〔傳公羊十年〕公
會齊侯于夾谷〔定公十年〕
曹鼎
同考試官訓導李批場中作此題者多拘泥而文
少通暢合題意而詞不窘者
僅見此篇耳宜錄出
考試官教諭鄭批理明辭整
考試官學正王批理完氣充當是作者
punctuated:
謂莫然茂盛之葛藟，乃蔓生微草耳，尚有所托而施條枚之上；況豈弟樂易之君子，其受福豈待於求耶？亦惟厥德不回，而無覬倖之心，故福不求而自至也。是則德之所在，福之所在，文王之為神所勞、為福所歸，何莫非一德所致哉！抑通考是詩：一章言文王得福之有道，二章言文王得福之自然，三章言文王作人之妙，至此則言其受福之本、求福之心也。大哉聖人豈弟之德乎！其所以為作人受福之本乎！此詩人所以歷叙而詠歌之也。猗歟盛哉！

春秋義
「齊人侵我西鄙，公追齊師至酅，弗及。」〔傳公羊十年〕「公會齊侯于夾谷。」〔定公十年〕
曹鼎
同考試官訓導李批：場中作此題者，多拘泥而文少通暢，合題意而詞不窘者，僅見此篇耳，宜錄出。
考試官教諭鄭批：理明辭整。
考試官學正王批：理完氣充，當是作者。
translation_en:
…say that those luxuriantly flourishing creepers and vines are merely trailing, humble plants, yet they still have something to rely upon and spread across the branches and stems; how much more so the joyous and easygoing gentleman—how could his receiving of blessings depend upon seeking them? It is only that his virtue does not swerve and he harbors no mind for undeserved fortune; therefore, blessings arrive of themselves without being sought. Thus, where virtue resides, there blessings reside. That King Wen was comforted by the spirits and became the歸 [convergence] of blessings—how could any of this not be brought about by his single-minded virtue! Moreover, examining this ode as a whole: the first stanza speaks of the way by which King Wen obtained blessings; the second stanza speaks of the naturalness with which King Wen obtained blessings; the third stanza speaks of the wondrousness with which King Wen cultivated men; and arriving at these stanzas, it speaks of the root of his receiving blessings and his mind in seeking blessings. Great indeed is the joyous and easygoing virtue of the Sage! Is it not the very root of cultivating men and receiving blessings? This is why the poet recounted it in sequence and sang of it. How admirable and magnificent!

Meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"Men of Qi invaded our western borderlands; the Duke pursued the army of Qi to Xi, but did not overtake it." [twenty-sixth year of Duke Xi [? transcribed as 傳公羊十年]] "The Duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu." [tenth year of Duke Ding]
By Cao Ding 曹鼎.
Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Li 李: Among those in the examination hall who wrote on this topic, most were overly rigid and their prose lacked fluency; this is the only essay I have seen that matches the meaning of the topic without its diction being constrained. It ought to be copied and selected.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zheng 鄭: The reasoning is clear and the diction is orderly.
Comment by Examiner Director of Studies Wang 王: The reasoning is complete and the vital breath is full; he must be an accomplished writer.

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
大國肆虐內之威而畏於赴敵者可譏大國懷陵內
之謀而勇於却敵者可喜此僖公不敢及齊之師聖
人能却齊之衆春秋備書而勇怯見矣且魯之與齊
以先世言之周公太公夾輔周室嘗有世好之盟也
以春秋之時論之桓公創伯糾合諸侯昭舊職也奚
有私怨之脩乎今也齊孝嗣世棄命廢職乃舉無名
之衆肆為西鄙之侵陵虐我郊保荼毒我人民則曲
而老者在齊直而壯者在魯矣齊何足畏哉夫何僖
公在位方齊之至而無防禦之策及齊之去而舉追
===
逐之師深入其地弗及而返夫以齊之強豈能勝秦
以魯之衆何弱於趙然澠池之會藺相如一奮其氣
威信敵國秦雖虎狼猶不敢動況以千乘之君而畏
齊之若是乎噫自反而縮雖千萬人吾往矣而僖公
不足以語此迨夫春秋之季齊景代興陵魯之志又
有甚於齊孝者矣有如夾谷之會聽犁彌之言為執
魯之計兩君就壇鼓譟而起則齊有莫敵之勢而魯
有不測之禍矣魯將如之何哉幸而聖人相禮左右
司馬之具足以破其詐裔夷亂華之卻足以革其心
punctuated: 大國肆虐內之威，而畏於赴敵者可譏；大國懷陵內之謀，而勇於却敵者可喜。此僖公不敢及齊之師，聖人能却齊之衆，《春秋》備書而勇怯見矣。且魯之與齊，以先世言之，周公、太公夾輔周室，嘗有世好之盟也；以春秋之時論之，桓公創伯，糾合諸侯，昭舊職也，奚有私怨之脩乎？今也齊孝嗣世，棄命廢職，乃舉無名之衆，肆為西鄙之侵，陵虐我郊保，荼毒我人民，則曲而老者在齊，直而壯者在魯矣，齊何足畏哉？夫何僖公在位，方齊之至而無防禦之策，及齊之去而舉追逐之師，深入其地，弗及而返。夫以齊之強，豈能勝秦？以魯之衆，何弱於趙？然澠池之會，藺相如一奮其氣，威信敵國，秦雖虎狼，猶不敢動，況以千乘之君而畏齊之若是乎？噫！「自反而縮，雖千萬人，吾往矣。」而僖公不足以語此。迨夫春秋之季，齊景代興，陵魯之志，又有甚於齊孝者矣。有如夾谷之會，聽犁彌之言，為執魯之計，兩君就壇，鼓譟而起，則齊有莫敵之勢，而魯有不測之禍矣，魯將如之何哉？幸而聖人相禮，左右司馬之具足以破其詐，裔夷亂華之卻足以革其心，
translation_en: When a great state unleashes its tyrannical might against the interior [i.e., Lu 魯], he who is fearful of engaging the enemy deserves ridicule; when a great state harbors schemes to encroach upon the interior, he who is courageous in repelling the enemy deserves praise. Thus, Duke Xi 僖公 did not dare to overtake the army of Qi 齊, whereas the Sage [Confucius] was able to repel the hosts of Qi; the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) records both in full, and therein courage and cowardice are made manifest. Moreover, as for the relationship between Lu and Qi: speaking in terms of their ancestors, the Duke of Zhou 周公 and Grand Duke [Jiang Ziya] 太公 jointly assisted the royal house of Zhou and once had a covenant of hereditary friendship; discussing it in terms of the Spring and Autumn period, Duke Huan [of Qi] 桓公 established the hegemony and assembled the feudal lords to illustrate their ancient duties—how could there be the nursing of private grievances? Now, when Duke Xiao of Qi 齊孝 succeeded to the rule, he cast aside the royal mandate and neglected his duties, raising an unprovoked host to wantonly invade our western borderlands, ravaging our suburban strongholds and tormenting our people. Thus, the one in the wrong and exhausted was Qi, while the one in the right and vigorous was Lu—what was there to fear in Qi? Why then did Duke Xi, while on the throne, have no plan for defense when Qi arrived, and only after Qi departed raise an army in pursuit, penetrating deep into their territory only to return without overtaking them? Now, with the strength of Qi, how could it surpass Qin 秦? With the multitudes of Lu, how were they weaker than Zhao 趙? Yet at the meeting at Mianchi 澠池, once Lin Xiangru 藺相如 roused his spirit, his awe-inspiring credibility extended over the enemy state; though Qin was like a tiger or wolf, it still did not dare to make a move—how much less should the ruler of a state of a thousand chariots fear Qi to such a degree! Alas! "If on self-examination I find that I am upright, I will go forward against thousands and tens of thousands." Yet Duke Xi was unworthy of speaking of this. By the late Spring and Autumn period, when Duke Jing of Qi 齊景 rose in turn, his ambition to encroach upon Lu was even more extreme than that of Duke Xiao of Qi. For instance, at the meeting at Jiagu 夾谷, he listened to the words of Li Mi 犁彌 and laid a plot to seize the ruler of Lu; when the two rulers approached the altar, [men] rose up with beating drums and clamor, so that Qi held an irresistible advantage and Lu faced an unfathomable disaster—what could Lu do about it? Fortunately, the Sage assisted in the ceremonies: the provision of the Left and Right Marshals (Sima) was sufficient to foil their deceit, and the rebuff against frontier barbarians throwing China into disorder was sufficient to reform their hearts; …

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
故揖讓指麾齊遂感服彼向也齊孝之眾不足以當
齊景僖公之世足以勝定公之末年舉兵追齊尚不
敢及詎意仲尼一言而能却齊之若此乎噫善養氣
者匹夫不為千乘屈於聖人有足徵雖然僖公之無
勇固不足論吾夫子之聖綏來動和神妙不測豈特
能變齊而已耶行乎季孫三月不違二邑迭毀變魯
之幾又可驗矣使魯克終用之則吾其東周之志不
徒托諸空言也奈何女樂魯庭聖轍汶上千載之下
不能不為之太息
===
楚人伐鄭〔僖公元年〕齊侯宋公江人黃人盟于貫〔僖公〕
〔二年〕遂伐楚盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕楚人陳侯蔡
侯鄭伯許男圍宋〔僖公二十七年〕晉侯齊師宋師秦
師及楚人戰于城濮楚師敗績〔僖公二十八年〕楚人
圍江晉陽處父帥師伐楚以救江〔文公三年〕
沈𤇍
同考試官訓導李批題本平易作者語多陳腐
令人厭觀融會傳註成文並作
得之矣非熟於麟經者能之乎
punctuated:
故揖讓指麾，齊遂感服。彼向也，齊孝之眾不足以當齊景，僖公之世足以勝定公之末年，舉兵追齊尚不敢及，詎意仲尼一言而能却齊之若此乎？噫！善養氣者，匹夫不為千乘屈，於聖人有足徵。雖然，僖公之無勇固不足論，吾夫子之聖，綏來動和，神妙不測，豈特能變齊而已耶？行乎季孫，三月不違，二邑迭毀，變魯之幾又可驗矣。使魯克終用之，則「吾其東周」之志，不徒托諸空言也。奈何女樂魯庭，聖轍汶上，千載之下，不能不為之太息。

楚人伐鄭〔僖公元年〕；齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人盟于貫〔僖公〕〔二年〕；遂伐楚，盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕；楚人、陳侯、蔡侯、鄭伯、許男圍宋〔僖公二十七年〕；晉侯、齊師、宋師、秦師及楚人戰于城濮，楚師敗績〔僖公二十八年〕；楚人圍江，晉陽處父帥師伐楚以救江〔文公三年〕。
沈𤇍
同考試官訓導李批：題本平易，作者語多陳腐，令人厭觀；融會傳註成文，並作得之矣，非熟於《麟經》者能之乎？
translation_en:
…Therefore, through his bowing and yielding and his gesturing in command, Qi was moved to submit. Previously, the forces of Duke Xiao of Qi (Qi Xiao 齊孝) were no match for those of Duke Jing of Qi (Qi Jing 齊景), and the era of Duke Xi (Xi gong 僖公) was more than a match for the final years of Duke Ding (Ding gong 定公); yet when Duke Xi raised troops to pursue Qi, he still dared not catch up with them—who would have thought that a single word from Zhongni 仲尼 [Confucius] could repulse Qi like this? Alas! That one who is good at nourishing his vital energy (qi 氣), even as a commoner, will not bend before a lord of a thousand chariots is amply attested in the Sage. Even so, Duke Xi's lack of courage is certainly not worth discussing; as for the sageliness of our Master—"pacifying them so they come, moving them so they are harmonious," wondrous and unfathomable—how could it merely be capable of transforming Qi and nothing more? When he acted in the administration through Jisun 季孫, for three months there was no violation of right, and the two cities were successively dismantled; the incipient sign of transforming Lu could again be verified. Had Lu been able to employ him to the end, then his aspiration—"I would make an Eastern Zhou!"—would not have been merely entrusted to empty words. Yet what could be done when female musicians entered the court of Lu, and the Sage's carriage tracks turned toward the Wen River (Wenshang 汶上)? A thousand years later, one cannot help heaving a deep sigh over it.

"The men of Chu attacked Zheng" [1st year of Duke Xi]; "The Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the men of Jiang, and the men of Huang made a covenant at Guan" [2nd year of Duke Xi]; "They thereupon attacked Chu, and made a covenant at Shaoling" [4th year of Duke Xi]; "The men of Chu, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, and the Baron of Xu besieged Song" [27th year of Duke Xi]; "The Marquis of Jin, the army of Qi, the army of Song, and the army of Qin fought with the men of Chu at Chengpu, and the army of Chu was utterly defeated" [28th year of Duke Xi]; "The men of Chu besieged Jiang; Yang Chufu 陽處父 of Jin led an army to attack Chu in order to rescue Jiang" [3rd year of Duke Wen].

Shen Jiong 沈𤇍.

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor (xundao) Li comments: The topic is inherently plain and straightforward, and the writers' language is mostly stale and trite, making them tiresome to read; [yet this candidate] thoroughly integrates the commentaries and annotations into a coherent essay, capturing the essence of this combined topic—could anyone not thoroughly versed in the Unicorn Classic (Linjing 麟經, i.e., the Spring and Autumn Annals) be capable of this?…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭鄭批〔乎故取之冠本房斷桓文晉襄用兵得失殆無餘蘊〕
考試官學正王批〔得胡傳之意〕
外患迭加於大國而伯主得安攘之道可予外患繼
加於小國而伯主失安攘之道可譏夫伯者之責莫
大乎攘夷安夏而尤在乎用兵之有法也春秋備書
桓文晉襄攘楚之事而得失見矣何則楚之始封辟
在荆山篳路藍縷以處草莽桃弧棘矢以共禦王事
===
而已豈意其暴横憑陵如春秋之世耶始也怒鄭即
齊則興兵以伐鄭繼也怒宋從晉則合兵以圍宋夫
宋鄭大國非附庸比也楚人伐之豈不悉索敝賦以
偕行乎使桓文之伯急於救患而失用兵之法則楚
必長驅中原而宋鄭之患不可紓矣幸而不然彼江
黄楚之羽翼也桓則遠結盟之以孤其勢合八國伐
楚而楚遂求盟曹衞楚之黨與也文則私許復之以
携其心會四國戰楚而楚遂敗績不必勞師救鄭而
伐鄭之謀自罷不待分兵救宋而圍宋之役自解桓
punctuated:
〔乎？故取之冠本房。〕
考試官教諭鄭批：〔斷桓、文、晉襄用兵得失，殆無餘蘊。〕
考試官學正王批：〔得胡傳之意。〕

外患迭加於大國，而伯主得安攘之道，可予；外患繼加於小國，而伯主失安攘之道，可譏。夫伯者之責，莫大乎攘夷安夏，而尤在乎用兵之有法也。《春秋》備書桓、文、晉襄攘楚之事，而得失見矣。何則？楚之始封，辟在荆山，篳路藍縷，以處草莽；桃弧棘矢，以共禦王事而已。豈意其暴横憑陵，如春秋之世耶？始也，怒鄭即齊，則興兵以伐鄭；繼也，怒宋從晉，則合兵以圍宋。夫宋、鄭大國，非附庸比也。楚人伐之，豈不悉索敝賦以偕行乎？使桓、文之伯，急於救患而失用兵之法，則楚必長驅中原，而宋、鄭之患不可紓矣。幸而不然。彼江、黄，楚之羽翼也，桓則遠結盟之，以孤其勢，合八國伐楚，而楚遂求盟；曹、衞，楚之黨與也，文則私許復之，以携其心，會四國戰楚，而楚遂敗績。不必勞師救鄭，而伐鄭之謀自罷；不待分兵救宋，而圍宋之役自解。桓、…
translation_en:
…〔Without being thoroughly versed in the Classic of the Unicorn [Spring and Autumn Annals], could one achieve this? Therefore I have selected it to head my examination ward.〕
Examiner and Instructor Zheng commented: 〔In judging the successes and failures in the use of military force by Duke Huan of Qi, Duke Wen of Jin, and Duke Xiang of Jin, it leaves almost nothing unexpressed.〕
Examiner and Director of Studies Wang commented: 〔It grasps the meaning of Hu An-guo's Commentary (Hu zhuan).〕

When external threats were repeatedly inflicted upon major states, the hegemons grasped the way of pacifying the Central States and repelling the barbarians, which is worthy of praise; when external threats were subsequently inflicted upon a minor state, the hegemon lost the way of pacifying and repelling, which is worthy of criticism. Now, the responsibility of a hegemon is none greater than repelling the barbarians and pacifying the Central States (Xia), and it lies especially in having proper method in the use of military force. The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) fully records the affairs of Duke Huan of Qi, Duke Wen of Jin, and Duke Xiang of Jin in repelling Chu, and their successes and failures are thereby revealed. Why is this so? When Chu was first enfeoffed, it lay far off in the Jing Mountains, riding in wicker carts and wearing ragged clothes to dwell in the wild brush, with peach-wood bows and thorn arrows merely to supply and defend the king's business. How could one have anticipated that it would become so violent, arrogant, and encroaching as in the age of the Spring and Autumn period? At first, angered that Zheng had aligned with Qi, it raised troops to attack Zheng; subsequently, angered that Song had followed Jin, it combined troops to besiege Song. Now, Song and Zheng were major states, not comparable to dependent statelets. When the men of Chu attacked them, did they not exhaustively levy their worn-out military quotas to march forth together? Had Duke Huan and Duke Wen as hegemons been overly hasty in rescuing them from disaster and lost the proper method of using military force, Chu would surely have driven deep into the Central Plains, and the calamities of Song and Zheng could not have been relieved. Fortunately, it was not so. Those states of Jiang and Huang were the wings of Chu; Duke Huan formed distant alliances with them in order to isolate Chu's power, and united eight states to attack Chu, whereupon Chu sought a covenant. Cao and Wei were the partisans of Chu; Duke Wen privately promised to restore them in order to alienate their hearts from Chu, and assembled four states to battle Chu, whereupon Chu suffered a crushing defeat. Without needing to weary the army to rescue Zheng, the plot to attack Zheng ceased of its own accord; without waiting to divide the troops to rescue Song, the campaign to besiege Song dissolved of itself. The achievements of Duke Huan and…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
文之功不其偉哉自是而後晉襄嗣伯楚復陸梁以
報沈之後興圍江之師夫江國小而弱非能與宋鄭
比也楚人圍之豈待徹四境屯戍守禦之衆與宿衛
盡行乎使晉襄能效桓文之為則楚必震恐而江圍
自解矣計不出此商臣之罪覆載不容也不能聲其
罪以致討齊秦之兵天下莫強也不能用其兵以為
援乃遣處父之孤軍遠攻陸梁之強國門于方城而
止遇夫息公而還既無以挫楚人暴狠之鋒又無以
解江人倒懸之苦晉襄之失不亦大哉雖然以功利
===
言之則桓文襄之得失較然矣以道義論之伐楚之
役不請王命擅合諸侯豈天吏之伐歟城濮之戰伐
衛致楚陰謀取勝豈王者之事歟噫仲尼之徒無道
桓文之事其有以夫
禮記義
仁者右也道者左也仁者人也道者義也厚於
仁者薄於義親而不尊厚於義者薄於仁尊
而不親
霍震
punctuated:
文之功，不其偉哉！自是而後，晉襄嗣伯，楚復陸梁。以報沈之後，興圍江之師。夫江，國小而弱，非能與宋、鄭比也。楚人圍之，豈待徹四境屯戍守禦之衆與宿衛盡行乎？使晉襄能效桓、文之為，則楚必震恐，而江圍自解矣。計不出此：商臣之罪，覆載不容也，不能聲其罪以致討；齊、秦之兵，天下莫強也，不能用其兵以為援。乃遣處父之孤軍，遠攻陸梁之強國，門于方城而止，遇夫息公而還。既無以挫楚人暴狠之鋒，又無以解江人倒懸之苦，晉襄之失，不亦大哉！雖然，以功利言之，則桓、文、襄之得失較然矣。以道義論之：伐楚之役，不請王命，擅合諸侯，豈天吏之伐歟？城濮之戰，伐衛致楚，陰謀取勝，豈王者之事歟？噫！仲尼之徒，無道桓、文之事，其有以夫！
禮記義
仁者右也，道者左也。仁者人也，道者義也。厚於仁者薄於義，親而不尊；厚於義者薄於仁，尊而不親。
霍震
translation_en:
… [Huan and] Wen—were their achievements not magnificent indeed! Thereafter, Duke Xiang of Jin (Jin Xiang 晉襄) succeeded to the hegemony, and Chu once again grew unruly and defiant. Following the expedition in retaliation against Shen, Chu raised an army to besiege Jiang. Now Jiang was a small and weak state, by no means comparable to Song or Zheng. When the men of Chu besieged it, would they have needed to withdraw all the garrison and defense troops from their four borders and march out with their entire palace guard? Had Duke Xiang of Jin been able to emulate the deeds of Dukes Huan and Wen, Chu would surely have trembled in fear, and the siege of Jiang would have been lifted of its own accord. Yet his strategy did not hit upon this: the crime of Shangchen was something that neither heaven nor earth could tolerate, yet he failed to proclaim that crime and launch a punitive expedition; the armies of Qi and Qin were the strongest in the realm, yet he failed to employ their forces as reinforcements. Instead, he dispatched the isolated force of Chufu to attack an unruly and powerful state from afar, only to halt after assaulting the gates at Fangcheng and turn back upon encountering the Duke of Xi. Having neither blunted the fierce and ruthless edge of the men of Chu nor relieved the desperate plight of the people of Jiang, was the failure of Duke Xiang of Jin not great indeed! Even so, if we speak in terms of功利 (utilitarian success and advantage), the successes and failures of Dukes Huan, Wen, and Xiang are plain to see. If we judge them in terms of moral principle and righteousness, however: in the campaign to attack Chu, assembling the feudal lords on one's own authority without requesting the king's mandate—how could that be the punitive expedition of a Heaven-appointed officer? In the Battle of Chengpu, attacking Wei to draw out Chu and winning victory through covert schemes—how could that be the deed of a true king? Alas! That the disciples of Confucius (Zhongni 仲尼) never spoke of the affairs of Huan and Wen—there was surely good reason for it!

Exposition on the Record of Rites (Liji 禮記)
"Benevolence is the right; the Way is the left. Benevolence is humanity; the Way is righteousness. One who is generous in benevolence but slight in righteousness is treated with affection, yet not revered; one who is generous in righteousness but slight in benevolence is revered, yet not treated with affection."
Huo Zhen 霍震

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭蕭批此題似易而難場中作者多
泛而不切講貫詳明而於理
不失者僅見此篇是宜錄出
考試官教諭鄭批此作以仁右道左通貫一篇之旨
最為切當
考試官學正王批辭理通貫
知仁道相資以為用當知仁義偏厚為有失盖仁也
道也義也並行而不相悖也然仁之與道既先後之
相資則夫仁義偏一又豈無所失哉今夫仁者人之
===
體也將有為也將有行也非仁則無以任重於先故
曰仁者右也以右者人所有事凡人之舉動必先之
也道者天之理也仁至于不可行不可節則理有所
不得已而為之輔故曰道者左也以左居不用之地
而助右之所不及也然是仁也非自外而至內也即
吾身所具之理而已故又曰仁者人也是道也非冥
行而妄作也即吾心制事之宜而已故又曰道者義
也道非仁不立義非人不行仁道相資為用如此則
仁義又豈可偏於一哉夫仁莫隆於父子父子之道
punctuated:
同考試官教諭蕭批：此題似易而難，場中作者多泛而不切，講貫詳明而於理不失者，僅見此篇，是宜錄出。
考試官教諭鄭批：此作以仁右道左通貫一篇之旨，最為切當。
考試官學正王批：辭理通貫。
知仁道相資以為用，當知仁義偏厚為有失。盖仁也，道也，義也，並行而不相悖也。然仁之與道，既先後之相資，則夫仁義偏一，又豈無所失哉？今夫仁者，人之體也。將有為也，將有行也，非仁則無以任重於先，故曰「仁者右也」，以右者人所有事，凡人之舉動必先之也。道者，天之理也。仁至于不可行、不可節，則理有所不得已而為之輔，故曰「道者左也」，以左居不用之地，而助右之所不及也。然是仁也，非自外而至內也，即吾身所具之理而已，故又曰「仁者人也」。是道也，非冥行而妄作也，即吾心制事之宜而已，故又曰「道者義也」。道非仁不立，義非人不行，仁道相資為用如此，則仁義又豈可偏於一哉？夫仁莫隆於父子，父子之道，
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Xiao comments: This topic seems easy but is actually difficult. In the examination hall, most writers were vague and missed the point.
