Only in this essay do we see an exposition that is thorough, clear, and does not lose sight of principle; it is fitting that it be selected for publication.

Examiner and County Director of Studies Zheng comments: This composition threads the idea of "humaneness as the right hand and the Way as the left" throughout the entire essay's main purport; it is most apt and fitting.

Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang comments: Both the diction and the reasoning are thoroughly coherent.

When one understands that humaneness (ren) and the Way (dao) rely upon each other to function, one ought to understand that favoring either humaneness or righteousness (yi) at the expense of the other is a failing. For humaneness, the Way, and righteousness operate in parallel without contradicting one another. Yet since humaneness and the Way rely upon each other in sequence of priority, how could leaning one-sidedly toward either humaneness or righteousness not result in a failing?

Now, humaneness is the very substance of a person. When one is about to act, or about to proceed, without humaneness there is no means to shoulder the heavy burden from the outset. Therefore it is said, "Humaneness is the right," because the right hand is what a person uses to handle affairs, and in all human movements it must take the lead. The Way is the principle of Heaven. When humaneness reaches a point where it cannot be carried out or cannot be moderated, then principle of necessity comes to its aid. Therefore it is said, "The Way is the left," because the left hand occupies the position of non-employment, assisting where the right hand falls short.

Yet this humaneness does not come from outside to enter within; it is simply the principle inherent in our own person. Therefore it is further said, "Humaneness is being human." And this Way is not blind action or reckless fabrication; it is simply the appropriateness with which our mind regulates affairs. Therefore it is further said, "The Way is righteousness." The Way is not established without humaneness, and righteousness is not practiced without the human person. Since humaneness and the Way rely on each other to function in this manner, how then could humaneness and righteousness be slanted toward only one side?

Now, humaneness is nowhere more exalted than between father and son, and the way of father and son…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
親親也義莫重於君臣君臣之道尊尊也仁之與義
皆原於所降之衷初未嘗有厚薄之分也惟其不知
道左以輔乎仁則厚於仁者薄於義矣故知有其親
而不知有其尊焉義之與仁皆根於固有之性亦未
嘗有厚薄之間也惟其不知仁右以先乎義則厚於
義者薄於仁矣故知有其尊而不知有其親焉誠知
其所以為左右則尊尊親親並行不悖又豈有厚薄
也哉抑考表記一篇言仁義之道不一而足上文既
曰仁者天下之表也義者天下之制也下文又曰仁
===
有數義有長短小大合是而觀于以見仁義之用於
己者不同而其體之所存者無不同仁義之施於人
者雖殊而其理之相資者無或殊讀禮者宜深味之
一馬從二馬三馬既立請慶多馬
何津
同考試官教諭蕭批投壺一篇本房作者頗多
而於一馬二馬處俱欠發明
此篇融會傳註組織成文故
表而出之
punctuated:
親親也。義莫重於君臣，君臣之道，尊尊也。仁之與義，皆原於所降之衷，初未嘗有厚薄之分也。惟其不知道左以輔乎仁，則厚於仁者薄於義矣，故知有其親而不知有其尊焉。義之與仁，皆根於固有之性，亦未嘗有厚薄之間也。惟其不知仁右以先乎義，則厚於義者薄於仁矣，故知有其尊而不知有其親焉。誠知其所以為左右，則尊尊親親，並行不悖，又豈有厚薄也哉？抑考《表記》一篇，言仁義之道不一而足。上文既曰「仁者天下之表也，義者天下之制也」，下文又曰「仁有數，義有長短小大」。合是而觀，于以見仁義之用於己者不同，而其體之所存者無不同；仁義之施於人者雖殊，而其理之相資者無或殊。讀《禮》者宜深味之。

一馬從二馬，三馬既立，請慶多馬。
何津
同考試官教諭蕭批：《投壺》一篇，本房作者頗多，而於一馬二馬處俱欠發明。此篇融會傳註，組織成文，故表而出之。
translation_en:
…is to treat one's kin with affection. No righteousness is weightier than that between ruler and minister, and the Way of ruler and minister is to honor the honorable. Benevolence and righteousness both originate in the moral sense conferred by Heaven; originally there was never any distinction of thick or thin between them. Only when one does not understand that the Way is on the left to assist benevolence do those who are thick in benevolence become thin in righteousness; therefore they know they have their kin, yet do not know they have those whom they must honor. Righteousness and benevolence are both rooted in our inherent nature; nor was there ever any gap of thick or thin between them. Only when one does not understand that benevolence is on the right to precede righteousness do those who are thick in righteousness become thin in benevolence; therefore they know they have those whom they must honor, yet do not know they have their kin. If one truly understands why they serve as left and right, then honoring the honorable and treating one's kin with affection will proceed together without contradiction—how then could there be any thickness or thinness between them? Moreover, if we examine the "Biaoji" (Record on Example) chapter as a whole, it speaks of the Way of benevolence and righteousness more than once. In the preceding passage it says, "Benevolence is the standard of the world; righteousness is the regulator of the world," and in the following passage it says again, "Benevolence has its degrees; righteousness has its long and short, its small and great." Viewing these together, one may see that although the application of benevolence and righteousness in oneself differs, the substance in which they reside is in no way different; and although the bestowal of benevolence and righteousness upon others varies, the principle by which they mutually support one another in no way varies. Readers of the Record of Rites (Liji) ought to savor this deeply.

"One horse-counter joins the two horse-counters; now that three horse-counters are set up, I beg leave to offer congratulations to the side with more horse-counters."
He Jin
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Xiao: Quite a few candidates in my examination ward wrote on this topic from the "Touhu" (Pitch-Pot) chapter, yet all lacked clear exposition regarding the "one horse-counter" and "two horse-counters." This essay thoroughly integrates the commentaries and annotations, weaving them into a coherent composition; therefore I have singled it out for distinction.

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭鄭批此作能發投壺立馬之意
必熟於禮者
考試官學正王批文有發揮
以少算而附多筭得一成而宜舉賀此司射告賓之
辭也夫投壺立馬所以表勝司射告賓安得不詳致
其辭哉記禮者知其然謂夫燕飲非投壺則無以樂
賓投壺非立馬則無以表勝勝者立馬取筭以為馬
者所以表其勝之數也謂筭為馬者馬乃威武之用
投壺亦是習武故云馬也司射於此宜何如哉必告
===
之曰禮以三勝為成但勝偶未必專頻得三如四矢
順入正爵既行此一勝而立一馬者也故必以此一
馬從夫勝偶之二馬用以足乎三馬之數焉八算俱
釋勝飲罍舉此再勝而立二馬者也故必取彼一馬
益乎在已之二馬庸以備夫三馬之算焉夫以一馬
從二馬則三馬於焉而立矣三馬既立是其勝已成
之時也馬之少者寧可以不之慶乎于以酌彼金罍
以慶夫多馬之人焉頻得三勝則三勝於焉而成矣
三勝既成是其禮垂畢之際也偶之劣者寧可以不
punctuated:
考試官教諭鄭批：此作能發投壺立馬之意，必熟於禮者。
考試官學正王批：文有發揮。
以少算而附多筭，得一成而宜舉賀，此司射告賓之辭也。夫投壺立馬所以表勝，司射告賓，安得不詳致其辭哉？記禮者知其然，謂夫燕飲非投壺則無以樂賓，投壺非立馬則無以表勝。勝者立馬，取筭以為馬者，所以表其勝之數也；謂筭為馬者，馬乃威武之用，投壺亦是習武，故云馬也。司射於此宜何如哉？必告之曰：禮以三勝為成，但勝偶未必專頻得三。如四矢順入，正爵既行，此一勝而立一馬者也；故必以此一馬從夫勝偶之二馬，用以足乎三馬之數焉。八算俱釋，勝飲罍舉，此再勝而立二馬者也；故必取彼一馬益乎在已之二馬，庸以備夫三馬之算焉。夫以一馬從二馬，則三馬於焉而立矣。三馬既立，是其勝已成之時也，馬之少者寧可以不之慶乎？于以酌彼金罍，以慶夫多馬之人焉。頻得三勝，則三勝於焉而成矣。三勝既成，是其禮垂畢之際也，偶之劣者寧可以不
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Zheng commented: This piece brings out the meaning of setting up the "horses" in the pitch-pot game; the author must be well-versed in the Rites.
Examiner and Director of Studies Wang commented: The essay shows thorough elaboration.
Attaching the fewer tallies to the greater number of tallies, and properly offering congratulations once a full round is achieved—these are the words with which the Master of Archery addresses the guests. Now, setting up "horses" in the pitch-pot game is the means of marking victory; when the Master of Archery addresses the guests, how could he not deliver his words in full detail? The recorder of the Rites understood this to be so, holding that in banquets and drinking, without the pitch-pot game there is no way to entertain the guests, and in the pitch-pot game, without setting up "horses" there is no way to mark victory. When the victor sets up a "horse," taking a tally to serve as a "horse" is the means of marking the count of his victories; as for calling the tally a "horse," the horse is an instrument of martial might, and pitching into the pot is likewise a practice of martial skills, which is why it is called a "horse." What, then, should the Master of Archery do at this point? He must announce to them, saying: According to ritual, three victories constitute a completed round, yet the winning side does not necessarily win all three in succession on its own. For instance, when four arrows enter smoothly and the regular penalty cup has been administered, this is winning once and setting up one "horse"; therefore, one must make this one "horse" follow the two "horses" of the winning side, using it to fill out the number of three "horses." When all eight tallies have been laid down and the cup for the victor to give drink is raised, this is winning twice and setting up two "horses"; therefore, one must take that one "horse" over there and add it to the two "horses" on one's own side, thereby completing the count of three "horses." Now, when one "horse" follows two "horses," then the three "horses" are thereupon set up. Once the three "horses" are set up, it is the moment when victory has been completed—how could the one with fewer "horses" not offer congratulations to the other? Thus, he pours from that bronze jar to congratulate the person with more "horses." And if one wins three times in succession, then the three victories are thereupon completed. Once the three victories are completed, it is the occasion when the ceremony is nearing its end—how could the inferior side not…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
□□□□于以稱彼兕觥以賀夫得勝之偶焉司射之
實之意如此豈特虛文而已哉大抵投壺射禮之細
亦男子之所有事者也故其舉行之間必貍首是歌
授矢是告欲其志正體直持之審固而後可以言中
也是則雖曰且以樂賓實則可以習容講藝而觀德
矣此先王所以不廢也歟
論
致治之法垂於萬世
王淮
===
同考試官訓導郭批〔本房論幾三百卷求其詞理條暢足以發題意者僅見此篇〕
同考試官教諭汪批〔立論於典實之中不騁浮辭而意已獨至可羨可羨〕
考試官教諭鄭批〔議論典實能發聖人作經之意〕
考試官學正王批〔有發越〕
聖人有功於世道其大矣哉何也盖扶世立教
聖人之本心也使其達而在上則致治之迹固
著於有為矣特其窮而在下故不得已於有言
punctuated:
□□□□，于以稱彼兕觥，以賀夫得勝之偶焉。司射之實之意如此，豈特虛文而已哉？大抵投壺，射禮之細，亦男子之所有事者也。故其舉行之間，必《貍首》是歌，授矢是告，欲其志正體直，持之審固，而後可以言中。也是則雖曰且以樂賓，實則可以習容、講藝而觀德矣。此先王所以不廢也歟！

論
致治之法垂於萬世
王淮
同考試官訓導郭批：〔本房論幾三百卷，求其詞理條暢，足以發題意者，僅見此篇。〕
同考試官教諭汪批：〔立論於典實之中，不騁浮辭，而意已獨至，可羨可羨。〕
考試官教諭鄭批：〔議論典實，能發聖人作經之意。〕
考試官學正王批：〔有發越。〕
聖人有功於世道，其大矣哉！何也？盖扶世立教，聖人之本心也。使其達而在上，則致治之迹，固著於有為矣；特其窮而在下，故不得已於有言，
translation_en:
… [four illegible characters], and thus raise that rhinoceros-horn goblet to congratulate the winning pair! Such is the true meaning behind the Director of Archery's words [?]; how could it merely be empty formality? In general, the pitch-pot game is a minor version of the archery ritual, yet it is also a matter with which men concern themselves. Therefore, during its performance, the "Lishou" ode must be sung and the presentation of arrows must be announced, desiring that one's mind be upright and body straight, holding the arrows with careful firmness, only after which can one speak of hitting the mark. Thus, although it is said to be a means to entertain guests, in reality it can be used to practice deportment, cultivate skills, and observe virtue. Is this not why the former kings did not abolish it?

Discourse
"The Methods for Achieving Good Governance Are Handed Down for Ten Thousand Generations"
Wang Huai

Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Guo: [Among the nearly three hundred discourse papers in my examination ward, in seeking one whose diction and reasoning are fluent and clear enough to bring out the meaning of the theme, I found only this piece.]
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Wang: [It establishes its argument on the basis of classical substance; without indulging in florid language, its meaning reaches a unique height. Admirable, admirable!]
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zheng: [The argumentation is classically substantial and able to bring out the sage's intention in composing the Classics.]
Comment by Examiner Director of Studies Wang: [Possesses incisive brilliance.]

How great indeed is the sage's meritorious service to the Way of the world! Why is this so? Because to uphold the world and establish teachings is the fundamental intention of the sage. Had he achieved eminence and occupied a position above, the traces of his achieving good governance would certainly have been manifested in active deeds; it was only because he was in distress and remained below that he had no choice but to express himself in words, …

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而致治之法垂於萬世實萬世之幸也聖人有
功於世道不既大乎盖嘗因是而論之天下之
生久矣或氣化有盛衰而人事之得失於是乎
生或人事有得失而氣化之盛衰於是乎轉治
亂相因理之常也聖人之生斯世亦惟撥亂而
歸治焉耳若吾夫子者正有心於行道濟時者
也假使其得邦家則綏来動和神妙不測而致
治之道行矣惜乎有德無位窮而在下所以作
春秋垂致治之法於萬世焉或者乃曰帝如堯
===
舜其德足以教天下致治之法垂於萬世宜矣
王如禹湯文武其功足以勸天下致治之法垂
於萬世似矣彼孔子也或絶粮於陳或見畏於
匡未嘗得志於當時也而致治之法安在或伐
木於衛或削迹於宋未嘗有土於當世也而致
治之法何有噫此以窮達論聖人也聖人果可
以窮達論哉聖人身雖窮而道則達也豈肯果
於忘世乎周室東遷王綱解紐人心不正甚矣
名分不明久矣人心不正治道之累也名分不
punctuated: 而致治之法垂於萬世，實萬世之幸也。聖人有功於世道，不既大乎？盖嘗因是而論之：天下之生久矣，或氣化有盛衰，而人事之得失於是乎生；或人事有得失，而氣化之盛衰於是乎轉。治亂相因，理之常也。聖人之生斯世，亦惟撥亂而歸治焉耳。若吾夫子者，正有心於行道濟時者也。假使其得邦家，則綏来動和，神妙不測，而致治之道行矣。惜乎有德無位，窮而在下，所以作《春秋》，垂致治之法於萬世焉。或者乃曰：「帝如堯、舜，其德足以教天下，致治之法垂於萬世，宜矣；王如禹、湯、文、武，其功足以勸天下，致治之法垂於萬世，似矣。彼孔子也，或絶粮於陳，或見畏於匡，未嘗得志於當時也，而致治之法安在？或伐木於衛，或削迹於宋，未嘗有土於當世也，而致治之法何有？」噫！此以窮達論聖人也。聖人果可以窮達論哉？聖人身雖窮而道則達也，豈肯果於忘世乎？周室東遷，王綱解紐，人心不正甚矣，名分不明久矣。人心不正，治道之累也；名分不
translation_en:
…so that the model for achieving good order was handed down to ten thousand generations—which is truly the good fortune of ten thousand generations. Is not the sage's merit toward the moral state of the world great indeed?

I have ventured to discuss the matter on this basis: The world has existed for a long time. Sometimes the cosmic transformations of qi flourish or decline, and from this arise the successes and failures of human affairs; sometimes human affairs succeed or fail, and through this the flourishing and decline of the cosmic transformations are turned. That order and disorder follow from one another is the constant norm of principle. When a sage is born into this world, his sole aim is to quell disorder and restore good governance. Someone like our Master [Confucius] was precisely one whose heart was set on putting the Way into practice and rescuing his age. Had he gained possession of a state or a ruling house, he would have comforted the people so that they came to him, and moved them to harmony in ways wondrously unfathomable, and the Way of achieving good order would have been put into practice. Alas, he possessed virtue without a ruling position and remained in obscurity below; therefore he composed the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) to hand down the model for achieving good order to ten thousand generations.

Yet someone might say: "With emperors like Yao and Shun, their virtue was sufficient to instruct the world, so it was fitting that their model for achieving good order was handed down to ten thousand generations; with kings like Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, their achievements were sufficient to encourage the world, so it seems reasonable that their model for achieving good order was handed down to ten thousand generations. As for that Confucius, at times he was cut off from provisions in Chen, and at times he was threatened in Kuang; he never fulfilled his ambitions in his own time, so where was his model for achieving good order? At times he had the tree cut down over him in Wei [or Song], and at times his footprints were wiped away in Song; he never possessed territory in his own age, so what model for achieving good order did he have?"

Alas! This is to judge a sage by adversity and success. Can a sage truly be judged by adversity and success? Though the sage's person was in adversity, his Way succeeded; how could he have been willing resolutely to forget the world? When the Zhou royal house moved east, the royal cords of authority came undone; human minds had become gravely unrighteous, and titles and obligations had long been obscure. Unrighteous human minds are an impediment to the Way of governance; obscure titles and obligations…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
明治法之害也聖人天理之所在不以為已任
而誰可於是托南面之權行天子之事假魯史
以寓王法撥亂世反之正叙先後之倫秩上下
之分而惇典庸禮之法立有德者必褒有罪者
必貶而命德討罪之用行百王之法度在是萬
世之準繩在是所以遏人欲於横流存天理於
既滅使亂臣有所懼而不得售其奸賊子知所
警而不得肆其欲為後世慮也至深遠矣是以
由一世至於百世而致治之法昭然而莫掩由
===
百世至於萬世而致治之法秩然而不泯凡其
人心以正而無邪慝之患者人皆以為世之治
也而不知所以然者伊誰之功歟聖人致治之
法有以維持之也名分以明而無凌抗之失者
人咸以為世之治也而不知所以爾者伊誰之
力歟聖人致治之法有以軌範之也法垂於一
世即聖人道在於一世而有一世之功也法垂
於百世即聖人道在於百世而有百世之功也
致治之法垂於萬世則萬世即聖人之道也非
punctuated: 明，治法之害也。聖人，天理之所在，不以為已任而誰可？於是托南面之權，行天子之事，假魯史以寓王法，撥亂世反之正。叙先後之倫，秩上下之分，而惇典庸禮之法立；有德者必褒，有罪者必貶，而命德討罪之用行。百王之法度在是，萬世之準繩在是。所以遏人欲於横流，存天理於既滅，使亂臣有所懼而不得售其奸，賊子知所警而不得肆其欲，為後世慮也至深遠矣。是以由一世至於百世，而致治之法昭然而莫掩；由百世至於萬世，而致治之法秩然而不泯。凡其人心以正而無邪慝之患者，人皆以為世之治也，而不知所以然者，伊誰之功歟？聖人致治之法有以維持之也。名分以明而無凌抗之失者，人咸以為世之治也，而不知所以爾者，伊誰之力歟？聖人致治之法有以軌範之也。法垂於一世，即聖人道在於一世，而有一世之功也；法垂於百世，即聖人道在於百世，而有百世之功也。致治之法垂於萬世，則萬世即聖人之道也，非
translation_en: … clear is a harm to the institutions of governance. Since the Sage is the repository of Heavenly Principle, if he did not take this responsibility upon himself, who else could? Thereupon he assumed the authority of the southward-facing ruler and carried out the affairs of the Son of Heaven, borrowing the history of Lu to embody the Kingly Law and bringing order out of a chaotic age to restore it to rectitude. He ordered the relationships of precedence and arranged the distinctions between superior and inferior, and thus the institutions of honoring the five relationships and employing the five rites were established; he unfailingly praised those with virtue and censured those with guilt, and thus the functions of rewarding the virtuous and punishing the guilty were put into practice. Herein lie the institutional measures of the hundred kings; herein lies the standard for ten thousand generations. By this means he stemmed human desires in their rampant flow and preserved Heavenly Principle when it was nearly extinguished, causing rebellious ministers to be afraid and unable to peddle their treachery, and villainous sons to know caution and be unable to indulge their desires. His concern for later generations was most profound and far-reaching. Therefore, from one generation to a hundred generations, the institutions for bringing about order are luminous and cannot be obscured; from a hundred generations to ten thousand generations, the institutions for bringing about order are orderly and cannot be obliterated. Whenever human minds are rectified and free from the affliction of evil and depravity, everyone considers it the orderliness of the age, yet they do not know to whose merit this is due—it is because the Sage's institutions for bringing about order are there to uphold them. Whenever titles and obligations are clarified and free from the fault of transgression and defiance, everyone considers it the orderliness of the age, yet they do not know to whose strength this is due—it is because the Sage's institutions for bringing about order are there to regulate them. When the institutions are handed down for one generation, the Way of the Sage abides in that one generation, and there is the merit of one generation; when the institutions are handed down for a hundred generations, the Way of the Sage abides in those hundred generations, and there is the merit of a hundred generations. When the institutions for bringing about order are handed down for ten thousand generations, then those ten thousand generations are themselves the Way of the Sage; is it not …

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
擬宋賜進士呂溱等瓊林宴及大學篇謝表
同考試官教諭林批典實得體
考試官教諭鄭批得宋表之體
考試官學正王批典則可觀
伏以
道配乾坤世際
皇風之清穆星聨奎璧時逢文運之昌隆
澤霈清班歡騰善類共惟
〇〇〇〇
聰明睿哲
恭儉寛仁好察邇言有虞舜之智克艱厥后躬大
禹之勤歌九叙勸九功黎元安養闢四門明四
目賢俊登庸臣溱等秉性凡愚賦才疎薄粗知
儒術學不逮于古人偶擢賢科名有慚於進士
叨
賜瓊林之宴載頒大學之篇
寵渥駢臻戰兢交集際風雲之慶會依
punctuated:
擬宋賜進士呂溱等瓊林宴及《大學》篇謝表
同考試官教諭林批：典實得體。
考試官教諭鄭批：得宋表之體。
考試官學正王批：典則可觀。

伏以道配乾坤，世際皇風之清穆；星聨奎璧，時逢文運之昌隆。澤霈清班，歡騰善類。共惟〇〇〇〇，聰明睿哲，恭儉寛仁。好察邇言，有虞舜之智；克艱厥后，躬大禹之勤。歌九叙，勸九功，黎元安養；闢四門，明四目，賢俊登庸。臣溱等秉性凡愚，賦才疎薄，粗知儒術，學不逮于古人；偶擢賢科，名有慚於進士。叨賜瓊林之宴，載頒《大學》之篇。寵渥駢臻，戰兢交集。際風雲之慶會，依
translation_en:
Imitation of a Song-Dynasty Memorial of Thanks for Bestowing on the Metropolitan Graduates Lü Zhen 呂溱 and Others the Qionglin Banquet and the Text of the Great Learning (Daxue)
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Lin: Allusive, substantial, and fitting in style.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zheng: Captures the style of a Song memorial.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang: Standard and well worth reading.

We humbly consider: When the Way matches Heaven and Earth, the age encounters the pure tranquility of the August Wind; when the stars link in the constellations of Kui and Bi, the times meet with the flourishing prosperity of literary fortune. As bounty showers upon the pure ranks of officials, joy surges among the good and virtuous. We respectfully reflect that [Your Majesty], endowed with keen intelligence and profound wisdom, is reverent, frugal, magnanimous, and benevolent. Loving to examine near words, You possess the wisdom of Yu Shun; able to recognize the difficulties of sovereign rule, You personally practice the diligence of Great Yu. Singing of the nine orders and encouraging the nine achievements, the common people are peacefully nourished; throwing open the four gates and clarifying the four eyes, the worthy and eminent are elevated and employed. Your servants Zhen and others, endowed with ordinary and foolish natures and gifted with meager and shallow talents, have a rough knowledge of Confucian arts, yet our learning does not reach that of the ancients; having by chance been selected in the examination for the worthy, we are ashamed of the title of metropolitan graduate (jinshi). We have unworthily been bestowed the banquet in the Qionglin Garden, and further granted the text of the Great Learning. As rich favors arrive side by side, trembling and apprehension mingle within us. Meeting this auspicious gathering of wind and clouds, and relying upon …

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
日月之光華臣敢不益究厥心益精于業效涓埃
而圖補念夙夜以惟寅明德新民期多士聿崇
乎正學
敬
天法祖願萬年永保乎
丕基臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉表稱
謝以
===
聞
策
第一問
同考試官教諭陳批〔五策筆勢滔滔此篇敷答尤詳〕
考試官教諭鄭批〔必有學之士也敷答救世立教之意詳盡可嘉〕
考試官學正王批〔條答詳明〕
聖賢講學於下欲正綱常之道必立言以啟後
punctuated:
日月之光華，臣敢不益究厥心，益精于業？效涓埃而圖補，念夙夜以惟寅；明德新民，期多士聿崇乎正學；敬天法祖，願萬年永保乎丕基。臣無任瞻天仰聖，激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

策
第一問
同考試官教諭陳批：〔五策筆勢滔滔，此篇敷答尤詳。〕
考試官教諭鄭批：〔必有學之士也，敷答救世立教之意，詳盡可嘉。〕
考試官學正王批：〔條答詳明。〕

聖賢講學於下，欲正綱常之道，必立言以啟後
translation_en:
… the brilliance of the sun and moon. How could your servant dare not examine his mind ever more deeply and refine his studies ever more diligently? Offering a tiny drop or speck of dust in hopes of making some contribution, I remain reverent day and night. In illuminating luminous virtue and renewing the people, I hope the multitude of scholars will revere orthodox learning; in revering Heaven and emulating the ancestors, I pray that for ten thousand years Your Majesty will forever preserve the great foundation. Your servant is overcome with the utmost emotion and trepidation as he gazes up at Heaven and looks to Your Sacred Majesty, and respectfully presents this memorial of gratitude for the Imperial hearing.

Policy Essays
First Question
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Chen: [The brushwork of the five policy essays flows like a torrent; the exposition in this answer is especially detailed.]
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zheng: [Surely a scholar of true learning! His exposition of the intent to save the world and establish teaching is thorough and commendable.]
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Wang: [The itemized responses are detailed and clear.]

When sages and worthies expound upon learning below, wishing to rectify the Way of the three bonds and five constant virtues, they must establish words to enlighten later…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
世
聖皇建極於上欲盡君師之責必敷言以教當世盖
聖賢立教不外乎明倫理以正綱常别善惡而
備勸戒也肆孔子之作春秋朱子之集小學曁
我
朝
列聖之頒誥布書何莫而非聖賢立言垂世之法皇
極敷言教民之理歟昔孔子生周衰之時承堯
舜禹湯文武之統集群聖之大成雖刪詩書定
===
禮樂贊周易而載諸行事則莫大於春秋也其
載君臣行事如宰咺歸賵則書名子突救衛則
書字美齊桓服楚而譏其專予晉文之奬王而
著其譎固美惡備載矣朱子生有宋之時紹周
程張邵之傳而集諸儒之大成雖集詩傳著易
本義註釋學庸論孟諸書而教人之法莫先於
小學也其述嘉言善行顔孟之可學杜季良之
不可效高允以直見旌翟黑子以欺獲誅之類
亦勸戒兼備矣洪惟我
punctuated:
世；聖皇建極於上，欲盡君師之責，必敷言以教當世。盖聖賢立教，不外乎明倫理以正綱常，别善惡而備勸戒也。肆孔子之作《春秋》、朱子之集《小學》，曁我朝列聖之頒誥布書，何莫而非聖賢立言垂世之法、皇極敷言教民之理歟？

昔孔子生周衰之時，承堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之統，集群聖之大成。雖刪《詩》、《書》，定《禮》、《樂》，贊《周易》，而載諸行事，則莫大於《春秋》也。其載君臣行事，如宰咺歸賵則書名，子突救衛則書字；美齊桓服楚而譏其專，予晉文之奬王而著其譎，固美惡備載矣。朱子生有宋之時，紹周、程、張、邵之傳，而集諸儒之大成。雖集《詩傳》，著《易本義》，註釋《學》、《庸》、《論》、《孟》諸書，而教人之法，莫先於《小學》也。其述嘉言善行，顔、孟之可學，杜季良之不可效，高允以直見旌，翟黑子以欺獲誅之類，亦勸戒兼備矣。洪惟我
translation_en:
…generations; when the Sacred Sovereigns establish the Supreme Ultimate from above, wishing to fulfill the responsibilities of ruler and teacher, they must set forth words to instruct their own age. Indeed, the establishment of teachings by sages and worthies goes no further than clarifying human relations in order to rectify the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues, and distinguishing good from evil so as to provide both encouragement and warning. Thus, Confucius's authoring of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), Master Zhu's [Zhu Xi's] compilation of the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue), and the promulgation of grand pronouncements and distribution of books by the successive Sacred Emperors of our Dynasty—which of these is not a model of sages and worthies establishing words to hand down to posterity, and the principle of the Supreme Ultimate setting forth words to instruct the people?

In antiquity, Confucius was born in the era of Zhou's decline; he inherited the succession of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, synthesizing the great achievements of all the sages. Although he expurgated the Odes (Shi) and Documents (Shu), fixed the Rites (Li) and Music (Yue), and wrote commentaries on the Zhou Changes (Zhouyi), when it came to recording actual deeds and affairs, nothing was greater than the Spring and Autumn Annals. In its recording of the deeds of rulers and ministers—such as writing the personal name of Administrator Xuan when he came to present funerary gifts, and writing the style name of Zitu when he went to rescue Wei; praising Duke Huan of Qi for subduing Chu while criticizing his專 [autocratic] actions, and approving Duke Wen of Jin's support of the King while exposing his craftiness—both admirable and wicked deeds were certainly recorded in full. Master Zhu was born in the era of the Song dynasty; he continued the transmission of Zhou [Dunyi], the Chengs [Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi], Zhang [Zai], and Shao [Yong], synthesizing the great achievements of the various Confucians. Although he compiled the Transmission of the Odes (Shizhuan), authored the Original Meaning of the Changes (Yi benyi), and wrote commentaries explaining the Great Learning (Daxue), Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), Analects (Lunyu), and Mencius (Mengzi), as a method for instructing people, nothing took precedence over the Elementary Learning. In its recounting of admirable words and good deeds—such as how Yan [Hui] and Mencius should be emulated, how Du Jiliang should not be imitated, how Gao Yun was commended for his uprightness, and how Zhai Heizi was executed for his deceit—encouragement and warning were likewise both fully provided. Humbly reflecting on our…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝臨御之日尊崇聖道表章儒書嘗
頒大誥三編具載李子安余仁三之徒奸貪兇頑
之罪無所示勸蓋當時勸善之典功臣賢相有
誥券制勅之褒孝順節義有旌表門閭之
詔皆誥所未載也
太宗文皇帝為善陰隲書首蔣王靈應終周婦感悟
孝順事實書首虞舜大孝終劉婦孝姑備載古
今善孝之實而無所示戒蓋當時際
重熙累洽之運四海被仁漸義摩之化既歷三紀
===
世變風移之時臣民皆知勸善故示戒之事皆
書所不錄也逮乎
宣宗章皇帝五倫書采輯古今嘉言善行有關於君
臣父子夫婦兄弟朋友之道者雖詳略不同其
義即小學明倫篇五倫之事也而春秋隱公元
年不書即位以正父子君臣之倫書公及邾儀
父盟于蔑鄭伯克段于鄢天王使宰咺來歸惠
公仲子之賵以正朋友兄弟夫婦之倫者其明
綱常之義寧有殊乎為善陰隲孝順事實所采
punctuated: 太祖高皇帝臨御之日，尊崇聖道，表章儒書，嘗頒《大誥》三編，具載李子安、余仁三之徒奸貪兇頑之罪，無所示勸。蓋當時勸善之典，功臣賢相有誥券制勅之褒，孝順節義有旌表門閭之詔，皆《誥》所未載也。太宗文皇帝《為善陰隲》書，首蔣王靈應，終周婦感悟；《孝順事實》書，首虞舜大孝，終劉婦孝姑，備載古今善孝之實，而無所示戒。蓋當時際重熙累洽之運，四海被仁漸義摩之化，既歷三紀，世變風移之時，臣民皆知勸善，故示戒之事，皆書所不錄也。逮乎宣宗章皇帝《五倫》書，采輯古今嘉言善行有關於君臣、父子、夫婦、兄弟、朋友之道者，雖詳略不同，其義即《小學》〈明倫篇〉五倫之事也。而《春秋》隱公元年不書「即位」，以正父子、君臣之倫；書「公及邾儀父盟于蔑」、「鄭伯克段于鄢」、「天王使宰咺來歸惠公仲子之賵」，以正朋友、兄弟、夫婦之倫者，其明綱常之義，寧有殊乎？《為善陰隲》、《孝順事實》所采
translation_en: …When Emperor Gao, our Grand Progenitor (Taizu), reigned, he revered the Way of the Sages and honored the Confucian books. He once promulgated the three parts of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao), which fully recorded the treacherous, greedy, vicious, and obstinate crimes of such men as Li Zi'an 李子安 and Yu Rensan 余仁三, without anything to serve as encouragement to virtue. This was because, among the institutions for encouraging goodness at that time, meritorious ministers and worthy grand councilors received the praise of patents of appointment, iron tallies, imperial decrees, and commands, while the filial, obedient, chaste, and righteous received edicts honoring their family gates—none of which were recorded in the Pronouncements. In the book Hidden Rewards of Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi) by Emperor Wen, our Grand Ancestor (Taizong), it begins with the spiritual responsiveness of Prince Jiang (Jiang Wang 蔣王) and ends with the awakening of the wife of Zhou; in the book True Accounts of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi), it begins with the great filial piety of Yu Shun 虞舜 and ends with the wife of Liu being filial to her mother-in-law. They fully record the true deeds of goodness and filial piety from antiquity to the present, without anything to serve as admonition. This was because that era met with a destiny of cumulative splendor and enduring harmony, when the Four Seas had been transformed by the gradual permeation of benevolence and the polishing of righteousness for three twelve-year cycles (thirty-six years); at a time when the age had changed and customs had shifted, subjects and people all knew to encourage goodness, and therefore matters meant as admonition were omitted from these books. Coming down to the book The Five Relationships (Wulun shu) by Emperor Zhang, our Ancestor of Proclaimed Virtue (Xuanzong), it compiles fine words and good deeds from antiquity to the present that relate to the Way of ruler and subject, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger brother, and friends. Although differing in level of detail, its meaning is none other than the matters of the five relationships in the "Illuminating Human Relationships" (Minglun pian) section of the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue). Furthermore, when the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) in the first year of Duke Yin (Yin Gong 隱公) does not record his "accession to the throne" in order to rectify the relationships of father and son and of ruler and subject, and when it records "the Duke and Yifu of Zhu made a covenant at Mie," "the Earl of Zheng overcame Duan at Yan," and "the Heavenly King sent Administrator Xuan to come and present funerary gifts for Duke Hui and Zhongzi" in order to rectify the relationships of friends, elder and younger brothers, and husband and wife—how could its principle of illuminating the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues be any different? As for those collected in the Hidden Rewards of Doing Good and the True Accounts of Filial Piety…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
陰德行孝之人雖多寡不一其事即春秋傳魏
顆從治考叔遺羹之類也而小學所稱叔敖黃
香劉寬之徒所紀虞舜文武之聖曾閔子路之
賢者其善孝之實寧有異乎嗟夫孔子朱子窮
而在下立言垂世既以正綱常備勸戒爲要
祖宗列聖達而在上建極敷言亦以正綱常備勸戒
爲急是可見千聖一心萬古一理而脩道之教
先聖後聖其揆一也愚生被
樂育之恩躬誦習之勤謹因明問所及略舉以對
===
惟執事進教之幸甚
第二問
鄧應仁
同考試官教諭林批書卷三百餘求其三場勻稱者
此卷前二場既優五策俱佳而
此策尤詳明取置魁選允協輿情
考試官教諭鄭批此策善得聖人處事化人之方非
有學識者不能
考試官學正王批允稱前場
punctuated:
陰德、行孝之人，雖多寡不一，其事即《春秋傳》魏顆從治、考叔遺羹之類也。而《小學》所稱叔敖、黃香、劉寬之徒，所紀虞舜、文、武之聖，曾、閔、子路之賢者，其善孝之實，寧有異乎？嗟夫！孔子、朱子窮而在下，立言垂世，既以正綱常、備勸戒爲要；祖宗列聖達而在上，建極敷言，亦以正綱常、備勸戒爲急。是可見千聖一心，萬古一理，而脩道之教，先聖後聖其揆一也。愚生被樂育之恩，躬誦習之勤，謹因明問所及，略舉以對，惟執事進教之，幸甚。

第二問
鄧應仁
同考試官教諭林批：書卷三百餘，求其三場勻稱者，此卷前二場既優，五策俱佳，而此策尤詳明。取置魁選，允協輿情。
考試官教諭鄭批：此策善得聖人處事化人之方，非有學識者不能。
考試官學正王批：允稱前場。
translation_en:
…those who accumulated hidden virtue and practiced filial piety, though varying in number, their deeds are of the same kind as those recorded in the Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu zhuan)—such as Wei Ke following his father's lucid instructions and Ying Kaoshu setting aside soup for his mother. And as for men like Sun Shu'ao, Huang Xiang, and Liu Kuan praised in the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue), as well as the sages Yu Shun, King Wen, and King Wu, and the worthies Zengzi, Min Ziqian, and Zilu recorded therein—how could the reality of their goodness and filial piety be any different? Alas! Confucius and Zhu Xi, though without high office and remaining below, established teachings to be handed down to future generations, taking the rectification of the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues and the provision of exhortation and admonition as their essential aim; our Imperial Ancestors and successive sage emperors, occupying the throne above, established the supreme standard and promulgated their teachings, likewise taking the rectification of the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues and the provision of exhortation and admonition as their urgent priority. From this it can be seen that a thousand sages share a single mind, ten thousand ages share a single principle, and in the instruction of cultivating the Way, the former sages and later sages follow the exact same measure. I, a foolish student, having received the grace of being joyfully nurtured and having personally devoted myself to diligent recitation and study, respectfully offer this brief outline in response to what your enlightened question has touched upon. May Your Honor advance and instruct me—I would be most fortunate.

The Second Question
Deng Yingren 鄧應仁
Comment by Associate Examiner, County Director of Studies Lin: Among more than three hundred scripts on the Book of Documents, in seeking one balanced across all three sessions, this script was already superior in the first two sessions, and all five of its policy essays are fine, with this essay being especially detailed and clear. Selecting it to be placed among the top ranks truly accords with public sentiment.
Comment by Examiner, County Director of Studies Zheng: This policy essay aptly grasps the sages' methods for handling affairs and transforming people; none without learning and insight could have produced it.
Comment by Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang: Truly matches the earlier sessions.

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天下之事常變不一也聖人處之惟一理天下
之人賢否不齊也聖人感之惟一心大哉理乎
其聖人處事之要乎至哉心乎其聖人感人之
本乎知此則可復明問之萬一矣夫聖如帝堯
胤子丹朱嚚訟不肖而用殄厥世聖如大禹父
鯀治水悻戾自用而汩陳五行此父子之變事
之難處者也堯乃不傳位於子而傳於舜遂使
授受得中而天下治平禹乃三過其門不入而
脩鯀之功遂使六府孔脩而萬世永賴蓋當禪
===
則禪當脩則脩允執厥中理之常也成湯當有
夏季世萬方百姓並告無辜武王當有商季世
百姓有過在予一人此君臣之變事之難處者
也湯乃興鳴條之師而為放桀之舉由是代虐
以寬而兆民允懷武乃因諸侯之會而為牧野
之誓由是大賚四海而萬姓悅服蓋當放則放
當伐則伐順天應人理之正也周公位冢宰正
百官群叔流言欲以間王室也而公避位居東
赤舄几几德音不瑕後因風雷之變成王遂感
punctuated: 天下之事，常變不一也，聖人處之惟一理；天下之人，賢否不齊也，聖人感之惟一心。大哉理乎！其聖人處事之要乎？至哉心乎！其聖人感人之本乎？知此，則可復明問之萬一矣。夫聖如帝堯，胤子丹朱嚚訟不肖，而用殄厥世；聖如大禹，父鯀治水悻戾自用，而汩陳五行：此父子之變，事之難處者也。堯乃不傳位於子而傳於舜，遂使授受得中而天下治平；禹乃三過其門不入而脩鯀之功，遂使六府孔脩而萬世永賴。蓋當禪則禪，當脩則脩，允執厥中，理之常也。成湯當有夏季世，萬方百姓並告無辜；武王當有商季世，「百姓有過，在予一人」：此君臣之變，事之難處者也。湯乃興鳴條之師，而為放桀之舉，由是代虐以寬，而兆民允懷；武乃因諸侯之會，而為牧野之誓，由是大賚四海，而萬姓悅服。蓋當放則放，當伐則伐，順天應人，理之正也。周公位冢宰，正百官，群叔流言，欲以間王室也，而公避位居東，赤舄几几，德音不瑕，後因風雷之變，成王遂感
translation_en:
The affairs of the world vary between the constant and the anomalous, yet the sage handles them with but a single principle; the people of the world are unequal in worthiness and unworthiness, yet the sage moves them with but a single mind. Great indeed is principle! Is it not the essential means by which the sage handles affairs? Supreme indeed is the mind! Is it not the fundamental root by which the sage moves people? Understanding this, one can reply to one ten-thousandth of your perceptive question.

Now, even for a sage like Emperor Yao, his heir Danzhu was deceitful, quarrelsome, and unworthy, thereby cutting short his lineage's succession; even for a sage like the Great Yu, his father Gun was perverse and self-willed in controlling the waters, throwing the Five Phases into disorder. These were anomalies between father and son, affairs difficult to handle. Yet Yao did not transmit the throne to his son, transmitting it instead to Shun, thereby ensuring that the giving and receiving attained the mean and the world was well-governed and at peace; and Yu thrice passed his own door without entering in order to carry on and complete Gun's work, thereby ensuring that the Six Treasuries of nature were thoroughly ordered and ten thousand generations could forever rely upon them. Indeed, abdicating when one ought to abdicate, and cultivating the work when one ought to cultivate it—sincerely holding fast the mean—is the constancy of principle.

Cheng Tang lived in the final age of the Xia dynasty, when the common people of the myriad regions all cried out in their innocence; King Wu lived in the final age of the Shang dynasty, declaring, "If the common people have faults, it rests upon me, the One Man." These were anomalies between ruler and minister, affairs difficult to handle. Yet Tang raised the army at Mingtiao and undertook the banishment of Jie, thereby replacing tyranny with leniency so that the millions of people truly cherished him; and Wu availed himself of the assembly of the feudal lords to make the oath at Muye, thereby bestowing great largesse upon the Four Seas so that the myriad people gladly submitted. Indeed, banishing when one ought to banish, and attacking when one ought to attack—complying with Heaven and responding to humanity—is the correctness of principle.

The Duke of Zhou held the position of Premier (zhongzai) and rectified the hundred officials. His younger brothers spread rumors, wishing to sow dissension in the royal house. Yet the Duke withdrew from his post and resided in the east, his red slippers calm and composed, his virtuous reputation unblemished; later, because of the anomaly of the wind and thunder, King Cheng was moved…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
悟而出郊以迎之孔子相定公會齊侯于夾谷
齊人鼓譟而起欲以劫魯君也而孔子俘不干
盟兵不偪好之言威重於三軍齊遂知罪而歸
三田以謝之處變而無疑懼相禮而却萊兵亦
惟順乎理耳此皆聖人處事之實也至若父頑
母嚚象傲勢若難化矣而卒致丕格姦亦允若
者由舜之心純乎誠孝之至然也侮慢自賢頑
固不服跡若難格矣而卒致三苗丕叙七旬來
格者由舜禹之心不尚威武專施德教然也太
===
甲嗣位欲敗度縱敗禮其失若習與性成也伊
尹營于桐宮居憂三年而遂致克終允德成王
幼冲弗造哲迪民康其性非卓然高明也周公
作無逸陳王業以訓告之而遂致教化大行盖
伊周之心拳拳忠愛者有以感之曾子子貢之
在聖門或質魯或貨殖賦性用心之偏者也聖
人甞語之使知自勵由是曾子隨事精察之久
子貢博學多識之積卒聞一以貫之之道焉太
師亞飯之為樂官或樂官之長或以樂侑食亦
punctuated:
悟，而出郊以迎之。孔子相定公會齊侯于夾谷，齊人鼓譟而起，欲以劫魯君也，而孔子「俘不干盟，兵不偪好」之言，威重於三軍，齊遂知罪，而歸三田以謝之。處變而無疑懼，相禮而却萊兵，亦惟順乎理耳。此皆聖人處事之實也。
至若父頑母嚚象傲，勢若難化矣，而卒致「丕格姦，亦允若」者，由舜之心純乎誠孝之至然也。侮慢自賢，頑固不服，跡若難格矣，而卒致「三苗丕叙，七旬來格」者，由舜、禹之心不尚威武、專施德教然也。太甲嗣位，欲敗度，縱敗禮，其失若習與性成也；伊尹營于桐宮，居憂三年，而遂致「克終允德」。成王幼冲，弗造哲迪民康，其性非卓然高明也；周公作《無逸》，陳王業以訓告之，而遂致教化大行。盖伊、周之心，拳拳忠愛者有以感之。曾子、子貢之在聖門，或質魯，或貨殖，賦性用心之偏者也；聖人甞語之，使知自勵，由是曾子隨事精察之久，子貢博學多識之積，卒聞「一以貫之」之道焉。太師、亞飯之為樂官，或樂官之長，或以樂侑食，亦
translation_en:
…came to his senses, and went out to the suburbs to welcome him back. When Confucius assisted Duke Ding of Lu (Dinggong 定公) at the meeting with the Marquis of Qi (Qihou 齊侯) at Jiagu 夾谷, the men of Qi rose up beating drums and shouting, intending to abduct the ruler of Lu. Yet Confucius's words—"Captives do not intrude upon covenants, nor do arms press upon friendly meetings"—carried more weight and awe than three armies; Qi thereupon recognized its offense and returned the three tracts of land in apology. Facing a crisis without doubt or fear, and repelling the Lai 萊 troops while assisting in ritual protocol, were likewise simply a matter of following principle. All these are real instances of how sages handled affairs.

As for having an obstinate father, a deceitful mother, and an arrogant brother Xiang 象, the situation seemed impossible to transform; yet it ultimately resulted in "having effected great harmony and preventing them from reaching wickedness," because Shun's 舜 mind was purely devoted to the utmost sincerity and filial piety. Being insolent, self-important, and stubbornly unsubmissive, their conduct seemed impossible to reform; yet it ultimately resulted in "the Sanmiao 三苗 being brought into great order" and "coming to submit within seventy days," because the minds of Shun and Yu 禹 did not prize martial might, but exclusively applied moral instruction. When Taijia 太甲 succeeded to the throne, he ruined the norms through his desires and ruined propriety through his self-indulgence, his failings appearing as though habit had become second nature. Yiyin 伊尹 built a residence at the Tong Palace (Tonggong 桐宮), where Taijia dwelt in mourning for three years, and thus brought it about that he "was able in the end to be sincerely virtuous." When King Cheng (Chengwang 成王) was young and immature, not yet achieving wisdom to lead the people to tranquility, his nature was not outstandingly brilliant; the Duke of Zhou (Zhougong 周公) composed Against Luxurious Ease (Wuyi 無逸), setting forth the royal enterprise to instruct and admonish him, and thus brought it about that moral transformation greatly prevailed. Indeed, the earnestly loyal and loving minds of Yiyin and the Duke of Zhou had that wherewith to move them. When Zengzi 曾子 and Zigong 子貢 were at the Sage's gate, one was dull by temperament and the other engaged in stockpiling goods—cases of one-sidedness in endowed nature or mental focus. The Sage once spoke to them so that they knew to exert themselves; consequently, through Zengzi's long-sustained precise examination of affairs as they came, and Zigong's accumulation of broad learning and much knowledge, both finally heard the Way of "one thread binding it all together." As for the Grand Music Master (Taishi 太師) and the Musician of the Second Meal (Yafan 亞飯) serving as music officials—whether as chief of the music officials or as one who accompanied meals with music—they too were…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
人典是職者也聖人自衛反魯而正樂由是伶
人賤工識樂之正皆知逾河蹈海以去焉盖聖
人之心同乎天地者有以化之此皆聖人感人
之由也雖然事無不可為者以其有此理人無
不可化者以其同此心聖人窮理盡性而廓然
大公故無不可為之事無不可化之人也學者
取法聖人當自存心觀理始管見如斯未知是
否姑此以塞明問
第三問
===
蒲錭
同考試官訓導郭批人望一策塲中答者多無事實
此作條答無遺是宜録出
同考試官教諭汪批此策随問随答畧無凝滯其
達於時務者歟
考試官教諭鄭批有考據有斷制策塲中之優者
考試官學正王批區處用人望在審衆論甚當
治天下之大要在乎收人望收人望之大幾在
乎審衆論盖人望不收則治功不成衆論不審
punctuated:
人典是職者也。聖人自衛反魯而正樂，由是伶人賤工，識樂之正，皆知逾河蹈海以去焉。盖聖人之心同乎天地者，有以化之。此皆聖人感人之由也。雖然，事無不可為者，以其有此理；人無不可化者，以其同此心。聖人窮理盡性而廓然大公，故無不可為之事，無不可化之人也。學者取法聖人，當自存心觀理始。管見如斯，未知是否，姑此以塞明問。

第三問
蒲錭
同考試官訓導郭批：人望一策，塲中答者多無事實，此作條答無遺，是宜録出。
同考試官教諭汪批：此策随問随答，畧無凝滯，其達於時務者歟！
考試官教諭鄭批：有考據，有斷制，策塲中之優者。
考試官學正王批：區處用人望在審衆論，甚當。

治天下之大要，在乎收人望；收人望之大幾，在乎審衆論。盖人望不收則治功不成，衆論不審
translation_en:
… people who held these offices. After the Sage returned from Wei to Lu and rectified the music, even lowly musicians and humble artisans came to recognize the correctness of the music, and all knew enough to depart across the Yellow River or out to the sea. This was because the Sage's mind, being one with Heaven and Earth, had the power to transform them. All of these are the means by which the Sage moved people. Even so, there is no affair that cannot be accomplished, because it possesses this principle; there is no person who cannot be transformed, because they share this mind. The Sage exhausts principle, fulfills human nature, and is vast and supremely impartial; therefore, there is no affair that cannot be accomplished and no person who cannot be transformed. Scholars who take the Sage as their model should begin by preserving the mind and contemplating principle. Such is my humble view; I do not know whether it is correct, and offer this provisionally to fulfill Your enlightened question.

Third Question
Pu Diao
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Guo comments: On the policy question concerning men of high reputation, most respondents in the examination compound lacked factual substance; this composition answers point by point without omission, and thus deserves to be recorded and published.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Wang comments: This policy essay answers each question as it arises without the slightest hesitation; surely the author is someone well-versed in current affairs!
Examiner and Instructor Zheng comments: Well-grounded in evidence and decisive in judgment, an outstanding piece from the policy examination session.
Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Wang comments: The arrangement that employing men of high reputation lies in examining public opinion is most fitting.

The great essential in governing the world lies in gathering men of high reputation; the great pivot in gathering men of high reputation lies in examining public opinion. For if men of high reputation are not gathered, the achievements of governance will not be realized, and if public opinion is not examined…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則賢否雜進能審眾論以收人望則治天下之
大要豈有加於此哉且士君子以一身之微繫
天下之觀望大矣因其人望而用之是所謂以
民治民以天下治天下何往而不濟何功而不
成哉是以古之循吏若召父杜母眾望之所在
也用之則吏民稱誦而郡國向治焉舊士如顧
榮賀循眾望之所歸也用之以結人心則江東
皆歸焉負節義之重望者李固也用焉而盜賊
請降負勳德之重名者郭子儀也用之而回紇
===
羅拜之二人者非繫於人望者乎且以東廣一
方言之如張九齡之道侔伊呂用之而能抑奸
辨賊余靖之文學知名用之而能論諫舉職他
如崔與之用之則兵民悅服而晚節恬退可尚
矣是則人望之有益於人國如此洪惟我
朝
列聖相承任賢圖治近而望於一鄉大而望於一方
又大而望於天下秉鈞持軸皆洞識天人之士
折衝禦侮皆才兼文武之人掌刑掌教者藹藹
punctuated: 則賢否雜進。能審眾論以收人望，則治天下之大要，豈有加於此哉？且士君子以一身之微，繫天下之觀望大矣。因其人望而用之，是所謂以民治民，以天下治天下，何往而不濟，何功而不成哉！是以古之循吏，若召父、杜母，眾望之所在也，用之則吏民稱誦，而郡國向治焉；舊士如顧榮、賀循，眾望之所歸也，用之以結人心，則江東皆歸焉；負節義之重望者李固也，用焉而盜賊請降；負勳德之重名者郭子儀也，用之而回紇羅拜。之二人者，非繫於人望者乎？且以東廣一方言之，如張九齡之道侔伊、呂，用之而能抑奸辨賊；余靖之文學知名，用之而能論諫舉職；他如崔與之，用之則兵民悅服，而晚節恬退可尚矣。是則人望之有益於人國如此。洪惟我朝列聖相承，任賢圖治，近而望於一鄉，大而望於一方，又大而望於天下。秉鈞持軸，皆洞識天人之士；折衝禦侮，皆才兼文武之人；掌刑、掌教者，藹藹
translation_en:
…then the worthy and the unworthy advance indiscriminately. If one can carefully examine public opinion in order to gather those who command popular esteem, then how could there be anything more essential to governing the empire than this? Moreover, although a scholar-gentleman in his own person is slight, the expectations of the empire that hinge upon him are great indeed. To employ men in accordance with their popular esteem is what is meant by governing the people by means of the people, and governing the empire by means of the empire—wherever one goes, what will not succeed, and what achievement will not be brought to completion?

Therefore, among the upright officials of antiquity, men like “Father Shao” [Shao Xinchen 召信臣] and “Mother Du” [Du Shi 杜詩] were where the hopes of the multitude rested; when they were employed, subofficial functionaries and the common people sang their praises, and the commanderies and principalities moved toward order. Veteran scholars such as Gu Rong 顧榮 and He Xun 賀循 were those to whom the expectations of the multitude turned; when they were employed to win over men’s hearts, all of Jiangdong 江東 submitted in allegiance. He who bore weighty esteem for integrity and righteousness was Li Gu 李固; when he was employed, bandits and rebels begged to surrender. He who bore a weighty reputation for meritorious service and virtue was Guo Ziyi 郭子儀; when he was employed, the Uyghurs lined up to bow before him. Were not these two men examples of how much hinges upon popular esteem?

Furthermore, to speak of the single region of eastern Guangdong [Dongguang 東廣]: someone like Zhang Jiuling 張九齡, whose Way matched that of Yi Yin 伊尹 and Lü Shang 呂尚, when employed was able to curb the treacherous and discern rebels; Yu Jing 余靖, renowned for his literary learning, when employed was able to remonstrate and fulfill the duties of his office; and others such as Cui Yuzhi 崔與之, when employed won the glad submission of soldiers and civilians alike, while his calm withdrawal from office in his later years was worthy of high esteem. Such, then, is the benefit to a state of men who command popular esteem.

Reflecting with awe upon Our Dynasty, a succession of sacred emperors has inherited the throne, employing the worthy and striving for good governance—selecting those esteemed locally in a single community, more broadly in a single region, and more broadly still throughout the entire empire. Those who hold the balances of state and grasp the pivot of government are all scholars with penetrating insight into Heaven and man; those who repel enemy assaults and ward off foreign aggression are all men combining civil and military talents; those in charge of punishments and those in charge of education are an abundant host of…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之吉人也興禮典樂者濟濟之多士也維藩維
垣而旬宣激揚之有方作郡作邑而撫摩鞠育
之有道所謂循吏舊士節義勳德咸舉用之而
無遺矣以故百年之間治道之盛覃布於海宇
仁恩之廣浹洽於人心黎元樂業邊塵不飛太
平之盛無有過於今日者矣柰何近年以来旱
澇相仍而郡國間有愁嘆之聲夷虜桀驁而邊
徼或有竊發之患是豈用非其望而然乎實由
有實德者固以人望而舉釣虛名者或以非望
===
而進賢否混淆故相掣肘矛盾而然耳為今之
計誠如周人用賢之法因民之所自擇而使之
入長出治如孟子用賢之術必徇國人之言而
徐加採擇則所用者皆所望而非所望者不得
以倖進而又持之以公道而不徇於私情專之
以委任而不雜於非人又何患愁嘆之聲不轉
為謳歌之音竊發之患不變為來格之化哉愚
也學不足以博古識不足以通今非敢以達時
務之俊傑自負也第以明問所及故忘其狂斐
punctuated: 之吉人也；興禮典樂者，濟濟之多士也。維藩維垣，而旬宣激揚之有方；作郡作邑，而撫摩鞠育之有道。所謂循吏、舊士、節義、勳德，咸舉用之而無遺矣。以故百年之間，治道之盛，覃布於海宇；仁恩之廣，浹洽於人心。黎元樂業，邊塵不飛，太平之盛，無有過於今日者矣。柰何近年以来，旱澇相仍，而郡國間有愁嘆之聲；夷虜桀驁，而邊徼或有竊發之患。是豈用非其望而然乎？實由有實德者，固以人望而舉；釣虛名者，或以非望而進。賢否混淆，故相掣肘矛盾而然耳。為今之計，誠如周人用賢之法，因民之所自擇，而使之入長出治；如孟子用賢之術，必徇國人之言，而徐加採擇。則所用者皆所望，而非所望者不得以倖進。而又持之以公道，而不徇於私情；專之以委任，而不雜於非人。又何患愁嘆之聲，不轉為謳歌之音；竊發之患，不變為來格之化哉？愚也，學不足以博古，識不足以通今，非敢以達時務之俊傑自負也。第以明問所及，故忘其狂斐，
translation_en: …admirable men; those who promote rites and direct music are a multitude of dignified gentlemen. Those who serve as regional bulwarks and walls propagate royal grace and encourage the good while suppressing the corrupt with proper method; those who govern commanderies and counties soothe and nurture the people in accordance with the Way. Those known as model officials, veteran scholars, men of integrity and righteousness, and men of merit and virtue have all been promoted and employed without omission. Consequently, for a hundred years, the flourishing of the way of governance has spread throughout the realm, and the breadth of benevolent grace has soaked deeply into the hearts of the people. The common folk rejoice in their livelihoods, dust does not fly on the frontiers, and the flourishing of grand peace has never surpassed that of the present day. Why is it, then, that in recent years droughts and floods have followed one after another, so that sounds of sorrow and sighing are occasionally heard among the commanderies and principalities; and the foreign tribes have been unruly and arrogant, so that outbreaks of banditry sometimes occur along the frontier marches? Could this really be because those employed do not match public expectations? In truth, it is because while those possessing genuine virtue are indeed recommended on the basis of public esteem, those who angle for empty reputation sometimes advance despite lacking such esteem. The worthy and the unworthy are confounded, and thus they hinder and contradict one another—that is the only reason. As a plan for the present, if we truly follow the Zhou method of employing the worthy—relying on whom the people themselves choose, and having them serve as leaders at court and governors in the provinces; and if we follow Mencius's art of employing the worthy—heeding the words of all the people of the state and then carefully making selections after deliberation—then those employed will all be those who command public esteem, and those who do not will be unable to advance by luck. Furthermore, if this is upheld with impartiality without yielding to private bias, and if responsibilities are delegated with focused trust without mixing in unsuitable men, what need would there be to worry that the sounds of sorrow and sighing would not turn into songs of praise, or that the trouble of sudden outbreaks would not be transformed into the civilizing influence that brings the distant to submit? Stupid as I am, my learning is insufficient to encompass antiquity, and my insight is insufficient to comprehend the present; I would not dare to pride myself on being anoutstanding talent who understands the affairs of the times. Yet because Your illustrious question touched upon this, I have forgotten my rashness and crudity…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而陳之如此惟執事進而教之幸甚
第四問
何津
同考試官教諭蕭批〔曆法學者多不究心此篇隨問而答必博洽之士也〕
考試官教諭鄭批〔考究詳明是殆用心於古學者〕
考試官學正王批〔不遺事實〕
論曆法之得失當明乎置閏論節氣之運行當
考其名義夫為政之本以治曆為先而治曆之
===
要又豈外乎置閏之與節氣哉此置閏之得失
不可以不明而節氣之名義不可以不知也粤
自黃帝迎日推策而曆書之傳其來尚矣逮夫
炎漢曆凡五變而莫善於太初豈非本於司馬
遷鄧平等所推而以律起者乎延及李唐曆凡
八變而莫善於大衍又非出於僧一行所作而
以數推者乎以至宋曆則太史局秘書省銅儀
之制極為精密此又其十變中之最者也自此
之外若杜預春秋長曆王朴欽天曆為可採焉
punctuated:
而陳之如此，惟執事進而教之，幸甚。

第四問
何津
同考試官教諭蕭批〔曆法學者多不究心，此篇隨問而答，必博洽之士也。〕
考試官教諭鄭批〔考究詳明，是殆用心於古學者。〕
考試官學正王批〔不遺事實。〕

論曆法之得失，當明乎置閏；論節氣之運行，當考其名義。夫為政之本，以治曆為先，而治曆之要，又豈外乎置閏之與節氣哉？此置閏之得失，不可以不明，而節氣之名義，不可以不知也。粤自黃帝迎日推策，而曆書之傳，其來尚矣。逮夫炎漢，曆凡五變，而莫善於《太初》，豈非本於司馬遷、鄧平等所推，而以律起者乎？延及李唐，曆凡八變，而莫善於《大衍》，又非出於僧一行所作，而以數推者乎？以至宋曆，則太史局、秘書省銅儀之制，極為精密，此又其十變中之最者也。自此之外，若杜預《春秋長曆》、王朴《欽天曆》為可採焉，
translation_en:
… and set them forth in this way. Should Your Honor advance me and instruct me, I would consider myself most fortunate.

Fourth Policy Question
He Jin 何津
Comment by Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Xiao 蕭: [Scholars rarely devote serious attention to calendrical science; this essay answers each point as asked, and its author must be a gentleman of broad and thorough learning.]
Comment by Examiner and County Director of Studies Zheng 鄭: [Its investigation is detailed and clear; this is surely someone who has applied his mind to ancient learning.]
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang 王: [It omits none of the historical facts.]

In discussing the merits and defects of calendrical systems, one must be clear about the intercalation of months; in discussing the movement of the solar terms, one must examine their names and meanings. Now, at the foundation of governance, regulating the calendar comes first, and how could the essentials of regulating the calendar lie outside of intercalation and the solar terms? Therefore, the merits and defects of intercalation cannot but be made clear, and the names and meanings of the solar terms cannot but be known.

Ever since the Yellow Emperor calculated the movements of the sun with counting rods, the transmission of calendrical writings has had a long history indeed. Coming down to the fiery Han dynasty, the calendar underwent five changes in all, yet none was better than the Grand Inception (Taichu 太初) calendar—was this not because it was based on the calculations of Sima Qian 司馬遷, Deng Ping 鄧平, and others, and took its start from the pitch-pipes? Extending down to the Tang dynasty of the Li 李 house, the calendar underwent eight changes in all, yet none was better than the Great Expansion (Dayan 大衍) calendar—and was this not because it came from the work of the monk Yixing 一行 and was calculated from numerical principles? Coming to the calendars of the Song dynasty, the construction of the bronze armillary instruments in the Directorate of Astronomy and the Palace Library was extremely precise, making them the finest among its ten calendrical reforms. Apart from these, works such as Du Yu's 杜預 Long Calendar of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu changli 春秋長曆) and Wang Pu's 王朴 Reverent Accord with Heaven Calendar (Qintian li 欽天曆) are worthy of adoption, …

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其餘則不足言矣然造曆之法當以置閏為急
彼其日與天會而多五日為氣盈月與日會而
少五日為朔虛曰氣盈曰朔虛非閏月所由生
乎推測之要當以正閏而分故易曰三年一閏
五年再閏又曰凡三百六十當期之日此以其
正數言也書曰以閏月定四時又曰朞三百有
六旬有六日此以其成數言也曰正數曰成數
非正閏所由分乎厥後秦用十月為歲首而常
以九月為閏則大失其推測之要矣宜乎漢武
===
帝之悟其謬也至若曆之為書不越乎二十四
氣氣之行有序而亦莫不有理存焉槩而言之
每月有節氣有中氣如丑之終寅之始則為節
寅之半則為中也一年有四立即是四時之節
氣二分二至即是四時之中氣也九十日之氣
往者過而來者續故謂之立焉春秋謂之分者
以其居乎九十日之半也夏冬謂之至者非以
其介乎巳陽午陰亥陰子陽之間乎穀雨芒種
以穀麥言也穀必原其生之始故居穀雨芒種
punctuated: 其餘則不足言矣。然造曆之法，當以置閏為急。彼其日與天會而多五日為「氣盈」，月與日會而少五日為「朔虛」。曰「氣盈」、曰「朔虛」，非閏月所由生乎？推測之要，當以正閏而分。故《易》曰：「三年一閏，五年再閏。」又曰：「凡三百六十，當期之日。」此以其正數言也。《書》曰：「以閏月定四時。」又曰：「朞三百有六旬有六日。」此以其成數言也。曰「正數」、曰「成數」，非正閏所由分乎？厥後秦用十月為歲首，而常以九月為閏，則大失其推測之要矣。宜乎漢武帝之悟其謬也！至若曆之為書，不越乎二十四氣。氣之行有序，而亦莫不有理存焉。槩而言之，每月有節氣、有中氣，如丑之終、寅之始則為節，寅之半則為中也。一年有四立，即是四時之節氣；二分、二至，即是四時之中氣也。九十日之氣，往者過而來者續，故謂之「立」焉。春、秋謂之「分」者，以其居乎九十日之半也；夏、冬謂之「至」者，非以其介乎巳陽、午陰，亥陰、子陽之間乎？「穀雨」、「芒種」，以穀、麥言也。穀必原其生之始，故居「穀雨」芒種
translation_en:
…The rest are not worth mentioning. However, in the method of calendar-making, the intercalation of months must be treated as the most urgent matter. When the sun meets the heavens, the excess of five days is called the "solar surplus" (qiying); when the moon meets the sun, the deficit of five days is called the "lunar deficiency" (shuoxu). Are not what are called the "solar surplus" and "lunar deficiency" that from which the intercalary month arises? The essential point of astronomical calculation lies in distinguishing between regular and intercalary. Thus the Book of Changes (Yi) says: "In three years there is one intercalation, and in five years two intercalations." It also says: "In all, three hundred and sixty, corresponding to the days of a cycle." This speaks in terms of the regular number (zhengshu). The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "By means of the intercalary month, fix the four seasons." It also says: "A full year consists of three hundred, six tens, and six days." This speaks in terms of the completed number (chengshu). Are not what are called the "regular number" and the "completed number" that by which regular and intercalary are distinguished? Later on, the Qin dynasty used the tenth month as the beginning of the year and always placed the intercalary month after the ninth month [as a "latter ninth month"], thereby greatly losing the essential principle of calculation. Rightly indeed did Emperor Wu of Han realize its error!

As for the calendar as a book, it does not go beyond the twenty-four solar terms (qi). The progression of the solar terms has an order, and in every case there is a principle inherent within it. Speaking in general terms, each month has a nodal qi (jieqi) and a medial qi (zhongqi); for instance, the end of chou and the beginning of yin is the nodal qi, while the middle of yin is the medial qi. In a year there are the Four Beginnings (sili), which are the nodal qi of the four seasons; and there are the Two Equinoxes (erfen) and Two Solstices (erzhi), which are the medial qi of the four seasons. In the ninety-day qi of a season, the departing one passes and the coming one continues it, hence they are called "Beginnings" (li, "establishing"). Spring and autumn are called "Equinoxes" (fen, "dividing") because they sit at the halfway point of the ninety days; summer and winter are called "Solstices" (zhi, "extremes")—is it not because they lie between the yang of si and the yin of wu, and between the yin of hai and the yang of zi? "Grain Rain" (guyu) and "Grain in Ear" (mangzhong) are spoken of with reference to grain and wheat. For grain, one must trace the beginning of its growth, hence "Grain Rain" is placed [in the middle of the third?—text reads "Grain in Ear" [?]]…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
月之中麥必要其成之終故處芒種於五月之
内驚蟄清明以風雷言也驚蟄者萬物出乎震
震為雷雷乃發聲於二月故居於二月焉清明
者萬物齊乎巽巽為風風乃潔齊於三月故居
之三月焉正月暑之始六月暑之終故小暑大
暑而在夏至之後也七月寒之始十二月寒之
終故小寒大寒而在冬至之後也八月節白露
九月節寒露然秋属金金色白白者露之色寒
者露之氣色先白而氣始寒寒固有漸矣十月
===
中小雪十一月節大雪然寒氣始於露中於霜
終於雪雪由小而至大能無漸歟居小滿於四
月之中盖一陰方此而萌當致防微杜漸之意
也置處暑於七月之内盖以暑氣於此而止非
如既雨既處之處乎秋分水始涸立冬水始氷
冬至水泉動至於立春則水氣流行矣立雨水
於立春之後者此也霜之前為露露由白而寒
至於寒露則露結為霜矣介霜降於寒露之餘
者亦非以此歟凡此皆變化之道神之所為也
punctuated: 月之中；麥必要其成之終，故處芒種於五月之内。驚蟄、清明，以風雷言也。驚蟄者，萬物出乎震；震為雷，雷乃發聲於二月，故居於二月焉。清明者，萬物齊乎巽；巽為風，風乃潔齊於三月，故居之三月焉。正月暑之始，六月暑之終，故小暑、大暑而在夏至之後也。七月寒之始，十二月寒之終，故小寒、大寒而在冬至之後也。八月節白露，九月節寒露，然秋属金，金色白；白者露之色，寒者露之氣，色先白而氣始寒，寒固有漸矣。十月中小雪，十一月節大雪，然寒氣始於露，中於霜，終於雪；雪由小而至大，能無漸歟？居小滿於四月之中，盖一陰方此而萌，當致防微杜漸之意也。置處暑於七月之内，盖以暑氣於此而止，非如「既雨既處」之處乎？秋分水始涸，立冬水始氷，冬至水泉動，至於立春則水氣流行矣，立雨水於立春之後者此也。霜之前為露，露由白而寒，至於寒露則露結為霜矣，介霜降於寒露之餘者，亦非以此歟？凡此皆變化之道，神之所為也。
translation_en: … the middle of the [third] month; wheat requires that we look to the completion of its ripening, so Grain in Ear (Mangzhong) is placed within the fifth month. Awakening of Insects (Jingzhe) and Pure Brightness (Qingming) are spoken of in terms of wind and thunder. At Awakening of Insects, the myriad things emerge in Zhen; Zhen corresponds to thunder, and thunder first sounds in the second month, so it is placed in the second month. At Pure Brightness, the myriad things are ordered in Xun; Xun corresponds to wind, and the wind cleanses and orders things in the third month, so it is placed in the third month. The first month is the beginning of heat, and the sixth month is the end of heat; therefore, Lesser Heat (Xiaoshu) and Greater Heat (Dashu) come after the Summer Solstice (Xiazhi). The seventh month is the beginning of cold, and the twelfth month is the end of cold; therefore, Lesser Cold (Xiaohan) and Greater Cold (Dahan) come after the Winter Solstice (Dongzhi). The nodal qi of the eighth month is White Dew (Bailu), and the nodal qi of the ninth month is Cold Dew (Hanlu). Yet autumn belongs to the phase Metal, and the color of Metal is white. White is the color of the dew, and cold is the qi of the dew; its color first turns white and only then does its qi become cold—thus cold certainly develops gradually. The medial qi of the tenth month is Lesser Snow (Xiaoxue), and the nodal qi of the eleventh month is Greater Snow (Daxue). Yet cold qi begins with dew, reaches its middle stage with frost, and culminates in snow; as snow progresses from lesser to greater, how could it be without gradualness? Placing Lesser Fullness (Xiaoman) in the middle of the fourth month is because the single yin is just then sprouting at this point, and one ought to apply the principle of guarding against the minute and checking gradual trends. Placing End of Heat (Chushu) within the seventh month is because the hot qi stops (chu) at this point—is this not like the word chu ("ceased") in the phrase "the rain has fallen and has ceased"? At the Autumnal Equinox (Qiufen), water begins to dry up; at Beginning of Winter (Lidong), water begins to freeze; at the Winter Solstice (Dongzhi), spring waters stir; and by Beginning of Spring (Lichun), the vapour of water flows abroad—this is why Rain Water (Yushui) is established after Beginning of Spring. Before frost, there is dew; dew turns from white to cold, and by the time of Cold Dew, the dew condenses into frost—is not placing Frost's Descent (Shuangjiang) in the wake of Cold Dew also for this reason? All of these are the way of transformation and the work of the inscrutable spirit …

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也愚何足以知此姑掇拾所聞以復惟執事進
教之幸甚
第五問
沈爕
同考試官訓導李批時務一策正欲觀士子學識
此作敷答詳明處置切當宜
在優等
考試官教諭鄭批議論正當切於時務
考試官學正王批有斷制
===
為政之道莫先於養民養民之要莫切於農桑
農桑為衣食之本而民生之至急者也衣食不
足則放僻邪侈無不為已雖有善政善教將安
施乎故孔子答問政以足食為先孟子論王道
以養民為首蓋此謂也古聖王知其然於是制
閭里均井地百畝之田勿奪其時五畝之宅樹
之以桑其惰者有三推九推之化以勸之其游
者有里布夫家之征以懲之其力之羸乏也有
受田歸田之期以節之其地之肥磽也有一易
punctuated:
也。愚何足以知此？姑掇拾所聞以復，惟執事進教之，幸甚。

第五問
沈爕
同考試官訓導李批：時務一策，正欲觀士子學識。此作敷答詳明，處置切當，宜在優等。
考試官教諭鄭批：議論正當，切於時務。
考試官學正王批：有斷制。

為政之道，莫先於養民；養民之要，莫切於農桑。農桑為衣食之本，而民生之至急者也。衣食不足，則放僻邪侈，無不為已，雖有善政善教，將安施乎？故孔子答問政以足食為先，孟子論王道以養民為首，蓋此謂也。古聖王知其然，於是制閭里，均井地，百畝之田，勿奪其時，五畝之宅，樹之以桑。其惰者，有三推九推之化以勸之；其游者，有里布夫家之征以懲之；其力之羸乏也，有受田歸田之期以節之；其地之肥磽也，有一易
translation_en:
… How could an ignorant person like me be sufficient to know this? I have merely gathered what I have heard in order to reply, and I would consider myself most fortunate if Your Excellency would advance and instruct me further.

Fifth Question
Shen Xie

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Li: In a policy essay on current affairs, one seeks precisely to observe the learning and insight of the candidates. This composition sets forth its answer with detailed clarity and proposes practical measures that are apt and fitting; it ought to be placed in the superior grade.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zheng: The discussion is upright and sound, and relevant to current affairs.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Wang: Possesses decisive judgment.

In the Way of governance, nothing comes before nourishing the people; among the essentials of nourishing the people, nothing is more urgent than agriculture and sericulture. Agriculture and sericulture are the foundation of food and clothing, and the most pressing necessities of the people's livelihood. When food and clothing are insufficient, the people will stop at nothing in waywardness, depravity, deceit, and extravagance; even if there are good policies and good teachings, how could they be put into effect? Therefore, when Confucius answered questions about governance, he put sufficient food first, and when Mencius discussed the Kingly Way, he placed nourishing the people at the head—this is what they meant. The ancient sage-kings knew this was so; therefore, they established village communities and equalized the well-field lands, ensuring that for a field of a hundred mou its agricultural seasons were not夺 [taken away], and that a homestead of five mou was planted with mulberry trees. For the indolent, there was the transformative example of the ruler's three pushes and the ministers' nine pushes of the plow to encourage them; for the idle, there were the taxes of neighborhood cloth and household levies to penalize them; for those whose strength was weak or exhausted, there were fixed ages for receiving and returning land to regulate them; and for the varying fertility and barrenness of the soil, there were the methods of resting the land for one year…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
二易之法以更之故男有餘粟女有餘布生長
老死於仁政者此也降及後世秦不師古任商
鞅廢井田開阡陌聽其所耕不限多少三代良
法美意殄滅盡矣由是富者田連阡陌而兼并
之患起貧者地無立錐而游手之民興𨁺稍桀
黠有資力者率舍勞就逸以趨末業而守耒耜
緣南畝者盡蚩蚩之氓賣絲糶穀常稱貸於其
前徴租索錢每取盈於其後終歲勤動而室遂
為之一空矣何怪乎膏梁者不耕而耕者糲飯
===
不充文繍者不蠶而蠶者裋褐不足天地生生
之仁幾乎息矣逮我
皇明受天明命撫有四海百年于兹恐民之飢寒也
故考課於守令者以農桑為首慮民之游惰也
故載之於版籍者以事產為先以至於
大誥又有互知丁業之條凡所以重農養民之法
無不備舉是宜老者衣帛食肉黎民不飢不寒
措天下於仁壽之域躋斯世於熈皞之天自二
帝三王以来未有盛於今日者也執事猶以太
punctuated: 二易之法以更之。故男有餘粟，女有餘布，生長老死於仁政者，此也。降及後世，秦不師古，任商鞅廢井田、開阡陌，聽其所耕，不限多少，三代良法美意殄滅盡矣。由是富者田連阡陌，而兼并之患起；貧者地無立錐，而游手之民興。𨁺稍桀黠有資力者，率舍勞就逸，以趨末業；而守耒耜、緣南畝者，盡蚩蚩之氓。賣絲糶穀，常稱貸於其前；徴租索錢，每取盈於其後。終歲勤動，而室遂為之一空矣。何怪乎膏梁者不耕，而耕者糲飯不充；文繍者不蠶，而蠶者裋褐不足，天地生生之仁幾乎息矣！逮我皇明受天明命，撫有四海，百年于兹。恐民之飢寒也，故考課於守令者以農桑為首；慮民之游惰也，故載之於版籍者以事產為先；以至於《大誥》又有互知丁業之條。凡所以重農養民之法，無不備舉。是宜老者衣帛食肉，黎民不飢不寒，措天下於仁壽之域，躋斯世於熈皞之天，自二帝三王以来，未有盛於今日者也。執事猶以太
translation_en:
… once-fallow and twice-fallow rotation to alternate them. Thus men had surplus grain and women had surplus cloth; that they lived, grew old, and died under benevolent governance was because of this. Coming down to later ages, Qin did not model itself on antiquity, employing Shang Yang 商鞅 to abolish the well-field system and open up the field pathways, allowing people to cultivate as they pleased without limiting the amount; the good laws and fine intentions of the Three Dynasties were utterly destroyed. From this, the rich had fields joined across the pathways, and the evil of land annexation arose; the poor had not enough land to stand an awl, and idle hands sprang up among the people. Moreover, those who were somewhat crafty and possessed capital and means generally abandoned toil for ease in order to pursue secondary occupations, while those who kept to the plow and worked the southern acres were all simple, ignorant folk. Selling silk and grain in advance, they constantly borrowed at interest beforehand; when rents were levied and money demanded, full payment was always exacted afterward. Though they toiled diligently all year round, their houses were consequently stripped bare by it. What wonder is it that those who eat fine meats do not plow, while those who plow do not have their fill of coarse rice; that those who wear embroidered silks do not tend silkworms, while those who tend silkworms do not have enough short coarse-wool garments, and the life-giving benevolence of Heaven and Earth has almost ceased!

When Our August Ming received the bright mandate of Heaven and came to rule over the Four Seas, a hundred years ago now, fearing lest the people suffer hunger and cold, in evaluating the performance of Prefects and Magistrates it made agriculture and sericulture the first priority; concerned lest the people be idle and lazy, in recording them in the population registers it put their occupations and property first; and even in the Grand Pronouncements (Da gao 大誥) there is also the statute on mutual knowledge of adult males' occupations. Every method for emphasizing agriculture and nourishing the people has been fully instituted. It is fitting, then, that the elderly wear silk and eat meat, the common people suffer neither hunger nor cold, the empire is placed in a realm of benevolence and longevity, and this age is raised to a heaven of prosperous peace—since the Two Emperors and Three Kings, there has never been a time more flourishing than today. Yet Your Excellency still regards the…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
平既久風俗日侈務本者少趨末者多以為意
外之憂欲求所以處之之法愚以為莫若定經
費抑兼并擇賢守令躬行勸率不妄興工役以
奪其時不横加賦斂以困其力勤有賞惰有戒
又於緇黄商賈市井官宦厮役技藝數者之中
擇其理所當禁者而驅之使復業理所當容者
而聽之使自便於勢有所不論焉守之以定力
持之以悠久則何患民有飢寒之憂乎吁救流
弊於積習之餘憂患害於未發之先此固儒者
===
所當究心也愚生處之之術不外乎此不識執
事以為何如
punctuated: 平既久，風俗日侈，務本者少，趨末者多，以為意外之憂，欲求所以處之之法。愚以為莫若定經費，抑兼并，擇賢守令，躬行勸率，不妄興工役以奪其時，不横加賦斂以困其力，勤有賞，惰有戒；又於緇黄、商賈、市井、官宦、厮役、技藝數者之中，擇其理所當禁者而驅之使復業，理所當容者而聽之使自便，於勢有所不論焉。守之以定力，持之以悠久，則何患民有飢寒之憂乎？吁！救流弊於積習之餘，憂患害於未發之先，此固儒者所當究心也。愚生處之之術不外乎此，不識執事以為何如？
translation_en: …peace has lasted so long, customs have grown daily more extravagant, few devote themselves to fundamental agriculture while many pursue secondary occupations—taking this as an unforeseen concern, you wish to seek a method for dealing with it. In my humble opinion, there is nothing better than fixing regular expenditures, curbing land annexation, and selecting worthy prefects and magistrates to personally lead and encourage the people, neither rashly initiating public works that rob them of their farming seasons, nor arbitrarily imposing taxes and levies that exhaust their strength, rewarding the diligent and warning the indolent; and furthermore, from among those several categories—Buddhist monks and Daoist priests, merchants and traders, marketplace idlers, official attendants and menial servants, and artisans—selecting those who in principle ought to be prohibited and driving them back to their agricultural occupations, while allowing those who in principle ought to be tolerated to do as suits their convenience, without regard to power or influence. If we uphold this with resolute strength and maintain it over a long duration, what worry will there be that the people might suffer from hunger and cold? Alas! Remedying current abuses born of entrenched habits, and worrying over calamities before they have even broken out—this is assuredly what Confucian scholars ought to set their minds to investigate. Your humble student's method for dealing with the matter goes no further than this; I do not know what you, sir, think of it?

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
皇上臨御之七年歲在辛卯實當大比
賓興之秋総賛兩廣軍務兼理巡
撫都察院右都御史韓雍巡按廣
東監察御史程宏暨藩憲大臣恪
遵
成憲預聘師儒為考試官至期斂所
部十郡士以試之凡百執事罔不
===
勤慎各共乃職而重光等司考校
者亦精白一心以公去取事竣得
其文之恊準彠者七十五人皆精
選也小錄告成僉謂重光宜有言
以序末簡夫治本於道道載於經
明夫經者道必深深於道者文必
工若孔子所謂有德者必有言是
已肆我
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序
皇上臨御之七年，歲在辛卯，實當大比賓興之秋。総賛兩廣軍務兼理巡撫都察院右都御史韓雍、巡按廣東監察御史程宏暨藩憲大臣，恪遵成憲，預聘師儒為考試官。至期，斂所部十郡士以試之。凡百執事罔不勤慎，各共乃職；而重光等司考校者，亦精白一心，以公去取。事竣，得其文之恊準彠者七十五人，皆精選也。小錄告成，僉謂重光宜有言以序末簡。
夫治本於道，道載於經。明夫經者道必深，深於道者文必工，若孔子所謂「有德者必有言」是已。肆我
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In the seventh year of His Majesty's reign, the year being xinmao [1471], it was indeed the autumn for the triennial examination and the presentation of worthy scholars as guests to the court. Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate Han Yong 韓雍, Assisting in the Supervision of Military Affairs and concurrently Grand Coordinator of Liangguang, Regional Inspector of Guangdong and Investigating Censor Cheng Hong 程宏, together with the senior officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, respectfully complied with the established statutes and in advance engaged Confucian masters to serve as Examiners. When the time arrived, they gathered the scholars of the ten prefectures under their jurisdiction to examine them. Every single officiating functionary was without exception diligent and cautious, each fulfilling his duties; and I, Chongguang 重光, and the others in charge of evaluating and grading the papers were likewise pure and united in heart, making selections and rejections with impartiality. When the affair was concluded, we obtained seventy-five men whose essays conformed to the standard rules—all of them fine selections. With the examination record completed, everyone said that I, Chongguang, ought to offer some words as a postface on the final pages.

Now, good governance is rooted in the Way, and the Way is conveyed in the Classics. Those who illuminate the Classics must be profound in the Way, and those who are profound in the Way must be accomplished in literary composition; this is precisely what Confucius meant by saying, "The virtuous are sure to have something notable to say." Therefore our…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
國家設科取士而試以文百有餘年
于兹無非欲得道德之士以為致
治之本也
列聖相承寔同一心
皇上協重華之德躋重熙之運恢弘治
道益崇科目故士之豪傑者胥此
焉出矧東廣為天下雄藩川嶽鍾
秀代不乏人文章節義照耀古今
===
諸士子生長是邦沐
國家作養之恩充聖賢體用之學故
其發而為文根經據理奇本乎易
葩原乎詩疏通發乎書之奧莊敬
著乎禮之經而筆削謹嚴又倣乎
春秋之旨誦而觀之鏘然瓊琚玉
珮之音越也燦然山龍華蟲之采
列也儼然夏圭商敦之器陳也非
punctuated: 國家設科取士而試以文，百有餘年于兹，無非欲得道德之士以為致治之本也。列聖相承，寔同一心。皇上協重華之德，躋重熙之運，恢弘治道，益崇科目，故士之豪傑者胥此焉出。矧東廣為天下雄藩，川嶽鍾秀，代不乏人，文章節義，照耀古今。諸士子生長是邦，沐國家作養之恩，充聖賢體用之學，故其發而為文，根經據理，奇本乎《易》，葩原乎《詩》，疏通發乎《書》之奧，莊敬著乎《禮》之經，而筆削謹嚴又倣乎《春秋》之旨。誦而觀之，鏘然瓊琚玉珮之音越也，燦然山龍華蟲之采列也，儼然夏圭商敦之器陳也。非
translation_en: … the dynasty has established examination categories to select scholars and tested them through literary compositions for more than a hundred years up to the present, solely wishing to obtain scholars of moral integrity and virtue to serve as the foundation for bringing about good governance. Successive sacred emperors have inherited one another's legacy, truly sharing a single mind. His Majesty harmonizes with the virtue of double brilliance and ascends to an era of cumulative splendour; he broadens the Way of governance and increasingly esteems the examination system, so that outstanding heroes among the scholars all emerge from here. How much more so since eastern Guangdong is a mighty province of the empire, where rivers and mountains concentrate their finest essence; no generation has lacked talent, and their literary accomplishments and righteous integrity have shone across past and present. The scholars born and raised in this region have been bathed in the dynasty's grace of nurturing and cultivation, and have filled themselves with the learning of the sages and worthies concerning substance and function. Therefore, when they express it as literature, it is rooted in the Classics and grounded in principle: its marvelousness is based on the Book of Changes (Yi), its luxuriance originates in the Book of Odes (Shi), its fluent comprehension brings forth the profundities of the Book of Documents (Shu), its solemn reverence manifests the constant norms of the Rites (Li), and its rigorous writing and pruning imitate the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu). When one recites and observes their writings, how resonant is the far-reaching sound of fine jade pendants and ornaments! How resplendent is the arrayed brilliance of mountain, dragon, and pheasant emblems! How dignified is the display of ritual vessels like the jade tablets of Xia and the grain bowls of Shang! If not for…

title: 成化七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
雋味道腴卒澤於聖學之淵海者
能之乎登名是錄固非倖然自茲
以往論秀春官擢第
大廷為名進士有官守言責之寄尚
當體道出治輔世康民以媲美乎
前烈垂耀於後世益有以見是科
得人之盛而主司選拔之公顧不
偉歟借使藉是為决科計而行不
===
逮焉者則非余之所望而亦非諸
士子之所以自期待也尚其勗之
成化七年秋八月既望江西饒州
府餘干縣儒學教諭鄭重光謹序
punctuated:
雋味道腴、卒澤於聖學之淵海者，能之乎？登名是錄，固非倖然。自茲以往，論秀春官，擢第大廷，為名進士，有官守言責之寄，尚當體道出治，輔世康民，以媲美乎前烈，垂耀於後世，益有以見是科得人之盛，而主司選拔之公，顧不偉歟？借使藉是為决科計，而行不逮焉者，則非余之所望，而亦非諸士子之所以自期待也。尚其勗之！

成化七年秋八月既望，江西饒州府餘干縣儒學教諭鄭重光謹序。
translation_en:
…one who has savored the rich flavor of the Way and been thoroughly nourished in the deep ocean of sage learning, who could accomplish this? To have one's name entered into this record is certainly no matter of mere luck. From this point onward, when they are evaluated as talents by the Ministry of Rites and pass in the Great Court to become renowned metropolitan graduates (jinshi), entrusted with official duties and responsibilities of remonstrance, they should embody the Way in bringing forth good governance, assisting the age and bringing peace to the people, so as to rival the splendor of past worthies and hand down glory to future generations. This will even further demonstrate the abundance of talent obtained in this examination and the fairness of the examiners' selection—would that not be magnificent? If, however, anyone uses this merely as a stepping stone for passing the examinations while his conduct fails to measure up, that is neither what I hope for nor what the scholars expect of themselves. May they strive earnestly!

Respectfully prefaced by Zheng Chongguang 鄭重光, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yugan County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, on the sixteenth day of the eighth month in the autumn of the seventh year of the Chenghua reign (September 1, 1471).
